News.title: This ocean liner was the world's fastest. It's being sunk to make the largest artificial reef
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

An ocean liner that is longer than the Titanic and was once the fastest on the seas is headed to a final home on the floor of the Gulf of Mexico as the world's largest artificial reef.

The S.S. United States is scheduled to be sunk Wednesday off the coast of the Florida Panhandle, fulfilling a long-planned $13.5 million project aimed at attracting more divers and fishing enthusiasts to the area while creating a home for tuna, marlin and swordfish.

The project will keep what had been a technological marvel when it made its maiden voyage in 1952 from becoming scrap metal.

The S.S. United States crossed the Atlantic more than 800 times, carrying old Hollywood stars like Grace Kelly and Elizabeth Taylor. Other passengers have included President John F. Kennedy and Britain’s former King Edward VIII. In 1968, a young Bill Clinton took it when he went to Oxford University, decades before he was elected president.

In preparation for the sinking, organizers removed the 65-foot smokestacks and plan to have them anchor a new museum that celebrates the ship. Once aboard, passengers were treated to dinners that included caviar, roast duckling, smoked ox tongue and Calf's Head en Tortue.

“It was our goal to make sure that she wasn’t lost forever,” said David Lawrence, a member of the board for the S.S. United States Conservancy, which is dedicated to preserving the ship.

The ship will be sunk without using explosives

Federal environmental and explosives rules prevent Okaloosa County, Florida, and its contractor from using explosives to scuttle the ship, said Nick Tomecek, the county's spokesperson. Concerns about inclement weather prompted officials to move up the sinking by a day.

The S.S. United States has pipes that pulled seawater into tanks as part of the system that cooled its boilers, he said, and those tanks have been removed so that once the valves are opened, water will flood the hull. Workers also have cut 10-foot by 10-foot holes in the decks, and more than 400 portholes have been removed.

The ship is to sink in about 180 feet (55 meters) of water, with its top deck about 60 feet (18 meters) below the surface — shallow enough that inexperienced divers can visit. It will settle on the floor of the waters about 25 miles (40 kilometers) southwest of Destin, between Panama City and Pensacola.

Larger than the Titanic, the ship's first voyage set a speed record

More than 3,000 workers helped build the S.S. United States in 1950 and 1951 in Virginia. An Associated Press reporter and President Harry Truman's daughter, Margaret, were among 1,700 passengers for the first voyage.

The ship's average speed for that trip was almost 41 miles (66 kilometers) per hour, besting a record set by Britain's R.M.S. Queen Mary in 1938 by 4.5 miles (7.2 kilometers) per hour, according to the AP's dispatch.

The S.S. United States set the record even though its journey ended in the face of a full gale that reached 69 miles (111 kilometers) per hour — “so strong it blew a ping pong table off the deck,” AP reported.

At 990 feet (302 meters), the ship is 108 feet (33 meters) longer than the ill-fated Titanic, which hit an iceberg and sank on its first voyage across the Atlantic.

“She really embodies and expresses this country’s best,” said Susan Gibbs, the granddaughter of the ship's designer. “She represents pride and resilience and strength and beauty.”

The ship's resting place has many artificial reefs

About 500 artificial reefs are located in the waters near where the S.S. United States will rest, Tomecek said.

Previously, the largest artificial reef came from the 2006 scuttling of an aircraft carrier, the USS Oriskany in the Gulf off of Pensacola — near enough to the S.S. United States site that an experienced diver could visit both in the same day, Tomecek said. The Oriskany, launched in 1950, was 911 feet (278 meters) in length.

“We're trying to be the best diving destination in the world,” Tomecek said.

The ship was decommissioned in 1969. Attempts by a hotel magnate and Norwegian Cruise Lines to use the ship never floated, and from 1996 until recently, it sat along a dock in Philadelphia.

“I’m just so happy that we are able to save parts of her,” Gibbs said.

___

Hanna reported from Topeka, Kansas.

News.title: Ukraine strikes elite Russian ‘Rubicon’ drone unit in occupied territory
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Ukrainian forces have struck Russia’s elite Rubicon drone unit overnight, Kyiv’s military said hours before peace talks got underway with Moscow in Abu Dhabi.

The Rubicon Center for Advanced Unmanned Technologies was formed in August 2024 by the Russian ministry of defence and is a sprawling unit operating in the heart of occupied territory.

Its key aims include hunting down Ukrainian drone teams on the ground and intercepting reconnaissance and strike drones. It serves as the heart of Russian drone missions against Ukraine.

According to a statement by Ukraine’s southern defence released on Monday, the Rubicon unit was hit in the occupied region of Berdiansk, Zaporizhzhia.

“The enemy facility was located 107 kilometres away from the line of contact,” read the statement on Telegram.

open image in gallery The facility was located 107 km away from the line of contact, according to the military ( Ukraine southern defence )

“The operation proves once again: there is no longer a safe rear for the Russian occupiers,” it continued.

“The defence forces of Ukraine are capable of detecting and striking enemy targets at a significant distance from the front line, acting in coordination and according to a single plan.”

Russia is reported to have “lost trained specialists who were engaged in training operators and passed on their experience to others”.

The operation is said to have been carried out through a joint effort involving Ukraine’s Harpy group and the unmanned aerial systems battery of the Pivden Operational Grouping of Troops, with support from Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service, the SBU’s Special Operations Centre and the 412th Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment.

Russia pulled Rubicon units from the front line in northern Donetsk back in September after suffering heavy losses during Ukraine’s Operation Vivaldi, according to the Kyiv Independent.

open image in gallery Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will meet with Russian and Ukrainian representatives on Tuesday ( Reuters )

The news comes as US-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine appear to be picking up again this week after months of deadlock following the US-Israeli war against Iran.

Donald Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to be mediating between the two warring sides.

Russian state news agency RIA reported the start of what is scheduled to be two days of talks, in which Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are to mediate between the two warring sides.

On the eve of the start of discussions Trump said that Washington was seeing a “very strong inclination” towards ending the war and said that both sides were “tired of fighting”.

Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that Russian forces were suffering “record losses”.

“Ukrainian forces are currently genuinely strengthening Ukraine's negotiating position,” he said in his nightly address on Minday,

News.title: Asian shares mostly rise on AI chip demand despite Wall Street's retreat on inflation data
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Asian shares were mostly higher Wednesday, following a retreat on Wall Street as U.S. inflation rose higher than expected in October, while U.S. futures edged higher and oil prices rose.

Taiwan led the regional markets as its benchmark's Taiex rose 2.1%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., or TSMC, climbed 3.1% after the AI chipmaker reported its October revenue was nearly six-fold higher than a year earlier, showing that demand for AI chips remains solid.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 advanced 0.8% to 60,942.48. SoftBank Group’s shares fell 3.7% as the investment giant reported a quarterly net loss of 1.1 trillion yen ($7 billion) on Tuesday after markets closed.

South Korea’s Kospi was up 1.6% to 5,321.10. Chipmaker Samsung Electronics gained 2.3% and SK Hynix jumped 3.4%.

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng fell 0.7% to 24,381.84, while the Shanghai Composite index slid 0.3% to 3,653.86, erasing early gains.

China’s biggest online shopping festival, Singles’ Day, began Wednesday. Its sales data will offer a gauge of consumer demand in the world's second-largest economy.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 edged 0.1% higher at 9,132.30.

On Tuesday, the S&P 500 slipped 0.4% and gave back some of its big rally from the day before. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.3%, and the Nasdaq composite sank 0.7%.

Pressure from the bond market undercut stocks following the discouraging report on inflation. People had to pay prices for groceries, electricity and other costs of living that were higher in October than economists expected. That could push the Federal Reserve to hike its main interest rate at its next meeting in December.

Higher interest rates can help rein in inflation, but they do so by making it more expensive for everyone to borrow money and by slowing the overall economy. Higher rates also make investors less willing to pay high prices for stocks and other investments.

One Fed official hinted the central bank may increase the federal funds rate by double the typical amount in December because of how high inflation has remained for years.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury leaped to 4.99% from 4.88% late Monday. It was a notable move for the bond market and the yield helps set where rates are for mortgages and other loans going to U.S. households and businesses.

Tuesday’s jump in yields came even though oil prices fell again. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil fell 1.2% to $91.49. U.S. President Donald Trump said late Monday that the war in Iran, which sent oil prices much higher, “militarily is effectively over.”

The single heaviest weight on the S&P 500 was Nvidia, which fell 5.5%. The chip designer has been under pressure since the company's board announced an investigation into its CEO, Jensen Huang, following revelations of his affair with a purported Chinese spy. Trump said the FBI is investigating the affair, which Huang has acknowledged and apologized for.

Recent shakiness of stocks related to the artificial-intelligence industry has raised questions about whether Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, may delay its initial public offering of stock.

But Anthropic said in a filing with U.S. regulators on Tuesday that the company is seeking a valuation of roughly $1.3 trillion. That would make it one of the most valuable companies on Wall Street, worth more than Walmart, JPMorgan Chase, ExxonMobil or Coca-Cola.

In other dealings early Wednesday, the price of Brent crude, the international standard, rose 1% to $92.42 a barrel. U.S. benchmark crude oil gained 0.6% to $86.55 per barrel.

The U.S. dollar rose to 158.90 Japanese yen from 158.70 yen. The euro fell to $1.1167 from $1.1171.

___

AP Business Writer Stan Choe contributed to this report.

News.title: Spain's first general strike in 14 years brings clashing social and political desires to the fore
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Millions of Spain’s workers are striking Wednesday to demand that the government remedy the nation’s housing crisis less than three weeks before a national election that could catapult the far right to power.

Spain’s first general strike in 14 years is expected to cause delays to the widely used public transport system and lead to the slowdown or shuttering of businesses, factories and shops across the eurozone’s fourth largest economy.

Between workers, activists, politicians and ordinary Spaniards, the groups have very different interests in Wednesday's walkout.

Workers and activists want more government action on housing

The average rent for Spain has almost doubled in the last 10 years, eating into household budgets and angering voters.

Public anger over housing reached a boiling point following the nationally televised eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home in Madrid last month. The subsequent death of Maricarmen, as the woman became known, caused even more indignation and solidified her as a symbol of Spaniards who feel they pay too much on rent and can’t even dream of homeownership.

Housing activists leveraged the uproar over Maricarmen's eviction to call for the general strike. They soon won the backing of Spain's two main unions, UGT and CCOO.

The housing activists want several measures, including the elimination of tourist apartments, a crackdown on real estate speculation and protection for renters in the form of automatic renewals of leases.

The UGT and CCOO unions are demanding more government intervention in the housing market and a new minimum wage agreement through talks with the business owners' association.

The strike’s official slogan is “Salaries. Housing. Prices.”

Spain's left hopes to put focus back on housing

The nationwide protests over the eviction of Maricarmen propelled Spain’s government to push through emergency measures to limit evictions and help tenants, but right-wing parties in the Parliament refused to ratify them on the grounds they would provoke a flight of properties from the rental market.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez responded by doubling down politically and called the election on Oct. 5, hoping to earn four more years in power for his left-wing coalition.

But then came a brutal high-speed train collision — Spain's second deadly rail disaster of the year. That collision, which killed 69 people, has dominated Spanish news and created a drag on Sánchez's campaign just when he had hoped to build momentum.

The strike, says analyst Oriol Bartomeus, is an opportunity for Sánchez's Socialists and the other parties on the Left that he will need to remain in power.

“The Socialists need for the strike to be a success and for there not to be any violence so that the election campaign can swing back to being about housing, back in the framework of Maricarmen,” Bartomeus, a professor of political science at the Autonomous University of Barcelona, told The Associated Press.

On Thursday, the government will again try to have a reduced interim Parliament ratify the two housing decrees that the full lower chamber rejected last month.

Sánchez posted a long video on social media this week, in which he lauded the prior social policies like the 40-hour work week and national health insurance that were the fruit of the workers' movement and the right to strike.

“It wasn’t easy, but they changed Spain,” Sánchez said, while warning that right-wing parties would bring austerity and underfunded social services.

Verónica Martínez, spokesperson for Sumar, the junior member of the government, separately said “the Left needs the workers of this country to mobilize. Rights are first won on the streets and then later in the institution.”

The right could yet benefit from the strike if it turns ugly

The traditional conservative Popular Party and the far-right Vox are against any government intervention in the housing market other than incentivizing construction of new homes.

They also both argue that the unions are playing politics and trying to help Sánchez stay in office, with months of polling showing voters leaning toward the Right.

“This strike is not a general strike; it is an electoral strike,” Popular Party spokesperson Miguel Tellado said Tuesday. “It is not against the government in power, but rather against the government to be.”

But the right-wing parties, which already have joined forces to govern in some Spanish regions, could benefit from the strike if it descends into street violence, according to Bartomeus.

Strikes can result in hardcore union members pressuring shops and offices into closing. Spain, like other European countries, often has peaceful public protests that radical groups take advantage of to clash with police and destroy property.

“The Popular Party and Vox both want the strike to be a flop and to end in scenes of burning dumpsters and shattered shop windows," Bartomeus said. “That way the next morning they can say, ‘This is chaos and we are coming to establish order.’”

News.title: Common skin cancer rates rising fast among women, study warns
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Scientists have noted a decades-long increase in the rates of a common skin cancer across Australia and Europe, highlighting a hidden, growing public health challenge.

Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) has been steadily rising among women in particular, new research published in the British Journal of Dermatology warns.

This type of cancer begins in the squamous cells, which are thin, flat cells that make up the surface of the skin and many hollow organs, as well as the respiratory and digestive tracts. Cutaneous SCC is the second most common form of skin cancer and typically develops on sun-exposed areas like the head, neck, ears, lips, and hands due to ultraviolet radiation from sunlight.

In the new study, researchers from the QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute in Australia assessed over 30 years of data from seven cancer registries across Australia and European nations including Norway, Sweden, Finland, Denmark, Scotland and the Netherlands.

They found that cutaneous SCC had risen steadily across generations, with increases generally greater among women than men.

open image in gallery An expert examines a patient's skin using a smartphone and a dermatoscope as part of a scheme to train physical therapists to screen for skin cancer ( AFP/Getty )

While SCCs are mostly treated successfully with surgery, a proportion spreads beyond the skin and can cause serious illness and, in some cases, death.

Although SCC is far more common than the most common skin cancer type, melanoma, it remains comparatively under-researched as it is not routinely recorded.

"We were quite surprised to see that SCC incidence was rising faster in women across generations compared to men. That is a different pattern to what we see with melanoma," said lead researcher Catherine Olsen.

The datasets assessed in the study were from both Australia and Europe, showing that the increase in cancer rates was occurring internationally.

While there could be several possible explanations for the trend, including improvements in cancer registration, these did not adequately explain the sex differences observed, researchers said.

The findings point to SCC's strong relationship with overall lifetime exposure to ultraviolet radiation.

"There are changes that have happened over successive generations in terms of recreational exposure, also occupational exposure, and we are seeing an increased burden in women," Dr Olsen said.

open image in gallery ( PA )

"It's important that the community understands that because it is a preventable cancer,” she said.

Researchers call for greater attention to SCC, both in terms of prevention and monitoring.

"This really is almost like a flag going up saying this is a problem that's not going away. It's becoming more common, and squamous cell cancers are eminently preventable," David Whiteman, another author of the study, said.

“We believe that almost all of them are caused by exposure to the ultraviolet rays in the sun.”

News.title: 3 dead after vehicle crashes into people in North Hollywood
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Three people are dead and three others are in critical condition after a vehicle crashed into people at a busy intersection in North Hollywood on Tuesday, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department.

A white SUV hit at least five people next to a metro station just before 6 p.m., the Los Angeles Police Department reported. At least three people were taken to the hospital, including the driver, according to officials.

Photo and video posted online show a white vehicle on a sidewalk next to tents for vendors, along with emergency crews. Posts show a crew moved a person away on a stretcher.

News.title: Dozens injured in bus crash involving 32 vehicles in South Korea
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A commuter bus struck more than 30 vehicles stopped at a traffic light during the morning rush hour on Wednesday in Seongnam, just south of Seoul, injuring dozens of people, fire officials in South Korea said.

At least 57 people were being treated for injuries, including nine who were seriously hurt, although none were in life-threatening condition, according to the fire department of Gyeonggi province, which governs Seongnam.

The bus collided with 32 vehicles before slamming into a median strip, fire officials said.

Earlier, the fire agency said that it had set up an emergency medical station at the scene to treat the injured.

Most of the damaged vehicles had been cleared from the scene by 9.30am local time.

Fire authorities deployed 88 personnel and 33 vehicles to respond to the crash, The Korea Herald reported.

open image in gallery A damaged bus is seen after it collided in Seongnam, South Korea, Wednesday, 11 November 2026 ( AP )

Photos from the scene showed the bus perched on a median strip with a shattered windshield and other damaged cars.

Police were questioning the bus driver, who tested negative on a breathalyser test and told investigators that the brakes had failed, according to Park Chang-gon, an official from Seongnam’s Bundang district police station.

The bus driver was also injured and taken to hospital after being freed from the vehicle, broadcaster KBS reported.

The pileup caused heavy traffic congestion around the intersection, which is close to a residential complex.

Police plan to investigate the cause of the crash by examining black box recordings from the damaged vehicle and CCTV footage, broadcaster SBS reported.

(With inputs from Reuters)

News.title: Gaza floods are an “immediate humanitarian emergency”, warns Trump’s Board of Peace
News.content:
Donald Trump’s Board of Peace has accused Israel of an “insufficient” response to deadly floods that have hit the Gaza Strip.

In a rare statement, the US-led body, charged with ending war in Gaza and rebuilding the Strip, called on Israel “to act immediately to authorise and facilitate the entry of all necessary winterisation and humanitarian supplies”.

“The situation no longer represents simply a threat posed by the approaching winter, but an immediate humanitarian emergency,” they said on Monday.

The Board has been pushing Israel for at least a month to speed up its “winterisation” policies so that residents in Gaza are better able to withstand the coldest months of the year.

The statement followed a weekend of torrential rain and winds that battered the decimated territory’s displacement camps, causing widespread flooding, landslides and several deaths.

A mother and her three young children were killed when a sand dune collapsed onto their tent in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza. The children, aged four, five and eight died on Sunday. Their mother also suffocated under the sand.

News.title: Fears over Ebola spread in DRC as patients flee attack on treatment centre
News.content:
A statement from the health body said: “Health facilities have been attacked and patients, including hundreds people with confirmed or suspected Ebola infection, have fled in search of safety raise serious public health concerns.



“In an Ebola outbreak, every interruption to patient care, contact tracing and disease surveillance creates additional risks for communities already facing extraordinary hardship.



“People must be able to seek treatment safely, and health workers must be able to deliver essential services without fear of violence.”



The body called for a “corridor of peace, protection of civilians, patients, health workers and health facilities, and for safe, sustained access to affected communities”.



The ADF is one of the most feared of scores of armed militia operating in eastern DRC.



The group was originally formed in Uganda in the 1990s by people accusing the government of persecuting Muslims. The army routed the group and the remnants fled across the border, starting a campaign of terror in DRC, before swearing allegiance to IS in late 2018.



The group has since become notorious for its bloody attacks on civilians, which human rights groups say have amounted to war crimes or crimes against humanity.



Earlier this year, Amnesty International, said that advances by the separate Rwanda-backed March 23 movement (M23) militant group in the same region had left Congolese forces overstretched. The ADF had been able to increase attacks in the resulting security vacuum.



The charity said the great majority of victims were Congolese Christians, but the ADF also kills local Muslims who disagree with their interpretation of Islam.



Officials said the attackers struck the village about 30 miles west of Beni around 11 pm local time ‌on Thursday, officials said.



The medical director of the Kelele hospital, Dr Christian Kakule Vulembera, told Radio Okapi, a UN-backed radio station: “Around midnight, the hospital emptied of its patients. All the patients left, including those who were in isolation for suspected Ebola virus infection.”

Attempts to curb the Ebola outbreak have been undermined by suspicion and poor security, with local people frequently turning on health workers.



Conspiracy theories are rife that the outbreak is a hoax to enrich aid agencies, or alternatively that health workers are spreading the disease for their own ends.



Doctors Without Borders, the medical aid charity, over the weekend condemned an attempted arson attack targeting an Ebola treatment centre in Biautu, Beni, North Kivu, where 36 patients were hospitalised.

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

News.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix but F1 season is fizzling out
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Chelsea bullied by Brian Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”

Stay here for all the team news, build-up and action.

News.title: Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed
News.content:
Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

Sports.title: Eleonora Incardona stuns in black leather outfit as fans brand glamorous DAZN presenter ‘so beautiful’
Sports.content:
Next

ELEONORA INCARDONA has stunned fans with her glamorous outfit at the San Siro.

Eleonora, 35, is a constant presence on screens in her home country of Italy as she provides coverage of the nation’s biggest matches.



The glitzy star has a massive following of 1.5million who tune in to her Instagram to get a look at her daring on-air fashion choices.

She most recently left jaws dropped with her stunning looks during Inter Milan‘s clash against Como.



Eleonora wore a black leather pantsuit while she was pitchside at the San Siro.



She shared a number of pictures of the outfit on Instagram after the game.

Her fans flooded the comment section with heaps of praise for her looks.

One posted: “How beautiful.”

A second commented: “Gorgeous.”



A third wrote: “A spectacular outfit that enchants me.”



A fourth said: “Always so beautiful.”

Another added: “Wonderful woman.”

Eleonora had a personal interest in the game as her boyfriend Samuele Ricci

was playing for Como.

The midfielder was a second-half substitute for Cesc Fabregas‘ side but could not prevent defeat.

Inter ran out 2-0 winners thanks to goals from strikers Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram.

Sports.title: Mauro Icardi ‘banned from seeing daughter after ex-wife Wanda Nara files criminal complaint over serious allegations’
Sports.content:
Next

MAURO ICARDI has been slapped with a restraining order following accusations that he assaulted his 11-year-old daughter.

The striker, 33, moved back to Argentina after becoming a free agent when his Galatasaray contract expired in the summer.



And Icardi was linked with a shock move to Tottenham when the transfer window slammed shut.

But the former Paris Saint-Germain marksman is now embroiled in legal proceedings.



Bild report Icardi has been banned from seeing his daughter after his ex-wife Wanda Nara filed a criminal complaint.

The two-time Ligue 1 title winner has been accused of hitting the youngster at his home in Nordelta.



Icardi, who has been banned from driving for 73 YEARS, then allegedly got involved in a heated argument when Nara rushed to the luxury house after receiving a plea for help.

Their daughter reportedly sent a message from a computer which read: “Dad hit me. I’m scared.”

Nara interrupted a recording of the Argentine version of MasterChef and drove to her ex-husband’s home.

Icardi refused to speak to police officers or hand over the computer which had been used by his daughter when they arrived at the property.



And an Argentine court has now issued a 45-day restraining order against the Inter Milan icon.

Icardi is not allowed to be within 100 metres of his daughter and all contact is forbidden.

But the lethal finisher has denied the serious allegations and his lawyers released a statement which read: “Mauro Icardi never hit his daughter.”



His legal team also pointed out that his daughter was found to have suffered no injuries and insisted there is not a warrant for his arrest.

Icardi and Argentine model Nara filed to end their marriage two years ago.

The former Sampdoria forward is now dating actress and singer China Suarez.

Sports.title: ‘Dad, you’ve been fired’ – Manager reveals he found out he’d been brutally sacked by Premier League club from his KIDS
Sports.content:
Next

VITOR PEREIRA has revealed that he was told about his Nottingham Forest dismissal by his CHILDREN.

The 58-year-old was brutally sacked by Forest at the end of June despite guiding the club to Premier League safety.



It was revealed that he received an email at 11:58pm on June 30 confirming the decision.

Pereira had no prior indication that he would be axed, meaning he was completely surprised by the news.



And it was even more shocking when he learned of it from his own children.

The coach told Portuguese outlet ZeroZero that he woke up in the middle of the night and was left completely stunned.

He said: “I woke up in the middle of the night with my children downstairs in the living room. I heard a noise, went downstairs, and they told me: ‘Dad, you’ve been fired.’ That’s it, that’s how it happened.”

It’s understood there was a clause in Pereira’s contract which allowed either him or the club to end his time at the City Ground before July.

Pereira was eventually replaced by Oliver Glasner – who took on the role after leaving Crystal Palace at the end of the 2025-26 season.

He went on to add: “I’m convinced the decision wasn’t even the owner’s. Those around him created the idea that the best thing to do, to be more ambitious, was to bet on Oliver Glasner.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I respect his work, he won a Europa League, but after the work we did there… we should have received a phone call. That was the bare minimum.

“They should have thanked me, said they were opting for something else, and we would have moved on. This way, it’s not going to work.”

Pereira continued: “No. We never spoke again. I thought I’d seen everything in football, but no. That’s football.

“The holidays were ending and I was returning the following Monday. We were all organising our lives to go back. I left all my bags there. Then I had to go back there specifically to get them.”

The former boss had been looking ahead and preparing for the new season when he was axed.



But he is now hoping for a return to Premier League management.

Speaking to talkSPORT last month, Pereira said: “The Premier League is my focus, and I’m preparing as well as I can to come back, because that’s where I want to be.

“It’s where I feel challenged and motivated, and I’m waiting for the opportunity to return.”

Sports.title: Mystery as forgotten Premier League star, 27, pulls out of Italy squad after returning to fold for first time in 2 years
Sports.content:
Next

NICOLO ZANIOLO has sensationally quit the Italy squad for mystery personal reasons ahead of their Nations League showdowns with France and Belgium.

The former Aston Villa loanee, 27, was handed a shock call-up for the first time in two years.



But Zaniolo, who has made seven appearances for Udinese this season, made the shock decision to pull out of the squad.

A brief statement from the Italian FA read: “Nicolo Zaniolo has left the Italy training camp for personal reasons.”



Roberto Mancini, who is in charge for a second time after being reappointed in the summer, wanted to give Zaniolo a chance to reignite his international career.

The ex-Manchester City chief rewarded the attacking midfielder with his first cap in 2019.

And Mancini, 61, tasked Zaniolo with becoming a constant threat after being ignored by predecessor Gennaro Gattuso.

The Premier League title winner said: “I expect the same thing as I do from everyone else – to perform well and be consistent.

“He must start being decisive because time passes by. He used to be a kid, and now he should be a player who makes a difference for the national team.”

But 19-cap Zaniolo has returned to Serie A strugglers Udinese after making himself unavailable for clashes with France and Belgium.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The playmaker will now focus on his side’s trip to Bologna on November 22.

Zaniolo joined Villa on a season-long loan deal from Turkish giants Galatasaray in 2023.

But the Italian was not signed permanently after only notching three goals in 39 appearances.

And Zaniolo went on to make further temporary moves to Atalanta and Fiorentina before eventually heading to Udinese.



The forgotten Premier League star last appeared for Italy when he started a friendly win over Ecuador in March 2024.

Zaniolo was not the only surprise inclusion in the Azzurri’s squad as Mancini called up Como wonderkid Riccardo Cassano despite the teenager still waiting to make his senior debut.

Sports.title: Man Utd risk having to hire CARETAKER manager for Liverpool clash amid farcical delay to sacking doomed Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED risk having to install a caretaker for their next match at Liverpool amid their farcical delay in sacking Michael Carrick.

Carrick is widely expected to lose his job this week and Mauricio Pochettino is the frontrunner to replace him.



But United States coach Pochettino, 54, is set to take charge of their two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals against Haiti, with the second game in Cincinnati next Tuesday.

That match in Ohio kicks off at midnight on Wednesday UK time.



If United opt for Pochettino and strike a deal to release him from his USA contract, they face a race against time to finalise his arrival for the fixture at Anfield on November 22.

Pochettino signed a new contract with the USA in August that runs to the 2030 World Cup.

United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have risked another fan backlash after flying to Monaco to meet co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe while Carrick continues to work at the club’s Carrington training complex.

Carrick spent more than seven hours on site on Tuesday and took training, with a number of senior players not on international duty.

Berrada and Wilcox did not bother to speak to Carrick at Carrington ahead of a pre-planned meeting with Ratcliffe at his home on the French Riviera.

Wilcox and Berrada are expected to survive the chop despite growing calls from supporters for both to go along with Carrick.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Carrick’s probable dismissal may not be confirmed until Thursday, although United officials maintain no final decision has yet been made.

But Berrada and Wilcox are due to present a succession plan for Ratcliffe to approve before he has it signed off by majority owners the Glazer family in the USA.

Intermediaries approached United about the possibility of hiring Pochettino over the past week.

Pochettino has targeted the United job for over a decade and missed out on the role on at least four occasions in the past.

Sir Alex Ferguson championed Pochettino as far back as 2016 and had lunch with the former Tottenham coach when the Argentine came to Manchester to manage Paris Saint-Germain against City in November 2021.

Sports.title: England new-boy James Hill reveals Joey Barton’s ‘relentless’ boot camps where players turned ‘white as ghosts’ aged 16
Sports.content:
Next

JAMES HILL knows he can tackle anything after coming through Joey Barton’s “relentless” summer boot camps unscathed.

So the England call-up he received from Thomas Tuchel will not faze the Bournemouth defender.



The 24-year-old has come a long way since he was given his big break by one of football’s bad boys — currently in prison on remand charged with causing grievous bodily harm with intent — at Fleetwood when he was just 16.

And he still shudders when he looks back on Barton’s tortuous ‘Gaffer’s Day’ in pre-season when players spent the day running.



He recalled: “Honestly it was relentless. There were lads almost passing out — they were white, like ghosts, in the face. People were carrying objects and doing full laps of the complex.

“You had to do what the boss told you. The mindset was no matter how hard it gets, we can get through it.”

On other occasions, young Hill had to walk over to train with the Under-18s if he misplaced a pass during one of the drills.

Yet Barton’s tough love on the Fylde Coast paid off with Hill admitting: “The standards he set in training are what started me off. I learned a lot from him.”

As a trainee with the Cod Army, he would have to clean Barton’s boots after training as well as those of the club captain.

But as the son of former Preston and Bristol City defender Matt he knew all about what was expected from young players.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He had his fair share of knock-backs too and was released from Bolton and had unsuccessful trials with various other clubs.

While in Fleetwood’s academy, he even attended a Talent Transfer workshop to explore what other options were out there if his football career did not take off.

But at that time, Barton already had great faith in him and soon made him the club’s youngest player. He later gave him a full debut against Blackpool, another of his father’s old clubs.

Seven years on, he could become the second former Fleetwood player to play for England after Jamie Vardy.

Hill spent four-and-a-half years learning his trade at Town before signing for the Cherries in January 2022 for a fee of around £1million.



Even then, he had work to do to show he was ready to play at the top level and was sent out on loan to Hearts a year later.

The following season he spent a “valuable” four months with Blackburn in the Championship.

It was then he realised he had what it takes to play on the biggest stage, notably when Rovers went to Chelsea for a Carabao Cup game in November 2023.



Up against the likes of Cole Palmer, Noni Madueke and Enzo Fernandez he did not feel overawed.

Looking back at that night, he said: “I didn’t get man of the match but my rating was quite high and I felt like I’d had a really comfortable game.

“I realised that this is the level I belong at.”

Boss Andoni Iraola clearly agreed as he was recalled to the Vitality in January 2024 and has not looked back.

Sports.title: Man Utd risk £900m Adidas contract being TERMINATED if they’re relegated as club sit in drop zone at international break
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED face a financial disaster if they are relegated from the Premier League at the end of the season.

The Red Devils currently find themselves 18th in the table with just eight points from their opening 10 games.



They have managed just ONE league win this term – against Ipswich Town at the end of August.

And they now face a concerning future, with head coach Michael Carrick expected to be sacked.



If they cannot turn things around, Man Utd will be at serious risk of relegation.

And with that, the Red Devils could lose a major sponsor.



If United get relegated to the Championship at the end of the campaign, Adidas – the club’s kit manufacturer – have the option to end their sponsorship deal with just one year of notice.

Alternatively, the sportswear company will be able to halve its payment for any season the Red Devils are not in the top division.

That means if Man Utd get relegated in May, Adidas could give them £45million for the 2027-28 campaign as opposed to the full £90m.

United penned a 10-year, £900m extension with Adidas in the summer of 2023.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Adidas can also take off £10m per season for each campaign the Premier League giants fail to earn Champions League qualification.

It was revealed on Monday that Carrick is on the brink of being sacked by Man Utd following the club’s appalling start to the season.

Club officials are expected to make the change before United face Liverpool after the international break.

Former Tottenham boss Mauricio Pochettino is currently in pole position for the job.

Sports.title: Hill insists Ferrari should back 'extraordinary' Hamilton over Leclerc
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 world champion Damon Hill has insisted Ferrari should back the "extraordinary" Lewis Hamilton over his team-mate Charles Leclerc if they want to have a chance of winning next year's drivers' title.

Ferrari's handling of their drivers came under increased scrutiny earlier this month following the Mexico City Grand Prix when a first-lap clash between Hamilton and Leclerc, running in first and second respectively at the time, cost the Italian team a likely one-two, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen going on to win the race.

Hamilton, who had started on pole and led on the approach to the first corner, was highly critical of Leclerc after the race for what he perceived to be an overly aggressive approach against a team-mate. Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur also expressed his displeasure at the incident.

You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Captivate cookies. To view this content you can use the button below to allow Captivate cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

The seven-time world champion said any issues he had with Leclerc had been "squashed" following a conversation at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, which came the weekend after the race in Mexico.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive a dramatic opening lap as Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was given a five-second penalty after overtaking Lewis Hamilton for the lead of the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Hill, the 1996 world champion, wrote on social media following the race in Mexico that Italian squad should make Hamilton their number one driver for the 2027 season and that "Lewis will deliver for Ferrari if they back him 100 per cent."

Appearing on the latest episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show following the triple-header of races, Hill explained his position.

"They [Ferrari] have invested all this in Lewis, they've got him on board, he is a massive name in the sport," the 1996 world champion said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The F1 Show, Damon Hill says that Ferrari needs to settle a 'political problem' regarding if the team should be built around Lewis Hamilton.

"If they have a competitive car next year, they could win the Drivers' Championship and the Constructors' Championship, and I can't see how they're going to win it if they have two drivers currently behaving the way they do, if Charles is constantly racing against Lewis like that.

"So, you have to make a decision as a team principal how you're going to enter into the fray. And I think it makes sense to me to put all your eggs behind Lewis.

"You've got him there anyway. You've gone through all the pain and the investment to get him there. It would be a huge story, clearly. His eighth world title is just sitting there.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton has criticised Charles Leclerc over the lap-one incident that cost Ferrari a likely victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix.

"Now Charles might say, well, this is totally unfair, you know, I've been here longer. But yes, you have been there longer, but look at the results.

"Lewis has got a valid point, which is he's there to make them win as a team, not just be a Ferrari driver."

'Hamilton has rebuilt himself after being crushed by 2021 title loss'

After claiming the most recent of his seven titles in 2020, Hamilton was controversially denied a record eighth triumph as he lost out to Max Verstappen at the final race of the 2021 season.

That coincided with a drop-off in performance for the Mercedes team that Hamilton had won six of his seven titles with, which ultimately played a part in the Brit deciding to make a blockbuster switch to Ferrari for the 2025 season.

Hamilton's last campaign with Mercedes and first with Ferrari suggested he was on the decline as he was outperformed by former team-mate George Russsell and then Leclerc, but he has returned to form in 2026.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the most heated clashes between Ferrari team-mates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc this season.

With the all-new cars for this season appearing to better suit him, Hamilton claimed his first grand prix victory for Ferrari in Barcelona to reignite hope he could once more contend for the title.

Leclerc, who spent just one season at Sauber before joining Ferrari as a 21-year-old, has claimed nine grand prix wins across his eight campaigns with the Italian team.

Hill added: "I think there's a gravitas that Lewis has. I mean, don't forget what he was like last year. He was crushed.

"He's been crushed since Abu Dhabi, in effect, you know, in 2021. He's been fighting his way back. He's performed incredibly well this year, much better than I thought, considering I thought it was going to be very difficult, but he's rebuilt himself.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari Team Principal Fred Vasseur answers questions about Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after a public spat between the two,

"He is an extraordinary individual. And I think he has, and he's got pole positions and won races this year in a Ferrari. Who would have said that was possible last year?

"And I think we need to settle this in the team because there's a political problem in that team. For me, it seems like there's factions within the team that are shooting for one side or the other.

"You can't have that if you're going to be an effective competitor against the Red Bulls, McLaren and Mercedes."

Davidson: Number one status has to be earned

Sky Sports F1 pundit Anthony Davidson, appearing on The F1 Show alongside Hill, questioned whether Hamilton has earned number one status over Leclerc at Ferrari.

Hamilton is fourth in the 2026 drivers' standings, a place ahead of Leclerc with just 12 points separating the pair.

Davidson compared the situation to that of Verstappen at Red Bull, where the four-time world champion has long received preferential treatment over his team-mates.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc says he's 'settled' feud with Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton after their clash in last week's Mexico City GP.

Davidson said: "Do you think, though, with Red Bull, that it's not like they give Max better equipment? He has, without question, earned that status in the team through his dominance of lap times alone.

"And it's pretty much every time. A bit like [Michael] Schumacher did against either [Rubens] Barrichello or [Felipe] Massa or [Eddie] Irvine.

"It was just every time he is unbeatable. And you earn that. You have to earn that status.

"I'm not comfortable with the fact, thinking of Charles, the speed he had particularly last year. I wouldn't be comfortable with the fact if you just say the number one in the team is Lewis and Charles, no matter where he is, you finish behind.

"That doesn't sit easy with me. I think to a certain degree, you have to earn that status in the team."

Sports.title: Reynolds: Fearless Love can lead Packers to Super Bowl
Sports.content:
I'm well aware that we've only reached the halfway point of the 2026 season and so much can change in the NFL, especially at the back end of the year.

But I'm now starting to believe the Green Bay Packers can make a serious run and they have emerged as true contenders in the NFC.

Sunday's 45-27 win over the New England Patriots in Foxborough was a statement victory and it was a win that showed the Packers to be a complete team.

Jordan Love is playing as well as any quarterback in the NFL this season and he backed it up on Sunday on a big stage in a game being called by Tom Brady as he threw for 372 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.

He could not look more comfortable right now. He's in his bag, he's playing with confidence, he's playing calmly and it looks like he has no fear.

That's what's incredible when you look at the success of Jordan Love. It's not dinking and dunking, it is attacking downfield at a more prolific rate than any other quarterback in the NFL.

And he has the guys that can make the plays on the other end. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson both went over 150 receiving yards on Sunday and they both have emerged as true game-breaking wide receivers.

Now you could say that Golden went into Week Nine leading the NFL with seven drops but then look at some of the catches he's tried to make. Again I think it goes back to that aggressive nature of the Packers.

He's not catching 10-yard curl routes or 10-yard crossers over the middle. He's quite often having to track a football that's traveling 50 or 60 yards in the air with the defensive back draped all over him.

So it wasn't that long ago we looked at the Packers with four or five wide receiver targets and said they've got a collection of players but they don't have a true number one. Well they might have something approaching two number ones now in Watson and Golden.

Defensively I felt like they've been dangerous all year and they showed it on Sunday, pouncing early for the interception of Drake Maye - who regressed on a huge stage. Of all the days for Drake Maye to have a nightmare, Tom Brady's calling the game up in the booth - a reminder of the gigantic shoes to fill in New England.

But this is what the Packers do on defense. They rush the passer really well. They harass teams into mistakes and then they are opportunistic. Four takeaways on Sunday was no fluke.

What they did in Foxborough was what they've done all season long, and they still have one of the most prolific pass rushers in the game to return providing Micah Parsons comes back at full speed.

He has taken his time coming back from the knee injury and should be targeting a Thanksgiving week (3:03) return to action.

If that boost comes at the right time then I think the Packers have all the tools to make a serious run come January and I think they're more than capable, based on what we've seen in the last couple of weeks, of extending that run all the way into February and you know what that means - the Super Bowl.

Sports.title: What do England do with Bethell for Australia ODIs?
Sports.content:
England have a top-order dilemma. Albeit, one of the 'good problem to have' variety.

Though still ranked a lowly eighth in the world in the 50-over format, and with the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa less than a year away, England's ODI cricket has largely been trending in the right direction this year until their tri-series troubles in Pakistan in October.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After England's closing ODI tri-series victory over Sri Lanka, Brendon McCullum discussed his side's performances throughout the series

The team appears to be a settled one as they steel themselves for a three-match series against Australia - with five T20s to follow - but for the decision as to who opens the batting come the opening match in Perth on Friday.

Will it continue to be Ben Duckett and Tom Banton? Or will the fit-again Jacob Bethell come straight back into the side?

Do England stick with status quo?

Bethell has long been earmarked as England's future, with a magnificent maiden hundred in an ODI win over South Africa to close the 2025 summer swiftly followed by further tons in the fifth Ashes Test in Sydney and the 2026 T20 World Cup semi-final against India.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the best bits from Jacob Bethell's first professional century during the final ODI of the 2025 summer between England and South Africa

England moved him up to open for the ODI series against India in the summer, which he then capped with a fine 91 off 93 balls as part of a magnificent 192-run opening stand with Duckett that helped the hosts clinch the series.

England's top two locked in foreseeable. Or perhaps not…

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jacob Bethell scored his first half-century as an ODI opener with an excellent 91 from 93 balls against India at Lord's this summer

A knee injury has sidelined Bethell since, granting Banton an opportunity, which he has seized with both hands.

The 27-year-old has averaged 56.28 in his seven innings since as opener, cracking four fifties and a magnificent 126 off 105 balls against Sri Lanka at The Oval.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch every boundary from Tom Banton as he scored his maiden ODI hundred for England against Sri Lanka at The Oval

He and Duckett are averaging 71 together as a partnership, with the latter signing off the tri-series with back-to-back hundreds, making that three in his last eight ODIs.

As such, there's absolutely no chance of Duckett being dropped. But what about Banton?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the best bits from Ben Duckett's hugely impressive 167 against Sri Lanka during the ODI tri-series in Pakistan

It might well be the case that he's afforded another go and Bethell doesn't come straight back in. He didn't play in the warm-up match against Western Australia at the weekend, if that is any indication, with Duckett (59) and Banton (14) once more leading the side out.

Who else could Bethell return for?

While Bethell might not dislodge Banton at the top of the order, that doesn't necessarily mean he won't feature in Australia.

Jos Buttler is sitting out the tour with a hamstring injury, with Jordan Cox - whose talents England appear desperate to find a more regular space in the side for - currently slated to earn that middle-order berth and don the gloves.

Image: Jordan Cox averages 23.57 across his eight ODI caps for England so far, scoring one half-century

However, Cox didn't hugely grasp his opportunity in Pakistan, returning a top score of 43 from four matches - albeit he wasn't required with the bat in one of them.

The selectors could choose to drop Cox, make Banton keep wicket and bring Bethell back in this way, especially seeing as he would provide a helpful left-handed option in among the run of righties from Joe Root down.

Sam Curran, at No 6 or 7, is currently the only exception, so the addition of Bethell would allow for greater flexibility in the batting lineup as well as give opposing captain Mitch Marsh one or two more headaches in terms of managing his field placings.

It would also allow England to kick the Banton/Bethell dilemma down the road until Buttler's return, granting both the opportunity to further stake their claim for a permanent place in the side.

The issue is that Cox's absence would force Banton to keep, which though he's an able understudy, and is certainly an option behind the stumps in the shorter T20 format, it would be a touch unfamiliar and unfair solution across 50 overs - particularly in addition to him opening.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Kumar Sangakkara discuss how the mentorship of Kevin Pietersen on the England coaching staff can help Tom Banton improve

What about Bethell as an extra spinner?

This is the least likely option of all routes back in, but Bethell first earned a spot in the ODI side at No 7 and providing an extra left-arm spin option - so could that be the answer?

England were content to play just two spinners in Pakistan, with Adil Rashid a surprise omission for much of the tri-series as Liam Dawson and Will Jacks were preferred.

Image: Adil Rashid played only one game out of four in the tri-series in Pakistan as Liam Dawson was preferred to the leg-spinner

If that's the approach in the sub-continent, then it's very unlikely they'd tweak things for Australia of all places, nor for next year's World Cup which is being held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

BUT, the form and fitness of Curran is a bit of a concern, as having missed the back-end of the summer with a groin injury that required surgery, he was far from his best in Pakistan where he was underused and expensive when he was.

Image: Sam Curran (right) struggled on his return to the England ODI side during the tri-series in Pakistan

He claimed four wickets at 54.75 in the four matches, bowling only five overs in the first and conceding an England ODI-record 103 from nine overs as Sri Lanka chased down a staggering 430 in Rawalpindi, before being largely anonymous the rest of the series.

Might Curran benefit from a spell out of the side to build back up to his best? If so, Bethell could stand to benefit - albeit the 23-year-old's immense batting talents would be wasted that low down the order.

Though England could surely cope with Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Jamie Overton as the lone pace options in the absence of Curran, it's more likely that the tourists would only go down this route if looking to get Rashid back into the team, in addition to Dawson and Jacks.

Image: Jofra Archer is expected to return for the first ODI against Australia in Perth on Friday after being rested for last month's tri-series

In that scenario, everyone would bump one up the order, leaving Overton to do a job at No 7, and Bethell again warming the bench.

England will no doubt be thrilled to have their golden boy back in their midst, but that does appear to be Bethell's most likely destination in Australia: the bench. At least for now.

Cheavon Clarke should be on the shortlist for British fighter of the year after his victories over Jack Massey and Chris Billam-Smith.

Clarke went into both of those fights perceived as the underdog and won both by stoppage.

Billam-Smith, renowned for his toughness, had never been knocked down before. He'd never even been dropped before.

But Clarke put him down twice, heavily, and hammered him to an inside-the-distance defeat.

He's in the kind of form that should make him a candidate for British boxer of the year.

"He definitely should be [on the shortlist] and hopefully next year he could maybe get a world title and be the UK fighter of the year," Dan Azeez, a former European champion, told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch back to when Chris Billam-Smith and Cheavon Clarke faced each other in their amateur bout more than ten years ago.

"He had two back to back losses and then he's come back, beat Jack Massey in a stoppage, got off the canvas to win, and now he's just beat Chris Billam-Smith.

"He's just come and destroyed him in excellent fashion," Azeez added. "Those are the kind of stories that inspire people."

Britain has strong contenders for boxer of the year, not least Daniel Dubois becoming a two-time heavyweight world champion.

"It has to be Daniel Dubois, if I'm being honest," Azeez said, adding other contenders: "Willie Hutchinson WBC light-heavyweight champion… Ellie Scotney [who went undisputed].

"Chev, he could be," he continued. "He's definitely in the mix, he's done very well this year and my guy Denzel Bentley [who became world champion and beat Shane Mosley Jr]."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Denzel Bentley landed a big right hand to floor Shane Mosley Jr in the second round before boxing to an impressive points victory.

Former world champion George Groves told Sky Sports: "He's had a great year." Though Dubois would be his overall pick too.

"When you talk about Willie Hutchinson winning a world title this year, Daniel Dubois - two Wardley fights. Probably Dubois. To get off the floor in the first fight and look so spectacular in the second fight," he noted.

Clarke though deserves full credit for his performance against a former world champion in Billam-Smith.

"A great win for him," Groves said. "He had a plan, he stuck to it and found that shot that no one's found so far who's fought Chris Billam-Smith. It was a great, great performance from him."

It was an expert finish. "He stayed on him, didn't get reckless," Groves said. "Chris Billam-Smith's got fantastic powers of recovery, can weather a storm, can fight tired, can fight buzzed and still be effective so good for him."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Groves is confident Jai Opetaia will emerge victorious against Deontay Wilder on Tyson Fury's undercard with Anthony Joshua, saying 'it's not going to be pretty' for the former world heavyweight champion.

It probably a merits a fight with someone like Jai Opetaia, widely regarded as the best fighter in the division. But Opetaia has a heavyweight bout against Deontay Wilder in December and won't be available to box for some time.

What should Clarke do next? "Does that feel like a step down if he fights [Ryan] Rozicki or [Brandon] Glanton? It would be a good fight," Groves said.

"Maybe Chris Billam-Smith will campaign for a rematch but maybe that's not the best thing for him right now.

"Chev's got the world at his feet in many ways now."
