That absence badly exposed United's lack of depth at left back, an area the hierarchy failed to address in the transfer window despite a clear need. Diogo Dalot, who was targeted by fans when he came off against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday, has played poorly while filling in on his unfavoured side.

With Patrick Dorgu now back in the mix, too, Shaw is hoping to be in contention for the trip to Anfield in what would be a timely boost for a defence that has conceded the joint-most goals in all competitions of any team in Europe’s top five leagues this season.

Defenders on Reds’ radar

Nothing has undermined Carrick's time as United head coach more than the defensive problems that have seen his team concede 15 goals in their last five games.

United chose to delay the overhaul of their defence until next year when they focused on rebuilding the midfield last summer, but it has proved to be a costly misjudgment with Matthijs de Ligt only just returning to action after a year out and a spate of injuries to Shaw, Lisandro Martinez, Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui.

It may force United into the transfer market in January and Confidential understands Brentford centre back Nathan Collins and Fulham’s Calvin Bassey have joined Jarrad Branthwaite of Everton on the list of potential targets.

United also want a striker after failing to offload Joshua Zirkzee and sign cover for Benjamin Sesko in the summer, but a loan deal is more likely.

Brentford's Nathan Collins and Fulham's Nigeria star Calvin Bassey have both joined United's list of centre-back targets

Relegation kit-astrophe

As if the prospect of relegation isn’t nightmarish enough for United after they dropped to 18th place in the table, the cost of going down would be astronomical.

Although parachute payments from the Premier League would cushion the fall in the unlikely event that United are relegated, kit sponsors adidas have the option to scrap their record £900million, 10-year deal which was announced in 2023 but only came into effect last year.

Under the terms of the contract, the German sportswear giant can cancel it if they give the club one year’s notice. Adidas can also halve their annual payment to £45m if United aren’t playing in the Premier League, and hit the club with a £10m annual penalty if they are not in the Champions League.

Banner clampdown

Two banners protesting against United’s owners were confiscated by stewards during Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

One that read ‘Jim Can’t Fix This’ was seized because its connection to Jimmy Savile was deemed to be inappropriate. Another declaring ‘We Don’t Want A New Stadium, We Want New Owners’ was taken down because it was blocking the view of some fans.

Club insiders say protests will always be allowed as long as they remain within the regulations. United kept a close eye on Sunday’s demonstration with a more visible police presence in the Stretford End and stewards asking fans as they entered that section of the stadium which group they were with.

The protest, which once again involved green and gold balloons being released before kick-off, was jointly organised by The Red Army, The 1958, Manchester United Youth Supporters Club, South Stand United and Retro Reds.

However, it seemed like a strange decision to confiscate the banners considering that United were in possession of them for more than 30 hours before kick-off since 10am on Saturday morning.

They are stored in the same place in the Stretford End before every game, so it was odd for United to demand that they be taken down when they could have refused for them to be handed out in the first place.

A banner protesting against United's owners was confiscated during the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa

Onana’s word perfect

While goalkeeper Senne Lammens was giving his worst performance in a United shirt against Villa on Sunday, the man he replaced at Old Trafford was faring a little better in Turkey.

Andre Onana kept a clean sheet in Trabzonspor’s win over Alanyaspor as they moved into second place in the Super Lig table behind Galatasaray.

It came three days after a Europa League defeat by Freiburg when Onana couldn’t resist a little light ribbing of English reporters at the game.

Asked by journalists from Daily Mail Sport and the BBC for a quick word, the Cameroon international didn’t disappoint. ‘I don’t speak English, bro,’ Onana said, in perfect English. Classic.

Sports.title: Australia DID tamper with the ball during 2017-18 Ashes just before 'Sandpapergate' scandal - and the whole team knew, admits former player Usman Khawaja
Sports.content:
Australia DID tamper with the ball during 2017-18 Ashes just before 'Sandpapergate' scandal - and the whole team knew, admits former player Usman Khawaja

Australia were doctoring the ball against England in the 2017-18 Ashes according to the latest revelations from Usman Khawaja’s whistle-blowing autobiography.

Within the chapter of the newly-released Sabr that covers the explosive claim that all of the Australian team were in on the sandpaper scandal in South Africa eight years ago, Khawaja goes on to reveal that ball tampering was embedded in the dressing room during the 4-0 series win over England that preceded it.

England’s players suspected that Australia had altered the condition of the ball in the third Test at Perth when despite heavy rain, the home attack managed to extract extravagant reverse swing to dismiss Joe Root’s side on the final day.

Reverse swing is most typically generated when the dry nature of the playing square scuffs up one side of the ball and the other is polished vigorously by the players on their trousers, using a combination of that friction and the application of sweat to create a smooth sheen.

However, Khawaja reveals that an attack featuring Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins, and Josh Hazlewood plus off-spinner Nathan Lyon had found other ways to get the ball moving off the straight in Adelaide and Perth that winter.

‘On day five, Starcy bowled that unforgettable ball to James Vince off the crack,’ he wrote.

Former Australia star Usman Khawaja claims all of the Australia team knew about the ball-tampering during the 2017-18 Ashes series

‘We were reverse swinging it late on day five. Actually, we were reverse swinging the ball the game before too - except it was much tougher, because it was the pink ball.

‘But we - and I say 'we', because were a team, whether you did the deed or not - had worked out that, if we raised the flaps up on the quarter seam on that ball, it was almost like it had a rudder on it and it'd start reverse swinging.

‘And before you start going at me, calm down. The whole world was doing whatever little they could to try and reverse swing the ball.’

Despite Khawaja’s caveat that such practice was commonplace, under Law 41.3 of the Laws of Cricket, players are strictly prohibited from taking any deliberate action that artificially alters the physical condition of the match ball.

Either prising up, scratching or deteriorating the quarter seam - the secondary seam on the ball that runs at a right angle to the prominent stitched one, and there to secure the leather pieces together - with fingernails, thumbs or foreign objects is illegal and punishable by match officials. A player caught in such an act can face a substantial fine and/or suspension.

If the quarter seam is raised, it can create a tiny flap of leather on the rough side of the ball, which disrupts the air flow on that side, and manufacturing reverse swing that would not occur naturally as a result.

Suspicion was raised in the away dressing room at the famous WACA ground when Australia overcame a three-hour rain delay on day five to pick off England's remaining six wickets for an Ashes-sealing victory that evening.

Only days after Australia’s skulduggery in Cape Town was exposed, leading to lengthy bans for captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, former England captain Alastair Cook revealed the hunch.

David Warner has supported Khawaja's claims, saying they are '100 per cent accurate'

Emphasising the huge differential in lateral movement achieved by the rival bowling attacks the previous winter, Cook said: ‘We did think in Perth, when the outfield was wet after the rain, how had they managed to get the ball reversing?

‘I didn't see anything, (but) we've been pretty good on the ball, managing the ball so that it can reverse swing at certain times. Jimmy (Anderson) is obviously very good at reverse swinging, we got it going a touch at Melbourne either way, but with those drop-in pitches we didn't get it going massively.’

Khawaja’s confirmation of the Australian dressing room culture follows Daily Mail Sport’s exclusive story in the aftermath of the Cape Town sting that David Warner had relayed tampering methods to England players over a drink at the end of the Ashes - an episode Cook personally reflected on in his own autobiography the following year.

It emerged earlier this week that, according to Khawaja, Australia had used sandpaper at Port Elizabeth - in the Test match that preceded the powder keg Newlands contest.

He also states in his book that the entire Australian team were in on the malpractice, not just the trio that were punished - a claim that Warner said was ‘100% accurate.’

However, breaking the silence of the four bowlers who released a statement in 2021 denying prior knowledge of a foreign object being brought onto the field in Cape Town, Starc said his recollection of events had not changed.

‘As far as our statement said, we weren’t aware of things being taken on the field, that’s where I’ll leave it,’ Starc said.

‘We weren’t aware anything was taken on to the field to be tampered with. We saw (the sandpaper) on the big screen in Cape Town.

‘As far as the book is concerned, I haven’t read it. I probably won’t read it. So that’s for Usman to elaborate on. I’ll stick to what I said five years ago, what I said at the time, eight years ago. Clearly, there’s different versions from different people, and I’ll leave it where I left it back then.’

The revisiting of sandpapergate has left a significant proportion of the Australian public demanding another probe, after Warner slammed the original eight years ago as ‘rushed and botched.’

However, Cricket Australia insisted it will not be reopening the investigation, with the organisation’s chief executive Todd Greenberg saying that there was not ‘any compelling reason’ to do so, despite Khawaja’s version of events contradicting previous ones to have made the public domain.

Ex-Australia captain Michael Clarke is leading the calls to revisit the inquiry into a team whose reputation is arguably already irreparably damaged, saying fans have not been able to move on from it.

‘They can't trust what's real. They don't know the truth until this gets reopened and the truth comes out,' Clarke told 2DayFM.

‘Now we've got this opportunity. I would just like to see whatever the truth is for it all to come out, allow people to finally tell the truth, and move on.’

While Smith and Warner were suspended for 12 months and lost their rights to leadership upon return and Bancroft - who was caught on camera trying to conceal the sandpaper in his trousers - was for nine months, no other Australian player or coaching staff member was censured.

But Bancroft’s response to being asked, in a 2021 British newspaper interview, if the bowlers’ knew - ‘it’s probably self-explanatory - reopened the festering sore of Australia’s past and triggered the unusual joint statement from Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and Lyon.

Now, courtesy of Khawaja’s determination for collective accountability, they face questions regarding their conduct in cricket’s most revered series of them all.

Sports.title: Man Utd draw up fresh plan that could save Michael Carrick ahead of crunch Monaco meeting
Sports.content:
Man Utd draw up fresh plan that could save Michael Carrick ahead of crunch Monaco meeting

Manchester United could still keep Michael Carrick in his role as they seek to further bolster their coaching line-up to ensure the under fire boss has more quality around him

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's future will be decided on Wednesday (Image: OLI SCARFF, AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United could yet keep Michael Carrick on as boss - but with additional coaching support as the club's senior figures weigh up their next move.

‌



‌



The likes of Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox will sit down at a summit with minority owner and Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe on Wednesday in Monaco, where the expectation is that Carrick will be removed from his role.

‌



He has presided over a run of one win in 10 Premier League games to start the season, which has left the club in the relegation zone. There has been a willingness to see Carrick succeed and the hierarchy have stood by him despite just three wins all season.

‌



And if Carrick is to remain in charge beyond the international break then there is the option to bring in more coaching quality around him, given the United boss has ultimately never been in charge of a Premier League club.

Bayern Munich coach Aaron Danks, who worked with Carrick at Middlesbrough and was seen as a potential appointment in the summer, is one option, reports the BBC.

Carrick already has Steve Holland alongside him. Holland was previously Chelsea's assistant and then worked as Gareth Southgate's No 2 for a number of successful years with England. But clearly the current set-up is not working and the club are looking to make a positive change.

‌



Ultimately they had never planned for a managerial change, and especially not this early in the season. As a result no one has been lined up and appointing managers midseason presents its own challenges, but there are a number of candidates on their radar, several being out of work.

Mauricio Pochettino is among those who are in a job, he's leading the USA but has been linked with the post previously. Eddie Howe left Newcastle in the summer and could be tempted back into management. His Premier League experience is a plus. Big name foreign coaches are also being eyed, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte are two of the names most regularly mentioned.

‌



View 2 Images Aaron Danks, currently at Bayern Munich, is seen as someone who could come in

Nagelsmann has led Bayern and Germany whilst Conte has won league titles with four different clubs - one of those being Chelsea. Both men who fit the bill of being able to lead a heavyweight club, even if United are at their lowest ebb during the Premier League era.

Article continues below

Carrick's blushes were saved on Sunday when United score twice in stoppage time to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa. United had twice trailed by two goals before making comebacks, but the game continued to showcase their flaws defensively, which have plagued them throughout the campaign.

Sports.title: Man Utd and Ineos' five shocking decisions as constant failure set to cost Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Since Ineos came on board at Manchester United back in 2024 they have made bad call after bad call and, even if results have been poor, Michael Carrick is poised to pay the price for those continued failings.

A summit in Monaco involving all of the Red Devils' senior figures on Wednesday is likely to conclude with Carrick being relieved of his duties at Old Trafford.

The club sit in the bottom three having won just one of their 10 Premier League games with the club sinking to new lows. Carrick has been unable to find the winning formula but, as many continue to point out, he has not been set-up to succeed in Manchester.

A lot of the issues that are rearing their head long pre-date Carrick's arrival and, even if Ineos arrived with a glimmer of hopes following the longstanding Glazer issues, the direction of travel in Manchester has not changed.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe is now being viewed much the same as the club's majority owners over in America. His lieutenants are also hugely unpopular with their number of poor decisions stacking up and up.

We take a look at the calls made by Ratcliffe, Ineos and co that have ultimately done nothing to make United the force they hope they can be, instead landing them in a possible relegation battle.

‌



Backing - and then sacking - Ten Hag

This was the first sign of the United hierarchy not sticking to their guns. Before the FA Cup final of 2024 they were looking at their options with Erik ten Hag presiding over a poor domestic campaign. All the signs pointed to him getting the sack. Yet a shock win over Manchester City caused a u-turn.

View 4 Images Ten Hag was sacked by United in 2024 (Image: Justin Setterfield, Getty Images)

In reality that result at Wembley should not have caused such a shift and, after handing Ten Hag a new deal, he lasted just nine games of the following season before he was sacked. Ratcliffe and those alongside him should've had more conviction come the end of 2023/24.

The Amorim saga

I mean this felt doomed from the start and the fact it went on so long seems purely down to the fact Ineos didn't want to admit they got their first managerial appointment wrong. Ruben Amorim won just 24 of his 63 games in charge, all whilst playing a style that was never going to suit United.

‌



His tenure come with a series of entertaining soundbites, which included him calling his side the worst Manchester United team ever and telling the board they need to sack him if they want to see a different playing style. He would ultimately get his wish 14 months after being appointed.

View 4 Images Ruben Amorim presided over Man Utd's worst ever Premier League finish (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Poor PR moves

Ratcliffe previously claimed that United were in danger of going out of business before his cost cutting measures were undertaken, not sure anyone particularly agreed with him there. But he and Ineos have excelled in PR disasters, which has bought them no goodwill from supporters.

From the cutting of hundreds of jobs to the removal of concession ticket prices to threatening to remove season tickets from those they wrongly accused of reselling their tickets. If Ratcliffe and Ineos are unpopular, then it is largely a situation of their own making.

‌



Neglecting the defence

You can say United's results from the New Year onwards were impressive, and they were, but it is the club's job to take a closer look at things. Had they done that they would've seen that Carrick's United conceded more than a goal a game across his 17 outings.

That was with a defence that hadn't seen a major signing since Leny Yoro, and even then he is seen as a player for the future. Otherwise it is made up of signings from several years ago and the club opted to plough £155m into their midfield in the summer.

View 4 Images Man Utd's defence has not been bolstered for several years

So few can be surprised that United have now conceded more goals than any top flight team in a major European league this season with a backline that includes the likes of Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez, Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw - the latter being signed when Louis van Gaal was at the club.

‌



Ignoring Carrick's red flags

It was mentioned earlier about the club's bosses sticking to their guns - or not. Well ultimately hiring Carrick was never part of the plan, he was a makeshift solution until the end of a troubled season. But wins over Arsenal, Manchester City, Aston Villa and Liverpool made the man hard to ignore.

What wasn't hard to ignore was the fact United had no European football and no domestic competitions to worry about. That meant Carrick was working with a fresh squad and had ample time to prepare for games. That was ultimately unrealistic and not a fair reflection of what was to come.

If Carrick wasn't the man long-term in January, then a few statement wins shouldn't have changed that. But it did, and we find ourselves where we are today.

Sports.title: Damning total cost of Man Utd sacking Michael Carrick for Mauricio Pochettino
Sports.content:
Damning total cost of Man Utd sacking Michael Carrick for Mauricio Pochettino

Manchester United are seemingly on the verge of sacking Michael Carrick following a poor start to the season, with Mauricio Pochettino

View 2 Images (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United may have to shell out more than £10million to sack Michael Carrick and bring in Mauricio Pochettino. The Red Devils have endured a horrid start to the new season, languishing in 18th with just eight points to show from their opening 10 matches.

‌



‌



As a result, many fans expect United to part ways with the 45-year-old during the November international break, leaving them plenty of time to source an apt replacement ahead of their return to Premier League football. That comes on Sunday, November 22, with the Red Devils making the trip to Anfield to face a fierce Liverpool.

‌



While a number of names have been linked with taking up tenure at Old Trafford, from Eddie Howe to Julian Nagelsmann, it is Pochettino who is thought to be the frontrunner in the event that Carrick is handed his marching orders. That would, however, require United to splash the cash on hiring and firing once more - in an era that Sir Jim Ratcliffe has made the club's dedication to cutting costs and making savings clear.

‌



Ineos make Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sack decisions ahead of crunch Man Utd talks READ MORE :

Carrick is currently contracted by the club until 2028, having signed a permanent deal this summer. As a result, United would have to pay the Englishman severance in the event that they choose to terminate that contract prematurely.

As per GiveMeSport, while Carrick has a one-year break clause embedded in his contract, United would still have to cough up the remainder of the year's salary to part ways with him. Thought to be commanding around £5m annually, that is thought to equate to around £3m considering Carrick is months into his contract.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Elsewhere, United would also have to pay compensation to Pochettino's current employers in the United States national team - to whom, the Argentine is under contract with until at least 2030. Reports suggest that Pochettino has a $10m (£7.4m) release clause in that deal.

Add that figure to the £3m that would be due to go Carrick's way, and United may have to shell out more than £10m to swap out Carrick for Pochettino this month - and that could rise higher with support staff. No strangers to sacking underperforming managers, the Red Devils have spent a fortune in hiring and firing head coaches over the past decade while trying to find the next Alex Ferguson.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

David Moyes is thought to have received around £5.2m when he was let go just one year into his deal at Old Trafford in 2014, while Lous van Gaal is said to have been paid out £8.4m for his exit in 2016.

‌



Jose Mourinho lived up to his 'Special One' moniker by taking home a £19.6m payday for his sacking in 2018, with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer receiving severance to the tune of a cool £10m three years later.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is feeling the heat (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Ralf Rangnick was afforded around £15m for his leave, Erik ten Hag saw £10.4m as per reports and the club are thought to have spent £8.2m to send Ruben Amorim packing in January. It comes as Sky Sports claim that club officials fear a change of face in the dugout may not be enough to reverse fortunes at Old Trafford.

Supporters and pundits have shown discontent with the club hierarchy, with bosses seemingly agreeing that problems within the club run deeper than within the dressing room. Whether the club will afford Carrick more time and address said problems as a result remains to be seen, although it appears as though the head coach has finite time within his current post.

Sports.title: Huntingdon race stopped to avert accident after jockey rides horse ‘the wrong way back’
Sports.content:
Huntingdon race stopped to avert accident after jockey rides horse ‘the wrong way back’

The flags were waved to bring the field for the final handicap hurdle due to the course taken by Tom Bellamy on the withdrawn Blues Singer

View 2 Images The flag was waved to stop the race at Huntingdon (Image: RACING TV)

The final race at Huntingdon on Tuesday was declared void for safety reasons after a jockey rode a withdrawn horse the wrong way down the track.

‌



‌



The Alan King-trained Blues Singer, having his first start of the season, was making his handicap debut at the track where he had captured a maiden hurdle in March.

‌



But when the eight runners were called forward by the starter, Blues Singer hung out the back, refusing to move forward for jockey Tom Bellamy. In the end the starter let the rest of the field go with the uncooperative King runner withdrawn at the start.

‌



Godolphin star Ombudsman to have career swansong in Japan Cup READ MORE :

The race then proceeded as normal, with no indication of what was to come, when the track’s flag men were suddenly deployed to stop the race. The jockeys eventually brought their mounts to a stop amid utter confusion as to why the race had been halted.

Racing TV subsequently showed footage of Blues Singer heading back to the stables travelling the opposite way to the runners in the race, following the chase course.

“It has to be something to do with Blues Singer, that’s the only thing we can assume,” said RacingTV reporter Chris Dixon.

‌



Back in the studio, host Richard Hoiles said: “I’m not 100 percent sure Tom Bellamy knew what he was doing going that way to be honest because he must have realised he’d meet the field coming the other way. Surely he would just follow behind.

View 2 Images Jockey Tom Bellamy (Image: PA)

‌



“It’s a void race so everyone is going to have their stakes refunded. Rather an awkward end to the Huntingdon card.”

The stewards’ report said: “An enquiry was held to consider the circumstances surrounding the deployment of the ‘stop race’ flag as the withdrawn horse Blues Singer appeared to head the wrong way down the track into oncoming runners via the bypass lane.

‌



“The clerk of the course, general manager, head groundsman, the starters, and all the riders involved in the race were interviewed. After hearing the evidence, a report was forwarded to the Head Office of the British Horseracing Authority for further consideration.”

Chief steward Tony McGlone told RacingTV: “At the start the number 3 horse, Tom Bellamy’s, was withdrawn because it was unruly and refused to line up.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

“So the race was then started and as the runners were coming round Tom, because he couldn’t get his horse to go right-handed, then decided to take his horse left-handed and go back towards the runners coming round.

Article continues below

“I was upstairs inside our box and we could see the horse galloping quite quickly against the flow of the runners, so the clerk of the course decided this could be a danger because there might be an accident. She called for the race to be stopped."

He continued: “He was going pretty quick and at that stage we had no reason to say he was in control of his horse. As he was going at speed towards the runners, the clerk of the course decided that the safest thing for horses and riders was to stop the race.”

Sports.title: Ineos make Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sack decisions ahead of crunch Man Utd talks
Sports.content:
Ineos make Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sack decisions ahead of crunch Man Utd talks

Manchester United's poor season could cost Michael Carrick his job but Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have come in for particular criticism as fans and pundits take aim at the duo

View 2 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe is ready to stick by two of his most senior figures - Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox (Image: Jacob King/Press Association)

Manchester United chiefs Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada retain the backing of Sir Jim Ratcliffe despite their competency coming under severe scrutiny.

‌



‌



The club go into the international break in the relegation zone and reports claim Michael Carrick will be axed this week, with both of the senior figures approving of his exit.

‌



However Carrick and the team's struggles have shone a light on the issues that run far deeper at the club. Among those is whether Berrada and Wilcox are fit for purpose given their previous experience and subsequent decision making on the red side of Manchester.

‌



They will have played their part in United potentially having a third different manager in the dugout inside a calendar year if Carrick is sacked. But despite their decision making clearly setting the club back, the Telegraph reports that Ratcliffe has no plans to remove them from their roles.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Wilcox and Berrada are expected to meet Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday as part of a summit for Ineos’s senior staff. It had long been pencilled in the diary but the situation at Old Trafford means Carrick's future will be front and centre.

The United hierarchy, namely Wilcox and Berrada, have been increasingly singled out by fans and pundits as a result of United's dire season - which has seen them win just one of their 10 Premier League games. Even Lisandro Martinez went as far as to call out Wilcox in the aftermath of their loss to Atletico Madrid, accusing him of not equipping the squad well enough.

‌



Wilcox in his role as the director of football has been hammered for the club's poor recruitment with chief executive Berrada ultimately overseeing the day-to-day football operations at the club.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's time as Man United boss may well come to an end this week (Image: Michael Regan, Getty Images)

‌



Ratcliffe appointed Berrada and Wilcox after taking control of the football department when he bought an influential minority stake from the Glazers in 2024.

Berrada was hired off the back of his work at Manchester City, where he had seen his reputation rise. It was at City that Berrada became aware of Wilcox, who was the club’s academy director before leaving to become director of football at Southampton. He was there 14 months before joining United, initially as technical director.

Article continues below

Among the poor decisions that have seen the pair criticised is the backing, and then the sacking, of Erik ten Hag. They hired Ruben Amorim despite his philosophy not being a fit for the club and opted to hand Carrick the job full-time despite obvious concerns over his prior experience and the wider circumstances that contributed to his interim success.

Sports.title: Godolphin star Ombudsman to have career swansong in Japan Cup
Sports.content:
Godolphin star Ombudsman to have career swansong in Japan Cup

Ombudsman will attempt to become the first British-trained winner of the Japan Cup since Alkaased in 2005 when he lines up in Tokyo on 29 November, with a $5million bonus also on the line before he retires to stud in 2027.

View 3 Images Ombudsman: Japan Cup will be final start (Image: Getty Images)

Godolphin star legend Ombudsman will have the opportunity to bow out on the world stage when he lines up for the Japan Cup later this month.

‌



‌



Joint-trainers John and Thady Gosden opted to sidestep a Breeders' Cup tilt for the Night Of Thunder colt following his triumph in the Champion Stakes. Instead, he will tackle a mile and a half for the first time in Tokyo on November 29, before heading off to stud duties at Darley's Kildangan Stud in Ireland in 2027.

‌



Regardless of the outcome in the Far East, Godolphin's managing director Hugh Anderson is convinced his place in racing history is already assured, describing him as "one of the best" horses ever to carry Sheikh Mohammed's famous colours.

‌



Anderson said: "John is a master trainer and has obviously got his eye very firmly on this prize. It's very exciting.

"Ombudsman's career has been a model of his kind and he has been beautifully trained. John really took his time with him both as a two-year-old and a three-year-old and what rewards we reaped as a result.

"There have been a lot of great racehorses in Godolphin's history but Ombudsman is one of the best because of the quality of the Group Ones he has won.

‌



"There is a pecking order in this sport and there are not many higher ranking than two Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot, the Juddmonte International Stakes and a Champion Stakes, he's right up there."

View 3 Images William Buick riding Ombudsman (all blue) to win the Qatar Racing Champion Stakes (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Ombudsman is set to renew his rivalry with reigning champion Calandagan in Japan, as the five-time Group One victor bids to become the first British-trained horse to triumph since Alkaased 21 years ago, while also pursuing a $5million bonus following his recent Ascot success where he defeated Francis-Henri Graffard's globe-trotting contender on Champions Day.

While Sheikh Mohammed's Singspiel captured Japan Cup honours in 1996, Ombudsman would make history as the first horse to claim the Group One prize wearing the Godolphin colours if successful in Asia.

‌



Such a victory would crown what has evolved into an excellent year for the global racing powerhouse, who recently witnessed Sovereignty deliver their maiden Breeders' Cup Classic triumph at Keeneland, following a robust conclusion to the European season that offers considerable promise for 2027.

View 3 Images Sovereignty (nearest): won the Breeders' Cup Classic (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"The Breeders' Cup Classic really was something and like Ombudsman, Sovereignty is out there in a class of his own," Anderson continued.

"He has won two of the massive international races that had never been previously won by Godolphin or His Highness – the Kentucky Derby and the Breeders' Cup Classic. For one horse to do both is seriously impressive and he will be a fabulous stallion."

Article continues below

He added: "The year is ending strongly and I have been on record saying it was a little bit flat earlier in the year – and it was always going to be difficult to match the quality of last year, but we have finished well.

"The two-year-olds have been very good this year and I think Charlie Appleby has shown how good a trainer he is to bring along the likes of Talk Of New York to win a Queen Elizabeth II Stakes at the end of the season."

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua has already decided next opponent after Tyson Fury
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua has already decided next opponent after Tyson Fury

Anthony Joshua will take on Tyson Fury next month but has already set his sights on avenging one of this previous defeats

View Image Eddie Hearn and Anthony Joshua (Image: Richard Pelham, Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua wants to avenge his defeat by Daniel Dubois following his showdown with Tyson Fury next month.

‌



‌



Joshua and Fury will clash in Cardiff on December 11 to settle their long-running rivalry. Fury is the favourite to have his hand raised at the Principality Stadium but Joshua has big plans beyond what promises to be the biggest fight of his career. Joshua was knocked out by Dubois at Wembley two years ago as his British rival defended his heavyweight world title.

‌



Dubois went on to lose his belt to Oleksandr Usyk but is enjoying his second reign as world champion having stopped Fabio Wardley in their two fights this year. And Joshua wants to beat Fury and then earn his revenge against Dubois, according to his promoter Eddie Hearn.

‌

Sports.title: Nine Man Utd players set to follow Michael Carrick out the door in mass exodus if boss is sacked
Sports.content:
Nine Man Utd players set to follow Michael Carrick out the door in mass exodus if boss is sacked

With Manchester United expected to part ways with Michael Carrick imminently, we're looking at the players who may follow him out the door

View 5 Images Michael Carrick is reportedly close to being sacked by Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Change appears to be afoot at Manchester United, with manager Michael Carrick reportedly on the verge of being sacked. Adjustments, however, may not be limited to the dugout, with several first team stars poised to follow Carrick out the door if and when the axe falls.

‌



‌



United have made a disastrous start to the season and head into the international break languishing 18th in the table after winning just one of their opening 10 Premier League matches. Defensive frailties have been a particular concern, with the Red Devils shipping 15 goals in their last five games in all competitions.

‌



Sunday's chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, despite a late fightback, looks to have been the final straw for Carrick, with the club now seemingly preparing for life without him. But while United begin drawing up a shortlist of potential managerial replacements, they may also need to consider which players might follow him out of the exit door.

‌



As many as nine senior squad members could find themselves either on the chopping block, or eyeing up a hasty getaway in the aftermath of Carrick's expected departure. Here, Mirror Football takes a closer look at all nine players.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Harry Maguire

Harry Maguire's rollercoaster Manchester United tenure appears to be reaching its natural conclusion as he enters the final few months of his contract. While the club hold the option to trigger a one-year extension, exercising it makes little footballing sense given that his form has been questionable for some time.

‌



The former club captain turns 34 in March and has been guilty of several costly lapses during United's latest defensive collapse. A fresh managerial appointment should signal the definitive end of an era, allowing both parties to part ways cleanly in the summer.

Lisandro Martinez

Once revered as United's defensive bedrock, Lisandro Martinez has endured an alarming fall from grace over the past 18 months. Persistent fitness struggles have severely hampered the Argentine's reliability, leaving United's backline constantly reshuffled and chronically exposed.

‌



Martinez is contracted until 2027, and though Old Trafford chiefs retain a one-year extension option, there is no pressing need to trigger it given the defensive cover already on the books. A new manager may well decide that the combative defender's physical peak has passed and look to rebuild the defence elsewhere.

View 5 Images Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire could leave Man Utd in 2027 (Image: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

‌



Mason Mount

Mason Mount's Manchester United move hasn't really worked. Plagued by persistent injury setbacks and underwhelming form, the former Chelsea midfielder now finds himself languishing down the pecking order behind Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo.

With his contract running until 2028, the two upcoming windows represent United's final realistic opportunity to recoup a respectable portion of their initial £55million investment. A clean break would suit all parties, handing Mount the fresh start he desperately needs to revive his stalling career.

‌



Bruno Fernandes

View 5 Images Bruno Fernandes has been linked with an Old Trafford exit for years (Image: Harry Cornish/PPAUK/Shutterstock)

Bruno Fernandes has long been linked with an Old Trafford exit and the club's current nosedive could finally push him toward the departure lounge. His public friction with Michael Carrick has noticeably strained relations with both the hierarchy and sections of the fanbase in recent weeks.

‌



While Carrick's sacking might seem to offer a reprieve, it could instead serve as the ideal cut-off point for a talisman whose on-pitch petulance can cause as many headaches as his goal contributions solve. Contracted until 2027 with a one-year option, United face a major decision over whether to prolong his stay or sanction a lucrative parting of ways.

Marcus Rashford

Marcus Rashford looked destined to leave Manchester during the summer, only remaining at the club after a prospective move to Barcelona collapsed. Bridges were effectively burned when he handed in a transfer request in December 2024 and his underwhelming displays since returning to United done nothing to repair that fractured bond.

‌



The forward's deal expires in 2028, making 2027 the critical juncture for United to command any meaningful transfer fee for their academy graduate. A separation now feels somewhat inevitable, offering Rashford the chance to rebuild his reputation - and his club career - away from the unrelenting Old Trafford spotlight.

View 5 Images Marcus Rashford's Man Utd return hasn't gone to plan (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Joshua Zirkzee

Brought in during the final months of Erik ten Hag's reign, Joshua Zirkzee has continually struggled to convince subsequent managers that he possesses the pedigree to lead United's frontline. The Dutch forward has spent the vast majority of his Old Trafford career confined to the bench, unable to make a lasting impression when handed rare opportunities, with Carrick even using the likes of Cunha and Mbeumo as makeshift No. 9s over Zirkzee.

The 25-year-old cannot afford another campaign playing second - or, in some cases, third - fiddle in a misfiring side when he should be commanding a starting berth. With United in dire need of a ruthless, reliable goalscorer, sanctioning a permanent move away would allow him to kickstart his career elsewhere.

‌



Kobbie Mainoo

Carrick's arrival earlier this year revitalised Kobbie Mainoo's Manchester United career after the young midfielder was frozen out under Ruben Amorim. However, any incoming manager could just as easily decide against building around the academy graduate, placing his rapid development in serious jeopardy once again.

Mainoo cannot risk another prolonged spell on the periphery, especially with several elite European clubs monitoring his situation closely. United chiefs showed an openness to entertaining offers for the England star last year, and they may be tempted to cash in if the next manager prefers a different midfield profile.

‌



View 5 Images Kobbie Mainoo may suffer if Michael Carrick is sacked (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Luke Shaw

Luke Shaw's 12-year stint at Old Trafford is drawing to a close as he approaches the final months of his current contract. Relentless injury setbacks have taken a heavy toll on the England international, leaving him a shadow of the dynamic left back who once dominated the flank.

‌



United desperately need energetic, durable full backs capable of withstanding the physical demands of modern top-flight football week in, week out. Allowing Shaw to leave on a free transfer next summer would clear substantial room on the wage bill and pave the way for a much-needed new addition, such as Newcastle's Lewis Hall.

Tom Heaton

Tom Heaton has been an exemplary squad player and dependable cover over the past six seasons, but his playing days are rapidly winding down. The veteran goalkeeper's contract expires at the end of the season, with no extension option in place to prolong his second stint at the club.

Article continues below

Having turned 40, the former England international is widely expected to call time on his playing career or transition into a full-time coaching capacity. A new managerial regime will inevitably look to modernise the goalkeeping department from top to bottom, making Heaton's exit a straightforward decision.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.
