In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: What REALLY triggered HSTikkyTokky's boxing night riot between Tommy Robinson and Mo Deen, as Muslim influencer breaks cover to claim 'set up'
Sports.content:
What REALLY triggered HSTikkyTokky's boxing night riot between Tommy Robinson and Mo Deen, as Muslim influencer breaks cover to claim 'set up'

The Muslim influencer at the heart of HSTikkyTokky's shut-down influencer boxing night claims he was 'told to' attack Tommy Robinson in a 'scripted' moment that sparked a riot which saw a man stabbed and two arrests made.

The 'Unhinged' event, held in Kilkenny, Ireland, and streamed to millions online was held 'without any authorisation from anybody', sources say, and promised to be a 'proper scrap between the most chaotic names in the internet scene' – with Muslim influencer Mo Deen and a rival calling himself MrTikTokUK on the undercard.

But the night, with a capacity of up to 2,000 young fans, had to be cancelled three fights before its conclusion when venue owners refused to let it continue.

HSTikkyTokky, the controversial British 'manosphere' influencer whose real name is Harrison Sullivan, is behind the Unhinged event company. He now claims it has been banned 'worldwide' in the wake of the carnage, while simultaneously talking up a fight card for next month – with hopes that far-Right activist Robinson will fight on it.

At the point of cancellation, Mo Deen had jumped from the ring to attack Robinson, metal chairs were being hurled across the crowd by fighting fans, Sullivan had been hit in the head by a glass bottle and racist and sexist comments were being broadcast on commentary online. Later, one man was stabbed and two people were arrested. One teenager has been charged.

Sullivan suggested the event had run 'absolutely brilliantly' because it was trending online. His claims of his company being cancelled appear to have little substance, sources close to boxing authorities say.

Mo Deen now says he has received death threats from Robinson's supporters and, in one video, suggested he feared a 'hit' would be put out on him.

For all those people who claim Tommy Robinson was simply the victim in what became a mini-riot in Dublin, watch this video.



TR might have well been kicked by MoDeen earlier )or attempted flying kick but debatable if there was actual contact), but it was after that incident had… — Nick Lowles (@lowles_nick) November 8, 2026

A mass brawl erupts at HSTikkyTokky's Unhinged 003 boxing event in Kilkenny on Saturday

Far-right activist Tommy Robinson sparked the violent riot with an altercation inside the ring

Muslim influencer Mo Deen has claimed he was 'told to' attack Robinson in a 'scripted' moment

At the Hub in Kilkenny, a 1,900-capacity community venue which hosted The Boomtown Rats at the start of the year and is welcoming Irish singer Gavin James next month, an already violent event broke out into a brawl after an altercation between Robinson and Deen – whose real name is Mohammad Kubba.

Robinson, currently on bail after being found guilty in October of harassing two Daily Mail journalists in a campaign that caused them to fear for their safety, arrived in Kilkenny as a ringside guest, accompanied by a large contingent of his supporters. He is due back in court on December 16 for sentencing, with the hearing potentially to result in a custodial sentence.

The chaotic scenes in Kilkenny were preceded by an equally unruly press conference on Friday evening, where multiple fighters launched themselves at one another in a series of violent clashes involving streamers, rappers, OnlyFans models and convicted sex offender-turned-YouTuber Paul Flaherty.

Flaherty, who was jailed for five years in 2018 after being convicted of sexually assaulting a woman he met on Tinder, had already been embroiled in a chaotic brawl at a Unhinged promotional event in September, with footage of the confrontation quickly going viral online.

Tensions rose on Saturday night when Sullivan and his influencer friend Ed Matthews, who starred alongside HSTikkyTokky in Louis Theroux's documentary Inside The Manosphere, invited Robinson to join them at the commentators' desk before Deen's fight.

Holding a copy of his book, The Grooming Gang Cover-Up, the 43-year-old activist made a series of inflammatory remarks about Islam, claiming that 'Muslims have been raping our country for 100 years' and citing false statistics about Muslim men and sexual offences.

After defeating MrTikTokUK, Deen – whose real name is Mohammad Kubba – climbed out of the ring and launched himself at Robinson with a flying kick, in a moment he has since claimed was staged and designed to raise tensions ahead of a potential future bout between the two.

Deen took to social media to claim his attack was staged as he sought refuge in a utility room

The initial brawl spilled into the crowd but was largely contained by security, who managed to defuse the situation. Deen, 41, subsequently left the venue as the remaining bouts got underway, only to be escorted back inside by event security after it was claimed Sullivan called for him to return and face Robinson in the ring.

Sullivan has denied the claim as well as the claim by Deen that he was following a script.

With tensions through the roof, and many racially diverse spectators left furious at Robinson's previous remarks, the far-Right activist launched his book towards Deen, sparking a physical brawl that violently went out of control.

Robinson was grabbed as punches were thrown, while people from both entourages were caught up in the melee.

Violence quickly spread through the crowd, with chairs and metal barriers hurled across the venue, spectators exchanging blows and others scrambling to escape the commotion as security desperately attempted to intervene.

A string of videos showing people screaming, pushing and throwing punches were published to social media in real time as the chaos continued for approximately 20 minutes. Shouts of 'Oh Tommy Robinson' bellowed out from the riot before the livestream, which was broadcast on platform Kick to approximately 1.8million viewers, eventually cut to black.

Police, who had been alerted to disturbances at the venue before the mass brawl broke out, arrested and detained a man in his 20s after another man was stabbed and rushed to hospital earlier in the evening.

A teenager was also arrested by the Gardai and charged with violent disorder.

‘Gardai attended the scene of a number of incidents on the night of Saturday 7th November, 2026 at approximately 9pm at a premises on the Dublin Road, Kilkenny,’ a police statement read.

’One male, aged in his 30s was assaulted and removed from the scene to St. Luke’s Hospital. A man, aged in his 20s was arrested and is currently detained under Section 4 at a Garda station in the South East.

‘A second male was arrested, an adult in his teens, for violent disorder and has since been charged. He is due to appear in court later today, no court sitting has been set at this time. Investigations ongoing.’

Despite the arrests and widespread violence, Sullivan attempted to restart the remaining bouts without spectators, solely for the event's livestream, before a visibly upset venue representative intervened to stop him.

Robinson brawled with Deen and his entourage after being invited into the ring by Sullivan

Robinson greets the event's organiser HSTikkyTokky, whose real name is Harrison Sullivan

HSTikkyTokky CRASHED OUT after someone in the crowd THREW a GLASS BOTTLE at him while he was interviewing a fighter 😳 pic.twitter.com/Uq8uSghkXC — clipmate (@clipmxte) November 7, 2026

A spokesman for the Hub has since said in a statement to Kilkenny Live: 'Following an incident the decision was made by the management of the venue to step in and stop the promotions company from continuing with their event.

'The Hub has a zero-tolerance policy towards violence, aggression or disorderly behaviour.'

As the violence unfolded, Deen took to social media claiming his initial confrontation with Robinson had been staged for entertainment but spiralled out of control.

As he and his entourage sought refuge in a small utility room, Deen urged that his post-fight fly kick was scripted as he hurriedly told his crew to 'lock the doors'.

'The whole place is surrounded,' a concerned Deen said as wild shouting could be heard in the background.

'There's fights everywhere, we're locked in a room right now. Listen I'll make this clear to every single person in the UK. I'm not trying to cause problems. This is like WWE, they said this is what the situation is. I followed the script.

'I'm getting death threats, people trying to kill me. I don't know about this, I just know this is what we had to do. Why is everyone trying to kill me right now?

'This is a message to all supporters of Tommy, supporters, gangs, whatever you are. I just followed the script they told me to agree with. Tommy's agreed to it, they've agreed to it, I followed it.'

'Look at my hands bro,' he added looking visibly shaken. 'My guys are getting rushed, look at my friend's face bro. This whole thing is crazy.'

Deen went on to plead with Elon Musk, whom he described as one of Robinson's 'friends', and the activist's wider network of supporters not to 'put a hit out' on him.

'A fight is a fight, hopefully anyone who is with Tommy and is friends and that, Elon Musk or whatever, don't put hits out on me,' he added, holding his hand to his heart.

Sullivan, who initially stated that the event went 'absolutely brilliantly' because it was trending globally, has refuted Deen's claims that the fight and aftermath was staged.

In a video on his YouTube channel, Sullivan said: 'I was sat next to Tommy. Do you think that I wanted to get f***ing fly-kicked and f***ing some fat belly over me? My watch nearly got popped off. Do you think that that was a plan? No. The plan was for them to face off in the ring.'

The 25-year-old manosphere influencer also dismissed claims that he intentionally attempted to stage an impromptu bare-knuckle fight between Robinson and Deen when the Muslim fighter was escorted back into the venue.

According to The Guardian, Sullivan repeatedly shouted 'let Tommy fight him' while Robinson's entourage – referred to by the YouTuber as 'Tommy's boys' – were permitted to enter the ring to face off with Deen and Co.

He added: 'What is that nonsense? You think I would want them to have a bare-knuckle fight for free, not to just face off and hype up the next event?'

🚨MUST SEE: Hstikkytokky has OFFICIALLY SOLD AWAY his UNHINGED PROMOTIONS COMPANY…



He goes on to apologise to all fans and every supporter 😳



HS: “I’ve had message from police and the boxing commission, I am no longer able to host @UnhingedEvents pic.twitter.com/6EopqIhyMr — KickClipz (@Kickclipzfeed) November 8, 2026

Chairs were hurled and punches were thrown as the event descended into absolute chaos

HSTikkyTokky appeared on Louis Theroux's Inside the Manosphere documentary this year

Sources have told Daily Mail Sport influencer events such as Saturday's Unhinged 003 tend to take place without authorisation from any official boxing body.

HSTikkyTokky had promoted the event as a 'proper scrap between two of the most chaotic names in the internet scene', with British rappers Russ Millions and Kirky set to headline a card that was ultimately abandoned before their bout could take place.

After initially hinting that a potential bout between Robinson and Deen had been in the works for next month, Sullivan appeared crestfallen on a later video as he called an end to Unhinged Promotions, claiming they had been shut down from operating 'worldwide'.

'I've had a lot of messages from police around the world, message from the boxing commission... I am not allowed to put an Unhinged event on anymore after Tommy Robinson riots at Kilkenny last night,' he said on his channel.

'Obviously it's massively disappointing, I wanted to grow the company Unhinged Promotions, I wanted to make it massive and huge and take over the world but the risks that have come in play from the decisions some of my staff have made has now led to us having to cancel any future event. We won't be back, but I will sure be supporting some of the other promotions around the world.

'I just want to apologise to the internet. I didn't want to ever have to put on events that risked the safety of people that came to support. I'm super sorry and I won't be doing an event again. I wish I could, but I'm not allowed to now.'

In case the message wasn't already clear, he stated again: 'There is no venue around the world that will take me, there is literally nothing I can do. I feel cornered, I feel lost, I feel gutted. I feel jobless, this was my passion, my desire, my life.

'Now it's been taken away from me over something that was meant to be a light-hearted promotion for the next event. I'm gutted and I want to say again, sorry to everyone.'

Sullivan's self-pitying demeanour offered a stark contrast to the buoyant figure he immediately cut after the chaotic event, which he claimed went 'absolutely brilliantly'. Footage from earlier in the night had shown him being hit by a glass bottle thrown from the crowd while he stood in the ring.

Thrilled that Unhinged's third event had trended globally on social media platforms as a result of the riots, he said: 'I think it went absolutely brilliantly. Listen it was controversial as f*** but please tell me other promotion on their third event is trending globally on Twitter like this, has generated over 200 million views across TikTok, Twitter and Instagram.

'So everyone who's hating, you're clearly still watching. The fights were absolutely brilliant up until the venue got closed down.

'I'm gutted that we didn't get to see the final three fights but s*** happens. I totally hold accountability for misjudging the amount of security that was needed and the types of people that were coming. I misjudged that.

'But what I won't listen to is that wasn't a f***ing great night of entertainment. It was huge. Every single person is watching what I do. Every single person likes to talk about what I do because I'm the number one at what I do.'

Robinson was holding a copy of his book, The Grooming Gang Cover-Up, as he entered the ring

Robinson, who is on bail before his sentencing in December, said 'Muslims have been raping our country for 100 years' as he riled up the crowd with inflammatory remarks about Islam

Irish mobster Paul Flaherty just KNOCKED OUT a boxer at HSTikkyTokky’s Unhinged boxing press conference 😳 pic.twitter.com/NHVJFG10Ij — vxdeo (@vxdeo) September 17, 2026

Sullivan has seen other boxing events shut down in the past. In January, he complained that 'hundreds' of complainants had called the local council and police to cancel a show in Basildon, saying that one of his fighters was a 'convicted child predator'.

The mayor of Kilkenny called the scenes this weekend 'absolutely disgraceful'. Andrew McGuinness said on local radio station KCLR: 'I am absolutely disgusted Kilkenny was used as a backdrop for such a horrendously managed event.

'They are grooming young people to behave in a way that's absolutely disgraceful. They have no respect for themselves, no respect for other people and particularly no respect for women.

'They groom thousands of people into going to these events. The fact there were minors and teenagers at the event is just absolutely appalling.'

Sports.title: Troubled ex-boxing world champion Adrien Broner wheeled out of concert and slumps over couch after falling unresponsive
Sports.content:
Troubled former boxer Adrien Broner has sparked major concern after viral footage showed him falling unresponsive at a concert on Saturday night.

Former four division boxing champion Broner, 37, was seen in the worrying state during a livestream while attending a 'Skilla Baby' concert in downtown Los Angeles.

In the viral footage, Broner could be seen looking dazed before slumping over on a couch. An EMS worker attended to him and helped carry him to a flight of stairs.

While taking Broner down the stairs, the ex-boxer appeared to fall in and out of consciousness before eventually regaining enough composure to walk down.

In the end, Broner was loaded into a wheelchair by friends and the EMS worker before being taken backstage and into a car outside the music venue.

It marks the latest concerning incident involving Broner, who recently had a run-in with police in Beverly Hills.

Troubled former boxer Adrien Broner has sparked major concern after viral footage showed him falling unresponsive at a concert

Broner had to be helped down a flight of stairs by an EMS worker while at the concert

At the end of October, Broner was among a group of men recording content on the streets of Beverly Hills for the social media platform, Kick, when local police arrived.

Viral footage from the incident shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner and his fellow content creator, Deen The Great.

A separate clip showed Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs.

Broner was seen trying to poke fun at the situation by doing a funny walk for the officers' benefit, but they did not seem amused.

'Broner was detained during a traffic stop as part of an investigation into a large street gathering in a residential area,' Beverly Hills police told TMZ in a statement. 'He was released from the scene and a citation was not issued.'

Broner is also currently among several defendants being sued in Los Angeles County over allegations of sexual battery, battery and assault.

'Plaintiff alleges that Broner repeatedly pressured Plaintiff for sexual activity after repeated refusals, attempted to isolate Plaintiff, repeatedly pressured Plaintiff while intoxicated, attempted unwanted physical contact, publicly humiliated Plaintiff, and made false sexual statements about Plaintiff to a livestream audience,' read the complaint, obtained by The Daily Mail.

Broner has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

Previously, in September of 2025, Broner was kicked off rapper Cam'ron's popular podcast after ignoring the host's warnings to stop flirting with his on-air co-host.

Sports.title: Scottish boxer Willy Hutchinson fulfils boyhood pledge by becoming world champion after famous victory
Sports.content:
Scottish boxer Willy Hutchinson fulfils boyhood pledge by becoming world champion after famous victory

Scotland is celebrating a new boxing world champion after Willy Hutchinson produced the performance of his life to beat Joshua Buatsi in Manchester and claim the vacant World Boxing Council (WBC) light-heavyweight belt.

The 28-year-old from Carstairs was superior in every department and toyed with his London-based rival while avenging the 2024 defeat he endured at the hands of Buatsi.

Hutchinson had insisted in the build-up he had matured since that setback and was a more complete fighter, and he went about proving it in devastating style by showing off expert footwork, evasive movement and sharp counterpunching to flummox Buatsi.

The judges scored the fight 117-112, 115-113 and 115-113, all in Hutchinson’s favour, and the majority of the crowd in the AO Arena went wild to acclaim the new champion.

The contest was initially for the interim title but was upgraded when American David Benavidez gave up the WBC gold to move up to cruiserweight. And it proved a dream come true for Scotland’s Hutchinson, who had told before the fight about how he’d targeted becoming a WBC champion at the age of 13.

As he celebrated a famous victory in the ring, an emotional Hutchinson said: ‘I want to tell the story one more time. I was 13 years old. My dad was working in Sweden. I signed it in a book, I said I will become a world champion. Let’s go!

Scotland's Willy Hutchinson lands a punch on Joshua Buatsi at the AO Arena in Manchester

Hutchinson proudly holds the WBC light-heavyweight title belt after outclassing his opponent

‘Can I say thank you to my coach because I’ll tell you one thing, without him I don’t think I’d be here today, let alone boxing. This man dug me out of a hole that I never thought that I would get out of, so this is all a bonus, baby.’

Hutchinson immediately set his sights on an all-British showdown against three-time former world title challenger Anthony Yarde, who was ringside in Manchester.

Eyeing up the Londoner, Hutchinson said: ‘Anthony Yarde, do you want some of this?

‘He’s no walkover but let’s go. Him next.’

Yarde, 35, responded: ‘It’s 100 per cent a fight I’d love to take.’

Another option could be the winner of next month’s mouth-watering tussle between Dmitry Bivol and Callum Smith in Yekaterinburg, Russia, where the other three light-heavyweight titles are on the line.

Beat the winner of that one and Hutchinson – who now boasts a record of 21 victories with two defeats – could find himself the undisputed light-heavyweight champion of the world in 2027.

Suddenly, things just got a whole lot brighter for Scottish boxing.

Sports.title: Boxing world stunned by 'worst injury ever seen' as British fighter, 29, is left with gruesome swelling after nasty head collision - as fans question why bout wasn't stopped earlier
Sports.content:
Boxing world stunned by 'worst injury ever seen' as British fighter, 29, is left with gruesome swelling after nasty head collision - as fans question why bout wasn't stopped earlier

Boxing fans were left stunned as Zak Miller's title fight was called off with the Englishman suffering horrific facial swellings.

The 29-year-old from Manchester was fighting in his home city against Gully Powar, on the undercard of Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson.

The featherweight bout was ended after 10 rounds following an accidental clash of heads in the seventh that left Miller with gruesome injuries.

With huge swellings on his face and cuts around his eyes, a doctor examined him in round nine before allowing the fight to continue.

Then referee Mark Lyson intervened shortly afterwards, waving off the bout as Miller was left disfigured with a huge lump above his left eye, one on his forehead and another below his right eye.

The injuries appeared to be a hematoma, severe swellings caused by damage where blood pools under the skin.

The fight went straight to the scorecards, with 24-year-old Powar taking the judges' verdict 96-95, 97-94 and 96-94 to land the vacant British featherweight title.

The fight has been STOPPED due to severe swelling on Zak Miller’s face! 😬#BuatsiHutchinson2 | Live NOW on DAZN ▪️ pic.twitter.com/ePPcK5SiPA — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) November 7, 2026

Zak Miller was left with horrendous facial swellings after a head collision

Miller and Gully Powar fought on but the swellings got worse

Miller's face was disfigured as a result of the cuts and swellings

Referee Mark Lyson intervened at the end of the 10th round, with judges awarding the win to Powar

Former world champion Carl Frampton, presenting on DAZN, described the swelling as 'the worst I've ever seen'.

And fans struggled to believe the fight had been allowed to continue, with one posting on X: 'Zak Miller needs to change his corner, the fact that the ref stopped it, as opposed to his corner doing so is ridiculous. I reckon they waiting on his cheeks and chin to be ballooned shaped before pulling him out. Shocking work.'

Another said: 'Was a nasty look for Zak miller! Hope his corner's decision to not throw towel in doesn’t come back to haunt them! Speedy recovery Zak.'

A third said: 'An absolutely disgusting amount of swelling on the head of Zak Miller tonight. I hope he's all okay.'

Sports.title: Olympics gender row boxer Imane Khelif to make professional debut: Algerian announces fight with 21-year-old in December... two-and-a-half years after controversial gold in Paris
Sports.content:
Olympics gender row boxer Imane Khelif will debut as a professional boxer in December – with the goal of winning a world title.

The Algerian fighter will take on women's boxer Clarida Sarabia, 21, in Paris – more than two years after being dragged into a controversy at the Olympics there.

Khelif has a naturally high level of testosterone – though takes medication to reduce it – and was engulfed in a gender row at the 2024 Games after failing a gender eligibility test with the International Boxing Association in 2023.

'It’s been over two years since I last boxed, and I've really missed being in the ring,' said Khelif.

'The last couple of years have been quite difficult. The time has come to turn professional, and I’m going to give it my all.'

The 27-year-old also said: 'Days became weeks, weeks became months. I waited, doubted. But deep inside, the fire never died. Behind closed doors, I kept fighting.

Olympics gender row boxer Imane Khelif will debut as a professional boxer in December

'Because this fight was never only mine. It was for everyone who dared to be, for everyone who refused to give up.'

Khelif's coach, Kamel Abdesselam, said that Khelif could challenge for a world title within three to five professional fights.

The 27-year-old also hopes to compete in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games, but must take a sex test to compete in the women's category after that was universally mandated by the International Olympic Committee.

Khelif won welterweight gold at the last Olympics.

A fellow gender row boxer, Lin Yu-ting, who claimed the featherweight title in Paris, was cleared earlier this year to return to World Boxing events after a sex test, casting doubt on the fairness of the controversy over her gender.

Khelif has not competed since sex tests were introduced by World Boxing in 2025, taking the fight to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in a bid to compete without being tested, for which a hearing is yet to be held.

But the fighter is happy to take a sex test for the next Olympics, saying to CNN in February: 'Of course, I would accept doing anything I'm required to do to participate in competitions.

'They should protect women, but they need to pay attention that while protecting women, they shouldn't hurt other women.'

Last year, Donald Trump signed an executive order entitled 'Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports'. The United States President referred to Khelif as a 'male boxer' who had 'transitioned' and 'stole the women's gold medal' by competing in Paris.

The President doubled down on calling Khelif a 'male' during a speech to Republican lawmakers in January.

Trump has previously claimed that Khelif is transgender. Our current understanding is that that is incorrect. The boxer was, as far as we know, born female, but is believed to possess the SRY gene, which is associated with male sex chromosomes.

'I respect everyone, and I respect Trump because he's the president of the United States,' Khelif told L'Equipe. 'Trump cannot distort the truth. I'm not trans, I'm a girl.

'I was raised as a girl, I grew up as a girl, people in my village have always known me as a girl.'

Sports.title: Jake Paul will make his boxing comeback on Christmas Eve in Dubai - just a year after suffering a double broken jaw in brutal defeat by Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Jake Paul will make his boxing comeback on Christmas Eve in Dubai - just a year after suffering a double broken jaw in brutal defeat by Anthony Joshua

Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua.

The YouTuber turned boxer will headline a Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) event on December 24, marking his first professional fight in Dubai.

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem, although Paul is understood to want the Dutchman to lose a significant amount of weight before they could agree to fight.

MVP have yet to confirm who Paul will face as he prepares to return to action following the most damaging defeat of his professional career.

The 29-year-old was stopped by Joshua in the sixth round of their heavyweight showdown in Miami on December 19, 2025, after struggling to cope with the Briton's size, power and experience.

Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua

Paul pictured fighting AJ at the Kaseya Center, Miami, Florida on December 19, 2025

Paul spent much of the early stages attempting to keep his distance from the former two-time unified heavyweight world champion, using his movement to evade Joshua's attacks.

But the contest began to turn decisively in the fifth round as Joshua increased the pressure, flooring Paul twice and leaving him struggling to cope with the relentless assault.

The American survived the round but was dropped again in the sixth before Joshua delivered the decisive blow, landing a powerful right hand that sent Paul to the canvas for a fourth time.

Paul failed to beat the referee's count, with the contest officially stopped at one minute and 31 seconds of the sixth round.

It marked the first knockout defeat of Paul's professional boxing career and his second loss overall, following his split-decision defeat by Tommy Fury in February 2023.

The damage extended well beyond the result. Paul confirmed immediately after the fight that he had suffered a double broken jaw, later sharing an X-ray on social media showing fractures in two places.

He subsequently had surgery to repair the injuries, with two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed. Recovery did not go according to plan, with Paul having to go back under the knife for a second time.

The severity of the injury raised questions over how long Paul would be sidelined and whether he would return to the ring.

The YouTuber-turned-boxer pictured alongside his fiancee Jutta Leerdam (Olympic champion)

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till

But the American has now confirmed his comeback, with Dubai set to host another major event as he looks to rebuild his boxing career.

'I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face,' Paul said.

'Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward.

'I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey.

'Dubai is a city that thinks big, breaks boundaries, and doesn't believe in limits. That's exactly the kind of place I want to make my comeback.

'We've got plenty of names on the list; let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out.'

Paul, who boasts a professional record of 12 wins and two defeats, has become one of boxing's biggest commercial attractions since making his debut in 2020.

His November 2024 bout against Mike Tyson attracted a reported 125million global viewers, while his showdown with Joshua a year later drew 33m.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem (above)

The announcement comes as MVP continues to expand its international presence, with the Dubai event being organised in cooperation with the Dubai Sports Council and the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism.

MVP co-founder and chief executive Nakisa Bidarian said Paul's return demonstrated his determination to continue competing after his injury against Joshua.

'Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport,' Bidarian said.

'This is more than a fight. It's a global event in one of the world's great destination cities, on one of the most special nights of the year, when families everywhere are together and watching.

'We're finalising an opponent worthy of Jake's return and look forward to sharing more in the coming weeks.'

Till, who previously challenged for the UFC welterweight title, has increasingly explored opportunities outside mixed martial arts since leaving the UFC.

Overeem, meanwhile, enjoyed a lengthy career at the highest level of MMA and kickboxing, competing in promotions including the UFC, Strikeforce and K-1.

The 45-year-old Dutchman has not competed in professional MMA since 2021, when he was released by the UFC following his defeat by Alexander Volkov but has stated he's interested in pursing a boxing career.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and wife Paris both break down in tears as they recount how he 'didn't want to live' in deep depression amid his alcohol and drug addiction in new Netflix documentary trailer
Sports.content:
A tearful Paris Fury has revealed how she was left 'scared' over husband Tyson's alarming health decline, with the heavyweight superstar opening up on his paralysing drink and drug addiction in a new documentary.

Tyson, 38, saw his life spiral out of control after reaching the pinnacle of boxing following his heavyweight title triumph over arch rival Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

The Gypsy King, speaking in Netflix's new documentary Tyson Fury, confessed how he had lost his 'whole point of existence' after his win in Dusseldorf, leading to a crippling addiction to alcohol and cocaine.

In the documentary trailer, Tyson says: 'All I wanted to was beat Klitschko. It was an obsession for me.

'I'd achieved all my childhood dreams, but my whole point of existence had been taken away. I didn't want to live.'

Tyson and Paris Fury both broke down in tears as they recounted his troubling addiction past

Fury revealed how he had lost his whole point of existence after winning the heavyweight title

Fury fulfilled a career-long obsession after beating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015

Tyson's wife and childhood sweetheart Paris, could only watch on as her husband's life unravelled, and was emotional as she recounted the traumatising episode.

'Straight after [the Klitschko fight], Tyson said to me "this is as good as it is ever going to get". I didn't understand at the time what he meant,' she says.

'The Tyson I knew was gone and I was so scared.'

The documentary, which charts Tyson's incredible rise to heavyweight champion of the world, tells how he grew up surrounded by strong male figures - where discussing emotions was off limits.

'Growing up in my family, there was no emotion shown. They were all hard nuts. Like 50cent said: "Show no love, love will get you killed."'

Fury fought back from his addiction problems to make his boxing comeback in 2018, before triumphing over Deontay Wilder in a sensational heavyweight trilogy against the big-hitting American - where he won the WBC title.

The Gypsy King sought to unify the heavyweight division against the all-conquering Oleksandr Usyk, but twice fell short in a pair of thrilling contests against the Ukrainian.

Netflix cameras have documented the lives of the Fury family since 2023. The latest series centred on Fury's decision to come out of retirement, plus the family's move from Morecambe to the Isle of Wight.

The streaming giant will broadcast Fury's mega-fight against Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11.

Sports.title: Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga arrested after striking baby mama on the head with a pistol in heated dispute
Sports.content:
Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery following a heated physical bust-up with the mother of his child.

Berlanga, who is signed to Dana White's Zuffa Boxing, was arrested and booked in Polk County, Florida, on one charge of battery and one charge of aggravated battery on Monday.

The fighter is alleged to have repeatedly slapped a woman before hitting her on the head with a gun, according to court documents obtained by the Daily Mail.

The alleged victim, the mother of Berlanga's son, told police that the pair became embroiled in a heated argument while the boxer was driving after leaving a gun range on October 18.

She claimed that the dispute turned physical when Berlanga began slapping her before reaching into the vehicle's cupholder and retrieving a pistol, according to police documents.

The boxer is then alleged to have struck the woman on the forehead with the magazine well of the gun.

Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery

The boxer is accused of hitting the mother of his child on the forehead with a pistol

He lost to Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in 2024

The woman claimed she attempted to escape from the vehicle and flee only for Berlanga to grab her arm and pull her back into the car. She eventually managed to exit the vehicle and sought safety at a nearby 7-Eleven.

Police said they observed swelling and bruising on her face which corroborated her allegations. They also said that they noticed a rip in her shirt and bruising on her inner arm consistent with her claims that Berlanga grabbed her.

When asked by officers if the gun Berlanga struck her with was real, the woman confirmed that it was and that she had witnessed the boxer fire the gun multiple times at the range around 20 minutes earlier.

The police report stated that she was unsure if she wanted to press charges, however, Berlanga was still ultimately arrested as officers declared it a domestic violence case.

Berlanga was booked on felony aggravated battery and misdemeanor battery touch/strike. He made his first court appearance on Tuesday and bond was set at $16,000, per court records.

Berlanga is a top rising boxer with a 24-2 record with 19 KOs. He went up against Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in September 2024 but lost by unanimous decision.

Earlier this year, he headlined an event at Madison Square Garden in New York City, where he delivered a KO loss to Steven Butler in the seventh round.

Sports.title: F1 2026 calendar update: Imola off the table, no plan B if Iran war escalates
Sports.content:
The Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix which will conclude Formula 1’s 2026 season are set to proceed as planned, provided there is no dramatic escalation of the Iran war.

The Middle Eastern conflict, which started in late February as the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, has destabilised the region. The calendars of many motorsport championships have been impacted – not least F1’s, whose Saudi Arabian race was cancelled while Bahrain’s round was postponed and hosted in Malaysia.

F1 has been monitoring the situation closely, with a Imola as an alternative season finale on the first weekend of December if Qatar and Abu Dhabi were unable to host their respective events.

Lusail did run its MotoGP round without major issues last weekend, though both Yamaha teams withdrew from the competition due to the geopolitical situation.

10 November was F1’s deadline to provide Imola with a final answer as to whether the Italian track would have to prepare for a grand prix in the next three weeks; it will not.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls Photo by: Zak Mauger / Motorsport Images

So the 2026 season will end with the planned Las Vegas-Qatar-Abu Dhabi triple-header, with travel insurance and governments’ travel advice currently allowing it.

However, there’s a caveat: F1 is aware it cannot guarantee the situation won’t change by early December and insists it will prioritise safety if the conflict escalates.

Team bosses have been maintaining a straightforward stance on the matter – they trust F1 and the FIA to make the right calls.

“I trust them to take the best decision for all of us,” Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur commented in Mexico. “Me, personally, I want to race. It doesn't matter where, but I want to race. Now, I will go where they will tell us to go.”

“Stefano and Mohammed have been pretty clear about the situation that Formula 1 follows what the international guidelines are, whether there are travel restrictions, airlines not flying, any warnings in the region, the kind of feedback that local governments are making,” his Mercedes counterpart Toto Wolff added in Friday’s press conference at Interlagos. “So not only the promoters, but what the local governments are making. And this is what you need to rely on, in my opinion, and I'm fully with that.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“I think that if riders stand up, who know nothing geopolitically about what's going on, but have an audience that listens, I think that is something that creates media value. But I would have done the same as MotoGP management has done. You want to ride or drive, go. If you don't want to, don't go. It's as simple as that, and everybody can take their personal decisions on that, and I respect that.

“Of course, you've got to be wary of what's happening in the next few days, a few weeks, and Stefano has his finger on the pulse to monitor that. If things were to get more dangerous and we would get that feedback, then he's going to be the first one, together with Mohammed, to protect the people that were meant to travel. So that's why I'm following their guidance.

“From what I'm hearing internally, it hasn't been raised. It hasn't been a topic. But also there, if someone feels they don't feel comfortable, he or she doesn't feel comfortable travelling, then it's something that I would always respect. And maybe that's an opportunity to give somebody else a chance. It wouldn't change anything for the relationship. I've always respected that some people didn't want to go to certain grands prix, and that's how I see it at the moment.”

Additional reporting by Ronald Vording

Sports.title: FIA reveals ADUO results in final review of 2026 F1 season
Sports.content:
The FIA has announced its final Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) results for the 2026 Formula 1 season, with no changes granted for any of the power unit manufacturers.

From this season, the FIA installed a mechanism in the F1 regulations which allowed power unit manufacturers the ability to make updates, if they fell behind the leading engine, in the form of tokens permitted under a performance scale.

After the first period in 2026, which ran from the Australian Grand Prix to the Canadian GP, it was announced that Red Bull Ford Powertrains emerged as the benchmark, while Mercedes’ internal combustion engine trails by between 2-4%, which gave the German manufacturer to one additional upgrade this year and one more next season.

Ferrari, Audi and Honda fell into the category of being more than 4% behind on ICE power, which grants them two upgrades during the current campaign and two more in 2027.

Red Bull Ford Powertrains asked for a review of the ADUO analysis, which delayed the official publication of the first results, as it disputed the results and being considered the manufacturer with the strongest engine.

As agreed before the start of the season by the teams, the FIA only measures the internal combustion engine, but once a manufacturer qualifies for ADUO, it is also allowed to modify electrical components such as the battery and MGU-K.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

So while Red Bull’s rivals have been able to install power unit upgrades across this season, the Milton Keynes-based effort has effectively faced an engine freeze.

In the third and final FIA analysis of ADUO – which took engine data from the Dutch GP up to and including the US GP – there has been no change and therefore no manufacturer will gain or lose its current concessions.

There was also no change in the second ADUO period over the summer.

“For the third period, the relative performance gaps to the leading ICE evolved, but these changes did not result in any additional homologations being granted to the Power Unit Manufacturers,” an FIA report stated.

Given the dispute over how ADUO is measured, the FIA is open to changes in the system in the future, subject to approval from the power unit manufacturers, while FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis is confident the concept is working as desired.

“The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached,” Tombazis said.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1.

“However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose. To that end, we have been working closely with the power unit manufacturers and teams to explore refinements to the methodology that will support the continued effectiveness of ADUO in future seasons.”

The next ADUO period will start in 2027, covering the opening six races of the F1 season from the Bahrain GP to the Miami GP.

Sports.title: What's behind Piastri's split with Webber – and what it means for his F1 career
Sports.content:
On the Monday after the Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix, Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber announced in a joint statement that the latter and Ann Neal would no longer manage the 25-year-old McLaren driver. The timing may come as a surprise – now rather than at the end of the season – but the news itself had been on the cards for some time.

The clearest hint came from Piastri during pre-season testing in Bahrain. While this writer was mainly interested in his opinion of the 2026 cars – which immediately brought a telling smile to Piastri's face – an Australian colleague raised the subject of Webber's changing role.

Read Also: Formula 1 Piastri and Webber terminate management agreement

"There wasn't anything specific, we just made a decision for things to look a bit different," Piastri said on that unusually cold February evening in the Bahrain paddock. "Mark is still very much involved and I've been in contact with him a lot over the last few weeks. He just won't be trackside as much anymore. So that's really the extent of it. There was nothing specific that triggered it."

Although that last point is essentially true, it is clear that the 2025 season was intense on several fronts – including behind the scenes, at least from Webber’s perspective. That was naturally closely linked to the 'papaya rules' through which McLaren tried to treat both drivers as fairly as possible, but which also made life difficult for the team at certain moments, as Andrea Stella frankly admitted at the beginning of this year.

It is no secret that Webber was not always happy with how McLaren handled certain moments on track, nor with the explanation for Piastri's dip in form during the final quarter of the season, which ultimately cost him the world title. It is important to emphasise, however, that a manager's role is also to defend the interests of his own driver, even though there are multiple ways of doing so.

Webber naturally had the experiences from his own Red Bull years in mind and wanted to prevent Piastri from ever being labelled a number two driver in the F1 paddock. In a recent interview with Autosport, former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner even described this as a key part of Webber's mentality, a worldview that Horner believes he brought into the cockpit.

"I think probably the difficulty with Mark was, he motivated himself through adversity. He always drove better when he felt that the world was against him," Horner said. "He could see this talent emerging in Sebastian [Vettel], and he was using everything in his locker to try and destabilise that, or to cause any tension in a way that would then fall back in his favour. I think as a team we were learning how to handle these dynamics."

Watch: Christian Horner on Toto, Abu Dhabi 2021 and Life After Red Bull.

The differences between Red Bull back then and McLaren today are considerable, however. Red Bull was led at the time by Horner and Helmut Marko, two men who were certainly no strangers to the political side of F1, whereas McLaren is now much more engineering-led under Andrea Stella, who constantly emphasises the principles by which he wants to go racing – including fairness. This brings a different dynamic and also means that any attempts to avoid being pushed into a number two role are viewed in a completely different light.

It must be emphasised that McLaren has never formally asked Piastri to change his management, but Autosport understands that the driver himself, with some input from those around him, has formed his own view of what he needs going forward.

In any case, the decision had already been made at the beginning of this year for Webber to take a step back and operate primarily 'behind the scenes' rather than being in the spotlight during race weekends. With hindsight, that was a first step towards this split, which, according to the statement, has come about by mutual agreement. "Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close," Webber said.

Piastri's development and a new reality in the F1 driver market

Aside from all that, it must also be said that Piastri's situation is very different now from what it was at the beginning of his career. Consequently, what he needs from the people around him has changed as well. This applies in two areas: his experience as a driver and the current situation in the F1 driver market.

In his younger years, Piastri needed Webber's experience as a racing driver more than he does now. When the Australian made his F1 debut at the age of 21 – and was, as Toto Wolff tends to describe young drivers, still a "deer in the headlights" – it helped to have a trusted figure by his side who had already experienced it all. Someone outside the team who was concerned solely with his interests and could help him avoid potential pitfalls.

When Autosport spoke to Piastri in Barcelona during his debut season, that was precisely the added value he highlighted: "Mark’s advice was to not underestimate the challenge of F1 and how big of a step up it is, not just from the cars but from everything: the amount of people you need to interact with, the media commitments, and the sponsor commitments. It's all much higher than before. I think having him reminding me of that before the season started was nice, not to be shocked when I arrived. That's probably been the biggest thing.

Oscar Piastri, McLaren F1 Team, 2nd position, is congratulated by Mark Webber in Parc Ferme Photo by: Steven Tee / Motorsport Images

"But he's very helpful with small driving tips here and there as well, and sometimes thinking of questions for the engineers that don't even come to my head at the moment.

"He's still very sharp. He thinks like a racing driver still and is always trying to get the best out of me."

More than three years later, Piastri has experienced all of this himself and therefore needs that hands-on guidance as a driver less than he did during his rookie season. Logically, this means that a different type of management can now suffice, with different priorities in that respect as well.

Moreover, the situation in the driver market has changed. Piastri is committed to McLaren for the longer term, with a contract running until the end of 2028. Yes, an extraordinary amount has been said and written about Piastri's seat this summer, particularly in light of the Max Verstappen rumours, which have been blown considerably out of proportion by certain publications. In reality, however, the Dutchman indicated that he had come much closer to retiring from F1 than to moving to another team, meaning Piastri has not seriously been looking elsewhere either.

He did describe it as 'flattering' that his name was linked with Red Bull during the summer months, but the reality is that this route appears to be closed for the coming years. After all, Verstappen has extended his contract, meaning Red Bull – provided it gives him a competitive car – has its lead driver in place. And with talents such as Isack Hadjar, Arvid Lindblad and perhaps Nikola Tsolov in the longer term, Red Bull appears perfectly capable of filling its second seat from within its own talent pool.

Add to that the fact that Mercedes and Ferrari also still have long-term lead drivers in Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc, and maintaining and further strengthening his relationship with McLaren seems far more important for Piastri than having contacts elsewhere, for example through Webber at Red Bull. These two factors may still make the timing surprising, but not so much the decision itself to end the partnership after Webber had already taken a step back.

Oscar Piastri, McLaren with Mark Webber Photo by: Getty Images

Finally, it must be said that Webber did play a key role in the early years of Piastri's career, one that should not be forgotten at a moment like this. Indeed, Piastri himself has not forgotten it either, as his quote in the joint statement demonstrates: "I'd like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years. Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward."

The most important move, of course, was leaving Alpine for McLaren, including Piastri's now-famous tweet. That was a period in which Webber's 'us against the world' mentality, as Horner described it, proved particularly useful. The move also saved Piastri from the quicksand that Alpine was, especially at that time. It is a decision for which he remains grateful, but this phase of his career calls for something different, and that explains why the partnership between two of the four most recent Australian F1 drivers has come to an end.

Webber played an important role in getting Piastri to where he is today, and the current seventh-placed driver in the championship has not forgotten that. But he feels that something different is needed for the next phase of his career, ideally one of harmony within McLaren – and, given all of the above, that is understandable.

Sports.title: How the Racing Bulls pendulum is swinging back towards Lawson
Sports.content:
When job security is in short supply, there's one solution for an Formula 1 driver. Be so good they can't ignore you.

That's easier said than done, but it certainly seems to be what Liam Lawson has taken to heart as he battled for his future over the recent Americas triple-header. Having been an integral part of Racing Bulls' rise to fifth in the constructors' championship, which will be the Anglo-Italian team's best-ever result, Lawson took ninth in Austin before bagging a pair of seventh-place finishes in Mexico and Brazil.

Following his challenger Nikola Tsolov's strong FP1 debut in Mexico, and Lawson's unfortunate run-in with Red Bull's stalwart Max Verstappen, signs are now pointing towards the pendulum having swung back in Lawson's favour with a decision expected over the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend next week. A report from The Race, which Autosport understands is accurate, says Lawson is now set to stay put after all with Tsolov coming on board as a reserve in 2027. Sources have indicated a final decision is close but not signed off yet.

Driving for his future has been exhausting for Lawson, even if it's not a new situation for the 24-year-old. Ever since he arrived as a deputy for the injured Daniel Ricciardo in 2023, Lawson has effectively been fighting for his seat, first from the sidelines and then as Ricciardo's full-time replacement with little to no job security beyond the next race weekend.



It all came to a head over the past triple-header as Racing Bulls and the wider Red Bull organisation kept delaying a final call between Lawson and Tsolov.



If Racing Bulls had been a standalone team, the decision to retain Lawson and Arvid Lindblad would have been a no-brainer. Rookie Lindblad is still seen as potential Red Bull material in the future. And while that window appears to have come and gone for Lawson, he has amassed 89 points as the highest point scorer outside the top four teams.



With Racing Bulls tasked to train young drivers for the Red Bull senior team though, it is understood Red Bull's Austrian parent company is particularly excited by F2 frontrunner Tsolov's promise. However, a decision to keep Lawson wouldn't necessarily work against Racing Bull's objective, as having such a solid benchmark in the other car has been useful to gauge Lindblad's performances this year too. Meanwhile, 19-year-old Tsolov would still benefit from a full year as a reserve driver, which includes more FP1s, private testing and simulator work.

Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

Racing Bulls qualifying head-to-head

Arvid Lindblad 7-14 (6-11 without sprints) Liam Lawson 9 (+1.253s in Q3) Australia 8 15 (+0.334s in SQ2) China (sprint) 13 15 (+0.019s in Q2) China 14 10 Japan 14 (+0.386s in Q2) 16 Miami (sprint) 17 (+0.171s in SQ1) 17 (+0.538s in Q1) Miami 12 9 Canada (sprint) DNS 9 Canada 12 (+0.349s in Q2) 15 (+0.777s in Q2) Monaco 10 11 (+0.255s in Q2) Barcelona 8 10 (+0.052s in Q3) Austria 9 10 (+0.440s in SQ3) Britain (sprint) 9 9 Britain 10 (+0.411s in Q3) 8 Belgium 11 (+0.491s in Q2) 9 Hungary 11 (+0.405s in Q2) 15 (+0.246s in Q2) Azerbaijan 12 16 (no time - grid penalty) Bahrain in Malaysia 11 17 (+0.281s in SQ1) Singapore (sprint) 8 10 (+0.412s in Q3) Singapore 9 9 United States 10 (No lap time in Q3) 9 (+0.088s in Q3) Mexico 8 14 (+4.638s in Q2 - rain) Brazil 5

Racing Bulls has also been explicitly asked by Austria to stand on its own feet both in terms of identity and performance, so that's why a dyed-in-the-wool F1 veteran like team principal Alan Permane would have been keen to maximise performance and stick with Lawson.



"The main factors are, as always, pace and speed. That's the very first thing we look for," Permane said when grilled on the topic on Friday in Sao Paulo. "But we're not just a team that exists solely to compete. We are here to bring young talent through, so we have to keep an eye on that. And that doesn't necessarily mean that we just keep churning young talent through the car. We need to maybe have some experience as well to measure that talent."

The clearest hint that a difference in opinion between the various stakeholders is what has really been holding up the decision came from Lawson himself. "I feel like Alan's been extremely supportive to me and I appreciate that a lot," he said. "I've enjoyed working closely with him and with the team this year. Obviously, it's a big organisation so..."



Permane recently inked a fresh deal until 2031 as Racing Bulls team principal and co-CEO, so it's obvious that his opinion carries plenty of weight. And it would stand to reason that Permane has wanted some assurances about his share in the decision-making before committing.

"Alan is doing a tremendous job, and the progress the team has made is a direct reflection of his experience, commitment and competitive mindset," said Permane's boss Oliver Mintzlaff, CEO Corporate Projects and Investments Red Bull. "He brings clarity, composure, and a deep understanding of what it takes to perform in Formula 1, while creating an environment where people can consistently deliver at their best."

Meanwhile, fans of Lawson and the team have been flooding the squad's social media channels urging it to re-sign the Kiwi. He said: "I appreciate all the support. I've seen it over the last few weeks. It's honestly really nice to see.

A treacherous Brazil weekend was one of Liam Lawson's finest. Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"Obviously, I would love it if it was more from a team. But at the moment I'm just trying to enjoy driving the car because with everything else going on I don't really know what else I'm meant to do. I don't really know what else I'm meant to say to you guys. So, at the moment I'm just going to keep driving and see what happens."

When it mattered the most, Brazil was perhaps Lawson's finest weekend yet. In treacherous conditions, Lawson took fifth on the grid, starting from third after grid penalties for George Russell and Charles Leclerc.

In the rain, he picked off McLaren's Lando Norris for second at the start, only to fall back to his natural position once drivers got their intermediate tyres back in the right operating window. Lawson battled to claim eighth on the road, being promoted to seventh after Leclerc was penalised for barging his way past in the closing laps.



Permane was obviously appreciative of how tough the past few weeks and months have been on one of F1 2026's standout performers, but said the team is nearly there.



"I realise it's frustrating for our drivers," he added. "I realise it's frustrating for everyone else, but we want to get it right, and we will get it right. I'm sure when we announce it in the coming weeks, everyone will be happy..."

Sports.title: Piastri and Webber terminate management agreement
Sports.content:
Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber have mutually agreed to terminate their management agreement, the pair have announced.

Webber and his wife Ann – who ran Mark’s career herself back in the day – became Piastri’s managers in 2019, the year the youngster narrowly beat Victor Martins to the Formula Renault Eurocup title and a spot on Renault’s F1 academy.

Piastri’s rise was meteoric from then on, as he clinched the Formula 3 title the following year – again marginally, with Theo Pourchaire and Logan Sargeant just a few points adrift – and won Formula 2 in 2021, also as a rookie, and with little competition that time.

Under Webber, Piastri made the career-defining move to leave the Alpine fold and sign a McLaren race deal for the 2023 Formula 1 season, which paved the way for his 2025 title bid. Across 88 career starts so far, the Australian has taken six pole positions and nine victories.

“We are proud to have played a pivotal role in the formative years of Oscar's career and to have placed him in F1 so that he could compete at the front so early on,” Webber said.

“Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close. This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure, and for us to embark on our new ventures. We wish Oscar all the very best for a long and successful career.”

Oscar Piastri, McLaren Photo by: James Sutton / Formula 1 / Formula Motorsport Ltd via Getty Images

Piastri added: “I'd like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years. Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward.”

Webber had taken a step back at the start of the 2026 season and no longer supported Piastri trackside, with a couple of new figures assisting the McLaren driver – Pedro Matos, his race engineer at Prema in Formula 2, and mental coach Emma Murray.

“There wasn't anything specific, just we made a decision for things to look a bit different,” Piastri said back in February. “Mark is still very much involved and I've been in contact with him a lot over the last few weeks. He just won't be trackside as much anymore. So that's really the extent of it.

“There was nothing specific that triggered it.”

Appearing on the High Performance Podcast in May, the 25-year-old added: “The relationship's good. Very thorough, is Mark. When I first got into F1, Mark was coming up with questions and ideas that literally hadn't even entered my brain. I would hear him say it and go like, 'How the hell did he think of that?' Or like, 'How am I ever going to think of that?'

Oscar Piastri, McLaren with Mark Webber Photo by: Getty Images

“And I think just with experience, we're always learning every day, but now starting my fourth year, I have either the answers to a lot of those kinds of questions that I wouldn't have had in the first couple of years, or I know the questions to keep asking, which just comes with experience.

“There's naturally less and less for Mark to do on the racing side of things the more experienced I become. But especially in the first couple of years, there are some lessons you have to learn the hard way, and there's no other way of doing it, but I'm sure there could have been plenty of other slightly annoying, tougher lessons to learn that I was probably spared because of Mark's experience and Mark's guidance.

“There's probably always going to be situations or things that have gone smoothly or almost problems that weren't problems that I'm never going to know about because Mark managed them for me. That's probably how it's changed in the last few years.”

Sports.title: Leclerc penalised for Lawson clash; Antonelli and Oliver Bearman also punished after F1 Brazilian GP
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc was handed a five-second penalty after the Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix for his clash with Liam Lawson, dropping the Ferrari driver down to eighth place in the final results.

The Monegasque was battling the Racing Bulls driver for seventh place on lap 69 of the Sao Paulo race when the pair made contact into Juncao, Turn 12, but both were able to continue and finish the race.

The clash did enable Leclerc to take seventh place from Lawson but the incident was placed under investigation for a post-race hearing.

After speaking to both drivers and assessing the video and data, the FIA stewards determined Leclerc was to blame and duly gave him a five-second penalty, dropping the Ferrari driver behind his rival and into eighth place in the final results.

The FIA stewards accepted that the contact was minor and in wet conditions, which was enough mitigation to keep the penalty to 5s and not a potential 10s punishment.

The FIA stewards report read: “While the contact was minor and Car 30 was able to maintain the lead thereafter, the driver of Car 30 claimed that the contact damaged the rear left rim of his car and also enabled Car 16 to get closer to him on track and then eventually overtake him 5 corners later. Furthermore, under the Driving Standard Guidelines, Car 30 had the right to the corner and it was for Car 16 to take the necessary steps to avoid a collision.

Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

“The driver of Car 16 claimed that it was a minor contact with no obvious sporting consequence.

“While we acknowledge that the contact was minor, having examined the fight on track between the two cars, we conclude that Car 16 was able to get closer to and thereafter overtake Car 30 because of the contact. The contact clearly disrupted Car 30 and allowed Car 16 to pull up alongside when it was further away before the contact. This was an obvious sporting consequence.

“In mitigation, the wet conditions coupled with the nature of the contact (i.e. minor) was taken into account in imposing a 5 second time penalty as opposed to a 10 second time penalty.”

Antonelli and Bearman also penalised for unsafe releases from pitstops

New F1 world champion Kimi Antonelli was also given a five-second penalty after the Brazilian GP for an unsafe pitstop release.

The Italian was released from his final pitstop of the race into the path of the oncoming Franco Colapinto and despite attempting to take avoiding action it was judged unsafe and a five-second penalty was duly handed out.

But because Antonelli finished over 20s ahead of Oscar Piastri, who was directly behind him on the road, it does not change his final finishing position of fifth place – as Mercedes secured this year’s F1 constructors’ championship.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

In a separate incident also involving Leclerc, Oliver Bearman was given a post-race five-second penalty for an unsafe release from a pitstop. The Haas F1 driver was released into the path of the Ferrari driver, which forced Leclerc to check-up in the pitlane.

The penalty has no consequence to Bearman either given he finished in 17th and one lap up on Sergio Perez in 18th place.

Sports.title: Antonelli explains "weird" spin and car instability which cost F1 Brazilian GP win
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli vowed to put aside his Brazilian Grand Prix anger to celebrate Mercedes winning the Formula 1 constructors' title, as he rued the balance issues and the spin that took him out of victory contention.

The new world champion had picked up the lead from polesitter Lando Norris at the start, and was building a pretty healthy lead over the Briton in the opening laps of the race. He held the lead either side of the first round of pitstops, as the circuit was dry enough for slicks, although Norris' undercut had taken a considerable chunk of time out of Antonelli's advantage.

At the start of lap 20, Antonelli then lost the car and this precipitated a spin at the opening corner. He was able to recover, but Norris had long since bolted past for the lead - and it left the Italian in the clutches of Isack Hadjar.

Antonelli had reported before his spin that he was worried he'd picked up a suspension issue, and that the car was pulling to one side under acceleration - and his difficulty with balance cost further positions to Hadjar and Max Verstappen. However, no clear cause had emerged during the race.

"I'm very disappointed for the race. I'm very angry to be fair, but I'm going to put all this aside for now because the team clinched the title," Antonelli said.

"We clinched the title for the team, and they all deserve it and I'm very proud to be part of this group and this team who has done and still does so much for me and I'm very happy for them. But talking about the race specifically, yeah, very disappointing.

Lando Norris, McLaren, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"We were on for the win up to that point. Also in the lead, once I was able to get some temperature I was getting to the rhythm. But yeah, the spin came which still is something I need to look at because I don't know why I lost the rear so quickly as well.

"Like no warning, nothing. But already to be fair when I put the soft, I felt something weird with the car. So, we need to check what happened but on the other hand yeah, shame because we lost the race there."

When speaking to Sky Sports, Antonelli expanded on the issue and noted that it was only occurring in the left-hand corners, particularly in higher-speed sections - which, around Interlagos, would account for much of the first and third sectors.

The tyre flat spots sustained in the spin made his life much harder; when he'd taken a second set of soft tyres, his improvement in lap time was demonstrable and this afforded an opportunity to challenge Hadjar late on.

"We need to check something with the geometry of the car, of the rear, because I had this issue only in left corners. So especially at the high speed was when I was feeling it the most," he told Sky.

"And the rear felt very unstable, even in coming into the finish line in the left kink, the rear was very loose, which was weird.

"We need to check something in the car to see if anything happened. But it was a very odd feeling. And then when I spun, the tyres were gone; all four wheels flat spotted. Only when then I put on the second set, we got back to pace. It was a shame."

Sports.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Norris wins in mixed conditions, Mercedes clinch constructors’ title
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has snared his third win of 2026 in a mixed weather Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix, defeating a resurgent Max Verstappen while Mercedes claimed the world constructors' championship.

After reclaiming the lead from his world champion successor Kimi Antonelli early on when he spun off, polesitter Norris thwarted Verstappen's latest stunning Brazil comeback in a race which both started and finished in the wet, bookending a dry spell.

Having survived a scare on the laps to the grid when he slid onto the grass at the tricky Turn 12, Antonelli picked off polesitter Norris for the lead into Turn 1 as the race started in intermediate conditions. Third-place starter Liam Lawson also followed the Mercedes through into second.

Alonso was the biggest loser as he dropped six places by going wide at Turn 3. Lewis Hamilton went the opposite direction, gaining 10 places to sweep into 11th, while Verstappen jumped to 13th after both drivers had started at the back of the grid with engine penalties.

As Antonelli built a five-second buffer to Lawson and Norris, Hamilton and Verstappen soon found each other, with Hamilton starting to struggle on worn rear tyres. The seven-time world champion couldn't follow Verstappen past Oscar Piastri and into the top 10, the Ferrari being passed by Aston Martin's Alonso instead.

Hamilton urged his team to bring him in for slicks and eventually got his wish on lap 15 of 71, being the first driver to make the switch. His immediate speed on the dry weather tyre triggered a flurry of pitstops across the grid as the entire field switched to softs as well, Antonelli and Verstappen waiting one lap longer than the other frontrunners.

Lando Norris, McLaren, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Manuel Eletto / Getty Images

After that shuffle, Antonelli kept the lead from Norris, Isack Hadjar and comeback hero Verstappen, who both made their way past Lawson. Russell, however, lost out by spinning in the pit exit, being fortunate enough to escape damage but dropping behind Piastri and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg.

Antonelli came under increasing pressure from Norris, reporting a problem with the suspension that made his car pull to one side. That became apparent in dramatic fashion as he spun off the track in Turn 1, releasing Norris into the lead but being able to rejoin.

Antonelli's handling woes continued as Red Bull duo Hadjar and Verstappen easily worked their way past into the podium positions, with Hadjar waving Verstappen by on lap 38.

After dropping five seconds behind Hadjar, Antonelli was able to stabilise things in fourth with a healthy buffer to Piastri, Lawson, Russell and Hulkenberg, while neither Ferrari driver was able to make much progress from the middle of the pack.

From starting at the rear, Verstappen suddenly found himself in second place just after halfway, with a nine second deficit to race leader Norris. Verstappen pulled the trigger on a second pitstop on lap 46 for a new set of softs, while Hadjar was bullish on making it to the end without stopping again.

As a light drizzle hit the track with 23 laps to go, McLaren pressed ahead with a second pitstop to softs for Norris. Hadjar abandoned the one-stop plan with a pitstop on lap 51 in response, leaving Antonelli in the lead as Mercedes decided to gamble on heavier rain or a safety car. But with the newly crowned world champion losing over a second per lap, Mercedes soon abandoned that plan with a lap 54 pitstop for new slicks.

As strategies converged again, Norris continued matching whatever Verstappen could throw at him as he defended a seven-second gap, with Hadjar another eight seconds in arrears in third.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

But the heavens started opening again on lap 62, which triggered a mass move to intermediates within the space of two laps, Norris and Verstappen both peeling in on lap 63 as Hamilton survived a spin on slicks right before pitting.

Unperturbed, Norris coolly controlled the treacherous final laps to snare his third win of the campaign, with Verstappen settling for second 14 seconds behind the McLaren driver, while Hadjar third another nine seconds behind.

Russell was fourth ahead of Antonelli, both cars overcoming late balance woes to earn Mercedes its ninth constructors' championship, its first such trophy since 2021.

Piastri was sixth for McLaren ahead of Leclerc and a valiant Lawson, who continues fighting for his F1 future with Racing Bulls but was unable to keep Leclerc behind in the closing laps.

Like Leclerc, Hamilton was unable to sustain a genuine comeback as he settled for ninth, with Hulkenberg taking the final point in 10th despite a 10-secondpenalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage.

Rafael Camara finished 20th and last on his home debut as Esteban Ocon's replacement, as Lance Stroll retired for the 14th time this season in the Aston Martin. Valtteri Bottas did not make the start due to a cross-threaded right-rear wheel nut on his Cadillac.

Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton travelled to the Gaza Strip today to see the work being done to bring humanitarian relief to those in the region.

He visited the Rafah land crossing between Egypt and the territory, plus a logistics facility where aid being sent to Gaza is processed.

The Ferrari driver has repeatedly called for peace in the region and criticised the lack of action from other countries. Over 74,000 people are estimated to have died in the war in Gaza which followed the Hamas attack in Israel on October 7th 2023, in which 1,195 were killed.

The North Sinai Governorate shared further details of Hamilton’s visit.
