Sports.title: F1 scraps back-up plan to race at Imola if Middle East GPs are cancelled – reports | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has committed to holding the final two rounds of the 2026 world championship in the Middle East or not at all.

The series had made contingency arrangements to relocate the final round it Imola in Italy if it decided the risks posed by the war in Iran meant it should not proceed with its races in the Middle East. Multiple reports now claim F1 has told Imola it will not be required to hold a race.

The world championship will resume at Las Vegas in the USA next week. Following that it is due to race at the Losail International Circuit in Qatar and Yas Marina in the United Arab Emirates on the following weekends.

The series cancelled its grands prix in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia earlier this year due to the war between Iran and the USA. It later held an event using the ‘Bahrain Grand Prix’ title at Malaysia’s Sepang International Circuit.

The political situation in the Middle East remains uncertain. US president Donald Trump this week suggested he would not escalate its military campaign in the region, but has made similar comments since beginning his war in February, only to subsequently launch further strikes. The US retains a significant military presences in the region and moved more troops there last month.

However Moto GP, which like F1 is owned by Liberty Media, raced in Losail on Sunday. It postponed its Qatar round in April due to the war.

Four bikes were missing from the field as Yamaha did not participate. Most of the series’ riders expressed concerns over visiting the country and asked the championship to provide extra guarantees for their security.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff defended Moto GP’s decision to race in Qatar. He criticised riders who expressed concerns about racing there, saying they “know nothing” about the situation.

Many television broadcasters also opted not to send their staff to the region.

The 2027 F1 season is due to begin in the Middle East with races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia next March. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali told investors last week “the disruption we experienced in the Middle East this year does not change our long-term regional strategy and ongoing partnership with our promoters.”

“This year, we currently remain scheduled to complete our calendar season and at this stage, continue to plan to finish the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi,” he added. “We will continue to monitor the situation. As always, the safety and security of everyone in the sport will remain our first and foremost priority.”

Many other series have cancelled events in the region due to the war in the Middle East. The World Endurance Championship called off its planned rounds in Qatar and Bahrain, replacing them with races in Italy and Spain. The 2027 Dakar Rally, previously held in Saudi Arabia, will take place in Africa. The 2026-27 Asian Le Mans series, which previously raced at Dubai Autodrome and Yas Marina, will take place in Europe under the name ‘Winter Le Mans Series’.

Sports.title: No F1 engine manufacturers to get extra upgrades after FIA’s third ADUO evaluation | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The FIA will not to offer any engine manufacturers the chance to perform extra power unit upgrades following its latest Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) evaluation.

Under new rules introduced as part of Formula 1’s 2026 power unit regulations the sport’s governing body controls how often manufacturers can upgrade their internal combustion engines.

The evaluations take place periodically throughout the season. The FIA has completed its third such evaluation and, as was the case during the second, determined no further engine homologation opportunities should be offered.

The third evaluation period concluded after the United States Grand Prix last month. The second followed the Hungarian Grand Prix.

The first evaluation period, which ran from the start of the season to the Canadian Grand Prix, remains the only time any additional upgrade opportunities were awarded. On that occasion Red Bull-Ford were found to have the top-performing power unit.

Audi, Ferrari and Honda’s units were found to be more than 4% less powerful. They were permitted two extra homologation opportunities this year and two more next year. Mercedes were found to be within 2% and 4% of the leading power unit and therefore received one extra upgrade this year and next.

Separately, in May the FIA changed the ADUO rules to allow any manufacturer which was 10% off the leading design to spend more money. The revision was expected to assist Honda following their poor start to the season.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Some have likened F1’s ADUO to the World Endurance Championship’s heavily-criticised Balance of Performance regulations. The FIA’s single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis defended the regulations but indicated they may be revised in coming seasons.

“Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached,” he said.

“The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1. However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose.

“To that end, we have been working closely with the power unit manufacturers and teams to explore refinements to the methodology that will support the continued effectiveness of ADUO in future seasons.”

Hamilton made a strong start to the race from 20th and briefly ran as high as ninth. But Max Verstappen overtook him and Ferrari then told him to let Oliver Bearman past.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia’s $100M Bluff to Lure Floyd Mayweather Out of Retirement
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is daring Floyd Mayweather Jr. to put his spotless 50–0 record on the line for a theoretical nine-figure payday.

The reigning WBC welterweight champion insists he will put the 49-year-old icon to sleep, claiming Mayweather will wake up $100 million richer for his trouble. The catch is simple: nobody has stepped forward with that kind of capital.

Garcia laid out his pitch on Kick with signature bravado: “Then, you wake up, and you’ve got $100 million. That’s good. You’re just going to get knocked out real quick. You love money, right? I’m going to test that theory on how much you love money.”

The math makes that purse an enormous stretch. At $80 per purchase, 1.5 million pay-per-view buys yield roughly $120 million in gross revenue. Once cable platforms, satellite providers, and streaming distributors take their cuts, production overhead gets covered, and Garcia secures his own check, a $100 million guarantee for Floyd evaporates.

Live ticket sales and brand sponsorships bridge some of the divide, but any backer writing that guarantee is gambling heavily. They must bet that modern audiences will shell out premium cash to see an aging Mayweather enter a real contest after a decade of theatrical exhibitions. Garcia generated massive numbers against Gervonta Davis, yet that blockbuster relied on Davis bringing an equally rabid audience.

Mayweather built an empire around being untouchable, an aura he preserves through low-risk exhibition tours. An authentic 12-round championship scrap completely shatters that protective bubble.

Ryan’s signature left hook poses immediate physical danger to a fighter turning 50, testing whether Mayweather’s legendary shoulder roll and counter instincts can outrun Father Time. Floyd stepped into a pro ring last in 2017 to dispatch Conor McGregor. He has not fought an elite, active professional boxer since outpointing Andre Berto in 2015.

Sanctioning politics complicate the picture just as much. WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman signaled that Mayweather could challenge for the title pending medical clearance and standard licensing. Even so, the WBC would face intense scrutiny for greenlighting a 49-year-old on a nine-year professional layoff ahead of deserving, active welterweight contenders.

With a broadcast partner, host city, and signed contracts entirely absent, Garcia’s February 6 target date looks increasingly like theater. Pointing toward Mayweather keeps Garcia dominating headlines while he entertains a practical matchup against Teofimo Lopez. Mayweather loses nothing by ignoring the noise. Garcia is the fighter with a date to fill, and finding a partner to share the stage matters far less than finding someone willing to fund it.

Mayweather isn’t 39; he turns 50 in February. At nearly half a century old, the physical drop-off is a complete biological cliff. In his exhibitions over the last couple of years, the reflexes, the spring in his legs, and the twitch speed that defined his prime are simply gone. What remains is muscle memory, shell defense, and pacing himself against novices, YouTubers, and MMA fighters who do not know how to cut off a ring or throw punches with real professional malice.

Putting that version of Mayweather in a sanctioned 12-round fight against Ryan Garcia, who is 28 and carries genuine, explosive power in his left hook, is not a competitive sporting event. A shell defense only works when you have the hand speed and counter-threat to keep a puncher honest. If you cannot deter a prime fighter from walking you down, the shell just turns you into a static target along the ropes. At 147, Garcia would walk through anything Floyd threw back, find the gaps, and the fight would likely be over as soon as Garcia committed to an exchange.

The financial reality makes it an even bigger non-starter. Riyadh Season and the Saudi backers have shown that while they will pay astronomical figures, they are spending with a purpose: legacy unifications, undisputed clashes, and top-tier matchups that build sports authority. The era of writing blank, nine-figure checks for absurd circus acts has dried up, especially with tighter watch on returns.

Paying $100 million to a 49-year-old fighter to take a severe beating in a sanctioned professional bout offers zero prestige and terrible optics. Nobody with that kind of capital is going to underwrite a one-sided blowout, and Floyd’s business instincts are still sharp enough to know that 50–0 is worth far more intact than whatever embarrassment awaits him in a real ring.

Sports.title: Jake Paul Calls Cédric Doumbé a Tune-Up
Sports.content:
Jake Paul plans to let his jab dictate terms when he meets Cédric Doumbé in Dubai on Christmas Eve. During their press conference in Paris, Paul labeled the former GLORY kickboxing standout an easy tune-up, projecting a stoppage inside four rounds. In his breakdown, Doumbé relies on wide, winging hooks that carry obvious warnings and operates behind a porous guard.

“Yeah, a lot of wild looping shots, no straight shots; everything he throws is predictable. He telegraphs his shots. He doesn’t set anything up. But he does have power, you know, behind them sometimes. Doesn’t have a good jab, not so good defense, and his chin is in the air. The body is open. There’s a lot, there’s a lot,” Paul said.

That critique points out real technical gaps, but it glosses over how kickboxers control space. In kickboxing, the threat of low kicks forces an opponent to stay light on their lead leg, preventing them from sitting down comfortably on a straight left. In a pure boxing ring, Paul steps forward without that hesitation. That lets him establish lead-foot dominance, pin Doumbé to the ropes, and lean on his cruiserweight bulk to tie up the smaller man whenever exchanges get chaotic. Doumbé spent the bulk of his combat career competing near 170 pounds, meaning Paul holds a clear frame advantage to grind on him along the perimeter.

Doumbé cannot afford to stand at mid-range waiting to time a home-run shot, because Paul will simply bank rounds behind the jab. His genuine opportunity comes from exploiting Paul’s habitual flaw: dropping the rear hand to chest level when stepping out of a combination. If Doumbé utilizes twitchy shoulder feints to draw Paul’s jab into the same rhythm, he can slip inside the line and fire his overhand right while Paul’s lead shoulder is fully extended. That requires disciplined ring cutting rather than the sudden forward blitzes Doumbé often used in GLORY.

Doumbé made no secret of his primary motive, pointing out the odd dynamic of facing an executive who signs the paychecks. “My boss will pay me to knock him the fuck out,” Doumbé stated. He gets eight rounds to prove his explosive power carries into a 200-pound cruiserweight ring on December 24 at Coca-Cola Arena.

Sports.title: Alycia Baumgardner Becomes A Two-Division Champion
Sports.content:
Arlington, Texas – On Sunday night, Alycia “The Bomb” Baumgardner became a two-division world champion by defeating the “Golden Turkish Warrior” Elif Turhan for the IBF world lightweight title. She may have put on the best performance of her career by showing her technical skills, being defensively sound and offensively great. She utilized her jab effectively, landing more jabs (92) than Turhan did total punches (50).

Elif (14-1, 8 KOs) was viewed as a dangerous power puncher with true knockout power, which, according to Alycia, the WBC/WBO/Ring Magazine lightweight champion Caroline Dubois avoided. Baumgardner was able to neutralize the Golden Turkish Warrior’s power, holding her to career lows in total punches landed – – 50 punches and held her in single digits of landed punches in all 10 rounds. Alycia was masterful offensively, landing 51 percent of her power punches, a career high for her. (Compubox).

At the post-fight press conference, Alycia (19-1, 7 KOs) told the media about the fight, “Tonight, we became a two-division world champion against a tough…tough opponent. This was someone I was very humble to fight, and I needed this fight to keep me humble, to keep me hungry, and again being the best fighter that I can be.”

With the win Baumgardner is one step closer to the undisputed super fight set to happen next year. First, she must await the winner of the unification match between Caroline Dubois (14-0-1, 5 KOs) and Stephanie Han (13-0, 3 KOs) scheduled to take place February 20 in El Paso, Texas. Both were present for the Turhan-Baumgardner match and want to be the opponent whom she’ll fight for the undisputed clash.

Caroline appears to be the favorite to win the unification match against Stephanie Han, and she’s been the most vocal, stating she wants to fight Alycia and become undisputed champion. When asked if she declined a fight with Turhan, she said it was not true, calling it absolute BS. After the fight, Baumgardner and Dubois exchanged stares and words. With Caroline asking Alycia multiple times, “Are we going to fight?” Dubois appears determined to be undisputed and may get her opportunity soon; she mustn’t overlook Han, who is fighting in her hometown in El Paso. The undisputed lightweight championship match will be one of the biggest in women’s boxing, setting up two potential superstars in the sport.

Sports.title: WBC Moves Pacheco Toward Canelo Despite Thin Record
Sports.content:
Diego Pacheco has inched toward a massive Canelo Alvarez payday without taking the fights that would prove he earned it. His ascent to the WBC No. 1 spot at super middleweight comes after he passed on opportunities against Christian Mbilli and Hamzah Sheeraz.

The WBC confirmed the ranking during its annual convention, per EverythingBoxing. Because Lester Martinez still holds the interim title, Pacheco’s top spot does not make him Canelo’s immediate mandatory challenger or secure the next championship crack. Instead, he meets Darius Fulghum on Saturday, November 14, in Carson, California.

That reality forces a hard question on the sanctioning body: what has Pacheco done against prime opposition to merit the highest numeric spot?

His resume features victories over Steven Nelson, Trevor McCumby, and Kevin Lele Sadjo. None of those names proves he belongs above the division’s true elite. Sadjo even scored a knockdown before dropping the decision. Pacheco has stacked up wins, yet he has bypassed the tests that would reveal his actual ceiling.

The Mbilli episode stands out because the sanctioning body was directly involved. After turning away from an IBF final eliminator to fight Nelson, Pacheco’s side pulled out of a WBC interim title matchup against Mbilli in 2025. Two distinct paths toward an elite opponent evaporated before he ever stepped through the ropes.

Pacheco justified that second move through business logic. He argued the money didn’t warrant heading to Quebec and taking a smaller financial split for a hometown draw.

“Honestly, the purse wasn’t that great,” Pacheco told The Ring.

Boxers have every right to reject offers that undervalue them. Sanctioning bodies, however, must evaluate real in-ring achievements. Turning away from a formidable foe may preserve a fighter’s bankroll, but it does not prove he could win the fight.

The missed clash with Sheeraz is tougher to excuse as routine positioning. That matchup was ordered for the vacant WBO world championship, offering Pacheco a direct shot at a legitimate belt. He walked away in January after talks entered purse bids.

Legitimate backstory accompanied the withdrawal. Eddie Hearn pointed to coaching and managerial friction, while Pacheco stated he felt unsettled with his camp. Those reasons carry weight, but declining a world title bout does not count as a victory.

Fulghum now arrives with a chance to wreck the design. Pacheco defends his WBC Silver strap at Dignity Health Sports Park, carrying extra risk thanks to his new position. A loss would shatter his argument for a Canelo date before he has even tested himself against a top-tier contender.

Martinez holding the interim belt also clouds the pathway. The WBC boosted Pacheco up the ladder while another fighter sits on the secondary championship.

Pacheco can validate his position by handling Fulghum and signing to fight a premier super middleweight next. For now, the top spot credits him for potential while overlooking the caliber of fighters he has actually shared the ring with.

WBC ordering Pacheco against Lester Martinez would force total clarity on the 168-pound picture. Either Pacheco proves he can handle an aggressive, heavy-handed puncher who can back him up, or Lester eliminates him and removes any lingering question about who deserves Canelo.

The sanctioning body will never mandate it, though. By giving Pacheco the No. 1 ranking while Lester holds the interim belt, Mauricio Sulaiman gives himself maximum room to maneuver. If Canelo decides he wants a clean, recognizable name with a major promoter behind him, they can trot out Pacheco. If Canelo prefers a mandatory with a regional belt to check a box, they have Lester.

If you looked at Christian Mbilli and decided the purse wasn’t worth the beating, and you backed out of a WBO world title shot against Hamzah Sheeraz during purse bids, Lester is the last guy you’re volunteering to fight.

Lester is high risk with zero casual crossover. He works behind heavy pressure, punches with power, and does not give you room to breathe. Kevin Lele Sadjo gave Pacheco absolute fits just by winging shots on the inside and dropping him. Lester brings that same kind of heavy, physical pressure, except he is bigger and hits harder.

Matchroom is not about to put Pacheco in with an avoided, heavy-handed Guatemalan who brings no pay-per-view juice when they can just feed him fighters like Darius Fulghum, sit on that No. 1 ranking, and pray Canelo calls their number before someone forces Pacheco to take a real test.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Wants Ryan Garcia After Paro
Sports.content:
Devin Haney is talking about Ryan Garcia and undisputed crowns at 147, but public wish lists rarely match promotional reality. Haney insists Garcia is his primary target after Liam Paro, presenting a four-belt unification as the ultimate prize. If Garcia falls short against Teofimo Lopez in their proposed clash, Haney claims he will gladly face Lopez instead.

Haney has to deal with Paro on December 19 at the Chase Center in San Francisco before any of those grand scenarios can materialize. Paro is not a prop. He is a tough, natural junior welterweight titleholder stepping up in weight, possessing the physical strength to test Haney inside. Haney enjoyed a distinct frame advantage at lightweight, but welterweight erases those physical cushions. Overlooking a durable southpaw to game-plan a dream tournament is a familiar trap in boxing.

“The Ryan Garcia fight is the fight that I want the most,” Haney said to the media. “It starts with Liam Paro, but, yeah, for sure. Once I win this fight, you guys know who I got my eyes on.”

Haney wants to believe that collecting straps automatically grants him control over Garcia. That is a tactical miscalculation. Belts do not dictate commercial power in modern boxing, pay-per-view draws do. Garcia demonstrated in their first meeting that he can generate massive gates and pay-per-view numbers on his own terms. Even if Garcia beats Lopez to capture the WBC and WBA belts, he does not need Haney to command enormous paydays. Haney needs Garcia to attempt to erase the most damaging night of his career.

Devin and Bill Haney have spent years operating under the purist boxing currency: belts equate to leverage. In their minds, capturing the WBO and IBF straps against Liam Paro gives them undisputed collateral, and in the traditional sanctioning body system, two champions meeting for all four belts automatically calls for an even split.

In the modern commercial landscape, belts do not sell pay-per-views. Garcia proved in April 2024 that his platform dwarfs the hardware. He brings millions of casual eyeballs, viral reach, and ticket sales that Haney simply cannot generate as an A-side. Ryan knows who drove the commercial engine of their first fight, and he knows who held the psychological upper hand by the final bell. Demanding parity from a fighter who views himself as the sole economic driver of the promotion is an immediate non-starter.

Without third-party intervention, Ryan has zero incentive to capitulate. He holds the win that damaged Haney’s commercial aura, meaning Haney is the one chasing closure, redemption, and a career-defining check. Ryan can fight Rolly Romero, Conor Benn, Gervonta Davis, or even pursue exhibition routes and generate massive purses without ever having to accommodate the Haney camp’s contractual demands.

The single wildcard that alters the math is His Excellency Turki Alalshikh. Riyadh Season has repeatedly shown a willingness to distort traditional pay-per-view economics by simply overpaying both sides to eliminate negotiating hurdles. If Saudi backing arrives with an astronomical flat guarantee that makes Ryan indifferent to the split, the fight happens.

If the bout has to survive on standard domestic pay-per-view metrics, Haney’s 50-50 stance is a poison pill. Unless Haney swallows his pride and accepts the reality of being the B-side on the financial sheet, the rematch remains trapped behind a wall of commercial delusion.

Haney addressed the possibility of facing either man, attempting to maintain an air of indifference while clearly favoring the grudge match.

“If Ryan is victorious, still got to beat Teo … or even if Teo is victorious, it doesn’t matter. I would take either-or for undisputed,” Haney said. “But obviously I want Ryan Garcia to win so that I could right that wrong.”

Garcia wandering into exhibition talks with Floyd Mayweather illustrates the fundamental problem with Haney’s strategy. Garcia moves wherever the maximum money and spectacle lie. Haney, meanwhile, is betting his trajectory on the sanctioning bodies and conventional promotional pathways.

When asked about the Mayweather rumors, Haney took a reserved stance. He pointed out that Mayweather’s name routinely circulates around potential bouts that never reach the ring, treating the talk as typical posturing until contracts get signed.

The promotional terrain presents an even larger hurdle than fighter preferences. Haney points to his DAZN deal as the vehicle that will deliver these mega-fights, but DAZN does not control the entire board.

“Other people were offering me crazy money,” Haney said. “Of course, DAZN gave me a great deal, but most importantly, if you don’t have the opponents, how can I become a great in the sport?”

Cross-platform negotiations between competing networks and rival promoters routinely swallow undisputed fights whole. Landing belts at 147 might look clean on paper, but turning a regional fight in San Francisco into a massive multi-network blockbuster against Garcia requires solving promotional gridlock that sanctioning body hardware cannot fix on its own.

Sports.title: William Zepeda vs. Jadier Herrera Announcement Expected Soon From Golden Boy
Sports.content:
Jadier Herrera is set to challenge WBC lightweight champion William Zepeda after the WBC passed him over when the full title was vacant. The fight will settle who holds the WBC’s only belt at 135 pounds.

Golden Boy is expected to announce the bout soon, according to Darshan Desai. From a pure business perspective, taking on Jadier Herrera is a terrible risk-reward calculation for Zepeda. Herrera brings almost zero casual name recognition, practically no box office draw, and zero commercial upside. What he does bring is slick Cuban pedigree, southpaw counter-punching skills, and enough technical ability to make Zepeda look ordinary.

If Zepeda dominates him, casual fans will shrug and dismiss Herrera as an obscure mandatory. If Zepeda struggles or gets outboxed, his entire commercial standing evaporates overnight. Meanwhile, the alternative landscape offers massive paydays and legitimate star-making opportunities. A unification clash against WBO champion Abdullah Mason is by far the biggest pure boxing event at 135 pounds right now.

Mason carries immense promotional backing and serious buzz. Unifying the belts against him would instantly establish the winner as the true king of the lightweight division. An in-house Golden Boy matchup with Floyd Schofield delivers pure domestic pay-per-view numbers and massive promotional traction. Schofield talks, sells tickets, and brings a built-in fanbase that turns any clash into an event.

A blockbuster showdown against Gervonta Davis remains the ultimate lottery ticket in the weight class, offering career-defining money and mainstream reach. Compared to those blockbusters, defending the WBC belt against Herrera is pure sanctioning body tax. It does nothing for Zepeda’s bank account, nothing for his profile, and risks everything he built by winning the title from Roach.

The only reason Zepeda is entertaining it is that the WBC forced his hand with a mandatory order to clean up its interim title mess. Outside of keeping the green belt, the matchup is all downside.

Herrera has held the interim title since January, when he stopped Ricardo Núñez. That same month, Shakur Stevenson moved up to light welterweight and beat Teofimo Lopez. The WBC subsequently stripped Stevenson of its lightweight title, citing unpaid sanctioning fees.

The WBC could have elevated Herrera or put him in a fight for the vacant championship. Instead, it approved a deal the promoters had already put together for Zepeda to fight Lamont Roach Jr. The winner was expected to face Herrera, and Zepeda took the belt by unanimous decision on August 1.

Zepeda had a case for the opportunity. He had held the interim belt himself before losing to Stevenson, and both he and Roach were highly ranked. Their promoters also had a fight ready to go. The WBC could fill the vacancy by sanctioning a bout that had already been agreed, leaving Herrera to wait for the winner.

The wait cost Herrera a chance to be one of the two fighters chosen for the vacant title. When the belt opened up, the WBC could have made Zepeda or Roach fight Herrera to win it. Its decision gave Zepeda a chance to become champion before he had to face Herrera. The interim belt secured Herrera the next fight. A deal between two promoters secured the first one.

Sports.title: Ramon Cardenas Tests Junto Nakatani After Inoue Loss
Sports.content:
Ramon Cardenas provides an immediate measuring stick for Junto Nakatani following his first career defeat. The veteran counterpuncher possesses the exact timing required to test Nakatani’s willingness to commit after taking a solid hit.

Promoter Sampson Lewkowicz confirmed at the WBC convention that Cardenas reached a deal with Nakatani’s promoter, Akihiko Honda, via reporting from Darshan Desai of EverythingBoxing.

Cardenas proved his danger by dropping Naoya Inoue with a sharp counter left hook in the second round of their May 2025 meeting before Inoue halted him in the eighth. Facing a southpaw like Nakatani presents a distinct target profile.

The orthodox overhand right carries lethal potential, particularly because Nakatani tends to finish straight lefts in an upright stance and retreat along a direct line. That straight exit negates his reach advantage, leaving a clear path for Cardenas to press forward while Nakatani carries his guard low.

The technical tell will surface in subsequent exchanges. Nakatani must establish his right jab to unlock sustained punch combinations. That constant offensive pressure forces Cardenas into a shell, taking away his counter opportunities.

Firing isolated straight lefts gives Cardenas a predictable timing read on Nakatani’s backward retreat. Protracted lulls between combinations only grant Cardenas extra seconds to plant his feet and set traps.

Discipline inside the pocket will prove decisive. Absorbing a heavy punch requires Nakatani to tie up immediately. Pivoting out to open canvas gives him room to re-establish distance without trading out of pride. Firing back instantly without set feet hands Cardenas a clean opening to string punches together.

A wide points victory will not reveal the entire picture. The critical details lie in Nakatani’s punch selection the minute after Cardenas lands flush, alongside his defensive movement once combinations conclude. Those exact sequences will expose whether lingering hesitation from the Inoue loss remains.

Sports.title: Reynoso Lists Five Options for Canelo Alvarez in 2027
Sports.content:
Trainer Eddy Reynoso expects Canelo Alvarez to enter the ring two or three times in 2027, eyeing five distinct paths according to The Ring. The lineup features a super middleweight unification, a mandatory defense against Lester Martínez, a light heavyweight clash with Willy Hutchinson, and return bouts against Terence Crawford or Dmitry Bivol.

The Ring notes that no sequence is locked in. Four specific rivals are on the table, while the unification route hinges on which 168-pound titleholder agrees to terms. That gives Canelo two clear avenues for his WBC super middleweight belt: take on Martínez for the mandatory slot, or meet a rival champion to collect more gold.

That list of five narrows down fast once reality enters the room.

WBA champion Jaime Munguía makes zero promotional or competitive sense. Canelo already dropped and thoroughly handled him in 2024, and sharing gym space only solidifies that neither man is looking across the ring at the other. With Munguía struggling to look convincing against fringe opposition like Nikita Zon, nobody is opening their wallet to see that replay.

Osleys Iglesias, the IBF belt-holder at 168, is pure poison for an aging fighter. He is big, heavy-handed, fundamentally disciplined from the Cuban school, and operates out of a sharp southpaw stance. He gives away none of the physical advantages older counterpunchers rely on to slow down the pace. Putting Canelo in with a prime, hard-hitting super middleweight who can control range with a stiff southpaw stick is precisely the kind of voluntary hazard Reynoso routinely steers clear of.

WBC light heavyweight champion Willy Hutchinson represents another completely unnecessary headache up at 175. He brings awkward angles, relentless volume, legitimate reach, and the kind of high-octane engine that drains Canelo’s low-output, single-shot style. Canelo struggled with movement and pace at light heavyweight against Dmitry Bivol in the past, and Hutchinson has the motor to exploit those exact same stamina traps without offering the massive global brand name that justifies taking the beating.

Speaking of Bivol, that ship sailed the moment the cards were read in 2022. Canelo spent years tossing out casual remarks about rematches under impossible conditions, yet never actually pushed to get back in the ring with him. Bivol completely neutralized Canelo’s offense with a disciplined high guard, clean distance control, and piercing combinations. Revisiting that fight would simply be paying to re-watch a masterclass in how to dismantle Canelo’s flat-footed rhythm.

That leaves the two names that actually make sense for the business plan:

Crawford is the cash cow and the safest big-money avenue on the board. Even coming off a defeat, Canelo knows Crawford cannot hurt him with single-shot super middleweight power. Crawford will be 39, coming off a long, comfortable layoff on the heels of his biggest career win, and has shown zero appetite to sit in the pocket and trade heavy leather.

If Turki Alashikh puts up the bankroll, Canelo gets maximum financial reward with zero danger of taking a devastating beatdown. Turki is not blind to entertainment value. He wants explosive, fan-friendly wars. What Crawford and Canelo produced in September was essentially an expensive sparring session dressed up as history. Crawford boxed on his toes, kept his distance, tapped his way through exchanges, and collected the decision.

Even if Netflix reported huge raw viewer counts for the first encounter simply because subscribers could watch at no additional fee, streaming services track engagement drop-offs and social sentiment. Casual viewers complained about the lack of action, and nobody came away demanding a repeat. Shifting a second fight to standard pay-per-view could result in disastrous buy rates, while Netflix or any other platform would have a hard time justifying paying massive purses for another twelve rounds of cautious circling.

Lester Martínez is the exact type of mandatory Reynoso smiles at. He is straightforward, comes forward in predictable lines, lacks elite defensive nuance, and sits right in the pocket where Canelo can time his signature counter hooks without chasing anybody around the ring. It lets Canelo fulfill an obligation, keep a belt polished, and put on an explosive showcase for the cameras without taking real systemic punishment.

The five-man list is great for keeping headlines spinning, but Crawford for the check and Martínez for the routine defense are the only two realistic lanes on that drawing board.

Ghana News.title: Where will the money come from? MP questions 24-hour economy funding
Ghana News.content:
The proposed financing model for the government’s 24-hour economy programme could come under pressure in 2027 if revenue targets are not met, the MP for Manso Nkwanta, Tweneboa Kodua Fokuo, has warned.

He said the government’s plan to create fiscal space for the programme depended heavily on revenue expected to be generated in the future, rather than funds already available.

That, he said, raised questions about the sustainability of the initiative, particularly with the economy projected to grow at a slower rate in 2027.

Speaking on the PM Express on Joy News on Tuesday, November 10, ahead of the presentation of the 2027 Budget by the Finance Minister, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Mr Fokuo said the government could struggle to finance the programme if revenue mobilisation fell short of expectations.

“It's not as if we have the money at hand now. No, we don't have the money now,” he said.

He explained that the financing arrangement appeared to rely on a proposed adjustment to the primary surplus target from 1.5 per cent to 0.5 per cent, creating room in the budget for spending on the programme.

However, he cautioned that the anticipated fiscal space was dependent on revenue that the government was yet to collect.

Mr Fokuo said the projected slowdown in economic growth from 6.2 per cent in 2026 to 4.9 per cent in 2027 could further complicate revenue mobilisation and place the programme's funding under strain.

“If you look at revenue that has been generated this year, even when the economy is growing at 6.2 per cent, versus 2027 that we are projecting to slow down to 4.9, what it means is that we are likely to struggle in terms of revenue for 2027,” he said.

He consequently questioned where the resources to support the programme would come from if government revenue underperformed.

“If we do struggle for 2027, then you ask yourself where would the funding for the new economy really come from?” he asked.

Financing concerns

Mr Fokuo also questioned the earlier approach to financing the 24-hour economy, saying the private sector had failed to respond as expected because the programme was announced without adequate measures to manage the risks associated with participation.

He said the absence of a clear risk-management framework had weakened private-sector appetite for the initiative, leaving government to consider a financing arrangement that placed greater responsibility on the public purse.

“When the private sector did not jump on board as was expected, because it was just a slogan, it was just a pronouncement, but nothing was done to really manage the risks thereof, the private sector had no interest,” he said.

He described the current arrangement as a repackaging of the programme, with government funding expected to play a more prominent role.

The MP's comments come as attention turns to the 2027 Budget, which is expected to provide further details on the government's economic priorities, revenue projections and financing plans.

The budget will be closely watched for clarity on how the government intends to fund the 24-hour economy initiative, attract private investment and ensure that its commitments are supported by sustainable revenue sources.

Ghana News.title: Gates Foundation says AGRA’s revised transformation strategy is strengthening Africa’s food systems
Ghana News.content:
Director of Economic Opportunity for Africa at the Gates Foundation, Enock Chikava

The Gates Foundation says AGRA’s revised strategy for transforming Africa’s food systems, which prioritises country-level needs and better connects farmers to markets, is helping strengthen the agrifood sector.

Director of Economic Opportunity for Africa at the Gates Foundation, Enock Chikava, says over the past two decades, AGRA and its partners have helped build key components of the agricultural system that African farmers depend on to succeed.

“By supporting about 35,000 agro dealers and 118 African seed companies—helping bring more than 650 improved seed varieties to market—they have expanded the capacity to develop and supply seeds that can help farmers improve their harvests,” he observes.

Established in 2006 with former Ghanaian UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan as its first board chair, AGRA is a pan-African institution focused on scaling agricultural innovations that help small-scale farming enterprises increase incomes, improve livelihoods, and enhance food security.

In an article on the website of the Gates Foundation reflecting on AGRA’s work over the last 20 years, Mr Chikava notes that AGRA’s “investments in agricultural research, advisory services and access to inputs have also helped build the infrastructure farmers need to make better decisions, increase productivity and earn more from their land.”

“These are important foundations for a more productive and prosperous agricultural sector,” he said.

Mr Chikava observes that the challenges facing farmers across sub-Saharan Africa are immense, and no single organisation or approach can address them all.

Crop yields in sub-Saharan Africa are half those in India and one-fifth those in the United States, reflecting significant constraints on soil quality and productivity.

Climate-driven extreme weather, El Niño, conflict and fertiliser price shocks linked to the Iran crisis are adding further pressure. The Hormuz blockade alone disrupted around a third of global fertiliser exports. Scientific assessments also warn that a 2°C rise in global temperatures could reduce crop yields in sub-Saharan Africa by about 10 per cent, he said.

Missed goals and the future of African agriculture

The Gates Foundation official recalls that when AGRA was established in 2006, it set ambitious goals for 2020 such as doubling productivity and incomes for 20 million smallholder households and halving hunger and food insecurity across 20 countries.

“These goals were not met, and civil society organisations have urged accountability for this failure. We agree. As a longtime funder, we share responsibility. Hunger across Africa remains unacceptably high, and progress in agricultural productivity has not translated into the improved food security and farmer incomes that are needed.”

He, however, says the Foundation has continued to fund AGRA because of the change in strategy. “Following a 2022 evaluation that found mixed outcomes for farmers, AGRA adjusted its strategy. We continued investing because its new approach was more closely aligned with countries’ own priorities and placed greater emphasis on connecting farmers to finance and markets,” he said.

“But continued investment cannot mean business as usual. It must mean learning from what fell short, listening to farmers, governments, civil society, and critics, and being willing to change course. Our responsibility is not simply to stay committed to African agriculture, but to ensure our investments deliver better results for the farmers and families they are intended to serve. We remain committed to that work for the long haul.”

AGRA President Alice Ruhweza has previously assured that the institution continues to learn from previous experiences. “We have learned that distributing seeds and fertiliser, while necessary, was never going to be sufficient on its own.”

“The harder, longer work is in building systems that hold together under pressure: linking climate adaptation to market development, connecting public investment to private sector participation, and helping governments strengthen the institutions that turn strategies into results.”

Achieving ambitions will take time

Mr Chikava notes that although hunger has not declined and farmer incomes remain too low, since 2005, cereal yields across Africa have risen by about 40 per cent, and farm output has nearly doubled in real terms.

He says the realities of farming across sub-Saharan Africa are complex, and there is no single path to growth and prosperity. “Our foundation’s approach is to back governments’ own agricultural development plans and give farmers the options and support they need to increase productivity and grow their incomes.”

Mr Chikava assures that despite different perspectives on how best to advance African agriculture, the Gates Foundation shares important ambitions with other organisations and partners. These include reducing dependence on imported inputs, making African countries less vulnerable to global price shocks, and creating more prosperous farming communities.

“Achieving these ambitions will take time and sustained effort, particularly given the many pressures facing farmers. We welcome more partners, ideas and solutions, and take calls for greater accountability seriously,” he said.

“By working together, we can help farming families across Africa increase their incomes and build lasting prosperity,” Mr Chikava concluded.

Ghana News.title: Dangote Cement shelves London listing, blames market conditions for blow to LSE
Ghana News.content:
Nigeria's Dangote Cement postponed its plans for a secondary listing in London on Tuesday, citing deteriorating market conditions, in a setback for the UK bourse.

The decision came after market volatility following the US midterm elections, but the company may revisit the plan to list in London when conditions are more stable, a person with knowledge of the situation said.

Wall Street tumbled last week after the Democrats' midterm victory deepened investor concerns about whether the AI boom can last, with London's benchmark FTSE 100 index also ending the week lower.

Dangote Cement, which listed on the Nigerian stock market in 2010, said in May it ​was in early talks over a potential London listing, a move that would have widened its access to overseas investors and capital.

It has floated the idea of a London listing several times over 15 years, but global downturns and the COVID-19 pandemic have ​derailed its attempts. It is part of the sprawling business empire of Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote, who launched ​Africa's biggest share sale yet in September with the initial public offering of his oil refinery.

Dangote Cement's board of directors, which met ‌on ⁠Tuesday, made the decision not to proceed with the listing plans in light of current market conditions and the firm's strategic priorities, it said in a statement.

"These are pretty awful conditions for anyone to attempt an IPO," said Samuel Kerr, an analyst at M&A analytics platform Mergermarket, pointing to the recent rise in equity ​volatility.

"Dangote could probably do a ​deal now, but if ⁠it has the option of waiting for a better market, that would probably result in a better outcome and perhaps a higher valuation."

NO EFFECT ON BUSINESS ​PLANS

A growing number of companies have either abandoned the London bourse or been bought ​out by larger ⁠rivals or private equity firms, while the IPO market has remained subdued.

African mobile money service Airtel Money, which made its London debut last month, has largely traded around its IPO price of £1.96 ($2.64) a share since its listing.

The cement company, which has a market valuation of 24.79 trillion naira ($18.4 billion), said its shares remain listed on the Nigerian bourse and that the decision does not affect its operations or business plans.

Ghana News.title: Cedi strengthens on GoldBod’s boost to forex liquidity; going for GH¢12.15 against a dollar at forex bureaus
Ghana News.content:
Cedi and dollar

The Ghana cedi strengthened against the US dollar over the past two weeks, following Goldbod’s support for the foreign exchange market.

The local currency clawed back gains on sustained forex supply from GoldBod’s spot auctions.

It improved modestly in the interbank market while remaining relatively stable in the retail market.

In the interbank market, the cedi appreciated by 0.09%, 0.14% and 0.50% against the US dollar, the pound sterling and the euro. It traded at GH¢11.64 against the US dollar, GH¢15.55 against the pound and GH¢12.98 against the euro, respectively.

In the retail market, the dollar and euro exchange rates remained unchanged at GH¢12.08 and GH¢ 13.60. However, it depreciated against the pound by 0.63% to GH¢16.00the dollar.

On a month-on-month basis, the cedi’s year-to-date depreciation narrowed by 0.69 percentage points to 10.07% at the end of October 2026, down from 10.76% in September 2026.

“We believe October’s US$1.011 billion intermediation, offered at a uniform market-clearing rate, significantly anchored demand expectations and guided market pricing”, said Databank Research.

“Looking ahead, our forecast points to a modest appreciation toward GH¢11.41 to a dollar by the end of the next fortnight, despite impending seasonal import demand pressures. With US$800 million earmarked for commercial bank auctions from a US$1.2 billion November 2026 gross intermediation, we expect sustained dollar liquidity to support near-term exchange rate stability”, it added.

Meanwhile, the cedi began the week going for GH¢12.15 against the US dollar at the forex bureaus.

Ghana News.title: Nigeria approves 145 new oil wells so far this year, regulator says
Ghana News.content:
Nigeria's upstream oil regulator has approved ​145 new well-drilling operations, 595 well re-entries and ‌39 field development plans (FDPs) so far this year as it seeks to boost crude output, attract investment and strengthen ​energy security, a senior official said on ​Tuesday.

The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) said ⁠the approvals reflected faster regulatory processing that has ​reduced project delays and costs for operators

"Year to date, ​about 39 FDPs have been approved. About 145 new well-drilling approvals granted. Year to date, about 595 well re-entry approvals ​were granted," NUPRC Chief Executive Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan said ​at an oil conference in Lagos

Eyesan, represented by Ahmad Abdullahi, ‌deputy ⁠director of basin administration, said faster approvals were helping operators advance projects needed to meet production targets and support energy availability

She said Nigeria had more ​than 100 drilling ​rigs, with ⁠46 active this year, up more than 300% from 2021 levels

Eyesan also said ​seismic companies had invested more than $100 ​million ⁠in Nigeria since the Petroleum Industry Act came into force three years ago, improving exploration data and supporting ⁠efforts ​to discover new oil and ​gas reserves

The regulator is also working to curb crude theft across ​the country

Ghana News.title: Congo’s Ebola cases surpass 11,000, government data show
Ghana News.content:
The number of confirmed Ebola cases in ​the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed ‌11,000, government data showed on Tuesday.

Confirmed infections now total 11,042, and 5,387 people have died, ​the data showed

The outbreak, caused ​by the rare Bundibugyo species of the ⁠Ebola virus, was declared in mid-May. ​There are no approved treatments or vaccines ​for this species

It is the second-largest and deadliest outbreak on record behind only the 2014-2016 West ​African outbreak, which infected more than ​28,600 people and killed more than 11,000

Eight of ‌Congo's ⁠26 provinces have been affected, and many deaths have occurred outside treatment centres

Delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have ​led to ​a more ⁠rapid spread of the virus than in previous outbreaks

The disease ​has now been reported in East, ​Central ⁠and West Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the ⁠continent ​to date

Ghana News.title: ‘New economy is repackaged 24-hour economy’ – Manso Nkwanta MP
Ghana News.content:
MP for Manso Nkwanta, Tweneboa Kodua Fokuo

The proposed “new economy” being advanced by the government is largely a rebranding of the 24-hour economy policy, with the key difference being a shift towards public financing after efforts to attract private sector investment failed, the MP for Manso Nkwanta, Tweneboa Kodua Fokuo, has said.

He argued that the economic pillars underpinning the two initiatives were essentially the same, particularly their emphasis on export expansion, import substitution and accelerated national development.

Mr Fokuo, who is the Deputy Ranking Member of Parliament’s Economy and Development Committee, said the government appeared to be presenting the 24-hour economy agenda in a different form, with public funds now expected to play a more prominent role in its implementation.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, November 10, ahead of the presentation of the 2027 Budget by the Finance Minister, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, he questioned whether the proposed new economic direction represented a fundamental departure from the earlier policy.

“If you look at what is being described as a new economy, in reality, it is not different from the 24-hour economy,” he said.

He explained that the 24-hour economy, particularly its expanded “24-hour economy plus” component, had also been designed to accelerate development through increased exports and the replacement of imported goods with locally produced alternatives.

According to him, the pillars now being associated with the new economy closely mirror those previously outlined under the 24-hour economy programme.

The MP said a major challenge with the earlier initiative was its reliance on private sector financing, which, in his assessment, failed to attract the level of interest required to make the programme successful.

“It does seem that the 24-hour economy was positioned as a programme that would be financed by the private sector, and that could not materialise. The private sector had no appetite at all for the 24-hour economy programme,” he said.

Mr Fokuo argued that the government's current approach appeared to be a re-presentation of the same policy, but with public financing taking centre stage.

He said the forthcoming 2027 Budget would provide an opportunity to examine the government's proposed economic direction, including how it intended to finance its programmes and translate its policy ambitions into measurable outcomes.

The Finance Minister is expected to present the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy to Parliament, setting out the government's spending priorities, revenue measures and economic plans for the coming year.

Ghana News.title: Oil rises from two-month low as Hormuz shipping attacks offset Iran truce hopes
Ghana News.content:
Oil prices rose on Wednesday after falling to two-month lows in the previous session, as the market swung between hopes for a de-escalation in the Iran ​war and concerns about ongoing attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent ‌futures climbed 71 cents, or 0.78%, to $92.20 a barrel by 0119 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 49 cents, or 0.57%, to $86.53.

New data showed that 37 ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and ​surrounding waterways in October, the highest monthly total since the start of the war, ​according to the Washington Institute for Near East Policy. And 10 attacks ⁠have been recorded so far in November.

Videos posted on social media on Sunday and verified ​by Reuters showed a Navig8 tanker on fire near the coast of Oman, one of three ​tankers hit on Sunday for using "unauthorised routes" through the strait, according to the Iranian state broadcaster.

Another tanker was struck northeast of Oman's Lima, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said on Tuesday. Iran's Revolutionary ​Guards Navy said in a separate statement on Tuesday that two tankers caught fire after ​hitting naval mines on the "unauthorised route" in the strait.

"Even in the event a deal is struck, an increase ‌in ⁠flows through the waterway would still depend on mine clearance, insurance costs and whether or not shipowners would even be willing to take the risk," LSEG analysts said in a November 10 note. "Meanwhile, attacks have not slowed."

In the previous session, oil prices initially fell by more than $3 a barrel after US officials downplayed the need for further military strikes against Iran, but then regained some of those losses after an Iranian security official said no talks were taking place between the two sides.

US crude oil stocks rose in the latest week, market ​sources said, ⁠citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude stocks rose by 9 million barrels in the week ended November 6, the sources said.

In Russia, oil refining capacity has been reduced by about 30% since ⁠late ​October following renewed Ukrainian drone attacks, industry sources said.

Russian and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first peace talks since February, as US President Donald Trump's envoys launched a fresh push to end the war.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Kennedy family joins US lawsuits to block Trump’s ‘unlawful’ arch plan
World.content:
Kennedy dynasty has filed a motion to stop Trump’s arch from obscuring JFK Eternal Flame and slain family gravesites.

Members of the prominent Kennedy family have filed a legal motion to halt the construction of US President Donald Trump’s 76-metre (250ft) “triumphal arch” in Washington, DC, arguing it mars the area near the graves of the family’s famous forebears.

On Tuesday, the nine plaintiffs, children and grandchildren of former Senators Robert F Kennedy and Edward M Kennedy, filed a motion to intervene and an accompanying complaint in two existing federal lawsuits to block the arch’s construction.

The project would sit near the final resting places of the late senators, buried alongside their brother, former President John F Kennedy, and the Eternal Flame commemorating him at Arlington National Cemetery.

Plaintiffs argued the proposed arch would “fundamentally alter the experience of visiting the gravesites”, a site that draws millions of visitors each year.

The intervention motion was filed by veteran Washington lawyer Norm Eisen and Democracy Defenders Fund, a centre-left legal advocacy group.

It contends that the National Park Service and the Department of the Interior authorised the granite, gold-ornamented structure, dubbed the “Arc de Trump” by critics, without required congressional approval.

The plaintiffs also argue the megastructure would destroy the intentionally designed, century-old line of sight between the Lincoln Memorial and the cemetery’s Arlington House across the Memorial Bridge.

Many plaintiffs

The high-profile intervention adds to an already sprawling roster of plaintiffs who have launched legal challenges against the polarising monument, including Vietnam War veterans, a historian, and the governments of the District of Columbia, Virginia and Arlington County.



Last week, District Judge Tanya Chutkan prohibited the Trump administration from breaking ground on the structure for another 14 days following the string of lawsuits.

Building the arch would be a “permanent denigration” of the gravesites, and the Kennedy offspring “would never again be able to appreciate both sites as they always have before, and as the Kennedy family always intended”, lawyers for the relatives wrote on Tuesday.

The project is just one component of the president’s effort to remodel much of Washington, DC, alongside a historic golf course renovation and threats to demolish the Kennedy Center.

But with Democrats seizing control of Congress in last week’s midterm elections, the overhauls may be set for heightened scrutiny.

Speaking on behalf of the Kennedy family, Rory and Maxwell Kennedy, children of the late senator Robert F Kennedy, said the action is about “protecting sacred spaces that belong to the American people”. They said several members of their slain family are “among the more than 400,000 veterans and family members buried or honored on this hallowed ground”.

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr, a Trump appointee who is estranged from much of his family, did not join the litigation.

World.title: GOP-led House report slams systemic failures in handling of Epstein case
World.content:
Congressional Republicans are pressing for renewed investigations into sex crimes cases involving disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein and accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell, accusing authorities of mishandling the case for decades.

The US House of Representatives Committee on Oversight and Government Reform on Tuesday released a new 137-page report marking the most comprehensive investigation yet by lawmakers into the federal government’s handling of the Epstein saga.

The findings condemned federal investigators and prosecutors in South Florida and Washington for alleged negligence, which the committee said allowed the late sex offender’s abuse to go unchecked as far back as 2005, when Epstein’s crimes first came to light in Palm Beach, Florida.

“What we found was both heartbreaking and infuriating,” Republican Representative James Comer of Kentucky, who chairs the committee, said in a video address.

“These women endured unimaginable abuse, and the federal government failed them at nearly every turn,” he added. “Had the government done its job, much of this abuse could have been prevented.”

The committee, which currently holds a Republican majority, is the House’s main investigative panel and has the power to subpoena witnesses and documents.

Democrats will take control of the chamber in January after a historic victory in the November 3 midterm elections, and California Representative Robert Garcia, the committee’s top Democrat, formally announced his bid to chair it in a letter to colleagues on Thursday.



Potential conflicts of interest

The latest findings cap a 15-month Republican-led congressional inquiry that involved 19 transcribed interviews and depositions, subpoenas to federal agencies, financial institutions and Epstein’s estate, and an extensive review of financial records.

Its conclusions asserted that a combination of bureaucratic indifference, missed warnings and compromised plea deals consistently shielded Epstein and his associates while denying justice to their victims.

In one such instance, GOP lawmakers sharply rebuked a controversial 2007 non-prosecution agreement in South Florida that effectively shelved Epstein’s federal case after he pleaded guilty to lesser state offences.
