The reports also expressed concern over carbon markets and offsetting schemes, which allow polluters to compensate for emissions through projects elsewhere, including commercial plantations and forestry initiatives.



The organisations warned that such arrangements could shift responsibility from major polluters to communities whose lands and natural resources are used for carbon projects.



Uganda’s climate plan, for instance, assigns significantly greater projected emissions reductions to commercial plantations than to its two natural-forest restoration measures.

The report also cited documented forced evictions associated with a forestry and carbon-credit project in Kachung, Uganda, as an example of the dangers of climate interventions that fail to protect community rights.



Contributing partners from the five-country study also called for greater accountability and community participation.

Also, the Founder and Chief Executive of Yielding Intersectional Movements in South Africa, Ndivile Mokoena said: “The persistent gap between global climate commitments and local realities raises critical questions about political will and economic systems that continue to prioritise profit and growth over human well-being and ecological sustainability. This report underscores the urgent need to move beyond promises to tangible implementation, adequate climate financing, and meaningful support for developing countries.”



Also, the Executive Director of Nia Environment & Zero Carbon Alliance in Uganda Acola Amina said: “Achieving a rights-based, ecofeminist climate agenda that reflects Uganda’s realities and responds to the needs of affected communities requires inclusive participation and collective commitment.”



The Executive Director of Centre pour la Justice Environnementale in Togo, Kwami Kpondzo said: “Carbon markets and geoengineering are not solutions to the climate crisis. Rather, they are dangerous distractions that risk worsening the plight of vulnerable communities, threatening livelihoods, and undermining genuine climate action. We must put people and the planet before profit. Nature is not a commodity for sale, and we remain steadfast in our commitment to defending it.”



Oluwafemi further said: “The Nigeria Energy Transition Plan and the Five-Country NDCs Reports offer an opportunity to rethink how energy policies and climate commitments serve people and communities. These reports emphasise that equity, transparency and accountability must remain central in every plan, while ensuring that affected communities have a meaningful voice in decisions that shape their future.”



The organisations called on African delegates attending the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, COP31, in Antalya, Türkiye, to reject carbon offsetting as a substitute for actual emissions reductions and oppose arrangements that allow continued fossil fuel pollution to be balanced against temporary carbon storage.



They also demanded a planned and funded phase-down of fossil fuel extraction, substantial public investment in decentralised renewable energy, affordable electricity and legally binding protections for workers and affected communities.



Other demands include grant-based climate financing from historically high-emitting countries, legal protection for communal land, transparent climate budgets and binding safeguards against corporate influence in national climate policy decisions.

The organisations insisted that Indigenous Peoples, smallholder farmers, rural women and frontline communities must have enforceable rights to reject projects that threaten their lands, livelihoods and access to natural resources.



Their intervention comes amid growing concerns over the widening gap between global climate commitments and actual emissions reductions.



The United Nations Environment Programme’s latest Emissions Gap Report projects that current policies could lead to 2.8 degrees Celsius of warming this century, while full implementation of national climate pledges could still result in 2.6 degrees Celsius.

World.title: Agbazuere backs Otti’s second-term bid after U-turn
World.content:
Dismisses alleged anti-Ngwa remark, cautions critics

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA—Former Chief of Staff to ex-Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, Prof. ACB Agbazuere, who was a vocal critic of Governor Alex Otti during the 2019 governorship election, has declared support for the governor’s re-election bid, saying he deserves a second term.

Agbazuere, now a member of Otti’s Campaign Advisory Council, also dismissed an allegation attributed to former Commissioner, Chief Charles Ogbonnaya, that the governor allegedly described Ngwa people as brainless, describing the claim as unfounded and politically motivated.

Speaking during a radio interview simulcast across several stations in Abia on Tuesday, Agbazuere cautioned politicians against making unsubstantiated allegations, warning that defamatory statements could attract legal consequences under Nigerian laws, including the Cybercrimes Act.

He said the allegation would not undermine Otti’s support base, particularly among the Ngwa people.

“Dr Alex Otti may love peace; Dr Alex Otti may not want trouble, but they should see that people like us are now with him. Anybody who wants to say anything should be careful and say what he knows to be true,” he warned.

Explaining his support for the governor, Agbazuere said the Otti administration had demonstrated commitment to infrastructure development, urban renewal, workers’ welfare and good governance.

He cited the reconstruction of Port Harcourt Road and Bank Road in Aba, the Omenuko Bridge and Arochukwu Road as evidence of the administration’s infrastructure drive.

He also commended the governor for what he described as regular payment of salaries, pensions and gratuities, as well as improvements in allowances for traditional rulers.

On criticisms that increased federal allocations should have translated into more development projects, Agbazuere argued that the rising cost of construction materials must be considered.

He cited the increase in the price of cement from about ₦2,000 to ₦12,000 per bag as an example of the inflationary pressures facing construction projects.

He challenged critics to visit the state and assess ongoing projects rather than evaluate the administration from a distance.

Describing Otti as a banker and trained economist, Agbazuere said the governor understood accountability and prudent management of public resources.

He urged Abians to look beyond party affiliations and support continuity, arguing that a second term would enable Otti to complete ongoing projects and consolidate his administration’s programmes.

He also recalled that during the 2023 governorship election, a leading opposition candidate had reportedly acknowledged Otti as the best candidate.

Vanguard reports that Agbazuere, a former Commissioner for Information, was previously among Otti’s vocal critics but has recently switched allegiance after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC), where he briefly sought political shelter shortly after Otti assumed office in 2023.

Agbazuere hails from Isiala Ngwa South Local Government Area, the same local government area as Governor Otti.

World.title: 2027: Lagos traders pray for Tinubu, Hamzat’s victory
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

Market leaders and traders across Lagos State have offered special prayers for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in the state, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, seeking their victory in the 2027 general elections.

The prayer session, organised by the Lagos State Market Advisory Council (LASMAC) in collaboration with the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy Affairs and Rural Development, was held on Tuesday at the Blue Roof Pavilion, Agidingbi, Ikeja.

The gathering brought together market leaders, traders, religious and traditional leaders, as well as government officials, who prayed for the success of APC candidates and the continued development of Lagos State and Nigeria.

Hamzat, who was represented by the Commissioner for Wealth Creation and Employment, Akinyemi Ajigbotafe, thanked the market leaders for the initiative, describing their prayers and show of support as a demonstration of their commitment to the progress of the state and the country.

He particularly commended the Iyaloja-General of Nigeria and Chairman of LASMAC, Chief Folashade Tinubu-Ojo, for her leadership and efforts in mobilising market stakeholders for the prayer session.

Hamzat urged traders to sustain their partnership with the government, promising that, if elected, his administration would strengthen engagement with the market community and ensure their interests were adequately represented in governance.

“I urge you to sustain your partnership with government. If elected, our administration will strengthen engagement with the market community and ensure your interests are adequately represented in governance,” he said.

He said the commitment was reflected in the inclusion pillar of his manifesto, The Lagos Promise, unveiled on October 30, 2026, adding that his proposed administration would build on the achievements of Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu.

According to Hamzat, markets and their leaders remain indispensable to Lagos’ economic growth and development, stressing that their contributions and concerns would continue to receive attention.

He also appreciated religious and traditional leaders for their spiritual support, assuring residents of his commitment to sustaining development, consolidating existing achievements and extending the benefits of governance to all segments of society.

Earlier, the Special Adviser to the Governor on Rural Development, Nurudeen Agbaje, described the gathering as timely, noting that market leaders remained important to the political and economic development of the state.

Agbaje also commended the Lagos State Government for its development initiatives and urged stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the government.

In her remarks, Tinubu-Ojo said the meeting was convened to deliberate on the forthcoming elections and strengthen cooperation among market leaders.

She reiterated the commitment of the market community to bloc voting, while urging the government to provide market leaders with the necessary opportunities and support to mobilise their members and fulfil their commitments.

The gathering ended with prayers by religious leaders for Tinubu, Hamzat and other APC candidates participating in the 2027 elections.

World.title: How AI is helping Nigerian farmers tackle crop diseases, improve farm decisions
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Cynthia Alo

With many Nigerian farmers still relying on traditional knowledge to identify crop diseases and determine appropriate treatments, delayed access to agricultural advice often means problems are left unresolved until they affect yields.



In some cases, farmers have to wait days for agronomists to visit their farms and recommend solutions.



CropCura, a digital agricultural innovation co-founded by Victor Onyekachukwu, is seeking to change this practice by bringing crop diagnosis and farm advisory services directly to farmers through technology.



Onyekachukwu said the application allows farmers to take pictures of affected crops and receive an AI-powered analysis and recommendations on possible solutions in less than a minute.



Apart from crop diagnosis, the platform provides weather information, an AI advisory service and digital farm mapping which allow farmers to access information needed to make decisions about their farms.



He said the innovation also addresses another longstanding challenge in Nigerian agriculture which is farmers’ difficulty accessing formal credit because of inadequate records.



Through digital farm profiles containing information about farmers, their locations, crops and farm sizes, Onyekachukwu said the technology will also combine a credit-scoring system that can help financial institutions assess farmers for lending.



The platform, he said, currently has more than 2,000 farmers, who have mapped over 10,000 hectares of farmland.



However, Onyekachukwu identified language barriers, limited smartphone access, low digital literacy and farmers’ distrust of technology as obstacles to wider adoption.



He said the government should introduce policies recognising verified digital farm profiles as acceptable evidence for accessing agricultural loans and grants.

World.title: Research-policy disconnect undermines agric interventions — Experts
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Cynthia Alo

Agricultural experts have attributed the disconnect between farmers, researchers and policymakers as a major factor undermining the effectiveness of agricultural policies and interventions.



This is even as they called for greater farmer participation in research design and policy formulation.



According to them, research priorities were often determined without adequate consideration of farmers’ immediate needs, while policy implementation was constrained by funding limitations, institutional bottlenecks and poor communication of research findings.



The experts spoke during the virtual inaugural episode of the Agricultural Policy Circle, organised by Farmosphere, with the theme, “Finding the Gap where Research, Policy, and Practice disconnect.”



Agriculture researcher, Ifunanya Orisekeh,said research questions were sometimes determined before researchers reached farming communities, leaving farmers to respond to problems that might not reflect their immediate realities.



She said research agendas were often shaped by funding calls, academic requirements and institutional timelines, while the time required to generate findings further widened the gap between research and practice.



She said: “Research agendas are shaped before a funding call comes up. For example, if there is a project that needs a student already set, by the time you reach the field, the question is already printed and the farmer is there to answer your question.



“So we can become very good in the research perspective. We are very good at answering questions that farmers have never asked.”



Orisekeh said research could take three to four years to produce findings, by which time the conditions confronting farmers might have changed.



She also questioned the practice of measuring project success by the number of farmers trained without establishing whether they continued using the recommended practices after project support ended.



Using conservation agriculture as an example, she said, “It is widely promoted and many farmers have widely dropped it as well once the project and even the report is over.”



She identified the mismatch between research schedules and farming seasons, inadequate representation of different categories of farmers and failure to return research findings to communities as other weaknesses.



Also speaking, Founder of AgricIncome Hub and Chief Executive Officer of Maxipharo Farms, Olaoluwa Farotimi, identified inadequate access to credit, unstable markets, poor extension services, logistics challenges and climate-related risks as major constraints confronting farmers.



He said agricultural financing often failed to reflect production cycles, while farmers had little control over market prices and could suffer losses from sudden policy changes.

He said: “There is no access to credit for farmers. For example, you have a production cycle of two months or a month, and you have to pay back in six months while your crop is still in the field’’.

Speaking from the policy perspective, Dr. Gideon Tups, an Economic Geography expert and Agricultural Policy and Global Bioeconomy specialist, said money and power are major constraints to translating research evidence into agricultural transformation.

Tups, a former Policy Adviser for Food Systems Transformation at GIZ, said governments needed to prioritise investments that delivered economic, environmental and social benefits, while recognising that agricultural transformation could face resistance from farmers, businesses and political interests.

World.title: COCEFAAA appoints new directors to strengthen cocoa, coffee farmers’ interests
World.content:
By Kafayat Kokumo

The Cocoa and Coffee Farmers Alliance Association of Africa (COCEFAAA) has appointed some stakeholders to its Board of Directors and country leadership positions to strengthen the representation and protection of cocoa and coffee farmers across West, East and Central Africa.



In a statement made available to Vanguard AgroBiz, Global President of the association, Comrade Adeola Adegoke, announced that the appointments include two Board Members, three Country Directors and two Deputy Country Directors, with representatives from Ethiopia, Kenya, Sierra Leone, Ghana and Cameroon.



The new appointees are Dr Liliane Kabondo Mbazumutima, a global public health leader, and Mr Raymond Katta, Executive Chairman of the Sierra Leone Produce Monitoring Board, both appointed as Board Members.



Others are Mr Abel Ayele Bunaro, Founder and Managing Director of BunAroma Specialty Coffee, appointed Country Director for Ethiopia; Mr Jack Ndirangu, Chairman of Kahiraini Coffee Factory, as Country Director for Kenya; and Mr Didan Sankoh, Director of Operations and Programmes at the Sierra Leone Produce Monitoring Board, as Country Director for Sierra Leone.



The association also appointed Mr James Kwarteng, Co-founder of Apocco Farms Limited, as Deputy Country Director for Ghana, while Prince Mahamadou Mamouda Almed, President of the Meme Cocoa Buyers Association (MECOBA), was named Deputy Country Director for Cameroon.



Commenting on the development, Adegoke said they were intended to reinforce the association’s commitment to protecting the rights and interests of cocoa and coffee producers across the continent.



He said: “This is to reinforce the commitment of the organisation to protect the rights and interests of our producers in cocoa and coffee sectors across the West, East and Central Africa in order to optimise their productivity, build sustainability in their activities, guarantee quality assurance, ensure their resilience and expand their incomes through fair pricing.”

World.title: Tinubu: I’ll Subsidise Farming, Not Fuel; Atiku, Obi Lying About Returning Subsidy
World.content:
• Says NELFUND is weapon against poverty

•North-west has rejected opposition’s claim that Tinubu is unwelcome in north, says Yari

Deji Elumoye, Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and Ibrahim Shuaibu in Dutse





President Bola Tinubu has declared that fuel subsidy would never return, dismissing those promising its restoration as liars.

Tinubu, however, stated that his government would subsidise farming and not fuel consumption.

Speaking at a rally in Jigawa State, yesterday, Tinubu said Nigeria could not continue to spend the future of its children to sustain a system that had become a national economic drain.

Director-General of All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC), Senator Abdul-Aziz Yari, told the campaign that the massive turnout for Tinubu in the North-west state had exposed the lie in the opposition’s claim that the president would not be welcomed in northern Nigeria.

The president declared at the rally, “To those who say subsidy is coming back, it’s a lie. Don’t let them lie to you again. It’s not going to come back. We cannot spend the future of our children today and feel that they will go tomorrow.

“Those who think they should bring subsidy back, they are liars. How will you pay for those commitments? How will you repair the roads? How will you maintain them? How will you function?

“We will subsidise farming. We will reward small scale farmers. Interest-free loan for farmers is coming. Prosperity is coming. Food security will happen.

“I hope you hear me, Nigeria. You hear me, Nigeria. There will be interest-free loan for small scale farmers. We are going to install mechanised farming service centre in six geographical locations. Mechanised farming.

“We have the arable land, we have the commitment, we have the people. We can feed ourselves and we will bring the food prices down to the minimum. I promise you on agriculture, mechanisation, irrigation and additional value for land, arable land.”

Tinubu said universities would be more involved in agricultural research and development than ever before.

He thanked the people for their loyalty and commitment, while promising to address the problem of insecurity head-on.

“I have heard you loud and clear,” he declared.

Tinubu added, “I know you have problems of insecurity in Nigeria. But working together, as your friend and partner, exchange information, anything you know about insecurity, report it immediately.

“I promise you, we are working hard to ensure that Nigeria is safe and our forces are well taken care of, housing, reward, regardless of where they come from. We will conquer insecurity.

“We have been through many wars. We will defeat our enemies. Enemies of unity, enemies of stability, enemies of all.”

The president stated that his government had strengthened the police and the armed forces and was paying better salaries today.

He described the student loan scheme, Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), as a weapon against poverty.

According to him, “We are taking away the problem of the education of their children by establishing the NELFUND. NELFUND is a weapon against poverty. Are you with me? NELFUND is a weapon against poverty. And we will continue in that direction.”

He announced that every money recovered from irregularities through the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was directed to NELFUND to educate the children, and every asset recovered would be invested in NELFUND.

Tinubu commended Jigawa State Governor, Umar Namadi, saying he has never seen so much progress made by one man.

He stated, “I have been here a number of years. I have never seen so much progress being made by one man. That is Governor Umar Namadi. He has worked so tirelessly and hard for all of us to benefit from the benefits of democracy.”

He urged the Jigawa electorate to re-elect Namadi for a second term.

Tinubu announced a major new support for farmers, declaring that the government would subsidise farming, not fuel consumption. He assured them that his government would invest in medical stability and opportunity in every local government.

He stated that he would lower the cost of living for security and provide reliable power, saying, “not the old privatisation that is not working. We will provide you with reliable power in (every part of) Nigeria”.

The president acknowledged the security challenges confronting the country and urged Nigerians to support security agencies by reporting suspicious movements and activities in their communities.

“I know we have the problem of insecurity, but see your neighbour as a friend and report any suspicious activities,” he said.

He pledged that his administration would intensify efforts to defeat insecurity through improved security infrastructure and better welfare packages for personnel of the police and armed forces.

The president said, “We will conquer insecurity and defeat our enemies. We are working to strengthen the police and the military with better salaries. We cannot mortgage the future of our children for today’s challenges.”

For his part, Yari said the massive turnout at the rally exploded the opposition’s claim that Tinubu would not be welcomed in northern Nigeria.

Yari told the president that the crowd before him was proof that the North-west stood with him.

He stated, “Your Excellency, Mr. President, these are your people, men and women and youths. This is North-west, where our opponents are campaigning that you are not going to be welcomed in the northern Nigeria.”

Yari stressed that the opponents had nothing to offer beyond what Tinubu had done for Nigeria, both as governor and as President, and what he had done for the north.

He said, “They have nothing to offer more than what you are doing for Nigeria, more than what you have done, when you were governor, and what you have done for this part of the country.”

Yari challenged those who called themselves core northerners to point to any candidate they had supported to victory.

He stated, referring to Tinubu’s strategic support for past northern leaders, “I will not repeat myself. I have said time and time again, those that you supported in northern Nigeria, the foundation you laid, supporting 1, 2, 3 in the northern Nigeria, I challenge those that are calling themselves core northerners whether they have supported a councillor and won an election, or supported a local government chairman win an election, or supported any governor win an election.

“But our candidate, our president, supported them and supported a person who became a president for the first time or the second time without choosing himself.”

World.title: APC-PCC Unveils 2027 Manifesto, Says No Nigerian Leader Matches Tinubu Since 1960
World.content:
• Boasts president has undertaken more comprehensive and massive structural reforms

• Hold us to account, Gbajabiamila tells Nigerians

• First Lady inaugurates new Lagos lodge in Abuja

Deji Elumoye, Olawale Ajimotokan and Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja





All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC), yesterday, unveiled President Bola Tinubu’s manifesto for the 2027 election, saying no Nigerian leader since 1960 has embarked on massive, comprehensive, structural reforms spanning all strata of society across all sectors. Spokesperson of the council, Dele Alake, disclosed this in Abuja during a media pre-sensitisation ahead of the launch of the APC manifesto for the 2027 presidential election, with the theme, “Translating Reforms into Shared Prosperity.”

Alake stated, “If you recall, in the last three and a half years, the party has been striving very strenuously to embark on reforms — reforms that are very unprecedented in the annals of Nigeria.

“And I stand to be controverted. I challenge anybody to a public debate on this. Since 1960, I’m a chronicler of history in a hurry. Since 1960 till date, or let me say till 2023, no civilian administration in this country had embarked on the massive, comprehensive, purposive structural reforms spanning all strata of society across all sectors and touching every end of society like the Tinubu government that we have in place.

“None, and if there is any, point it out to me, and I challenge you to a public debate. And I say this with a sense of conviction, not because I’m a part of that government, or not because I’m a member of the political party. I’m a participant observer because I’m participating in the government. But as a journalist, I’m also an observer, so I’m a participant observer.”

Alake emphasised that the manifesto was a reflection of three and a half years of difficult reforms that had delivered macroeconomic stability.

He stressed that the title of the manifesto captured what the administration had been doing since coming into office — putting in place reforms, executing projects, and policies that had culminated in stabilising the economy.

He maintained that no other leader in Nigeria’s history had looked at the country’s structural economic problems and decided to confront them head-on, regardless of political consequences.

Alake stated that Tinubu did not behave like a typical politician, who was thinking about the next election, but decided to address the structural deficiency of the country without minding the consequences.

He said, “No other leader in the history of this country has looked at the structural problems, structural economic problems of this country, and decided to take the bull by the horns and confront those problems head on, regardless of its political consequences, regardless of even the leader’s own political situation and aspiration, and that is the nuance that Bola Ahmed Tinubu is made of.”

Describing Tinubu as a statesman, and not an ordinary politician, Alake said, “He does not think of himself; he thinks of the nation, and that’s what a statesman should do.

“Ordinary politicians will think of the next election and avoid contentious policies that probably could (harm) their political aspirations, but not President Bola Ahmed Tinubu because he puts the nation ahead of self.”

Chief of Staff to the President, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, said the APC manifesto for the years ahead was not a campaign document, but an inviolable contract between the people and their leaders.

Gbajabiamila pointed out that at the heart of the document was the conviction that every Nigerian should share in the country’s prosperity.

He stated, “A manifesto, in its strictest sense, is simply a contract between the people and their leaders. It is an inviolable contract, and we take the strict interpretation of what a manifesto represents as gospel under this administration. Your country should give your best efforts a fair chance.”

He said Nigerians already worked hard — rising early, travelling long distances and making sacrifices so their children could go further than they did.

According to him, “A nation worthy of such efforts must make it possible for honest work to produce a decent life.”

The chief of staff defined a Nigeria that worked for everyone as one where parents could meet their families’ needs and still save for tomorrow, and where a young person could expect that ability and effort will open doors.

He added, “Belonging to Nigeria should carry real value in your daily life. You should be able to access public services without begging for favours.

“A public hospital, for instance, should never need to know which political party you voted for before treating you. These are the expectations by which this manifesto asks to be judged.”

Gbajabiamila recalled that in 2023, Tinubu took responsibility for a country facing problems that could no longer be deferred, confronting the subsidy burden and a distorted foreign exchange system, admitting also that the decisions had placed real pressure on households.

He said, “Those decisions have now placed real pressure on households. We must speak honestly about that experience because the people living through it deserve to be heard. Nobody should have to pretend that life is easy at the moment.”

He, however, stressed that leaving those problems untouched would have continued to weaken Nigeria’s ability to invest in the future.

Gbajabiamila stated, “The president had a choice to govern as a politician or as a leader. The difference between a politician and a leader is that while a politician thinks about the next election, a leader thinks about the next generation. And that is exactly what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has demonstrated.”

The chief of staff listed early gains from the reforms, including NELFUND student loans covering institutional fees and living costs, tax reforms providing relief for lower-income earners and qualifying small companies, and Electricity Act opening the way for states to establish their own electricity markets.

“We have already shown that government can widen the possibilities in a person’s life,” Gbajabiamila said.

The former Speaker of the House of Representatives said the manifesto rested on four pillars — security and a more affordable life, supported by energy infrastructure, and a government that answered to the people it served.

Using the example of a farmer, he explained the practical meaning, “Security allows him to reach his farmland, while better storage protects what he harvests. A dependable road helps him get his produce to the market.

“When these things work together, his labour earns more, and food reaches his family at a lower cost. That is the practical meaning of translating reforms into shared prosperity.”

He emphasised that the manifesto committed the government to halving the number of out-of-school children by 2031, installing seven million additional electricity meters, and expanding health insurance coverage so illness is less likely to destroy a family’s finances.

Gbajabiamila said the government would publish targets, identify those responsible, and report progress to the public. He added, “We ask Nigerians to believe in this programme, and we are giving them the means to judge it.

“For those of us in public office, this is an obligation to work. The president’s determination must be matched by performance across government.”

Gbajabiamila charged APC to take the programme seriously enough to explain it, take it into communities, and listen when people say what still needs to change.

He stated, “A party asking to continue in government must be prepared to answer to the people whose mandate it seeks. We must earn support through the quality of our work, the strength of our case and the seriousness of our conduct under President Tinubu.

“In 2027, we will ask Nigerians for the mandate to carry that work forward and ensure that its benefits reach even further.

“Too many of our people have learned to lower their expectations of what their country can do for them. Part of our job in this election is to raise our people’s expectations so that they can see what lies beyond the present situation.”

Gbajabiamila added, “We owe our children something better than an inheritance of diminished expectations. The child studying tonight should have a fair chance of becoming the professional she hopes to be.

“The man opening his workshop tomorrow should be able to grow beyond the struggle to keep it open. Their ambitions deserve a country organised to help them succeed.”

Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Atiku Bagudu, said the economic reforms introduced by Tinubu would translate into improved living conditions and prosperity for ordinary citizens, particularly hardworking Nigerians and vulnerable groups.

Bagudu stressed that Tinubu remained conscious of the economic difficulties facing ordinary Nigerians, adding that the president is determined to ensure they benefit from his administration’s policies.

He said Tinubu was committed to ensuring that his policies improved citizens’ livelihoods, adding that the APC communications team and other officials have worked hard to develop the party’s 2027 manifesto.

Bagudu stated, “All of us, the ministers, alongside the vice president, have reason to be proud of the last Nigerian Economic Summit. This is because the private sector unanimously acknowledged that Mr President had delivered on the promises he made.

“They are doing well, announcing investments in Nigeria commensurate with what he promised and what he has delivered. But, as we all know, even before anybody tells him, Mr President acknowledges that we have done well.

“However, until we deliver and ensure that every Nigerian feels the impact of prosperity, especially hardworking Nigerians and those who need support, we still have work to do.”

Bagudu recounted how Tinubu, during his campaign in Zamfara State, directed a State House official to give money to a struggling carrot seller whose sales had been poor, describing the gesture as evidence of the president’s concern for ordinary Nigerians.

He said, “But the APC manifesto for our president does not end with a team. The manifesto belongs to all Nigerians who are members of his team and believe in the profundity of his message.

“What you are going to see certainly includes some elements that you have already seen, as well as a broader vision. For Mr President, if Brazil can become a $2tn economy, why can’t Nigeria?

“So, Mr President, without being influenced by any outsider, said we should confront our reality and address these challenges. As I have said, he was not concerned about the next election but about prosperity.

“Indeed, we are seeing the benefits of having a leader who has a profound understanding of what Nigeria can become and is courageous enough to lead us towards that reality.”

The member representing Kiru/Bebeji Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon. Abdulmumin Jibrin, said Tinubu had delivered infrastructure projects that previous administrations failed to complete.

Jibrin stressed that successive governments that spent between three and eight years in office failed to complete the two major road projects in the area, Abuja-Kaduna Road and Kaduna-Kano Road.

He stated, “My brother here, in the Ministry of Works, also did a fantastic job in terms of infrastructure, particularly if I may be biased towards the northern part of the country, where some people claim we have been short-changed. That is not true.

“At least, this is a government that has been in office for three years. I have no problem with previous administrations. Perhaps, if I do, it is only in my mind; I am not saying it publicly. Officially, I have no problem with them.

“But we had governments that spent eight years, five years, three years and another eight years in office. None of them completed the Abuja-Kaduna Road. None completed the Kaduna-Kano Road.

“This government, in less than three years, completed the Kaduna-Kano Road. By November or December, this same government is expected to conclude the Abuja-Kaduna Road.

“Dawanu is the largest agricultural market in Kano.

“Honourable Pande is here. The government has made a substantial commitment to the Dawanu Market. It is the largest agricultural market in West Africa.”

Presenting the manifesto, Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr. Jumoke Oduwole, unveiled its key economic targets, including accelerating Nigeria’s annual economic growth to six per cent, expanding available electricity generation to over 10,000 megawatts, and creating one million export-related jobs for young Nigerians by 2030.

Oduwole, who also serves as Deputy Director of the Manifesto and Policy Directorate of the APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, disclosed the targets yesterday in Abuja while presenting an overview of the party’s manifesto.

She explained that the document was designed to consolidate the achievements of the Tinubu administration and outline the next phase of the government’s development agenda, which she described as a transition from economic reforms to shared prosperity.

Oduwole said Tinubu had, in his October 1 address to Nigerians, declared that the country was moving from reforms to prosperity, following more than three years of difficult but necessary economic adjustments.

She said the manifesto was anchored on four broad pillars: a secure and resilient nation; improved quality of life and affordability; energy, infrastructure and economic growth; and effective and accountable governance.

Oduwole explained that the framework was developed following consultations with stakeholders across the country, including members of the Federal Executive Council, the National Assembly, state governments, heads of agencies, development partners, civil society groups, women, persons with disabilities, party officials, and the media.

She said the objective was to ensure that the manifesto reflected the expectations and aspirations of Nigerians rather than being based solely on the assumptions of the party or government.

The minister stated that the document also reviewed the eight priority areas of APC’s 2023 manifesto, assessing what had been promised, what had been achieved, and the areas requiring further intervention.

On electricity, Oduwole said available power generation would be scaled up to more than 10,000 megawatts, while transmission and distribution infrastructure would be strengthened and energy access extended to underserved communities.

She added that the administration would expand domestic food production, storage and processing, with a target of halving post-harvest losses and improving the movement of goods across states to reduce transportation costs.

Other priorities included reducing living costs, expanding employment opportunities, increasing real incomes, improving access to affordable credit, strengthening national security, expanding quality education and accessible healthcare, and providing affordable housing and secure land access.

In his submission, Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, challenged critics of Tinubu’s economic reforms to look beyond immediate economic difficulties, insisting that the benefits of the policies are increasingly reaching ordinary Nigerians, irrespective of political affiliation or social status.

Responding to concerns that only a privileged few were benefiting from the reforms, the minister stated that government interventions were designed to serve Nigerians across political and economic divides.

He cited the Abuja-Kano road project, maintaining that access to public infrastructure us not determined by political affiliation, wealth or social class.

On security, Idris recalled the previous atmosphere of fear along the Abuja-Kaduna corridor, where motorists had to establish whether bandits were operating along the route before embarking on journeys.

He said the situation had improved considerably, allowing travellers to undertake journeys with less anxiety and without the uncertainty that previously characterised movement along the highway.

First Lady: Governance Should Be Gauged Through Infrastructure, Functional Institutions, Public Assets Must Outlive Political Leaders

First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, called on political leaders to preserve and improve public assets for future generations, saying governance should be measured by the quality of infrastructure and institutions bequeathed to the people. The first lady, who stated this while inaugurating the reconstructed Lagos State Governor’s Lodge in Asokoro, Abuja, commended Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu for delivering the new facility, describing it as a reflection of Lagos State’s commitment to excellence and responsible management of public infrastructure.

Mrs. Tinubu, who performed the ceremony in place of her husband, President Tinubu, said public assets belonged to the people and must be preserved, improved, and developed to serve generations yet unborn.

She explained, “Public assets belong to the people, and it is our responsibility as leaders to preserve what has been entrusted to us, improve it where necessary, and provide lasting infrastructure that future generations can inherit and benefit from.”

She stated that the timely completion of the project demonstrated the commitment of the Lagos State government and the efforts of those involved in its execution.

Mrs. Tinubu recalled that the old structure was demolished in October 2025 to make way for the new facility, which she described as a befitting official residence for the Lagos State governor and his family whenever they visit Abuja.

She stated, “I commend the governor for recognising the importance of having a befitting official residence for the governor of Lagos State and his family whenever they are in Abuja.

“What gladdens my heart is that you are leaving this Government Lodge better than you found it. As we inaugurate this facility, my prayer is that it will remain a place of peace, comfort, and hospitality for the governors of Lagos State and their families.”

The first lady said Lagos, as Nigeria’s commercial hub and Centre of Excellence, deserved infrastructure that reflected its standing and aspirations.

In his remarks, Sanwo-Olu described the inauguration as another historic milestone for Lagos, explaining that the new lodge is designed not merely as an official residence but as an institutional centre for government business, strategic engagements, and the state’s relationship with the federal government.

The governor said Lagos, despite not being Nigeria’s capital since the relocation of the seat of government to Abuja in December 1991, continued to maintain significant economic and political interests at the centre of national administration.

He said the old lodge had served the state for several decades but no longer adequately reflected the present status and growing responsibilities of the state.

“We believe that Lagos deserves a rebuild, and that is what has happened and what we are doing here today,” he said.

Sanwo-Olu disclosed that the project, which was awarded to Julius Berger Nigeria Plc, was delivered in about 15 months.

He commended the construction company for completing the project within the agreed period, despite the technical demands involved, including excavation close to 10 meters deep.

The governor said the new building belonged to the people of Lagos and would provide a suitable environment for receiving guests, holding meetings, and advancing the state’s interests in the nation’s capital.

He disclosed that the building carried the Lagos State seal and motto, “Justice and Progress,” which he said communicated the state’s identity and commitment to strengthening its partnership with the federal government.

Sanwo-Olu appreciated Tinubu for the federal government’s support for Lagos through interventions in roads, railways and bridges.

He said the state’s more than 22 million residents appreciated the president’s interventions and expressed confidence that his administration would continue to serve the country.

The governor, who will leave office in May 2027, said the facility was built for successive administrations rather than for his personal enjoyment, saying, “I believe a government should build things, not stay long for itself to enjoy.”

He added that the responsibility of governance was to leave public institutions and infrastructure better than they were inherited and create legacies that would endure beyond individual administrations.

Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, described the reconstructed lodge as a renewed institutional presence of Lagos State in Abuja, about 35 years after the state and other federating units established their presence in the Federal Capital Territory.

Hamzat said the project was a strategic investment aimed at providing a more conducive environment for official engagements, hospitality, government business, and interactions with the diplomatic community and private sector.

The inauguration attracted former governors of the state, including Babatunde Fashola, Akinwunmi Ambode, and members of the National Assembly, the Lagos traditional rulers, white cap chiefs, members of the Lagos State Executive Council, captains of industry, and other dignitaries.

World.title: ADC Campaign: Transferring Case to Lifu Deliberate, to Frustrate Us Despite Protest
World.content:
• Accuses judge of refusing to release CTC of judgement

• Berates Tinubu’s campaign council, says re-election messages divisive and empty

Chuks Okocha in Abuja





African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) said the decision to transfer the party’s suit to Justice Peter Lifu was a deliberate attempt to frustrate the suit, despite ADC’s earlier protest.

The party said that explained why Lifu was denying the release of the Certified True Copy (CTC) of his judgement that sacked the leadership of the party.

ADC PCC said Justice Emeka Nwite had already begun hearing the case before it was eventually transferred to Lifu.

The campaign council stated, ‘’Despite our formal protest to the Chief Judge, Justice John Tsoho assigned the case to Justice Lifu the very next day—a decision that exposes Justice Tsoho’s bias and culminated in a judgement so brazenly rascally that it must not be allowed to stand.’’

A statement by Director, Strategic Communications ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, said, ‘’Our lawyers have taken the legal questions before the esteemed justices of the Court of Appeal.

“We respect their authority to decide them. We also come before the court of public opinion with the documents that show how this case reached Justice Lifu.

‘’Nigerians deserve to know why Justice Nwite was prevented from concluding a case he had already begun hearing.”

ADC-PCC added, ‘’We call for the immediate release of the full judgment in this matter. The ADC must be given the official copy and the reasons for the decision so that we can proceed with the appropriate legal action.

“Withholding the judgment obstructs our right to challenge it and denies the appellate court the benefit of a complete record.

‘’The plaintiff’s request to remove the case from Justice Nwite cited delay and a loss of confidence in obtaining a timely hearing. Justice Nwite had not recused himself. He remained a serving judge, and the case was already before him.”

ADC-PCC explained, ‘’Our counsel responded to the request on 11 May 2026. The letter listed the adjournments, challenged the plaintiff’s account of who caused them and protested that the request amounted to forum shopping.

‘’On 2 June, ADC National Secretary Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola wrote to Justice Tsoho, asking him to reverse the reassignment. The letter stated plainly that the party had no confidence in Justice Lifu’s impartiality and formally protested the transfer. Yet, the case was assigned to Justice Lifu the next day.

‘’Justice Tsoho received our protest. Why did he proceed with the transfer? What did he find in the plaintiff’s allegation of delay that outweighed the court record and our protest? Let him publish his reasons. Let Nigerians read them beside the letters.”

ADC-PCC alleged, ‘’The sequence and timing of this transfer raise grave concerns about bias and create an appearance that the process was not handled with the impartiality this matter demanded.

“Justice Tsoho must answer those concerns openly. The public is entitled to know why our formal protest was set aside and why the case was reassigned the very next day.

‘’Our concern about Justice Lifu was reinforced in a different suit. He ordered INEC to deregister the ADC and four other parties despite a Court of Appeal order staying proceedings.

“The appellate court described his decision to proceed as the ‘highest form of judicial impertinence’ and invoked Supreme Court authority on ‘judicial rascality’.

“It later nullified the deregistration judgement.”

ADC-PCC said, ‘’Then there is Justice Musa Liman’s certified judgement. He dismissed a challenge to the ADC leadership for lack of merit and locus standi.

He held that the internal party dispute was non-justiciable, declared the leadership handover lawful and held that INEC was entitled to recognise the National Chairman and National Secretary.

“Justice Lifu, sitting in the same Federal High Court, could not simply make those orders disappear. That is one of the questions our lawyers have placed before the Court of Appeal.”

The campaign council also stated, ‘’We might even sympathise with Justice Tsoho. He faces a Code of Conduct Bureau inquiry over allegations concerning undeclared bank accounts. There have also been press reports alleging that a large sum of cash was found in his wife’s possession, though the EFCC has not publicly confirmed that report.

“None of these allegations establishes guilt. But if powerful people have a hold over the Chief Judge while such matters hang over him, he owes Nigerians the courage to say so.

‘’If no pressure influenced this transfer, he should give the public a full account of his decision. Whatever his predicament, the ADC’s right to a fair hearing cannot be made to pay for it.”

ADC-PCC declared, ‘’Judicial officers should remember how court decisions deepened the crises preceding the end of our First and Second Republics. The names of Chief Justice Adetokunbo Ademola and Justices John Taylor and Lionel Bairamian remain in the judicial history of the First Republic; Justices Ayorinde, Alao and Popoola remain in that of the Second. Today’s judges must consider what history will say of their own decisions.”

The campaign council stated, ‘’The National Judicial Council must examine the transfer, the formal protest Justice Tsoho received and Justice Lifu’s conduct. The ruling APC should be bold enough to face Atiku Abubakar on the political battleground and answer for the hardship Nigerians endure.

‘’The hallowed chambers of our courts must not be turned into arenas for political combat. Nigerians must see those who would rather fight their opponent through court manoeuvres than meet him at the ballot box.

‘’Atiku remains our candidate. The law is on his side, not sentiment. We will defend that position before the Court of Appeal and keep the record before Nigerians. Their right to choose their president must never become a bargaining chip in anyone’s struggle for power.’’

ADC-PCC Berates Tinubu’s Campaign, Says Re-election Messages Divisive and Empty

ADC-PCC condemned Tinubu’s re-election campaign messages as divisive, vague, uninspiring, and devoid of any credible account of his administration’s performance.

The council said rather than present a comprehensive scorecard of his three-and-a-half years in office, Tinubu had resorted to political tantrums, name-calling, and verbal attacks on opponents.

In a statement by Director of Media and Publicity, ADC Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC), Kola Ologbondiyan, the council said Nigerians were expecting clear explanations on the administration’s massive borrowings, the gains of fuel subsidy removal, worsening insecurity, widespread hunger, and the escalating cost of living.

It stated, ‘’Instead, the president’s campaign outings in Kaduna, Rivers and Jigawa states were dominated by personal attacks and recycled promises, offering nothing new to Nigerians.’’

The ADC-PCC particularly challenged Tinubu to account for his much-publicised electricity pledge: “If I don’t give you electricity, don’t vote for me for a second term.”

According to the council, the president has failed to fulfil that promise, even as millions of Nigerians continue to endure unreliable electricity supply, while he has reportedly invested in alternative power arrangements for his personal comfort.

It described Tinubu’s renewed promises on electricity during his Jigawa campaign as an attempt to repackage old, unfulfilled commitments as fresh electoral promises.

The council also questioned the administration’s much-touted mechanised farming agenda, asking what has become of the 2,000 tractors reportedly imported from Brazil several months ago, which it alleged were yet to make any meaningful impact on agricultural productivity.

World.title: Eno: Our People Excited over Approval for the Establishment of Íbom Deep Sea Port
World.content:
Okon Bassey in Uyo

Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has expressed excitement of the people of the state for the approval of the financing arrangements for the Ibom Deep Sea Port Project by President Bola Tinubu.

“This approval marks a defining moment in our state’s economic journey,” he said in a state broadcast to the people of the State yesterday.

“The Ibom Deep Sea Port is not just an infrastructure project; it is a gateway to economic transformation, international trade, investment, industrial growth and employment opportunities for our people.

The governor expressed gratitude to President Tinubu for his confidence in the state and his commitment to the development of the nation, assuring him of the full cooperation to ensure the successful realisation of the phistoric project.

“Mr President, to whom much is given, much is also required. Akwa Ibom assures you that we will respond enmasse on January 16, 2027, as we will give you all our votes in support of your continuity in office from May 29,2027,” he said.

Eno expressed appreciation to the people of the State for the overwhelming reception and extraordinary hospitality extended to Mr President and his team.

“I thank our traditional rulers, religious leaders, political stakeholders, youths, women, security agencies, public servants, students, and everyone who contributed to the success of this historic visit,” the governor stated.

World.title: 2027: We’re Ready to Ensure Credible and Transparent Polls in Osun, Declares REC
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has disclosed that preparations for the 2027 General Election in Osun State were on course, with nine of the 14 major activities on the electoral timetable already completed.

Speaking with journalists, in Osogbo, at a press Conference, the Resident Electoral Commissioner, Mrs Oluwatoyin Babalola, stressed that the commission had intensified preparations to deliver a free, fair, credible and transparent election across the state.

She said INEC was building on the gains recorded during the August 15, 2026 governorship election, which recorded a voter turnout of 1,010,684 out of 2,339,233 registered voters, representing 43.2 per cent participation.

According to her, “The election witnessed seamless deployment of electoral personnel and materials, while the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) functioned effectively in all 3,763 polling units across the state.”

She added that the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) recorded one of its highest success rates, with 87 per cent of polling unit results uploaded by 4:30 p.m. on election day.

“Providing an update on voter registration and PVC collection. Mrs Babalola disclosed that the state’s PVC collection rate had risen to 81.74 per cent, leaving only 18.26 per cent of cards yet to be collected. She urged eligible voters to pick up their cards ahead of the elections,” she said.

The commission also announced that Osun currently has 5,763 functional BVAS machines available for the general election, including 1,328 backup devices to address any technical emergencies on election day.

“On election staffing, the REC revealed that recruitment of ad hoc personnel was ongoing through INEC’s portal, stressing that only competent, neutral and professional applicants would be considered for election duties,” she noted.

According to her, INEC had already commenced several strategic trainings for electoral officials, while additional programmes for security personnel, presiding officers and collation officers had been scheduled ahead of the polls.

World.title: ADC: Why is INEC Condemning ‘Rig and Die’ But Silent on APC’s AK-47 Threat
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The African Democratic Congress (ADC), has questioned the alleged inconsistency in the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)’s response to threats of electoral violence, following its condemnation of the “rig and die” slogan ahead of the 2027 general election.

In a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the party recalled the widely reported remarks attributed to Edo State APC Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, threatening the use of AK-47 rifles against those who refuse to vote for President Bola Tinubu.

According to Abdullahi, “Why has INEC found its voice to condemn ‘rig and die’ but remained conspicuously silent on the threat by an APC chairman to use AK-47 rifles against opposition voters? Is a slogan more dangerous than a gun? Or does the identity of the person making the threat determine what INEC considers electoral violence?

“If INEC is concerned about the language of those warning against electoral rigging, should it not be even more concerned when a political party official threatens voters with AK-47 rifles? Has INEC referred the matter to security agencies? If not, why not?”

The ADC said the Commission’s latest intervention was appropriate, but it must not give the impression that it was only concerned when the ruling party is at the receiving end.





The party rejected electoral violence in all forms, whether threatened by opposition supporters or officials of the ruling party.

“However, INEC cannot demand peaceful elections without demonstrating equal concern for those threatened with violence.

“Its responsibility is not merely to condemn inflammatory language, but to demand an environment that permits every Nigerian to vote freely,” he stated

World.title: NUPRC Apologises as Portal Upgrade Stalls Oil Service Firms’ Activities
World.content:
Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has apologised to oil and gas ser-vice providers over inability to access its Oil and Gas Industry Service Permit (OGISP) portal, blaming the outage on an ongoing upgrade of its electronic licensing infrastructure.

The apology was contained in a statement issued by the management of the commission and posted on its official X handle yesterday.

According to the commission, the disruption was triggered by the migration and upgrade of its Commis-sion Electronic Licensing & Permit System (CELPS), an exercise which commenced on November 6, 2026.

The upgrade has since locked service companies, contractors and consultants out of the OGISP platform, which is mandatory for operating in Nigeria’s upstream sector.

“The Commission offers its unreserved apology to all users who have had difficulty accessing the OGISP portal since the exercise began,” NUPRC said a note.

The OGISP permit is the primary regulatory gateway for companies providing services to exploration and production companies in Nigeria. Without a valid permit, service firms cannot bid for contracts, mobilise to sites, or renew existing service agreements with operators.

The portal downtime therefore means that new applications, renewals, and modifications that require regulatory approval are effectively stalled for the period, with implications for project timelines and compliance status of affected firms.

But the NUPRC said the upgrade was intended to improve user experience, strengthen cybersecurity and reduce turnaround time for approvals.

In recent times, the commission has ramped up the automation and shortening of its processes in line with the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021, which mandates it to create an enabling environment for upstream investment.

This move has reduced paperwork, cut timelines as well as human interface and has blocked leakages in the issuance of permits by the commission.

“The upgrade is meant to improve user experience, strengthen the security of the system and shorten the time it takes to process applications,” the commission stated, adding that its technical team is work-ing to complete the migration “in the shortest possible time.”

NUPRC said it expects the portal to be fully restored and running smoothly within the ‘next 24 hours’ from when the statement was made public.

World.title: NERC Approves N30bn for Fresh Tranche of Nationwide Free Metering Programme
World.content:
• Installations to be completed before May, 2027

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved N30 billion for tranche ‘C’ of the Meter Acquisition Fund (MAF) under the Presidential Metering Initiative (PMI), in a fresh push to elim-inate estimated billing and close Nigeria’s huge metering deficit.

The approval was contained in Order No. NERC/2026/121 on the ‘Operationalisation of Tranche C of the MAF’, which the commission said took effect from November 2, 2026. The order was made public yesterday in Abuja.

Anchored on the N30 billion, the new tranche establishes the framework for procuring and deploying meters free of charge to electricity consumers nationwide, with priority for all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerated metering of Band B customers.

Under the scheme, NERC said the N30 billion will be shared among the 11 electricity Distribution Com-panies (DisCos) strictly in proportion to their respective contributions to the Fund.

The commission stressed that sharing must be equitable across states within each Distribution Company (Disc) franchise area to avoid lopsided deployment that has characterised previous interventions.

The MAF, introduced in 2024 as part of President Bola Tinubu’s presidential metering initiative, is funded through a dedicated levy on electricity tariffs. It is designed to complement other metering pro-grammes including the Meter Asset Provider (MAP) scheme, the National Mass Metering Programme (NMMP) and the World Bank-supported Distribution Sector Recovery Programme (DISREP).

Tranches A and B, totaling about N59 billion, were rolled out between 2024 and 2025, but data as of September 2026 still show up to 47 per cent of registered customers unmetered.

According to the Order, Discos are mandated to undertake transparent procurement from eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers (LMMAs) and MAPs with verified meter stock. To curb price in-flation, NERC fixed maximum procurement prices based on the median national MAP online bid prices from the September 2026 bid cycle.

According to the Order, payment to providers will be in two stages, with 70 per cent upon verified de-livery of meter stock and the balance of 30 per cent upon confirmation of complete installation. This structure is aimed at preventing a repeat of past experiences where meters were paid for but not de-ployed.

The commission reiterated that all meters under the programme shall be installed free for customers, warning that extortion would attract sanctions.

“Every meter must prominently display the relevant Disco’s name, the applicable MAF tranche and the inscription ‘not for sale’. Where a Disco initiates the relocation of an existing customer’s connection point for revenue protection purposes, the cost shall be borne by the Disco,” NERC stated.

The Order also provides for sanctions where a Disco defaults, delays or procurement irregularities im-pede installation. To ensure accountability, NERC directed that all supply and installation contracts be filed with the commission, while the Fund Manager, Discos and meter providers will be subjected to mandatory monitoring, reporting and evaluation.

All installations under Tranche C must be completed on or before 31 May 2027, the commission said, urging strict compliance by stakeholders.

The metering gap remains one of the biggest driver of commercial losses and consumer complaints in the Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry (NESI).

The commission added that the Order reinforces its commitment to closing the national metering gap, improving revenue assurance, enhancing service delivery and protecting electricity consumers.

“To ensure accountability and transparency, the Order prescribes monitoring, reporting and evaluation requirements for the Fund Manager, Discos and participating meter providers. All supply and installa-tion contracts must be filed with the commission. All meter installations under Tranche C must be com-pleted on or before 31 May 2027.

“The commission urges all stakeholders to comply strictly with the provisions of the Order, which rein-forces its commitment to closing the national metering gap, improving revenue assurance, enhancing service delivery and protecting electricity consumers,” NERC stated.

World.title: Kaizer Chief latest news and rumours: Phili, Mokwana, Mayo
World.content:
It’s an international break, but Kaizer Chiefs news never stops. The club has some encouraging updates on key players, including Langelihle Phili.

When will Phili return for Chiefs?

21-year-old Kaizer Chiefs winger Langelihle Phili has been sidelined since injuring his ankle in training after the 1-1 draw against Mamelodi Sundowns on 15 August. Phili has missed eight matches across all competitions, but his return is on the horizon.

Kaizer Chiefs boss Da Cruz speaks to the media

Speaking to the media following Chiefs’ 2-1 win over Siwelele, Fernando Da Cruz said that Phili has rejoined the squad for full training and his return is imminent.



“[Langelihle] Phili restarted this week [last week] with the squad and has been taking part in football sessions on the field,” Da Cruz told journalists in Polokwane. “So, he is close to restarting to play in competitions.

“Maybe he will be ready for the semi-final; we don’t know, but we’ll work a lot with him during this FIFA [international] break for [November].

MAYO, Mokwana BOLSTER Kaizer Chiefs‘ OPTIONS

It’s been a good week for the club. Chiefs wrapped up the signing of 27-year-old former Sekhukhune winger Elias Mokwana. Meanwhile, Khanyisa Mayo’s return from injury runs in parallel to Phili’s, so both could return to the fold against Sundowns.

World.title: Proteas vs Bangladesh Tests: Squad, dates, where to watch
World.content:
Temba Bavuma leads the Proteas into two Tests against Bangladesh in November 2026. Image: Wikimedia Commons, Proteas Men CSA (X).

Can South Africa tighten their grip on the World Test Championship mace?

The Proteas get their Test series against Bangladesh underway this weekend.

Here are all the details on the squad, dates, and where to watch the action.



Proteas vs Bangladesh: Fixture details

Cricket South Africa has confirmed the dates of the upcoming Test series on its website.

The first Test runs from 15 to 19 November at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg.

The second Test takes place from 23 to 27 November at SuperSport Park in Centurion.



DStv will broadcast the games on the SuperSport Cricket channel (212).

South Africa are expected to name a pace-forward XI for these matches.

According to the ICC, coach Shukri Conrad said Highveld pitches tended to favour pace and bounce.



“So with that in mind, there will be greater focus on our seam-bowling options.”

With coach Conrad aware of the likely conditions, he has selected a squad built for a strong bowling display.

South Africa and Bangladesh name squads

Anrich Nortje has returned after leaving the second Test against Australia with a groin injury.



He joins Marco Jansen, Kagiso Rabada, and Wiaan Mulder among the notable pace bowlers.

Coach Conrad has also retained some spin options, including Simon Harmer and Keshav Maharaj.

Changes to the squad that faced Australia include Tony de Zorzi back after a hamstring injury.



Zubayr Hamza was also named in the squad after last representing South Africa in a Test in 2024.

For South Africa, winning means more control over the World Test Championship race.

They claimed a crucial Test win over Australia in August, and the hosts will be wary of the threat of an upset.
