World.title: ‘I did not sign up’: Obren on getting cast in ‘Married at First Sight’
World.content:
On the Unscripted podcast, Obren Msuku, a former Married at First Sight Season 3 cast member, revealed that he never applied to be on the hit reality show.

Instead, one of the content producers approached him with an opportunity to join the show.

OBREN MSUKU WAS APPROACHED TO BE ON ‘MAFS’

Several participants from the show have been hopping from one podcast to another, where they have shared their side of the story, since viewers only see an edited version of who they truly are.



During a recent episode, which drew over 900 comments on YouTube, it was now Obren’s turn to lift the veil after his ex-wife, Laurinda Mabunda, made unsavoury remarks about him.

The former couple met and married on the show.

The 38-year-old entrepreneur revealed that a content producer had approached him, explaining that the show was short of prospective husbands and asked if he would be keen to take part.

The host, Peter Manjate, asked, “Why 

Obren responded: “I did not sign up. I did not write an email to Married at First Sight and say, ‘I want to get married.’ No,” he began.

“So, because I’m in the media industry, there’s a lady who’s one of the content producers. She reached out. She said, Listen, we need husbands on the show,’ he continued.



“At the time I’m single from a six-year relationship. I haven’t been dating for like a year. Yes, I was seeing people here and there, but nothing serious,” he added.

“I was like, okay. It took time though for her to convince me because I was a bit sceptical. I’ve never been one to chase clout, especially with my background. I could have been famous any day over the past 15 years,” he said.

He added, “I just gave myself a bit of grace. I was like, ‘Go for it. Why not?’ Maybe this could be an opportunity for you to meet the love of your life.”

CORRECTING MISCONCEPTIONS

Season 3 of Married at First Sight was filled with romance and drama, but for Obren, the experience leaned more towards the latter.

According to him, the infamous “list” was a turning point in his journey because he felt betrayed after Laurinda spoke negatively about him during the girls’ pajama party.

The drama started when Hlulani Ngobeni, one of the husbands on the show, jotted down the juicy gossip that his wife, Nompumelelo Sobhuza, had shared with him after returning from the party.

Hlulani then shared the list with the group, sparking the 3rd degree from fellow cast members especially Obren whose name topped the list.

The allegations against him included money laundering, car theft, and the back-room situation at his childhood home.

During the interview, Obren addressed several misconceptions and allegations that plagued him throughout the show.

World.title: Cape Town may have lost 15% of its wetlands over a nine-year period
World.content:
The report indicates 'significant wetland transformation' due to factors like urban expansion. Image: Zandvlei Trust/ Facebook

The Mother City may have lost more than 5 000 hectares of potential wetland area in nearly a decade, according to the City’s latest spatial trends report.

The 2025/26 Spatial Trends and Implementation Tracking report gives an overview of development and land use patterns in Cape Town from 2012 to 2026.

According to estimates, wetland area in the metro fell from approximately 33 106 hectares in 2016 to 28 002 hectares in 2025.



That represents a net decline of roughly 5 104 hectares, or 15%.

Where Cape Town’s wetlands are under pressure

The report identifies several areas affected by wetland loss and degradation.

These include Driftsands Nature Reserve, where associated vleis have been affected by land invasions during the Covid-19 period.



Noordhoek vlei has also been impacted by the expansion of informal settlements from Masiphumelele.

Other affected areas include the Diep River and Kleine Stink River floodplains, seasonal vleis in the Slangetjiebos section of False Bay Nature Reserve, and vleis along the lower Kuils and Eerste rivers.

“On-the-ground observations indicate significant wetland transformation and degradation associated with urban expansion, land invasion, pollution, and hydrological modification,” the report states.



Cape Town’s Rondevlei Nature Reserve. Image: Wikimedia

Drought and development

The report says rainfall patterns also influenced the estimates. The severe 2015–2018 drought, followed by wetter years, coincided with fluctuations in potential wetland extent.

It suggests reduced surface water availability and weaker hydrological connections contributed to lower estimates between 2017 and 2022.

“Although modest recoveries were observed during wetter years, the overall declining trend suggests that longer-term pressures, including urban expansion, land transformation, hydrological modification, and climate change, could be contributing to persistent wetland loss across Cape Town,” the report concluded.



Important note: The figures stated above are based on wetland probability mapping rather than a direct count of wetlands or vleis physically destroyed. The City used a machine-learning classification method to identify potential wetland areas across Cape Town.

Meanwhile, over the same period, informal structures in Cape Town have increased by 67%. Read more on that story here.

World.title: How and why is Tatjana Smith representing the Netherlands?
World.content:
How and why is Tatjana Smith representing the Netherlands? Images via Facebook/Canva

South Africa’s most decorated swimmer, Tatjana Smith, has made the difficult decision to switch to representing the Netherlands with immediate effect.

This comes after she shared her grievances about her experience with the aquatic national governing body, Swimming South Africa, in a recent interview on Carte Blanche.

The 29-year-old recently returned to competing internationally after a premature retirement in 2024. At the time, the star athlete – whose sister-in-law is Rachel Kolisi – had won one silver and one gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics.



TATJANA SMITH TO REPRESENT THE NETHERLANDS – HOW IS SHE ELIGIBLE?

In a bombshell video statement, Tatjana Smith announced that she would be switching national allegiance as a professional swimmer from South Africa to the Netherlands.

The 29-year-old explained that representing the European country could provide her with high-performance support, financial stability, and a more sustainable swimming career.

Tatjana is eligible to represent the country because her father, René, was born in the Netherlands, which grants her both South African and Dutch citizenship.

René moved from Naaldwijk, the Netherlands, to South Africa in 1989, where he met Renske, a South African woman. The couple welcomed two daughters, Tatjana and her sister Fabienne, in Johannesburg

In 2021, Tatjana’s parents and sibling relocated to the Netherlands, where they now permanently live.

The swimming icon has made it clear that she has neither renounced her South African citizenship nor does she plan to move permanently to the Netherlands. 

She has also emphasised that her decision does not diminish her pride in having represented South Africa.

WHAT HAPPENS TO HER MEDALS?

With confirmation that she will now professionally represent the Netherlands at future competitions, what happens to the medals she has earned for South Africa?

Tatjana Smith has won a large collection of medals, including her Olympic ones, such as

Tokyo 2020: Gold – 200m breaststroke.

Tokyo 2020: Silver – 100m breaststroke.

Paris 2024: Gold – 100m breaststroke.

Paris 2024: Silver – 200m breaststroke.

Although she switches allegiances, her medals are not transferable to the Netherlands and remain South African accolades. However, her future results will be credited to the Netherlands.

World.title: WMO warns of ‘off the charts’ climate extremes as El Niño strengthens
World.content:
The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has warned that a very strong El Niño event could intensify global heat and extreme weather into 2027.

Raising concerns about the impact on vulnerable communities, food production and water supplies.

In its latest State of the Climate Update 2026, released on 9 November, the United Nations agency said the world was experiencing a prolonged period of exceptional temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels.



The report found that the past 12 years have each been the warmest on record.

Global average surface temperatures between January and September 2026 reached approximately 1.47°C above the pre-industrial average.

The WMO expects this figure to rise further by the end of the year as El Niño strengthens.



WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said the state of the global climate in 2026 gave new meaning to the phrase “off the charts”.

She warned that hundreds of millions of people had already experienced extreme heat this year, while heatwaves, tropical cyclones and heavy rainfall were increasing the risks facing communities.

Southern Africa faces warmer conditions

The warning is particularly relevant to southern Africa, where the WMO’s seasonal outlook points to warmer-than-normal conditions between November 2026 and January 2027.



The forecast, based on climate models from several international partners, including the South African Weather Service (SAWS), also points to shifts in rainfall patterns across different parts of the world.

For southern Africa, the warmer outlook raises concerns about the potential effects of prolonged heat on water resources, agriculture and communities already vulnerable to extreme weather.

However, the outlook does not mean that every part of the region will experience the same rainfall conditions.



El Niño can bring different impacts to different areas.

Why El Niño is raising concerns

El Niño is a natural climate pattern that develops when sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean become warmer than normal.

The WMO said the current event has been strengthening since August and is expected to reach record strength by December.



The world’s oceans absorb about 90% of the excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases, making ocean warming a major factor in the changing global climate.

The WMO also reported that global sea levels reached their highest point in the satellite record in 2026, while ocean heat continued to rise.

Extreme weather puts lives and livelihoods at risk

The agency warned that El Niño could increase the risks of heatwaves, droughts and heavy rainfall well into 2027.



These conditions could affect food production, worsen water shortages and increase health risks, particularly in communities that depend on rain-fed agriculture.

The WMO also highlighted the human cost of recent extreme weather events.

The WMO said its 2026 update uses data available up to September and does not yet capture the latest impacts of the strengthening El Niño.



Its final State of the Global Climate 2026 report is expected in March 2027

World.title: UK children's author David Walliams accused of sex assault, grooming teens
World.content:
LONDON - UK media on Tuesday published allegations that British comedian and children's author David Walliams groomed teenage fans and sexually assaulted a 15-year-old girl as well as harassing young female colleagues.

The claims, published by The Guardian newspaper and ITV news channel, came after a joint investigation into allegations by multiple women dating as far back as 2003.

Walliams, who lost a High Court battle against being identified in the UK media and did not appeal, denied targeting teenagers and using his fame to manipulate them to have sex, his lawyers told media.

His lawyers did not respond to a request for comment from AFP.

The Guardian published a letter Tuesday from Walliams, saying he "behaved thoughtlessly" in casual relationships.

But he said: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law".

Now 55, Walliams starred in the BBC's "Little Britain" sketch show in the early 2000s and was a judge on commercial broadcaster ITV's "Britain's Got Talent".

He also penned books such as "Mr Stink", "Gangsta Granny" and "The Boy in the Dress", with his work translated into more than 50 languages and reportedly selling 50 million copies.

When seeking to block the publication of the reports, Walliams' legal team argued he was "highly likely" to die by suicide if they were published.

The High Court heard he made two suicide attempts this year and was detained in a secure hospital last month.

Almost all the women making claims were identified only by first names, some changed at their request.

World.title: Support for death penalty in US at lowest level in 55 years: poll
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Support for the death penalty among Americans has fallen to its lowest level in 55 years, according to a poll published on Tuesday.

Forty-nine percent of US adults are in favour of the death penalty for convicted murderers and 45 percent are opposed, the Gallup poll found.

The last time support for capital punishment was below 50 percent was in 1971, when it was also at 49 percent, Gallup said.

The Gallup poll of 1,200 adults was conducted between October 1-19 and has a margin of error of plus or minus four percentage points.

The polling began one day after the botched execution by lethal injection in the state of Tennessee of convicted murderer Christa Pike.

Pike survived deadly doses of pentobarbital and was rushed to the hospital in critical condition. She has since been returned to prison but said recently that she is in constant pain.

Pike is the only inmate to survive after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.

Laura Porter, executive director of the US Campaign to End the Death Penalty, said the polling shows the country is "at a pivotal turning point in public opinion on the death penalty."

"Americans have been horrified by the recent botched executions, as well as the proposal to livestream an execution," Porter said. "At the same time, both Republican and Democratic governors have been granting clemencies at an increasing pace.

"The death penalty is being seen for what it is, an utter failure."

US President Donald Trump recently cancelled a controversial plan to livestream the firing squad execution of a convicted military base mass shooter.

California Governor Gavin Newsom announced this month he was commuting all death sentences in the state to life imprisonment, a move that will affect more than 500 prisoners.

Gallup said a majority of Americans over the age of 50 tend to favour the death penalty for convicted murders while younger Americans oppose it.

It said 73 percent of Republicans back the death penalty, 50 percent of Independents and just 28 percent of Democrats.

There have been 35 executions in the United States this year, all by lethal injection.

The death penalty has been abolished in 23 of the 50 US states, while three others -- California, Oregon and Pennsylvania -- have moratoriums in place.

Nidal Hasan, an army psychiatrist who shot dead 13 people at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009 in an Al-Qaeda-inspired attack, is set to be executed at the military base by firing squad on December 3.

World.title: After fridge hacks, home appliances could be next, warns EU cyber chief
World.content:
BRUSSELS - After recent attacks on supermarket fridges, home appliances could be next, the EU's cyber chief told AFP on Tuesday, as he urged Europe to invest more to counter growing cyber threats.

Supermarkets in at least 12 European countries were hit by cyberattacks in October and November, with France the worst affected.

"Security should not and cannot be an afterthought," Juhan Lepassaar, executive director of the EU's cybersecurity agency ENISA, said.

"Today it was fridges, tomorrow it could be routers, the day after tomorrow it could be home appliances and so forth."

Lepassaar spoke to AFP in Brussels where he unveiled the Athens-based agency's latest biennial report on the state of the EU's cybersecurity.

"All incidents can be avoided, but the question is, are we ready to invest to make it happen? Cybersecurity is not cheap," he said, calling on manufacturers to make products that are secure "by design".

Cybersecurity is crucial, Lepassaar said, because "every single service that you are depending on as a citizen, as a human being, contains a layer whereby there is a digital element in it, a piece of code which if not protected can be hacked."

A worst-case scenario would mean losing services "you depend upon: the policemen arriving, the fire brigade arriving, the hospital functioning, the transport giving you a ride from point A to B."

"These are the things that we depend on to function well and 24-7," he explained. "And if they don't, we will have an immediate impact."

Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in cyberattacks on October 11 and 12, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.

France on Monday said it held Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) responsible for the cyberattacks on supermarkets.

Lepassaar would not comment directly on France's accusation, but said Iranian and Russian "state-aligned actors" were known to target Europe.

He pointed to "a lot of collaboration" between them.

"China, Iran, People's Republic of North Korea, there are a lot of state-aligned threat actors which do target European companies and European interests," Lepassaar said.

He welcomed EU cyber rules that will fully enter into force next year, and the bloc's plans to "double the size of ENISA and also its resources."

It would "never" be enough, he said, "but it is a first good step".

World.title: Gauff upset at WTA Finals, Pegula back on track
World.content:
INDIAN WELLS - Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova upset Coco Gauff to storm into the last four of the WTA Finals at Indian Wells on Tuesday as Jessica Pegula reignited her challenge with victory over Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk.

Czech eighth seed Noskova took advantage of a shaky serving performance by Gauff to complete a 6-3, 6-3 victory in group one to book her place in the semi-finals.

Noskova broke Gauff's serve four times on her way to claiming the first set, and then grabbed the decisive break early in the second before sealing victory with her ninth ace of the match.

"I'm very happy, obviously every win counts in this competition," Noskova said afterwards. "Coco is a big competitor so I had to be ready for everything that would come my way today.

"You have to play to the very last point with Coco because she can always help herself out with her serve and fighting spirit. I felt like I played great to put some pressure on her," added Noskova, who defeated Ukraine's Kostyuk in her opening group match on Sunday.

The defeat leaves Gauff and Pegula vying for the last remaining semi-final berth from group one.

Pegula, beaten by Gauff in her opener Sunday, overcame a topsy-turvy second set to defeat Kostyuk 6-2, 7-5. Kostyuk is eliminated following Tuesday's defeat.

"I feel like I'm playing well," Pegula said. "I felt my match against Coco was a super high-level match and that was a great match today.

"It's so tricky with her because you just don't know what's gonna come -– she will just step in and inject pace, she'll come and kamikaze the net, she goes for returns or her serve can get hot. That's what makes it difficult to play her."

The 32-year-old American had looked in complete control in the first set, breaking Kostyuk in the first and seventh games to take the opener 6-2.

A chaotic second set began with four consecutive service breaks before Kostyuk held for a 3-2 lead.

The Ukrainian then had a break point in the next game but was unable to take advantage as Pegula held for 3-3.

The next four games went with serve but Pegula finally grabbed the decisive break in the 11th game. She converted her fourth break point to take a 6-5 lead before holding for the match, sealing victory when Kostyuk smacked a forehand long.

World.title: Mapisa-Nqakula's corruption trial resumes
World.content:
PRETORIA - Former Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula’s corruption trial resumes in the High Court in Pretoria.

A warrant of arrest was issued for her after she failed to appear in court on 2 October, citing ill health.

The warrant was held in abeyance until today and will be executed if she fails to appear.

Mapisa-Nqakula faces 12 counts of corruption and one count of money laundering.

The state alleges she solicited R4.5-million in bribes and received R2.1-million in cash.

She denies all the charges.

World.title: eNCA coalition builder | The numbers game in Ekurhuleni
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Voters made their choice in the 2026 Local Government Election, but the question of who gets to govern the country’s major metros is now in the hands of political parties.

In Ekurhuleni, the Democratic Alliance finished first with 66 seats, but it will need support from other political parties to secure a majority in council.

eNCA election analyst Wayne Sussman provides three possible coalition scenarios that could get the 113 seats needed for a majority in Ekurhuleni.

The first option he explores is a Government of National Unity possibility that would include the DA and the African National Congress (59 seats).

A partnership between these two parties will see them securing 125 seats, which is well above the line needed to form a government.

READ | eNCA coalition builder | Three possible paths to govern Tshwane

A second scenario is a coalition between the DA and ActionSA, who have 40 seats.

But the two parties would have only 106 seats, leaving them seven seats short of a majority.

They would need a third coalition partner like the Freedom Front Plus, which has 11 seats.

However, the big question is whether ActionSA would get into bed with both the Freedom Front Plus and the DA.

The third possibility could be an ANC-led coalition that excludes the DA.

That partnership could see the ANC (59 seats), combined with ActionSA (40 seats) and the Economic Freedom Fighters with their 14 seats.

That would give those three parties exactly 113 seats, just enough for a majority.
