World.title: Ladies in White Leader Released After Two Days in Detention
World.content:
Berta Soler was injured in her right foot as a result of violence during her arrest. / Facebook/Ángel Moya

Berta Soler was subjected to violence during her arrest, confined to a dark cell, and interrogated by State Security.

By 14ymedio

HAVANA TIMES – Berta Soler, leader of the Ladies in White, was released on Monday after being held by State Security for 46 hours, during which her whereabouts were unknown. Her husband, Angel Moya, announced the news on social media: “Released bearing the marks of violent repression.”

Moya reported that Berta Soler was released at around 10 a.m. “on a public street, near the headquarters of the Ladies in White,” in the Havana neighborhood of Lawton. In his post, Moya provided details about an injury the activist sustained to her right foot as a result of the violence during her arrest.

Soler was taken to the Aguilera police station in Diez de Octubre and later transferred to the Cotorro police station, where, according to the activist, she received medical attention before being confined to a dark cell.

According to Moya, before her release, Soler was interrogated by an officer from the State Security Investigation Department at Villa Marista. The officer questioned her about what had happened during the peaceful protest at which she was arrested, reminded her that she was under a precautionary measure of house arrest and that the measure could be revoked, and warned her that she would soon be summoned for questioning.

The post included photographs of the injury Berta Soler sustained to her foot during her arrest. Hours earlier, Moya had denounced her detention, saying he had overheard police officers mention that they had seen his wife “walking with a painful limp.”

According to activist Blanca Reyes, Moya went that same day to the Revolutionary National Police (PNR) station on Aguilera Street, in Lawton, in Havana’s Diez de Octubre municipality, to find out where the opposition leader was being held, “since she was beaten and no one knows whether she is at a police station or in a hospital.” Reyes stated: “Our sister’s situation is worrying.”

According to Moya’s account, on Saturday, two days after Soler had been arrested for several hours alongside fellow Lady in White Mara Cristina Labrada — the same Thursday that Yoani Sanchez, director of 14ymedio, was also arbitrarily detained — Berta Soler joined a “public and peaceful protest” with about 20 women from Lawton who were suffering from a lack of water.

The water shortage, Moya claims, is “intentional,” caused by the state-run company Aguas de La Habana to harm the Ladies in White headquarters and the area “within a 50-meter radius.”

Shortly after 10 a.m. that day, “several high-ranking State Security repressors” arrived at the scene and spoke with the protesting women, while the security operation was reinforced over the following hours.

“At noon, representatives of the state-run company Aguas de La Habana arrived and offered an explanation that also failed to convince the protesting women,” Moya recounted. His impression was that the authorities “had no intention of resolving the underlying cause of the problem, which is the deliberate manipulation of the water supply valve.”

With no satisfactory response, half an hour later the demonstrators blocked traffic on Porvenir Avenue, “using their own bodies as barriers.”

Moya said he did not witness the end of the protest because he had already been arrested by the political police and taken to the Aguilera station, where he overheard that his wife was walking in pain and that she had subsequently “been taken in a patrol car to another location,” which was not identified.

After an eight-hour interrogation, Moya was released, but his wife was not. The activist also clarified that “with the exception of Berta Soler, none of the women participating in the protest belong to organizations opposed to the Cuban communist regime. They are working women.”

The regime has intensified its persecution of activists and journalists on the island in recent weeks. Also on Saturday, dozens of residents took to the streets in El Cobre, Santiago de Cuba, to demand the release of Yoel Alejandro Perez Serrano, a young activist known for his community work who had been detained hours earlier by State Security in an operation involving armed agents.

As for independent journalists, before Yoani Sanchez’s detention, Adelth Bonne Gamboa and Camila Acosta, both contributors to CubaNet, had also been arrested during the same week.

Meanwhile, Rolando Pérez Lora, an evangelical pastor known as the Preacher of Christ, was forcibly transferred from Havana to Las Tunas, where he was released on Monday, with a pending police summons.

According to reports from the Cuban Observatory for Human Rights and the Alliance of Christians of Cuba, Perez Lora had been detained while providing pastoral support to a young Christian member of the religious organization, who was also arrested.

In mid-September, State Security also detained Henry Constantin, director of La Hora de Cuba. In his case, rather than being released like the other journalists mentioned above, he was transferred to Kilo 7 prison in Camagüey, where he remains in pretrial detention on a charge of disobedience.

First published in Spanish by 14ymedio and translated and posted in English by Havana Times,

Read more from Cuba here on Havana Times.

World.title: Leo XIV draws some 650,000 to Córdoba with a homily on holiness
World.content:
Leo XIV draws some 650,000 to Córdoba with a homily on holiness

11th Wednesday, November 2026 - 02:12 UTC Full article

On Wednesday, Leo XIV will celebrate his last Mass in Argentina in Luján, in Buenos Aires province, and then fly to Peru

Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass on Tuesday in Córdoba, in central Argentina, before some 650,000 people, according to the newspaper El País, in a homily devoted to holiness and local saints. “There is no better way to teach than by setting an example with one’s own life,” he told the faithful, urging them to practise their faith concretely in daily life.

The pontiff left Buenos Aires at 7.30 a.m. and landed in Córdoba an hour and a half later. The Mass was held at the grounds of the Argentine Aircraft Factory, covering more than 200 hectares, with 50 giant screens. Many pilgrims came by bus from other provinces, walked the last stretch before dawn and camped in the open. Among them were 28 altar boys from a parish in Jujuy, 900 kilometres away, who raised the travel money by selling food and holding pet shows. “I was left with all my hopes,” said Dora Ponce, 76, who did not manage to see the popemobile pass and followed the ceremony on a screen.

In his homily, Leo XIV recalled figures such as Father Brochero and Mama Antula, venerated above all in the interior of the country, and highlighted Córdoba’s religious history, marked by the arrival of the Jesuits in the 16th century. Its Jesuit Block has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.

After the Mass the Pope privately received a group of about 20 people from various social struggles, among them Alba Camargo, who as a child was abducted during the last dictatorship (1976-1983) and lost relatives to forced disappearance. Camargo asked him to name the disappeared and for his words to encourage those who know something about those crimes, including members of the clergy, to come forward. The Vatican has not given details of the meeting.

In the afternoon, the Pope greeted crowds from the balcony of the Archbishopric, the same one John Paul II appeared on in 1987, and met members of religious orders at the Cathedral of Our Lady of the Assumption. “There are stages in priestly and consecrated life in which remaining is already a very concrete form of self-giving,” he told them. The meeting was especially moving for the cloistered nuns who prepared the celebration: they baked 400,000 hosts and polished the chalices and liturgical items.

Attendance at the Córdoba Mass was lower than in Buenos Aires, where authorities estimated some 2.5 million people, and than the million the provincial government had anticipated. On Wednesday, Leo XIV will celebrate his last Mass in Argentina in Luján, in Buenos Aires province, and then fly to Peru, where President Keiko Fujimori will receive him that night.

World.title: Hamburg hearing opens as Argentina seeks to halt Sea Lion and the UK disputes jurisdiction
World.content:
Hamburg hearing opens as Argentina seeks to halt Sea Lion and the UK disputes jurisdiction

10th Tuesday, November 2026 - 15:31 UTC Full article

Because the United Kingdom chose the International Court of Justice for such disputes and Argentina opted for the Hamburg tribunal, the merits of the case must be settled by an arbitral tribunal

The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea began hearing Argentina and the United Kingdom in Hamburg on Tuesday over Argentina’s request for provisional measures to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands. Argentina argued that the resources of a disputed continental shelf cannot be exploited unilaterally, while the United Kingdom rejects the tribunal’s competence to rule on what it considers a question of sovereignty.

“The islanders cannot appropriate the resources of the disputed continental shelf,” said Argentina’s agent, Ambassador Mario Oyarzábal, presenting his country’s four requests: that the UK prevent the start or continuation of exploitation at Sea Lion, refrain from granting new permits, preserve information obtained during exploration and protect the marine environment. Oyarzábal cited the islands’ 2021 census, with 3,142 usual residents, of whom 1,625 hold the residence status granted by the Governor, and said those resources “belong to the Argentine people”.

Jurist Marcelo Kohen, an adviser to the delegation, said Argentina refers to sovereignty only to show that its claim to the continental shelf is plausible. “The land dominates the sea. That is why, and only why, we refer here to Argentine sovereignty,” he said, arguing that it is enough that the United Nations recognises the existence of the dispute. Argentina relies on UN General Assembly resolutions 2065 of 1965 and 31/49 of 1976, which call on the parties to avoid unilateral decisions, and warns that oil once extracted could not be restored by a later ruling. Dutch jurist Nico Schrijver, an expert on sovereignty over natural resources, also addressed the tribunal.

The United Kingdom is presenting its position in the afternoon session. Ahead of the hearing, Attorney General Ellie Reeves, who leads the British delegation, told The Times that the UK respects international law and the tribunal “but we don’t believe they have jurisdiction to hear a claim around sovereignty”. “We are absolutely clear that this is sovereign British territory,” she said. A spokesman for Prime Minister Andy Burnham insisted that “the hearing is not about the sovereignty of the Falklands” and that the islanders “have the right to develop their natural resources”, according to DPA.

Because the United Kingdom chose the International Court of Justice for such disputes and Argentina opted for the Hamburg tribunal, the merits of the case must be settled by an arbitral tribunal. Hamburg can only order provisional measures while that tribunal is being constituted, if it finds that the arbitral tribunal would have prima facie jurisdiction, that there is urgency and that the right invoked is plausible. Argentina’s Frida María Armas Pfirter, the tribunal’s vice-president, recused herself from the case, so Argentina appointed Raúl Vinuesa as judge ad hoc; the UK chose Vaughan Lowe. Both were sworn in on Monday.

The hearing concludes on Wednesday with a second round from each side. According to an expert consulted by Infobae, the decision could come around Friday, November 13. Sea Lion, operated by Israel’s Navitas Petroleum and Britain’s Rockhopper Exploration about 200 kilometres north of the archipelago, is expected to begin drilling in January 2027.

The hearing coincides with Princess Anne’s arrival in the islands on Monday and comes ahead of the debate on Argentina’s sovereignty defence bill in the Chamber of Deputies, scheduled for Thursday. The British government announced in October that it will introduce legislation to protect companies from possible Argentine sanctions.

World.title: Venezuela signs a memorandum with ExxonMobil for the oil major’s return after leaving in 2007
World.content:
Venezuela signs a memorandum with ExxonMobil for the oil major’s return after leaving in 2007

10th Tuesday, November 2026 - 14:52 UTC Full article

The signing took place in Caracas in the presence of acting President Delcy Rodríguez and ExxonMobil Upstream President Dan Ammann

Venezuela on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding with US oil company ExxonMobil with a view to its return to the country, which it left in 2007 after the nationalisation of the last privately held oilfields under Hugo Chávez’s government. The document is not a contract, and no investment figures or timelines have been disclosed.º

The signing took place in Caracas in the presence of acting President Delcy Rodríguez and ExxonMobil Upstream President Dan Ammann. Rodríguez called it a “very important signing”, reached after “months of negotiations for an effective return” of the Houston-based company. She said the memorandum covers “brownfield and greenfield” fields, that is, those already producing and those yet to be developed, with “billions of barrels of reserves”, and said ExxonMobil has “the capacity, technology and investment needed”. She also expressed hope that it would “very soon translate into concrete agreements”.

Ammann said the memorandum is “an important first step” in a process he hopes will lead to the company’s return. “We believe our unique capabilities, combined with this country’s extraordinary resources and Venezuela’s long history in oil and gas production, will bring significant benefits to all parties involved,” he said.

The rapprochement contrasts with Rodríguez’s position a little over a year ago. In March 2025, when she was Nicolás Maduro’s vice president, she accused ExxonMobil of “conspiring against Venezuela for more than a decade” to undermine its territorial integrity and take its resources.

Since Maduro’s removal from power following the US military operation on January 3, President Donald Trump has urged US energy companies to invest in Venezuela. In April, Rodríguez reported meetings with ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips, among other companies, after a reform of the hydrocarbons law opened the sector to private and foreign investment.

World.title: Nicaragua: Ortega reappears after 68 days as the government gives no word on his health
World.content:
Nicaragua: Ortega reappears after 68 days as the government gives no word on his health

10th Tuesday, November 2026 - 13:35 UTC Full article

Ortega walked slowly and looked frail, and the official broadcast avoided close-ups

Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega reappeared in public on Monday night, 68 days after his last appearance, at a tribute in Managua to Carlos Fonseca, founder of the ruling Sandinista National Liberation Front. It was his longest absence since returning to power in 2007. The government has never reported on his health or explained his absences.

Ortega, who turns 81 on Wednesday, attended the event at the old Plaza of the Revolution accompanied by his wife, co-president Rosario Murillo, who announced it on Sunday, members of the Sandinista Youth and relatives. He did not give a speech. “Carlos, here are the young people, those who will never forget you, who will never betray you, who will always be loyal to you, until death,” he said in brief remarks. According to international press reports, he walked slowly and looked frail, and the official broadcast avoided close-ups.

His last appearance had been on September 2, at an event marking the anniversary of the Army. His absence broke the 61-day record set in 2024. According to a count by the newspaper Confidencial, Ortega had appeared only 11 times so far in 2026, compared with an average of 26 between January and October in each year from 2018 to 2025. In September, the ceremony to receive the Central American independence torch was held without him or Murillo, and their children Maurice and Camila Ortega Murillo attended instead.

During his absence, the National Assembly approved a constitutional reform that abolished the vice presidency and created “presidential designees”, twenty months after the reform that created the co-presidency. Opposition analysts interpreted it as an attempt to secure the continuity of power within the presidential family. Also in that period, Nicaragua refused to receive Natasha Franceschi, the ambassador designated by US President Donald Trump, and Washington recalled its top representative in Managua, Elias Baumann, for consultations, according to El País. Neither Ortega nor Murillo has offered public explanations.

World.title: Princess Anne and Sports VIPs present at official opening of Falkland Islands Sport Complex
World.content:
Princess Anne and Sports VIPs present at official opening of Falkland Islands Sport Complex

10th Tuesday, November 2026 - 10:55 UTC Full article

HRH The Princess Royal and Vice Admiral Sir Tim Laurence will be present at the opening this Tuesday

The Falkland Islands Government and National Sports Council are proud to announce the official opening of the Falkland Islands’ new National Sports Complex, this Tuesday 10 November, in the presence of HRH The Princess Royal and Vice Admiral Sir Tim Laurence.

Attending VIPs from the world of sport include Katie Sadlier, CEO of Commonwealth Sport, and Andrew Inkster, Chair of the Island Games Association.

Other international sporting VIPs have offered their congratulations to the Falklands and the Sports Council on this long-awaited boost to provision for the Islands’ sporting community.

Lord Moynihan, Olympic rowing silver medalist and Chair of the British Olympic Association for London 2012, said “nothing could give me greater pleasure than learning of the new national sports facility there. What’s particularly impressive is it’s going to cover so many sports – and there’s already so much sporting activity in the Falklands. So this is a very special occasion for me, it’s a special occasion for the BOA, and I congratulate you all.”

Asanka Gurusinha, Sri Lankan World Cup-winning cricketer in 1996, expressed how impressed he was “that you have built a cricket pitch as well. Infrastructure plays a major part in the development of sport, and this investment will support all athletes to perform better and to have a dream to achieve their goals. I hope one day I can visit this beautiful place and see it for myself.”

Baroness Davies of Devonport, Olympic silver medalist and Commonwealth Games champion swimmer, offered her “many congratulations on your fantastic new sports complex in the Falkland Islands. What a brilliant thing that you’ve done. Young people need sport more than ever, we need to look after ourselves, we need to have fun, we need to get off our mobile phones. I wish you all the best.”

Sophie Kurzman, emerging Jackaroo with Australian bowls, competed alongside the Falklands earlier this year in Australia: “Opening up facilities like this and supporting their athletes is one of the most fundamental things a country can do for its athletes and itself. So a huge, heartfelt congratulations.”

Brigadier Charlie Harmer, Commander British Forces South Atlantic Islands, said he had “had the privilege of playing sport in lots of places, but to be able to play here, at the National Sports Complex, is a huge privilege for me, and indeed for the rest of my forces, be they Army, Navy or Royal Air Force. For us to have a chance to be a part of this community and continue to support the development of Falkland Islands sport is very, very important to us.

Numerous young Falkland Islanders competing overseas and at the national level have also sent messages of congratulation back to Stanley.

The National Sports Complex is a joint project between FIG, the National Sports Council, and private sponsors. Five and a half years in the making, it represents the first major investment in Falklands sporting facilities since the construction of the Stanley Leisure Centre and Swimming Pool some 30 years ago, with the long-term strategies of ensuring sport for all, achieving sporting excellence, and safeguarding and strengthening sport.

Chair of the National Sports Council, Mike Summers OBE, said “the creation of the National Sports Complex has already enabled additional developments like the cricket pitch and the archery Gold Centre. The 3G floodlit pitch already delivers significant enhancements in junior football participation, overall skill levels and the introduction of touch rugby. We look forward with huge anticipation to the use of the new sports hall to provide opportunities in a wide range of existing and new sporting activities, and providing a key focus for community development. Whilst enhancements to sports assets and outcomes has been our primary driver, this development also offers significant opportunities to those who manage the health of the Falklands population, with exercise tailored to all ages and abilities, and to all sectors of society. This is a major investment in sport, but most important of all it is an investment in our community.”

Steve Dent, FIG’s Director of Development and Commercial Services, said he was “absolutely delighted to see the National Sports Complex opening its doors. This is a hugely positive development for the Falkland Islands and, most importantly, for the next generation of young athletes. It will provide an expanded range of opportunities for young people to discover new sports, develop their skills, challenge themselves and reach their full potential. I am excited to see the breadth of opportunities this facility will create and the positive impact it will have on sport and physical activity in our community for many years to come.”

Marcus Morrison, Stanley Leisure Centre Manager, said “it is incredibly exciting to see the National Sports Complex completed and ready to open its doors to the community. As Manager, it is a proud moment to see a facility that will create new opportunities for people across the Falkland Islands and help meet the growing demand for sport and physical activity, complementing the already popular Stanley Leisure Centre. What excites me most is the potential to welcome teams and athletes from around the world, showcasing both our sporting ambitions and the unique community spirit of the Falkland Islands.”

The facilities now on offer will contribute to health and wellbeing in the Islands, and the huge support we get through the Falklands’ engagement with international competitions like the Island Games and Commonwealth Games.

The complex encompasses a floodlit all-weather football/rugby pitch; an indoor centre for archery, bowls, and cricket nets; and a new 50x52m sports hall to cater for existing and new sports, including (Gl)ice-hockey, indoor football, basketball, netball, volleyball, tennis, table tennis, weightlifting, and climbing. Exercise studios will also facilitate yoga, Pilates, dance exercise and ballet, as well as spin classes.

The sports hall additionally incorporates changing rooms, office and storage areas, a mezzanine viewing area, and a potential café area; and the all-weather pitch is equipped with spectator stands and toilets.

All of these works, other than specialist installation supervision, have been delivered by local contractors and suppliers.

The facility as a whole is already reaping considerable rewards, including burgeoning youth attendance, new women’s and girls’ teams in several sports, and fresh qualifications and training in various disciplines.

MLA Roger Spink, portfolio holder for Development and Commercial Services, said “the new sports facility and all-weather pitch funded by the Falkland Islands Government, as well as considerable contributions from the private sector which enhanced its facilities, together with the Falklands companies involved in its construction, shows what can be achieved by teamwork. The construction led by the NSC Chair and his team will provide a range of first-class facilities for a wide range of sport in our community, improving physical health, mental resilience, and social connection. I’m sure I echo the thoughts of the entire community in saying how delighted we are to be able to welcome Her Royal Highness and Sir Tim back to the Islands for this official opening.”

The National Sports Complex will go a long way to giving our sportsmen and -women the proper conditions in which to enjoy a wide range of sports and exercise programs, and better prepare for international events.

World.title: UK Defense minister admits Special Forces under mounting pressure and legal scrutiny
World.content:
UK Defense minister admits Special Forces under mounting pressure and legal scrutiny

10th Tuesday, November 2026 - 10:48 UTC Full article

Mr Streeting spoke to BFBS Forces News at his first Remembrance Sunday service as defense secretary. Picture: BFBS

Britain’s Defense Secretary Wes Streeting has acknowledged the mounting pressures facing UK Special Forces (UKSF) amid ongoing legal scrutiny, as he attended his first Remembrance Sunday service since taking up the role.

Asked by BFBS Forces News what he promises service personnel to meet the challenges ahead, Mr Streeting pointed to members of UKSF whose service often goes “unseen and unsung.”

“Today, they live under a cloud, worrying about whether they are going to be persecuted rather than thanked for their service,” he said. “Those are things I need to put right – there's going to be a process; it's not simple.”

“But on days like today [Remembrance Sunday], they galvanize me, and they galvanize the entire government around our responsibility and our duty to stand by our armed forces, by our veterans and their families.”

Acknowledging there was “much more to do”, the defense secretary said he was looking forward to working closely with the Armed Forces community to “make good on the commitment that we owe them”.

Mr Streeting's words echo the growing unrest and anxiety among UKSF members, following escalating waves of retroactive legal security. Central to this is the Independent Inquiry relating to Afghanistan.

Chaired by Lord Justice Sir Charles Haddon-Cave, the public inquiry is examining operations carried out by the Special Air Service (SAS) between mid-2010 and mid-2013.

It is investigating allegations that SAS members executed men and children during detention raids, that unlawful conduct was concealed, and that military police subsequently failed to investigate properly.

The inquiry could lead to further criminal investigations into the alleged killings and any cover-up. It can establish facts and recommend further action, but any prosecution would be separate. (BFBS)

World.title: UK with eyes from space: launches its second military satellite, Titania
World.content:
UK with eyes from space: launches its second military satellite, Titania

10th Tuesday, November 2026 - 10:44 UTC Full article

UK launches Titania, giving the Armed Forces improved observation from space, along with new trial network of ground sensors to monitor threats to UK satellites.

Britain has a new pair of eyes in space, with the successful launch of British-built military satellite Titania. The launch – completed last month from California on an Space X rocket– will further help the Armed Forces coordinate their efforts on and above Earth, by improving their ability to observe military activity on Earth from space.

Titania is the second satellite in the UK’s growing constellation of military satellites in orbit, following the successful launch of Tyche in October and will be operated by UK Space Command as part of the ISTARI program.

Like Tyche, Titania weighs around 100kg – about the size of a washing machine – and orbits the Earth every ninety minutes, travelling at twenty-seven thousand kilometers per hour.

The successful launch comes as the Ministry of Defense (MOD) also stands up Project Inaros, a new trial of an advanced network of sensors designed to monitor space from three sites around the world.

Secretary of State for Defense Wes Streeting MP said: “The new space age is here. Space underpins everything from weather forecasts and financial transactions to sat-navs and mobile phone connections, and it is critical for our national security and military operations.

“Having Titania now in orbit and Project Inaros stepping up how we watch over our satellites means we can see threats sooner, making the UK safer.

“Titania and Inaros are British-built and British-designed, backed by more than £3 billion of investment in space capabilities. That means highly skilled jobs across the UK, a stronger industrial base, and a more secure United Kingdom”.

Air Chief Marshal Sir Harv Smyth, the Chief of the Air Staff, said: “The ability to observe the Earth from space is critical to both national resilience and military advantage. This will be demonstrated by Tyche and Titania, alongside Juno and Oberon in the years ahead.

“We will monitor these vital satellites using state-of-the-art technology around the world, including our Inaros sensors – to ensure our Armed Forces can fight and win wherever they are.

“Under the ISTARI program, MOD is delivering satellites and supporting ground systems to expand space-based intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, giving British troops around the world an operational advantage.

“Titania was designed and built in Hampshire by the partnership of Defense Science and Technology Laboratory (Dstl) and BAE Systems as part of a £9.5 million contract, and will be followed by satellites Juno, with SSTL, and Oberon, with Airbus Defense and Space.

Andrea Thompson, Managing Director, BAE Systems Digital Intelligence & Land, said: “This program highlights the strength of the UK’s sovereign space capability and the critical role it plays in protecting the nation. Building on our established heritage in space, we are proud to be investing in advanced technologies, strengthening specialist skills and supporting highly skilled jobs across the UK.

“As a trusted partner to Government, we remain committed to delivering innovative space solutions that enhance the nation’s resilience, security and prosperity for the long term”.

Dr. Paul Hollinshead, Chief Executive Officer, Dstl, said: “Dstl has been at the heart of Titania, from the original concept, through Science and Technology investment, technical development, program delivery, and successful launch.

“The achievement reflects the expertise, resilience, and dedication of the Dstl team and showcases the value of long-term Defense Science and Technology investment, delivering mission success for our armed forces.

“Project Inaros will trial three ground-based neuromorphic sensors, developed by British Australian company Optera in partnership with the National Security Strategic Investment Fund, to monitor movements in space from sites in the UK, Australia, and British facilities on the island of Cyprus.

“This cutting-edge technology, which mimics biological processes by detecting changes in light, could be developed to be an early warning system to spot unusual or threatening activity near UK satellites. Information gathered by Inaros will help UK Space Command units, like No. 1 Space Operations Squadron, No. 2 Space Warning Squadron, and the new No. 3 Space Effects Squadron, to safeguard the UK satellites which guide British ships, connect mobile phones and warn of missile attacks”.

Titania and Inaros will help deliver on the recognition in the Strategic Defense Review that space is increasingly vital to the UK’s national security and daily life. The work is part of the £3bn committed by the Defense Investment Plan for space-based capabilities to protect UK assets in space and strengthen deterrence on Earth. The DIP has committed £298 billion of spending over the next four years.

World.title: Falklands Sports Complex, the joint effort of Government and private sector companies
World.content:
Falklands Sports Complex, the joint effort of Government and private sector companies

10th Tuesday, November 2026 - 10:38 UTC Full article

The National Sports Council, NSC, has delivered this project as a community service at no fee; the Falklands Government has provided the funding for design, procurement and construction

The opening of the new multi-sports Falkland Islands National Sports Complex makes the Islands’ community reflect on the joint effort that brought this to fruition.

The National Sports Council, NSC, has delivered this project as a community service at no fee; the Falklands Government has provided the funding for design, procurement and construction, supplemented by major donations from private sector companies. Access, parking and services has been provided by FIG under a separate contract.

Local design company Ajax Ltd. were retained to provide design and engineering services, and have themselves sub-contracted architectural services, design and project assistance to Arch Henderson Ltd from Aberdeen.

The Complex is estimated to have cost in the range of £5 million.

The NSC has one paid part-time employee to provide project management services, and the NSC Project Board oversaw the project, interfacing as required with the FIG Joint Supervisory Committee. Local company SG Accounts provides project accountancy services. All of the works, other than specialist installation supervision, have been delivered by local contractors and suppliers.

World.title: Aguascalientes students take top prizes at international robotics competition
World.content:
Student teams from the north-central Mexican state of Aguascalientes earned three awards at an international robotics competition in Germany over the weekend.

The Aguascalientes team, nicknamed Lanceros Overclock, won the high school division (ages 14 to 20) of Robo Shuttle at ROBOchæmpions, held Saturday and Sunday in the city of Lörrach.

Robo Shuttle is an event in which the budding scientists build and program autonomous robots to follow a marked course while transporting pingpong balls.

The team NexumAMG finished second in the same event and division, while the MagiBot squad took second in the middle school division (ages 11 to 14) of Robo Clash — in which team-built robots face off in a battle arena.

Competition rules required teams of two to four students.

Separately, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum honored students from Aguascalientes on Tuesday for an earlier victory in Japan, according to the state government.

In August, students from José Guadalupe Posada General Secondary School No. 6 won the FastBot Middle School division at the RoboRAVE world championship in Osaka. Next year’s RoboRAVE world championship is set for Houston.

Tuesday’s presidential recognition came during the National Meeting of Students in Science at the federal Education Ministry in Mexico City. The gathering recognized young people’s international achievements in science, mathematics, robotics and technology.

In Germany, Mexico’s winning teams represented three schools: Lanceros Overclock from the Lanceros de Aguascalientes state civic high school; NexumAMG from José Guadalupe Posada; and MagiBot from Magisterio Nacional Elementary School.

Overall, 16 students from Aguascalientes competed, but the names of the winners were not included in official results.

According to organizer Phaenovum — a student research center in Lörrach, Germany — the inaugural competition hosted teams from Mexico and Egypt in addition to regional competitors. It succeeded RoboRAVE Germany, a previous local version of RoboRAVE.

The organizer published results in five categories spanning races, robot duels, transport tasks and autonomous firefighting.

One challenge required robots to extinguish a candle flame autonomously.

Teams prepared and tested their robots Saturday before Sunday’s judging, awards ceremony and public demonstrations.

Aguascalientes students have also earned recognition elsewhere: José Guadalupe Posada students won two third-place awards at RoboRAVE in Silicon Valley in July 2025, while a Panamerican University team from the state finished sixth at RoboCup in Brazil that year with a search-and-rescue robot, according to the state government.

With reports from Futuro Bajío and Phaenovum

World.title: Auto parts sector posts best month on record
World.content:
The value of auto parts production in Mexico increased 9.1% year over year in August to reach US $11.118 billion, according to the National Auto Parts Industry (INA), a trade association.

That is the highest monthly production value on record for Mexico’s auto parts industry. A wide range of auto parts are made in Mexico, including electrical components, transmissions, engine parts, suspension components and clutches.

In the first eight months of 2026, the value of auto parts production in Mexico was $85.8 billion, according to INA, an increase of more than 8% compared to the same period of last year. Coahuila is Mexico’s top auto parts manufacturer, followed by Guanajuato and Nuevo León.

Presenting the latest data on auto parts production on Monday, INA’s head of economic studies, Julio Galván, said that Mexico’s auto parts sector is benefiting from the development of North American supply chains and the replacement of Asian imports with locally manufactured components.

Galván said that Mexico plays a “strategic role” in the North American supply chain. Unlike Mexican vehicles, auto parts made in Mexico can enter the United States tariff-free provided they comply with United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) rules. INA said last year that only about 8% of the nation’s parts manufacturers are not in compliance with USMCA regulations.

INA: Mexico’s auto parts exports exceeded $74 billion between January and August

INA reported that Mexico’s auto parts exports were worth $74.32 billion in the first eight months of 2026. Almost three-quarters of that total came from shipments to the United States.

Mexico imported auto parts worth $49.77 billion between January and August, leaving it with an auto parts trade surplus of $24.56 billion.

Galván said that Mexico and the United States have a “very strong” relationship in the auto parts trade, meeting each other’s needs in the automotive sector. However, the United States’ auto parts imports from Mexico decreased 1% in value year over year in the first eight months of the year to $54.35 billion, according to INA.

Despite that, Mexico remains the world’s top supplier of auto parts to the U.S., capturing almost 45% of that country’s total market for auto parts imports between January and August.

INA estimates that the total value of auto parts production in Mexico this year will be around $126 billion. The industry group predicts that Mexico’s 2026 auto parts exports will total $109 billion.

With reports from El Economista

World.title: In Mazatlán, García Harfuch announces US $48M security package for Sinaloa
World.content:
Listen to this article

Federal Security Minister Omar García Harfuch announced on Monday a 900-million-peso (US $48.2 million) security investment in Sinaloa, a state plagued by cartel violence.

García Harfuch announced the investment at an event in Mazatlán, where National Defense Minister Ricardo Trevilla Trejo pledged that the military won’t withdraw from Sinaloa until “conditions of peace” are reestablished in the state.

Part of the 900 million pesos will be used to purchase new vehicles and equipment for Sinaloa state police as well as municipal forces in Culiacán and Mazatlán. Money will also be used to bring a new highway surveillance center into operation.

In a social media post, García Harfuch said that the federal Security Ministry (SSPC) will supply 200 vehicles to police forces in Sinaloa. Among the vehicles will be armored pickup trucks, armored tactical vehicles and motorcycles. The Sinaloa government said in a statement that the vehicles are in addition to 100 police cars previously given to state police by federal authorities. The National Defense Ministry delivered an additional 80 vehicles to Sinaloa police on Monday.

In addition to 200 vehicles, the SSPC will supply three surveillance drones and radio equipment to state police and the municipal forces in Culiacán, the state capital, and Mazatlán, Sinaloa’s top tourism destination.

García Harfuch said that the vehicles and equipment will be delivered to the police forces on Dec. 15. He said that the C4 Carretero, as the new highway surveillance center is called, will begin operations the same day.

On X, García Harfuch wrote that the C4 Carretero will strengthen surveillance along 250 kilometers of highway in the “Culiacán-Mazatlán-Durango corridor.”

The surveillance center will operate with 240 “intelligent monitoring points“, 720 cameras and 30 license plate readers, the security minister said.

Speaking at a military facility in Mazatlán, García Harfuch also said that the federal government was signing new security collaboration agreements with Sinaloa Governor Graciela Domínguez Nava. On X, he pledged that federal forces would “continue to work together [with local authorities] to make progress in the pacification of the state and provide greater security for Sinaloa families.”

García Harfuch also wrote that “with the support of the National Intelligence Center, intelligence and investigative capabilities will be expanded through the addition of new specialized units in the state.”

More than 2 years after cartel violence escalated, Sinaloa remains one of Mexico’s most violent states

Much of the violence in Sinaloa since late 2024 has been related to fighting between the “Los Chapitos” and “Los Mayos” factions of the Sinaloa Cartel. A long-running dispute between the two factions escalated in September 2024, around six weeks after Joaquín Guzmán López, one of the sons of convicted drug lord Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán, kidnapped Sinaloa Cartel kingpin Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada and forced him onto a private plane that flew both men to New Mexico, where they were arrested by U.S. authorities.

While homicides have declined in Sinaloa this year, the state remains among the most violent in Mexico.

Data presented by the federal government at President Claudia Sheinbaum’s Tuesday morning press conference showed that there were 1,156 homicides in Sinaloa in the first 10 months of 2026, a reduction of 18.8% compared to the same period of last year. Despite the decline, Sinaloa ranked as the fourth most violent state in Mexico in terms of total homicides between January and October. Almost 8% of all homicides in Mexico this year were perpetrated in the state.

Domínguez, the Sinaloa state governor, acknowledged on Monday that efforts to achieve peace have not yet succeeded.

“We haven’t achieved what we all want — to restore peace — but we are working tirelessly and with total dedication,” she said at the event in Mazatlán.

Domínguez became interim governor of Sinaloa in August after Governor Rubén Rocha Moya stepped down for a second time. In April, U.S. prosecutors formally accused Rocha Moya and nine other current and former Mexican officials of drug trafficking and related weapons offenses, alleging that they colluded with the Sinaloa Cartel. Mexican officials have said that U.S. authorities haven’t provided sufficient evidence to warrant the arrest of the 77-year-old ex-governor, who denies any wrongdoing.

More than 22,000 federal troops are deployed in Sinaloa

Trevilla Trejo said on Monday that 22,667 Defense Ministry (Defensa) personnel are currently deployed in Sinaloa. Both the Mexican Army and the National Guard fall under the ministry’s authority. Military planes, helicopters, drones and over 1,700 vehicles are part of Defensa’s deployment in Sinaloa.

More than 12,000 of the federal troops are deployed in Mazatlán while almost 6,500 are based in Culiacán, according to information presented by Trevilla Trejo. Just over 4,000 troops are deployed in other parts of Sinaloa.

For his part, García Harfuch reported that more than 3,000 people were arrested in Sinaloa between Oct. 1, 2024 — the date Sheinbaum was sworn in as president — and Oct. 31, 2026. He said that authorities seized 7,200 firearms and 145 tonnes of drugs in the state in the same period, while 2,600 clandestine drug laboratories were dismantled.

Business group proposes reducing taxes in Sinaloa

Insecurity in Sinaloa has taken a toll on the state’s economy this year, although there were signs of recovery in the second quarter, during which there was 5% year-over-year growth.

Still, according to the Mexican Employers Federation (Coparmex), 44,000 jobs have been lost in the state over the past year. The business group also says that the state’s employment informality and labor poverty rates have risen, while families’ incomes have declined.

In that context, Coparmex released a statement on Monday under the title “Sinaloa demands security, employment and an urgent economic recovery strategy.”

The business group proposed an “agenda of action” made up of “six priorities” aimed at restoring Sinaloa’s “economic dynamism.” Among the priorities are “strengthening security to restore investment and jobs” and boosting “governance and public-private coordination for the recovery of Sinaloa.”

In the statement’s section on the latter priority, Coparmex calls on the Sinaloa and federal governments to “analyze extraordinary economic and fiscal support measures that help preserve jobs, avoid closures of businesses and maintain productive activities in the regions that have been most affected by the insecurity crisis.”

“In this context, we have proposed the implementation of a temporary fiscal stimulus scheme that includes a reduction in the IVA [value-added] rate from 16% to 8%, under conditions similar to those in the border region, as well as a 50% reduction in income tax for companies and productive activities that are currently facing a particularly adverse environment,” Coparmex said.

IVA is 8% in Mexico’s northern and southern border regions. It remains to be seen how authorities will respond to Coparmex’s call for taxes to be cut in Sinaloa as well.

With reports from El Economista, Animal Político, Río Doce, López-Dóriga Digital and Línea Directa Portal

World.title: Pemex begins fracking feasibility studies in Coahuila
World.content:
Mexico is conducting feasibility studies in Coahuila that could lead to the use of hydraulic fracturing — fracking — to extract gas from under the northern border state.

Petróleos Mexicanos (Pemex, the state-owned oil company) has drilled a well in the Coahuilan community of Hidalgo to assess the characteristics and availability of the water and to ensure that the water source is separate from that used for human consumption, Pemex Director General Juan Carlos Carpio Fragoso told members of Congress on Monday.

“We are waiting for the results that will confirm the characteristics of the brackish water and verify that there is no connection to freshwater aquifers,” Carpio Fragoso said.

Water availability is one of the conditions established by the government to allow fracking to take place in Mexico. “If there is not enough safe drinking water, the project will not move forward,” Carpio said.

Fracking is a hydrocarbon extraction method that involves drilling deep into the ground and injecting water, sand and chemicals under pressure to fracture the rock, thereby releasing gas or oil. The method can help operators access hard-to-reach deposits.

The Sheinbaum administration is considering expanding fracking operations in Mexico to reduce the country’s dependence on gas imports, particularly amid global price volatility and uncertainty about the future of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement.

Mexico currently imports up to 75% of its gas supply from the United States.

A government technical committee assessed the Burgos and Sabinas-Burro-Picacho basins in the northern states of Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas and found they have the greatest potential for fracking operations, with prospective resources of 120.8 million cubic feet, as reported by the magazine Expansión.

However, experts believe that reducing Mexico’s gas import dependence will require developing 24 entirely new natural gas exploration and production projects to supply an additional 9 billion cubic feet per day, with an estimated required investment of $108 billion.

Mexico’s Environment Minister Alicia Bárcena said in October that there is a “series of restrictions under which fracking cannot be carried out at this time,” including water availability. If the study area of Hidalgo, Coahuila, yields sufficient availability of deep, saline water, then fracking pilot tests could potentially proceed.

With reports from López-Dóriga Digital, Expansión, Excelsior and Reuters

World.title: Mexico and China launch joint archaeological project in Yucatán
World.content:
Mexico and China have agreed to an international research and cooperation initiative that aims to expand knowledge and contribute to the preservation of Maya archaeological heritage.

On Nov. 6, Mexico’s Culture Ministry and the National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) formalized the Yaxcopoil-Tanmul Archaeological Project, a collaborative research initiative involving Mexican specialists and those from Shandong University in China.

The initiative was presented in Yaxcopoil, a small community in the state of Yucatán located within the southern inner ring of the massive Chicxulub impact crater.

In attendance were the Chinese ambassador to Mexico, Chen Daojiang, INAH’s technical secretary José Luis Perea González and Yucatán Culture Minister Silvia Patricia Martín, as well as researchers and students from Shandong University, ejido (communally-owned land) authorities and representatives of nearby communities.

A day later, Yucatán Governor Joaquín Díaz Mena presented details of the project proposal to the Chinese Embassy with the goal of expanding bilateral cooperation and strengthening historical ties that date back to the 19th century when Chinese families began migrating to the peninsula. More than 200,000 people in Yucatán have Chinese ancestry.

Díaz Mena said he hopes to expand exchange programs between universities in Yucatán and China, and promote joint research and technological development projects.

Another objective is to diversify exports and expand the presence of Yucatecan products in the Chinese market.

Ambassador Chen Daojiang expressed his government’s willingness to strengthen trade, tourism, cultural and educational ties with Yucatán, as well as explore opportunities for collaboration in technology, innovation and sustainability.

The Yaxcopoil-Tanmul project arose after local residents expressed misgivings about the opening of a quarry early this year, eventually calling on INAH to investigate the extractive venture.

INAH sided with the community and the quarry proposal was quashed, with INAH favoring the importance of preserving the links between cultural heritage and the communities that inhabit the neighboring territories.

“Archaeological heritage is not separate from society; it belongs to a shared history and represents a collective responsibility,” Perea González said. “No project can be considered successful if its results remain locked away in specialized publications and do not return to the community that made its realization possible.”

The collaboration with Shandong University will allow researchers and students from both nations to share experiences and knowledge about Maya archaeology, and will strengthen academic ties between Mexico and China.

With reports from 24 Horas, Once Noticias and Reporte Indigo

World.title: Openbank: Mexico’s new Digital Economy Law could reduce cash use by up to 50%
World.content:
Mexico’s new Digital Economy Law could conceivably reduce cash use by 50% as it increases access to credit, according to Juan José Galnares, CEO of Santander’s Openbank México.

However, Galnares cautioned that the law could be a victim of its own success if its reduction of cash use is implemented too aggressively.

To that end, Nitin Prabhu, global head of Openbank — a 100% digital bank with 1.6 million customers in Mexico — proposed first digitizing only government payments. He also proposed making it cheaper and easier for small businesses to accept electronic payments by, for example, reducing or eliminating the charges merchants pay to accept and process electronic payments, known as merchant acquiring fees.

President Claudia Sheinbaum has sought to allay concerns regarding the new law, formally the Digital Economy Law for Digital and Electronic Payments, particularly with regard to how exactly it will prohibit the use of cash.

Although Sheinbaum said that the goal of the new law — enacted last week — is to reduce the use of cash in Mexico, she insisted cash would not be phased out.

Instead, the goal is to increase digital payments, especially by identifying specific sectors in which the acceptance of digital and electronic payment methods will be the only form of payment.

For instance, cash payments at highway toll booths and gas stations will be eliminated by the end of this year (the latter’s goal being the reduction of fuel theft and fuel smuggling).

Furthermore, the Digital Economy Law establishes that when a contingency arises that makes it impossible to carry out digital transactions, payment in cash or check will be allowed.

Cybersecurity company IQSEC said the new law presents challenges beyond technological adoption, as it involves strengthening the security of electronic transactions, protecting user information and ensuring the continuity of services in the face of potential incidents.

Still, the administration insists the advantages — including access to credit — of the Digital Economy Law are worth the challenges. When a person starts paying or receiving money digitally, these transactions generate a history that financial institutions can consider when evaluating a loan application.

With reports from Expansión and La Jornada

World.title: México state logs sharp rise in homicides as national rate halves: Tuesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

📉 Homicides down 50% from AMLO’s final month: National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported an average of 43.4 homicides per day in October, compared to 86.9 in September 2024. It was the lowest daily rate for any October in 12 years. Homicides fell 22.9% from October 2025 and 54.5% from October 2020.

National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported an average of 43.4 homicides per day in October, compared to 86.9 in September 2024. It was the lowest daily rate for any October in 12 years. Homicides fell 22.9% from October 2025 and 54.5% from October 2020. 🚨 México state tops homicide rankings after sharp revision: The state recorded 1,564 homicides in the first 10 months of 2026, or 10.6% of the national total. That is up from 818 at the end of September, but only 160 homicides were recorded in October, according to preliminary data, meaning totals from earlier months were revised upward. Officials didn’t comment on the increase.

The state recorded 1,564 homicides in the first 10 months of 2026, or 10.6% of the national total. That is up from 818 at the end of September, but only 160 homicides were recorded in October, according to preliminary data, meaning totals from earlier months were revised upward. Officials didn’t comment on the increase. 🇲🇽 Seven states account for over half of homicides: Guanajuato (1,213), Baja California (1,203), Sinaloa (1,156), Chihuahua (1,103), Guerrero (804) and Morelos (723) followed México state for total homicides in the first 10 months of 2026. The seven states accounted for 52.5% of the 14,799 homicides nationwide.

Guanajuato (1,213), Baja California (1,203), Sinaloa (1,156), Chihuahua (1,103), Guerrero (804) and Morelos (723) followed México state for total homicides in the first 10 months of 2026. The seven states accounted for 52.5% of the 14,799 homicides nationwide. 📊 Homicides decline in every state: Compared to January-October 2025, homicides fell 77% in San Luis Potosí, the largest reduction. Nayarit, Quintana Roo, Baja California Sur and Nuevo León recorded declines of more than 50%.

Compared to January-October 2025, homicides fell 77% in San Luis Potosí, the largest reduction. Nayarit, Quintana Roo, Baja California Sur and Nuevo León recorded declines of more than 50%. 🚔 74,033 arrests for high-impact crimes since October 2024: Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said authorities also seized 37,625 firearms and 588.6 tonnes of drugs, and dismantled 2,841 clandestine drug labs.

Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said authorities also seized 37,625 firearms and 588.6 tonnes of drugs, and dismantled 2,841 clandestine drug labs. 🙌 “There’s no one like them anywhere in the world”: Sheinbaum praised her security cabinet and asked which country of Mexico’s size and population, facing similar organized crime problems, has cut homicides in half in two years. “[There are] none,” she said.

Why today’s mañanera matters

Federal officials presented the government’s monthly security report at President Sheinbaum’s Tuesday morning press conference.

The most striking statistic was that México state — a state that includes many municipalities in the metropolitan area of Mexico City — recorded 1,564 homicides in the first 10 months of 2026. What makes the figure remarkable is that it is 91.2% higher than the homicide total the government reported for México state in the first nine months of the year.

On Tuesday morning, officials didn’t comment on the dramatic increase that catapulted México state to the top of Mexico’s homicide rankings. However, it would appear that homicides have been significantly undercounted in the state this year and that a correction was recently made. The homicide data reported by the federal government on a monthly basis is compiled from statistics it receives from Attorney General’s Offices in Mexico’s 32 federal entities.

The data presented today shows that about one in ten homicides in Mexico so far this year was perpetrated in México state.

Another striking statistic from today’s mañanera is that more than 74,000 people have been arrested for allegedly committing high-impact crimes since Sheinbaum took office on Oct. 1, 2024. In other words, there was an average of 97 arrests per day for high-impact crimes between the start of October 2024 and the end of last month.

Homicides declined 50% in October compared to last month of AMLO’s presidency

National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported that there was an average of 43.4 homicides per day in October, a decline of 50% compared to September 2024, the final month of Andrés Manuel López Obrador’s six-year term as president.

She highlighted that there was an average of 43 fewer homicides per day in October than in September 2024, when the daily average was 86.9.

Lowest October homicide rate in more than a decade

Figueroa presented a graph that showed that the daily homicide rate last month was the lowest of any October in the past 12 years.

Compared to October 2025, homicides declined 22.9% last month.

Compared to October 2020, when there was an average of 95.4 homicides per day, the reduction last month was 54.5%.

México state recorded the highest number of homicides between January and October

Figueroa reported that 52.5% of all homicides in Mexico in the first 10 months of 2026 were committed in just seven states.

She said that México state — Mexico’s most populous state — recorded the highest number of homicides among the country’s 32 federal entities.

Data presented by Figueroa showed that there were 1,564 homicides in México state between January and October, a figure that represents 10.6% of the national total.

México state’s homicide count increased from 818 at the end of September to 1,564 at the end of October, an increase of 746 in the space of a single month. Figueroa didn’t comment on the sharp increase. There were only 160 homicides in México state in October, according to preliminary data. The increase therefore reflects upward revisions to homicide totals in México state in earlier months this year, in addition to homicides reported in October.

In any case, México state now leads the country for homicides in 2026. According to data Figueroa presented on October 13, México state had the fifth-highest homicide count in the first nine months of 2026, behind Baja California, Guanajuato, Chihuahua and Sinaloa.

In the first 10 months of 2026, Guanajuato recorded the second-highest number of homicides, with 1,213, according to the latest data. That figure represents 8.2% of the 14,799 homicides reported in Mexico in the period.

The five states that recorded the next highest homicide counts in the first 10 months of 2026 were:

Baja California: 1,203 (8.1% of the national total)

Sinaloa: 1,156 (7.8%)

Chihuahua: 1,103 (7.5%)

Guerrero: 804 (5.4%)

Morelos: 723 (4.9%)

Oaxaca, Michoacán and Jalisco ranked eighth, ninth and tenth, respectively, for total homicides in the first ten months of 2026. Mexico City ranked 12th with 635 homicides.

Yucatán recorded the lowest number of homicides among Mexico’s 32 federal entities, with just 22 between January and October.

Homicides declined in every state in the first 10 months of 2026

Figueroa reported that homicides declined in every federal entity in the first 10 months of the year. Compared to the January-October period of last year, homicides fell 77% in San Luis Potosí, the largest reduction of any state.

Four other states recorded year-over-year declines in homicides of more than 50%. They were:

Nayarit: 71.8%

Quintana Roo: 57.7%

Baja California Sur: 54.1%

Nuevo León: 50.1%

Five other states recorded year-over-year declines of more than 40%. They were:

Zacatecas: 48.8%

Aguascalientes: 46.3%

Guanajuato: 45.6%

Sonora: 42.7%

Michoacán: 40.5%

Figueroa highlighted that homicides in Michoacán have declined since the implementation in November 2025 of Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice, an initiative devised in response to the assassination of Uruapan Mayor Carlos Manzo on Nov. 1, 2025, and general insecurity in the state.

Over 74,000 arrests since Sheinbaum took office

Security Minister Omar García Harfuch reported that 74,033 people were arrested for allegedly committing high-impact crimes between Oct. 1, 2024 and Oct. 31, 2026. Among the offenses classified as high-impact crimes are murder, kidnapping, violent robbery, rape and extortion.

According to the information presented by García Harfuch, authorities seized 37,625 firearms and 588.6 tonnes of drugs between Oct. 1, 2024, and Oct. 31, 2026.

In addition, authorities dismantled 2,841 clandestine drug laboratories in the same period.

García Harfuch said that 34 people have been arrested in connection with the “planning, execution and cover-up” of the assassination of Carlos Manzo. Among those detained are Ramón Ángel Álvarez Ayala, identified as the mastermind behind the crime, and his brother Rafael Álvarez Ayala, who was arrested in Guadalajara last Sunday after a shootout with Mexican Navy personnel.

The two brothers, known as “R1” and “R2,” are allegedly leaders of the “Los Rs” faction of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel.

‘There’s no one like them anywhere in the world’: Sheinbaum praises security officials

Sheinbaum told reporters that she is “extremely grateful to the security cabinet I chose.”

“There’s no one like them anywhere in the world,” she said, referring to officials such as García Harfuch, Defense Minister Ricardo Trevilla Trejo, Navy Minister Raymundo Pedro Morales Ángeles and Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez.

“… Tell me a country … of Mexico’s size and population, with problems such as those of Mexico in terms of organized crime, that has reduced homicides by half in two years,” Sheinbaum said.

“[There are] none,” she asserted.

World.title: MND Local San Miguel de Allende: Art, jazz and community causes
World.content:
Just as Día de Muertos passed into the rearview mirror in San Miguel de Allende, a host of other community events and activities popped up to help fill the void. An annual artisan fair is occupying the Jardín Principal, and the annual International Jazz & Blues Festival begins this week. Other special events include a three-day art experience next week and a pet sterilization nonprofit’s request for donations for a fundraising garage sale.

Read on for more about a few of the many community activities happening in and around San Miguel de Allende this month.

Wool and brass artisans take over the Jardín Principal

1 of 5

Dozens of local artisans working with wool and metal have set up booths around the Jardín Principal and will be there from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily through Nov. 15 to sell their work and show the public how these traditional crafts are produced.

Several of the artisans are demonstrating how they hand-weave rugs and other textile pieces, as well as shape sheets of metal into embossed frames for mirrors and other objects such as light fixtures, hearts and stars.

Ramiro Rodriguez Cordova is on hand with his 100% wool rugs, mats, table runners, bedspreads and curtains, which he weaves at his studio in Colonia Providencia. His “Los Tejedores” (“The Weavers”) business has been producing woven textiles for more than 35 years.

Handmade metal products from Arte de San Miguel include hearts in various designs and other creative metalwork produced by Yolanda Yáñez Trejo and Fabricio Mendoza Vásquez at their studio in Colonia San Felipe Neri. Their son, Maximilian, is staffing their booth to show and sell his parents’ designs.

The annual Wool and Brass Fair began in 1978 and was originally held in the Centro Cultural Ignacio Ramírez El Nigromante (Bellas Artes). The craft sector is considered a main mover of San Miguel’s economy, and exhibiting this work in one of the city’s major tourist destinations could help artisans sell 10 times more than in their traditional workshops.

Get ready for the annual Jazz & Blues Festival

The 32nd annual International Jazz & Blues Festival kicks off Wednesday, Nov. 11, at 1 p.m. with a free Didactic Jazz Concert featuring the Antonio Lozoya Jazz Trio at Casa El Nigromante, Umarán 28, in Centro.

The festival ends on Sunday, Nov. 15, with a tribute to Sting showcasing singer and actress Alicia González, the San Miguel Blues & Jazz Collective and other guests. That show starts at 6 p.m. at the Instituto Allende auditorium, Ancha de San Antonio 22.

In between, the festival schedule includes free films about Benny Goodman and Chet Baker, plus three other paid-admission concerts. For additional information on the free events and to purchase tickets for the paid-admission ones, go here.

Three-day immersive art experience coming soon

Art of the Story, a nonprofit arts organization in San Miguel, is producing SPARK, a three-day immersive experience of creative discovery for adults. It is being held Nov. 17-19 at La Casona Convention Center, Josefina Orozco 2, Colonia San Antonio.

The event will include exhibitions, presentations, spoken word, poetry, performance, conversation and hands-on experimentation, the group said, and will be presented in English.

According to Art of the Story, the goal of the event is to present “a welcoming space for participants to discover what happens when creative expectations are set aside” and not to teach people how to become artists.

Passes range from 300 to 1,000 pesos depending on the desired length of time at the event. More information is available here.

Wanted: Donations for Rosey’s Wish benefit garage sale

Rosey’s Wish SMA, which provides free spay and neuter services for pets in rural areas outside San Miguel, is looking for gently used donations for its upcoming benefit garage sale scheduled for Nov. 28.

Sale of the donated items (no books or clothing, please) will help the nonprofit exceed its recently reached goal of providing 2,000 free sterilizations this year through its mobile clinic.

Particularly helpful are household items, electronics, bedding, items for pets, kitchenware and tools. Donated garage sale items may be picked up or dropped off. More information about how to donate can be found on the group’s Facebook page.

Rosey’s Wish is named for a sick and malnourished street dog rescued in October 2023 at the Presa la Cantera reservoir a few miles from downtown. She was rescued and fostered and then found a permanent home.

Cathy Siegner is an independent journalist based in San Miguel and Montana. She has journalism degrees from the University of Oregon and Northwestern University.

What to See & Do

WEDNESDAY IN SÃO PAULO

TODAY’S PICK — PAULISTA CULTURE DAY Japan House, then MASP, on Avenida Paulista Start at Japan House São Paulo on Avenida Paulista, open Tue–Fri 10am–6pm. Entry is free, so it is the easy first stop. Walk to MASP, also on Paulista, which is open Wednesday to Sunday 10am–6pm. Tickets cost R$85 today, as the free day is Tuesday. Arrive at MASP by early afternoon to leave a full two hours before closing at 6pm. The Metrô fare is R$5.40 a journey. Both venues are on the Paulista corridor, so you can do them on foot with a coffee break between.

OUTDOORS — IBIRAPUERA Parque Ibirapuera, in Vila Mariana, is open 5am–midnight daily and is free. It works as a morning or late-afternoon walk if the sky stays dry. MAC USP, inside the park, is open Tue–Sun 10am–9pm and is free. It is a good indoor fallback if rain arrives.

Latin America is anxious about money and wary of Washington, and today every country is counting the cost in its own currency.

The Continent’s Mood Today

Latin America woke on 11 November worried about prices and the dollar. Front pages in Brazil and Chile both led with the US House vote of 211 to 204 on 10 November to send an impeachment bid against Pete Hegseth, the US Defense Secretary, to a committee, which effectively stops it.

The charges include US strikes on boats in the Caribbean, so the region reads the case as a verdict on Washington’s military reach.

Brazil – Counting Reais It Does Not Have

The government has outlined about R$80bn (about US$14bn) of spending savings for the 2027 budget. The debate includes how to treat the constitutional health and education spending floors.

The 2027 budget bill promises a primary surplus of R$18.6bn (about US$3.3bn). The Senate’s fiscal watchdog, the IFI, expects a deficit of R$86.1bn (about US$15.4bn) instead.

Simone Tebet, a former planning minister, has argued that changing the floors would save little, about R$4bn to R$5bn (US$0.7bn to US$0.9bn) in health. Behind the argument sits an old fear of a fiscal cliff, and the real’s slide on 10 November showed that the fear is live.

The budget fight matters abroad because it shapes how much the government must borrow, and therefore how much investors want to be paid. At the central bank, the rate-setting committee held the benchmark Selic rate at 13.75% on 4 November and promised caution, so borrowing costs stay high.

For a foreigner in Brazil, expect a weaker real and tighter credit to last through the budget debate.

Mexico – Hope on the Road, Strain at the Till

A migrant caravan of about 900 to 1,000 people, mostly Hondurans, crossed into southern Mexico on Friday 6 November, heading for Tapachula. They hope for a path north, and the road is long.

At home, October inflation rose to 3.75% and producer prices climbed 5.60%. Car output fell 17.7% in the month, which is a worry for factory towns.

Shoppers are bracing for Buen Fin, Mexico’s annual discount weekend, which opens on Friday 13 November. For a foreigner in Mexico, Buen Fin bargains are real, but check the price history before you buy.

Paraguay – A Locked Door and a Hollow Room

Paraguay has a new president and a former one in custody. Pedro Alliana replaced the removed Santiago Peña on 6 November, and on Monday 9 November he asked ministers and agency heads to offer their posts.

A judge ordered Peña held before trial in the case of Ueno Bank, a digital lender with almost three million clients; he has not been convicted. Prosecutors raided his summer house on 8 November, and a hidden vault there stayed shut on Monday.

Until the vault opens and the court case moves, the questions stay unanswered. The mood is distrust of institutions.

For a foreigner in Paraguay, expect political noise and keep banking and property paperwork scrupulously clean.

Chile – Volcano Alerts and a Falling Peso

The peso weakened on 10 November. Chile’s October trade surplus came in at US$2.55bn, a cushion, but one that does not calm nerves.

Sernageomin, Chile’s geology and mining agency, keeps the Nevados de Chillán volcano on yellow alert after repeated eruptive pulses, and it has not ruled out new events of similar or greater energy. Chileans in the south know volcanoes well and watch the alerts closely.

The peso’s slide fed the same worry about prices that runs through the region today. For a foreigner in Chile, a weaker peso makes dollars go further, but check Sernageomin alerts before travelling south.

Argentina – Waiting for a Number

On Thursday Indec, Argentina’s statistics agency, publishes October inflation, and the market expects 1.8%. Disinflation has slowed, and households feel it.

Households are watching every price tag under President Milei.The mood is impatience, with households wanting the lower prices they were promised. For a foreigner in Argentina, expect prices to keep rising roughly 2% a month, so budget in dollars and review rents often.

Colombia – A Peso Under Pressure

October inflation edged up to 6.3%, and the peso stayed weak. Colombians feel the weaker peso in imported goods and in rents, and the inflation figure keeps households watching prices.

The 2027 election campaign is never far from the conversation. For a foreigner in Colombia, a weak peso helps visitors, while 6.3% inflation raises rents and local costs.

The Shared Mood

From São Paulo to Santiago, people spent 10 November checking what their money buys. Currencies fell, budgets were argued over and inflation numbers were awaited.

Under it runs a familiar memory of cycles that end in austerity. Today the hope is that this time the adjustment arrives before the crisis does.

Anxious about prices and currencies, which weakened against the dollar on 10 November.

The government has outlined about R$80bn (about US$14bn) of spending savings for the 2027 budget, and it is arguing over how to treat health and education spending floors.

Indec publishes it on Thursday 12 November. The market expects 1.8%.

01 Yields touch the 5% line, and gold pays

Wall Street slipped in the latest session. The S&P 500 closed at 7,521 (-0.38%), the Dow at 52,232 (-0.30%) and the Nasdaq Composite at 25,066 (-0.74%).

The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.983% (+2.45%), a hair below 5%. The dollar index climbed to 102.2 (+0.6%), and gold fell 2.41% to $4,039 an ounce.

Gold pays no interest, so a higher yield and a firmer dollar hit it hardest. The VIX eased to 19.46 (-2.31%), which reads as repricing rather than panic.

US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October after seasonal adjustment, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics said, but it could not publish a 12-month rate because of a gap in 2025 data. The CPI s.a. index was forecast at 337 against 336.3 before, while the core inflation rate and the Cleveland CPI readings are not yet in our calendar feed.

Energy supply is tightening quietly. The EIA reported commercial crude stocks at 409.8 million barrels for the week to 30 October, down 0.9 million, and distillates at 99.3 million, down 3.6 million (eia.gov).

02 The Fed speaks six times on Thursday

Hammack, Barr, Goolsbee, Daly, Schmid and Williams all speak on Thursday. With the 10-year near 5%, investors will listen for any sign that officials accept tighter financial conditions.

The Treasury also sells 30-year bonds, and the previous auction cleared at 5.618%. A weak sale would push long yields higher and add to the pressure on emerging markets.

The budget balance is expected at a deficit of 298, against 27 the previous month. That is a reminder of how much debt Washington still has to place.

Housing already feels the strain. The 30-year mortgage rate stood at 7.18% in the prior reading, and existing home sales are forecast at 3.98 million, against 3.99 million.

03 Brazil: a Selic on hold, and a dollar that will not help

On 4 November Copom held the Selic at 13.75%, ending five straight quarter-point cuts. The vote was unanimous, and the bank urged “serenity and caution” while citing a worsening external environment.

A yield near 5% in Washington and a stronger dollar are exactly that pressure. They make it harder for Brazil to cut without weakening the real.

Inflation leaves little room anyway. IPCA stood at 4.58% in the twelve months to September, above the 4.5% ceiling of the tolerance band, and the Focus survey sees 5.2% for 2026.

Thursday’s October IPCA is forecast at 0.26% for the month and 4.74% over twelve months. Copom meets again on 8 and 9 December, and a hot print would make a hold the base case.

China offers a counterweight for commodity exporters. October imports rose 41.6% from a year earlier, against a 32% consensus, while exports grew 35.2%.

Strong buying from Asia helps Brazil, though the narrower trade surplus of US$105.28 billion (712.78 billion yuan, against 859 billion expected) shows how much of it is inbound.

Ongoing: A worsening external environment, a firm dollar and Brazil’s inflation above its 4.5% ceiling. All three limit how far the Selic can fall from 13.75%.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does gold fall when Treasury yields rise?

Gold pays no interest, so a higher yield makes holding it costlier. A firmer dollar adds to the pressure, as it makes gold dearer for foreign buyers.

Why do US yields matter for Brazil?

Higher Treasury yields draw money away from emerging markets and tend to weaken the real. That limits how far the central bank can cut the Selic.

What is the Selic rate now?

Copom held it at 13.75% on 4 November, ending five consecutive quarter-point cuts. The vote was unanimous.

Is Brazilian inflation under control?

Not yet. IPCA was 4.58% in the twelve months to September, above the 4.5% ceiling, and Thursday’s October reading is forecast at 4.74%.

When is the next Copom meeting?

Copom meets next on 9 December 2026. Policy is expected to stay restrictive, according to the bank’s own statement.

Think of Brazil’s morning as a tug of war between a strong dollar abroad and a strong oil company at home. The real, Brazil’s currency, has lost ground for four sessions in a row, and the dollar sits 0.1% below its 12-month high.

The Ibovespa, Brazil’s main stock index, is 18.0% below its 9 October peak of 209,067 and still 13.7% above its November 2025 low. Tuesday’s 0.52% fall is only a subordinate line in that larger slide.
