World.title: Pula Wins the Title of the Best 15-Minute City in the Region
World.content:
November the 10th, 06 – Pula has won the title of the best 15-minute city in the region, with around 60% of the people in this city getting from A to B within a quarter of an hour.

As many as 60% of Pula residents get from A to B within a quarter of an hour. In contrast, in Zagreb, more than 80% of citizens travel for much longer. There’s a coastal Croatian city in which one reaches their job, school, family obligations and more, all in the time it often takes a resident of Zagreb to leave a car park. Poslovni reports that this remains the case even as a city that receives hundreds of thousands of visitors from all over the world in summer. In spite of that, it has preserved what most European cities have long since lost – order and peace on the roads. That city didn’t win only in Croatia, as this Friendly City Index research spans 62 cities across 11 countries.

pula takes first place

The biggest city in Istria was victorious among 62 cities. This is because as many as 60 percent of surveyed Pula residents manage to reach most of their everyday destinations within 15 minutes. The research , which was carried out by Syno International in 62 cities across Croatia, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Ukraine, Bulgaria and Azerbaijan, show that Pula residents live the everyday life that many desire: one in which less time goes on travel, and more remains for and free time.

“Pula was packed with events this summer, and thousands of visitors from all over the world week after week filled the Pula Arena at concerts of the biggest music stars. Despite the hustle and bustle, tourists and the expected crowds of the peak summer season, the average Bolt ride lasted 11 minutes, and almost 80 percent of all rides finished in less than 15 minutes. Our mobility and user movement data thereby additionally confirm what Pula residents highlighted in the Friendly City Index research: Pula is indeed a 15-minute city,” said Sanja Babić. Such a city rhythm is not a coincidence. Short distances and roundabouts, which in Pula at many key intersections have replaced traffic lights and enable more fluid traffic without long waiting, make Pula an example of how urban mobility can be simple and efficient.

zagreb remains the croatian record holder… at the very bottom of the list

Zagreb failed the 15-minute city test, and rather catastrophically so. The majority of surveyed Zagreb residents consider that the capital is still far from the vision of a city within a quarter of an hour’s reach, so it found itself at the bottom of the ranking, in 50th place, with a result of 18 percent. A surprise also came in the form of Zadar, which last year led the regional ranking with approximately 54 percent of respondents, and this year fell to ninth place, with 46 percent. This year’s analysis was also expanded to Pula and Dubrovnik, whereby the number of covered Croatian cities was increased from five to seven. In addition to first-placed Pula, Split occupies fourth and Osijek fifth place, both with a result of 50 percent. They were followed by Zadar, Rijeka in 16th place with 38 percent, Dubrovnik in 38th place with 23 percent, and Zagreb as the last among Croatian cities.

pula beats bucharest

The Friendly City Index research, in which residents of 62 cities in 11 countries assessed whether they reach their everyday destinations within 15 minutes, showed that at the opposite end of the ranking from the winner Pula is Romanian Bucharest, which took last place in the research. In Bucharest only six percent of residents reach destinations within a quarter of an hour, which means that that share in Pula is as much as ten times higher than in the Romanian capital. Among the capital cities Bratislava fared the best, but even it with a result of 26 percent occupies only 30th place in the overall ranking.

what is the Friendly City Index?

The Friendly City Index is an international research that compares the quality of life in cities of Central and Eastern Europe as the residents themselves see it: how much time they need to work, educational, health and sports facilities or the shop, how close green areas are to them, what the cycling and traffic infrastructure is like. The research was conducted on Bolt’s initiative by the company Syno International, and this year’s edition covers 62 cities in 11 countries: Croatia, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Ukraine, Bulgaria and Azerbaijan. The ranking of 15-minute cities is based on the share of respondents who reach most everyday destinations within a quarter of an hour.

People who still want to live in cities move into them primarily because of practicality, but the accelerated growth and development of cities can make everyday life much more challenging. That’s why the concept of the 15-minute city is a good check of what the real situation is. It shows where cities succeed, and where there is room for improvement. The recipe for success is almost universal – fewer crowds, better public transport and more available alternatives to the private car. If people daily spend more time travelling, that indicates the negative consequences of urban planning that ultimately reflect on the quality of life, from the household budget to health.

World.title: 'Alien' rockers Henge to bring Cosmic Dross to Tallinn in 2027
World.content:
British act Henge, who perform as extraterrestrials spreading peace through a genre they call Cosmic Dross, are to appear in Estonia next year.

The band, from Manchester, are to play the Paavli Culture Factory a little over a year from now, on November 16, 2027, as part of a 75-concert world tour behind their fifth album "Humans", due out early next year.

Henge, sometimes styled HENGE, performs as four fictional characters: Zpor on vocals and guitar, Goo on bass, Sol on synthesizers and Nom on drums. According to their own story, they arrived from distant galaxies to spread peace and prepare humanity for life beyond its home planet.

Their music combines progressive rock, psychedelia and rave culture. Live, the group pairs instrumental passages and electronic rhythms with costumes and a visual language borrowed from science fiction films.

Beyond the stage, they have expanded their fictional world into a comic series made with artists including Boo Cook, an illustrator who has worked on the British cult comic 2000 AD.

Founded in 2015, their albums so far are "Attention Earth!" (2018), "ExoKosm" (2020), "Alpha Test 4" (2023) and "Journey to Voltus B" (2025), a concept album about a planet whose inhabitants are on the brink of discovering nuclear power. The vinyl B-side carries two parallel grooves leading to two different endings — one where the civilization uses nuclear fusion peacefully, one where nuclear winter arrives.

Henge won Live Act of the Year at the 2018 Independent Festival Awards and took silver for Best Music Video at the 2022 Tokyo Film Awards.

Henge appear at the Paavli Culture Factory (Paavli kultuurivabrik) in Tallinn on Tuesday, November 16, 2027.

World.title: Estonian mardipäev, kadripäev traditions await UNESCO decision
World.content:
Estonia's centuries-old mardipäev and kadripäev customs were nominated for inclusion on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list. A decision is expected in early December.

Monday was St. Martin's Eve, or mardilaupäev, in Estonia, and to help hype up the nomination, a group of dressed up mardid went door to door in Tallinn's Old Town that evening.

The mardid even visited the Estonian government on Toompea Hill, entering Stenbock House to sing, do cartwheels in front of the prime minister, tell riddles and perform other traditional antics — including bless Prime Minister Kristen Michal with good luck.

"He's a good lad who needs strength and energy, and could use a switch as well," said one mart, adding that the bundle of birch twigs was a health-boosting switch.

Whether the Estonian tradition makes it onto UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity will be decided at a committee meeting in China in early December.

The Estonian Folklore Council (EFN) is leading the nomination.

"We're hopeful," said another mart, asking why shouldn't these centuries-old traditions be included on the list, like the smoke sauna. "We've submitted our application, and we're still making a little noise today, and then we'll be on our way there."

'It's a two-way dialogue'

Laura Liinat, a Cultural Heritage Department adviser at the Ministry of Culture, said the chances look good, though she stopped short of calling the outcome.

She said the tradition's value lies not only in the mardid and kadrid keeping alive the custom of dressing up and going door to door, but also in the interaction between the costumed visitors and the people who welcome them into their homes.

"It's a two-way dialogue, and the hosts who receive the mardid and kadrid play just an important role," Liinat explained. "The way we welcome them may be a reflection of how we treat one another."

St. Martin's Day falls on November 10, and much like Halloween, or All Hallow's Eve, dressed up marts traditionally make their rounds the night before, on St. Martin's Eve.

Kadrid follow suit on kadrilaupäev, or St. Catherine's Eve, on November 24.

World.title: Rapla student discovers a different Estonia as Kihnu exchange student
World.content:
While many students go abroad on exchange, one young Rapla student chose a different adventure: two weeks at a tiny island school in Kihnu.

Rosmary, known as Roosi on the island of Kihnu, is a student at Rapla Vesiroosi School. While she initially had her sights set on an exchange to the U.S., Roosi did some research and realized she'd fall behind on school back home.

Instead, she wanted to experience what it was like to learn in a much smaller class setting.

"My own school is really big, with around 20 students in each class," Roosi said. "Here, there are only 20 students in the whole school. I thought it'd be really interesting to see how that works."

Before the exchange, Roosi had never even visited Kihnu, a small island in the Gulf of Riga covering less than 17 square kilometers.

Now she is just the second student in her class at Kihnu School, and she loves how closely students from first through ninth grade are connected.

"It's basically one big family," she said. "That's so sweet."

'They've been so helpful'

During her two-week stay, Roosi also has to keep up with assignments from her school back home. She was initially worried about falling behind on her work, but said Kihnu's teachers have gone out of their way to help her stay on track.

"They've been so helpful and have made time to help me keep up with my other schoolwork too," she added.

Asked about what she misses from life on the mainland, Roosi admitted she misses shopping, her family and her dog. Her host family at Kolde Farm has its own dog too, however, along with some 200 farm animals, from horses to highland cattle.

World.title: Estonian kickboxer ahead of WBC fight: More girls than boys in the gym now
World.content:
Estonian kickboxer Astrid Johanna Grents is fighting for a WBC international title on Saturday, saying girls now sometimes outnumber boys in the training hall.

Grents, who won European Games gold in 2023, says Saturday's fight, at the Tondiraba Ice Hall against Italy's Ludovica Ciarpaglini, is the most important of her life — win it and she can challenge for a world title.

One inspiration is the number of women and girls training nowadays, compared with when she started over a decade ago.

"When I started out, there were very few girls doing boxing. Now you see that sometimes there are even more girls than boys in the gym, and you see they even have more discipline about coming to training every day than the boys," she told "Terevisioon," adding the sport has grown hugely in Estonia.

Grents, fights under the name Asteroid, took up kickboxing 12 years ago looking for a new hobby. She has also trained in classical boxing and kickboxing, but her main style is Muay Thai.

"I have the ability to defend myself and I think that makes you very confident. It has become such a part of my life that I can't imagine not going to training today."

She said the sport clears her head and is a great workout. "During a boxing session you can't think about anything, you have to be in the moment." She contrasted that with gym training, where people tend to scroll on their phones between sets: in kickboxing you get three minutes of work and a minute's rest, with no time to think about anything except getting your breath back.

World.title: Binturong breakout means Tallinn Zoo without a single Nicobar pigeon left alive
World.content:
Tallinn Zoo has lost its entire collection of an exotic species of pigeon after being killed by two escaped binturongs, Eesti Ekspress reported .

The pair of binturongs, also known as bearcats and native to southeast Asia, had absconded from their enclosure, and the Nicobar pigeons, found in the islands of the same name and further east, proved easy prey: Two if the three birds were killed outright and the third having to be put down after an injury inflicted by the arboreal viverrids turned necrotic.

The binturongs, who after a competition were named by the public Maimu and Maru, live in a rainforest house that opened at the zoo a few years ago, and their escape bids in recent months had become somewhat of a regular feature.

However, this time it went further than mischief – while they may appear "cute," a binturong's soft muzzle hides 36 to 40 sharp teeth; in their natural habitat, Nicobar pigeons have few predators, and roost in large flocks at night.

Their iridescent green-blue feathers also make them stand out.

The binturongs have reportedly climbed out of their enclosure at the zoo four times since August this year — the first during the Ironman event in Rocca al Mare, when noise from a nearby stage is thought to have driven them to seek somewhere quieter — and, after a mesh-covered enclosure failed to confined them, in October. They now await relocation, something which the zoo had planned anyway. Initially they were both thought to be female, but it later turned out one of the binturongs is a male.

World.title: Pensioners' party founder: Estonia must find more money, not take it away
World.content:
The founder of a new political party representing older people in Estonia wants to give that demographic a voice, and to fund a rise in pensions by boosting the economy and industry.

Ago Kokser heads up the newly founded party, Generations (Põlvkonnad), which he says will appeal to all age groups.

As we know, a political party must have 500 members [to legally register]. You held the founding meeting of your party on Saturday. What exactly is its status? Could it already be referred to a political party?

We wanted to set up a political party, and the founding meeting has taken place. We formed a provisional board, and now we have time to recruit members. I believe we will reach the required 500 members within the next week. Interest has been very high. We have already received 390 expressions of interest, and we have officially registered more than 50 members in just one day. When I have met people, everyone has been full of praise and said it was high time this was done.

So there are already around 390 people interested?

People who have indicated that they are willing to join us. We have an email address, but we did not have a party membership application form ready. It had not been available on the website. Now it is on the website, and people can immediately sign up and join the party there. We are also working directly with people. I give you my word that we will get this done.

This is by no means your first time as a member of a political party. You have been in the Center Party and the Reform Party. Those parties are still active, and there are other parties with strong ratings and very good prospects of entering the Riigikogu. Why did you feel that none of the existing parties offered a way to put your ideas into practice?

Initially, I had no such ambition at all. I was also involved with pensioners and pensioners' organizations, and we had a very large network across Estonia, with more than 24,000 members. But in recent years, the government's position has been that organizations do not need operating subsidies. That they should figure out for themselves how to manage and find money. But funding is only available for projects, not for keeping organizations alive.

We approached members of the Riigikogu, the chair of the Social Affairs Committee and the prime minister to ask whether a solution could be found. Promises were made, but a year passed, and nobody wanted to answer the phone or reply to emails anymore.

We called together the extended board to decide what to do. Should we disband or continue operating? We decided it was too early to disband because we still have ideas. And we could continue operating, since the network is already there.

So why shouldn't pensioners have their own representation? At the same time, people have asked me about the various attempts to establish pensioners' associations years ago. But political parties absorbed this interest group, and those organizations eventually disappeared. Now we felt it was the right time to come forward again because there is interest.

Politicians think that if they raise pensions a little, pensioners will be satisfied. They get their money and keep quiet. But there are more than 310,000 pensioners now. People want to have a say, not just be sitting at home. Communication is important.

In fact, whenever we are portrayed pictorially, we are depicted either with a walking stick or in a wheelchair. But we do not all use walking sticks; I did not come to this interview in a wheelchair or with a walking stick.

In our consideration, older people are those aged 55 and over, right through to end-of-life. We still have some capabilities. We have knowledge, skills and life experience.

And we decided this is not simply a party for older people. We need to involve everyone, the different generations. Young people also have many of their own problems, young families have problems, working-age people have their problems. And everyone of working age will eventually reach retirement age, so they should be able to prepare for that period of their lives.

The idea is certainly good, and the name Põlvkonnad [Generations] is very good, but from a marketing perspective, things seem to have gone a little wrong for you. You said from 55 to the end of life. I think a 55-year-old might be very offended to be referred to as "elderly."

But why would they be offended? When our media says that people aged 55 and over have a particular difficulty finding jobs. They are not accepted, and employers do not want to hire them.

I remember when I was younger, when the Estonian state was restored. Back then, people said that anyone over 30 could be written off; that there was nothing to be done with them.

We welcome all who want to join us. We do not set an age limit, but welcome people who have a good character, want to have a say and believe they have something to contribute.

Because at present when all these laws are being drafted, we are only sometimes involved. We are asked to give our opinions when everything has already been decided. In reality, only cosmetic changes can be made by that stage. And we are not involved in the decision-making process.

But we have the ability to contribute, we could have a say, but for some reason nobody wants to listen to us. So, now we have decided to try and see whether we can make ourselves heard.

You have major designs on taking part in next year's Riigikogu elections. Older people have always been very active voters, so you also have a strong base of support. What would be your main promises and issues, pensions aside, going into the elections?

There are actually many things. We wondered whether our little group had the right to put together the entire program. We will draft it, and everyone else gets to vote on it when we assemble the party's program. We still have a little time at the moment.

But you must have some ideas. You surely discussed these issues on Saturday. What are they then?

There is the care reform, how people can live out the final years of their lives with dignity and on their pensions. Pensions, the size of pensions, as although indexation exists, it does not guarantee that people's quality of life will be maintained, since prices are rising faster than pensions can keep up.

Are you pledging to hike pensions?

Of course, the entire system needs an overhaul. Everyone says we have no money for pensions and cannot do anything.

But if we change the system now, and 20-year-olds start approaching things differently, they will reach retirement age in 50 years. The decisions we make now will have an impact 50 years from now.

We also have to think about that, not just about what we do today and assume that in five years everything will be new and functioning. It will not.

You have been involved in pensioners' organizations. What changes could be made to Estonia's pension system?

There could be many changes. Perhaps we should review indexation, how the money comes in and how it is handled.

Should people, how should I put it, have to live on the edge of subsistence when they become pensioners? Or should they be able to live a dignified life?

Where the money would come from, I cannot say. Cutting or saving money is the easiest approach. But the goal of a society is to live well.

One political party once promised that in five years we would be among the five richest countries. That is what we should be striving for.

The purpose of politics is to stimulate the economy. If we do not stimulate the economy, we will get nowhere. We will simply decline.

What is your idea for stimulating the economy? I would still like to get to the question of where to find the money to raise pensions.

We have some very capable specialists who have retired. We can bring them together and form working groups.

Of course, there are many issues, as I said, including care reform, access to healthcare and mobility.

Just an hour ago, we were talking about how the main problem with Estonia's healthcare system is that there is too little money.

Yes, there is too little money. But everyone keeps saying õõ there is never enough money, while at the same time we hear in the news that a million goes here, another million goes there, and ten million goes on something else.

As I understand it, we do have money. The question is whether it is being directed to the right places and used properly. That is another matter.

Then I have a very good opportunity to ask you: if you had to take money away from somewhere, where would you take it from? Where is too much money being allocated at the moment?

I would not immediately say where money should be taken away from. I would find more of it.

In the near future, we need to find where additional money can come from. We need to focus on that and direct all our energy toward it, rather than looking for ways to take money out of somebody else's pocket.

So where would the additional money come from?

From the economy, from production. That means not just the soft-sector jobs we have here, but we need to work intensively on industry and encourage the development of manufacturing and industry.

That is where the money will come from.

World.title: Tallinn's 2027 budget prioritizes education and crisis preparedness
World.content:
The Tallinn city government approved its draft 2027 budget on Tuesday. The budget totals €1.3 billion, including €168 million in investments.

Education, transportation and social welfare account for the largest share of the city's operating expenditures.

Operating expenditures are projected at €1.1 billion, while total revenue is expected to reach €1.2 billion. Tallinn's net debt burden is projected to remain within the limits set out in the city's budget strategy by the end of 2027.

The city will continue to waive kindergarten fees, provide support payments for parents caring for children at home and support the transition to Estonian-language education.

In 2027, construction of the new Kullo youth center and Tallinn Helen School building will be completed, while work will continue on an extension to Jakob Westholm High School.

Investments in education and youth programs are budgeted at €70.8 million.

Tallinn city bus and tram. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Transport vehicles will get upgrades

Public transportation will remain free for Tallinn residents in 2027.

The budget allocates €31 million for transportation investments, including €29.5 million for road construction and repairs. Planned projects include work on Pärnu maantee, Peterburi tee and Rahumäe tee.

AS Tallinna Linnatransport also plans to replace 60 aging diesel buses and continue upgrading tram and trolleybus infrastructure.

The city will continue funding care services for children with extensive support needs and 24-hour general care services for older residents.

Funding for personal assistant services will also increase to support the independent living of people with disabilities.

Social welfare operating expenditures are budgeted at €145.4 million, with an additional €13.6 million allocated for investments.

In health care, the city will continue supporting the family doctor on-call service and mental health prevention programs for children and young people.

The budget allocates €1.5 million to improve crisis preparedness in apartment buildings.

In total, nearly €3.1 million is earmarked for crime prevention and public safety initiatives.

The city plans to expand shelter capacity, improve the readiness of designated emergency kindergartens and organize practical crisis preparedness training for residents.

The Tallinn City Council building. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Cultural institutions and sports facilities to be upgraded

Major projects planned for next year include the renovation of Kadriorg Stadium, upgrades to the A. H. Tammsaare Museum and further development of the library network.

Investments in culture and heritage preservation are budgeted at €11.9 million, while €14.4 million is allocated to sports and recreational activities.

Tallinn will continue preparing its new comprehensive plan, aimed at improving access to services close to home and guiding the city's long-term development.

The city also plans to simplify procedures allowing apartment associations to use city-owned land for parking spaces and waste collection facilities.

Operating expenditures for circular economy initiatives are budgeted at €4.9 million. The city will continue preparations for waste management reform and promote the separate collection of waste.

Maintenance of parks, green spaces and other public areas, as well as protection of the natural environment, will also continue.

The 2027 budget allocates €4.7 million to business development.

Through the Test in Tallinn program, the city will continue cooperating with companies to pilot new products and services in the urban environment.

The city government will now submit the draft budget to the Tallinn City Council for consideration.

World.title: Kaire Sepper: There are debts you can legally refuse to pay
World.content:
Debts are meant to be repaid. At least in an ideal world. Yet there are debts that people can legally refuse to pay, but thousands still do so, writes Kaire Sepper.

I have spent years working with debt collection, first in a bailiff's office and now as an attorney helping clients. Debts should be repaid. But should all debts? The answer is no.

The issue is also a hot topic at the national level. This summer, the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs circulated a proposal to amend the Code of Enforcement Procedure, under which debtors would be allowed to keep more of their wages in an effort to reduce envelope wages. In January, the Supreme Court clarified the rules governing the publication of time-barred debts. Estonians also lost €21 million to scammers in the first nine months of this year.

All three issues raise the same question: when does a debt stop being a debt that must be paid? The answer is more often than many people think. Here are three examples.

Time-barred claims in enforcement proceedings

I will begin with my favorite topic: enforcement proceedings. If enforcement of a claim has become time-barred, the debtor may refuse to pay it. The debt technically still exists, but a bailiff can no longer collect it through compulsory enforcement. The general rule is simple: enforcement of a claim arising from a court judgment becomes time-barred after 10 years.

There are 75,000 debtors in Estonia who are subject to more than 400,000 ongoing enforcement proceedings. A large share of proceedings initiated before 2016 involve collection of time-barred claims, and proceedings launched in 2016 are reaching the limitation period now. I am referring to private claims, such as apartment association debts and lender claims. Fines and tax debts expire under different rules and generally much sooner. Of course, there are exceptions, such as child support claims or proceedings that have been suspended for some reason, but the general rule remains the same.

Debtors must take the initiative and submit an application asserting that the claim is time-barred. Enforcement will not stop automatically. When withdrawals from the second pension pillar were made in 2021, an estimated €70 million went toward debt repayment. Many debtors unknowingly repaid claims that had long since become time-barred. Every day, employers transfer money from employees' wages to bailiffs to cover debts that could no longer legally be enforced.

"Many debtors unknowingly repaid claims that had long since become time-barred."

For creditors, however, the message is that it is time to review enforcement proceedings involving their debtors and obtain an overview from bailiffs. The principle of "first come, first served" applies in enforcement proceedings, and it is unwise to wait and hope a debtor will eventually start paying voluntarily. There are more options than many people realize: enforcement proceedings can be initiated in another country, Revolut and Wise accounts can be seized, and debtors' movable property and inheritances can also be attached.

Time-barred debt collection claims

The second category consists of debts pursued by collection agencies that are, in fact, already time-barred. In many cases, the collection agency's only leverage is the threat of adding a person to a payment default register.

In a January 30, 2026 ruling, the Supreme Court stated very clearly that publishing information about a time-barred debt in a payment default register is permitted only in exceptional circumstances. A time-barred claim does not necessarily reflect a person's creditworthiness because a time-barred obligation may legally be left unpaid.

An even more important conclusion followed. If an individual challenges publication of the debt, the registry operator must demonstrate a compelling reason for publication that outweighs the debtor's interests, regardless of whether the debt is time-barred or not. The logic of "we will keep publishing it until you pay" no longer applies.

Therefore, before paying a collection agency, individuals should determine whether the claim is valid in the first place. If they are added to a payment default register, they should consider whether there is a sufficient legal basis for doing so.

Loans taken out by scammers

Every day, media outlets report cases where scammers have emptied the bank accounts of individuals and companies through fraudulent schemes. In more serious cases, scammers have also taken out loans in their victims' names. Several Estonian court rulings have found that lenders do not have the right to recover such loans from fraud victims.

People should therefore not feel embarrassed or rush to repay loans taken out by scammers. The recommended first step is to consult a legal adviser, who can assess the situation and suggest the best course of action. Legal proceedings are not always necessary.

That is why fraud victims should preserve all evidence rather than begin deleting it. Save all correspondence, call logs and other relevant material. Victims should also notify the police, their bank and the lender. After that, they should contact a legal adviser.

The law does not help passive parties

In summary, not every debt must be repaid. If a creditor has not been proactive in recovering the money owed, debtors have the right to use the options provided by law: seek recognition that a claim is time-barred, refuse payment of a time-barred claim and challenge an unjustified payment default listing.

The same principle applies in both directions. Creditors who fail to take active steps to recover debts cannot be surprised when claims become time-barred. Debtors who do not know their rights may end up paying debts they do not actually owe. The law does not help passive parties, whether creditor or debtor. Both sides must take active steps to achieve the best outcome for themselves.

World.title: World leaders to address COP31 as Turkiye pushes for new climate deal
World.content:
ANTALYA, Turkiye: World leaders will set out their climate priorities in speeches at COP31 in Turkiye on Wednesday, as negotiators seek agreement on a plan to increase the share of electricity in global energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels. Delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya as global greenhouse gas emissions show little sign of falling and wars, inflation and other crises compete for political attention.

A UN report last month found the world on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the Paris Agreement to prevent the worst ‌of climate ‌change.

Former French Prime Minister Laurent Fabius, who presided over the 2015 Paris ‌climate conference and leads an advisory council of former COP presidents, said the speeches could give political impetus to the negotiations.

“It is an opportunity for leaders to make some announcements, and more this time, to explain how they will implement, because the key word in Antalya is implementation,” he told Reuters.

Scores of world leaders – including presidents and heads of government – will begin their rapid-fire speeches on Wednesday afternoon and continue through the day on Thursday, according to the COP31 schedule.

Wednesday’s speakers are expected to include Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who was re-elected at the end of October, and whose ‌country hosted last year’s climate talks.

European Commission President Ursula von ‌der Leyen, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, and Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine will also speak on Wednesday.

The ‌United States, the world’s largest historical emitter, has skipped the talks for the second year ‌in a row after President Donald Trump – who has called global warming a hoax – withdrew the US from climate cooperation following his return to office in 2025.

Age of electricity?

COP31 host Turkiye has so far been pushing the government representatives attending the conference to put a goal on electrification at the center of a final deal, ‌even as critics say it may do little to curb warming.

The proposal targets a rise in electricity’s share of total global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, up from a little over a fifth now, theoretically reducing greenhouse gas emissions from cars, factories, and buildings.

But the proposal does not include language requiring new power to be generated by clean energy sources, and world governments have yet to clarify a broader plan to transition away from fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas.

“It is long past time to stop treating the transition away from fossil fuels as taboo or intractable,” United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told the conference on Tuesday, urging countries to produce clear timelines for the transition.

The previous COP in Brazil was unable to reach consensus on the need for a global plan to reduce dependency on fossil fuels. The Brazilian COP presidency has in recent weeks, however, published a roadmap aimed at keeping that idea central to the climate negotiations. It asks countries to first plan and assess their energy systems by 2028, then work together to reduce fossil fuel supply from 2031.

World.title: Nvidia CEO affair revives push for tougher US line on China
World.content:
WASHINGTON, United States: The scandal engulfing Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang could have its biggest consequences in Washington, where China hawks are seizing on the affair to push a hard line that had been put on the back burner under President Donald Trump.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and turned it into the world’s leading supplier of the processors that power artificial intelligence, admitted on Sunday to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom US intelligence officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence.

Trump, who has relied on Huang as an adviser on AI, called him “an honorable guy” and said Huang told him he had no idea the woman was a spy.

Huang has spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China, and Trump last year cleared Nvidia’s H200 chips for export there over objections from hawks in both parties.

“China hawks in policy circles in Washington DC were quite frustrated with the decisions and really wanted to see a more aggressive approach around export controls to China,” said Aalok Mehta of the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

“They will now see some fruits of their efforts.”

Many in Washington see the United States as locked in a Cold War-style race with China for technological and military dominance, and these hawks have bristled at Trump not conforming to that.

“What we are heading into is one of the most serious investigative efforts in a substantial period,” said Kurt Campbell, a former US deputy secretary of state and co-founder of consultancy The Asia Group.

Lawmakers will want to know when the government learned of the alleged links, whether the president was warned and whether the contacts shaped his China policy, Campbell said.

The New York Times has reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed the allegations to Trump in May, but the president chose not to act.

Nvidia committed $25 million to Trump’s White House ballroom — among the largest donations — months after securing his approval to resume chip sales to China, The Washington Post reported. Nvidia has said the gift was independent of its business interests.

Three Republican House committee chairs have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on November 18 about his dealings with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s safeguards against espionage.

Not ‘invincible’

Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center, said Republicans long feared crossing Trump.

But with the party having lost control of Congress and Trump “no longer this seemingly invincible political brand,” some may feel freer to break with him, Chan told AFP.

That could revive the AI Overwatch Act, a bipartisan bill that would let Congress review and block licenses to export advanced AI chips to China and other adversaries.

The revelations have given hawks “new enthusiasm” to push through the stalled annual defense authorization bill with export control measures attached, said Emily Benson, head of strategy at Minerva Technology Futures.

The key question is Trump, she said, who holds a veto that only two-thirds majorities in both chambers can override.

Commerce Department staff have also pushed for new rules, including curbs on Chinese remote access to advanced AI chips, but Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick will not act without Trump’s instruction, tech news outlet The Information reported.

The department has already drawn scrutiny for reportedly halting a probe into Megaspeed’s dealings with Nvidia.

Tighter rules risk upsetting the trade truce Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping reached last year.

Export control legislation seen by Beijing as targeting China “would almost certainly invite swift retaliatory action by Beijing to destabilize US supply chains,” Benson said.

The FBI is looking into the spying allegations, Trump said, while the Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia chips into China, NBC News reported.

Megaspeed denies smuggling, and Beijing has dismissed the spying claims as smears.

If wrongdoing were found and Huang forced out, “that would have huge implications for AI in the US, given that he has played such a pivotal role in pushing forward Nvidia but also the whole industry,” Chan said.

But even short of Huang’s downfall, “Nvidia’s traction within the halls of Congress and within the administration is likely to be significantly reduced or completely eliminated,” Mehta said.

World.title: Thomas Markle, father of Meghan, cut off his ankle monitor, DOJ says
World.content:
FLORIDA: The 82-year-old estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, cut an electronic monitoring device off his ankle, just days after his arrest for keeping child sexual abuse material in storage units in California, authorities said Tuesday.

Thomas Markle was in custody awaiting a hearing in federal court in Tampa, Florida, First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said.

He was arrested shortly after he cut off the ankle bracelet at 1:45 a.m., Essayli said.

Markle’s arrest on Friday followed the seizure of approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives, and books that contained suspected child sexual abuse images in storage in the Los Angeles area, Essayli said.

During his arrest last week, he was taken from a senior care center in Lakeland by ambulance. Hours later, a judge allowed Markle to be released on the condition that he be electronically monitored, which typically means wearing an ankle tether.

The judge also ordered a mental competency exam and a report by Nov. 20.

His daughter, Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex married Prince Harry at Windsor Castle in 2018. They have two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. She is an American citizen and actor who starred in the US television drama “Suits.”

Meghan recently said she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father’s former home. She also revealed that a letter containing “troubling allegations” about him had been sent to police in London in 2019.

“It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated,” Meghan said of the letter. “I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them.”

Thomas Markle was living in the Philippines this year when he suffered a stroke and had his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the US

His arrest followed reports by The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, that Meghan’s half brother found a collection of child sexual abuse images while clearing out their father’s home in the Philippines. That discovery led to information about two US storage units in California, which Markle had rented since 2008.

World.title: Linda Noskova bests Gauff to reach WTA Finals semis, Americans battle for second spot
World.content:
INDIAN WELLS, California: Linda Noskova became the first to qualify for the semifinal round of the 2026 WTA Finals, defeating Coco Gauff 6-3, 6-3 in 1 hour and 15 minutes on Tuesday.

“Coco’s a big competitor, so I was ready for everything to come my way today,” said Noskova, the No. 8 seed. “I feel like I held myself through a lot of tough situations.”

Noskova, the reigning Wimbledon champion, posted a straight-sets victory to guarantee her advancement out of round-robin play. The remaining Group 1 berth will come down to Gauff or Jessica Pegula, who eliminated Marta Kostyuk from contention on Tuesday.

The 21-year-old Noskova is making her WTA Finals debut after winning her first Grand Slam title in July. She followed up her Sunday win over Kostyuk with a strong performance against Gauff, who narrowly defeated Pegula in her first round-robin match.

The youngest woman to make five consecutive WTA Finals since Martina Hingis (1996-2000), the 22-year-old Gauff fell behind by a double-break in the first set and was unable to keep up with Noskova’s consistent play.

Noskova won five games in a row to earn a set and 3-0 lead and struck her ninth ace on match point.

Pegula, who finished runner-up at the WTA Finals in 2023, kept hopes of a semifinal return alive by defeating Kostyuk after two losses to the Ukrainian this season. Kostyuk was a late alternate to the eight-woman field following World No. 1 Elena Rybakina’s withdrawal due to a viral illness.

Despite having no chance to advance to the semifinals, Kostyuk will play Gauff on Thursday for the opportunity to avoid an 0-3 round-robin record and to earn an additional $230,000 in prize money. The final Group 1 standings will be determined by Thursday’s results.

World.title: Saudi environmental security forces arrest citizen for illegal hunting at wildlife reserve
World.content:
RIYADH: The Special Forces for Environmental Security arrested a Saudi citizen for violating the Environment Law by hunting without a license in Imam Turki bin Abdullah Royal Reserve.

The individual was found in possession of an air rifle and four, hunted, wild animals.

Legal procedures were taken against him.

The SFES stressed the importance of complying with the Environment Law and its implementing regulations, which prohibit illegal wildlife hunting.

It noted that hunting without a license carries a fine of SR10,000, hunting in prohibited areas carries a fine of SR5,000, and hunting a warbler without a license carries a fine of SR5,000.

The SFES urged the public to report any environmental or wildlife violations by calling 911 in Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Region, or 999 and 996 in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s other regions.

All reports will be treated with complete confidentiality, and informants will bear no liability.

World.title: Chelsea frustrated by Hacken in women’s Champions League, Man City win
World.content:
PARIS, France: Chelsea were held to a goalless stalemate by Hacken in the Women’s Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City earned a first win of the competition.

The London club hit the woodwork twice in Sweden as an inspired showing by Hacken goalkeeper Jennifer Falk also helped keep the visitors at bay.

Chelsea are third in the league phase table after four matches, one point behind defending champions and pacesetters Barcelona, although the perfect Catalans hold a game in hand.

However, several teams, including Lyon and Arsenal — both of whom are just a point behind Sonia Bompastor’s side — could leapfrog them this matchday.

“It’s a frustrating result,” Blues boss Bompastor told UEFA.

“We came here with the ambition of winning the game... But tonight it didn’t go that way. We need to learn from this.”

Women’s Super League champions Man City enjoyed a 4-1 success at Inter Milan to earn a first win in the league phase after drawing their first three outings.

A first-half Aoba Fujino brace canceled out Elisa Bartoli’s opener for the hosts by half-time.

Kerstin Casparij and Grace Clinton were on target after the break to send City up to seventh in the table.

Paris Saint-Germain fell to a first defeat as Bayern Munich held on to win 2-1 at the Parc des Princes and climb to second in the table, ahead of Chelsea on goal difference.

Klara Buehl’s strike five minutes from half-time proved the winner as she added to PSG goalkeeper Katarzyna Kiedrzynek’s early own goal to put the Bavarians in a comfortable position.

Paulina Dudek halved the deficit from the spot midway through the second period but Bayern held on.

PSG lie in ninth place on five points.

In the Spanish capital, Real Madrid downed visitors Paris FC 3-0 thanks to three second-half strikes.

A first win of the league phase sent Pau Quesada’s side eighth in the table on six points, while Paris FC lounge 16th on two points.

Arianna Caruso broke the deadlock in the 55th minute and Lineth Beerensteyn thumped home soon after.

Linda Caicedo made the points safe with nine minutes remaining as she finished smartly from Felicia Schroeder’s reverse pass.

“It was really important to pick up the three points today because we hadn’t won any of our first three games,” Caruso said. “We have to try to finish among the top teams.”

Roma held on to beat Swiss side Servette 2-1.

On Wednesday, eight-time winners Lyon are in action away to Juventus.

World.title: US Republicans derail bid to impeach Pentagon chief
World.content:
Washington, United States: Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, handing President Donald Trump a victory days after his party’s crushing midterm election defeat.

The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively derailing a planned vote Wednesday on whether to bring formal charges against the embattled Pentagon chief.

The resolution was introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, a Trump critic who was the only member of his party to oppose the procedural maneuver, according to US media.

The impeachment drive had threatened to deepen Trump’s troubles after Democrats swept last week’s midterms, with anger at the sputtering Iran war and soaring fuel prices helping drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans.

Republicans still hold a narrow House majority until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. And 11 Democrats missed the vote.

Trump hailed the procedural defeat as an “EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot,” in a post on Truth Social, while Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, in a post on X, called the vote as a “TOTAL VICTORY!”

“We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest,” Parnell added.

Hegseth earlier Tuesday dismissed the impeachment effort as a “farce” and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under Trump.

“It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it,” he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the accusations “slander” and “sabotage.”

Moments after Hegseth’s televised appearance, Trump signaled his support.

“Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS,” the 80-year-old president wrote on his Truth Social platform.

Vice President JD Vance also backed the defense secretary, saying he had “obviously not” committed impeachable offenses.

‘Would do it again’

Massie’s eight articles of impeachment accused Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.

Several related to the eight-month Iran war, accusing him of violating the War Powers Resolution, which places limits on US military interventions without congressional authorization.

Other allegations involved the 2025 conflict with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, which Massie branded “extrajudicial killings.”

He also accused Hegseth of suppressing free speech by trying to punish Democratic Senator Mark Kelly over a video urging military and intelligence personnel to refuse illegal orders.

Hegseth defended the operations in Yemen, Iran, Venezuela and against alleged drug smugglers, while seeking to equate the impeachment effort with an attack on US troops.

“I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow,” he said.

The decision to send the resolution to committee halts the immediate impeachment drive but does not prevent Democrats from reviving the effort after taking control of Congress in January.

Massie, who lost his Republican primary to a Trump-backed challenger, will leave Congress at the end of his term.

World.title: Iraq, BP discusses increasing oil industry investments
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister for Energy Affairs Mohsen al-Mandalawi and officials from British Petroleum (BP) met on Tuesday in London to discuss prospects for a strategic partnership between Iraq and the British firm.

The two sides discussed strategies to increase investments in the energy sector, serve mutual interests, and support the Iraqi economy, according to a statement released by al-Mandalawi’s media office.

The meeting addressed plans to broaden the scope of oil and gas exploration across Iraq, employ modern technologies for development, and create a promising investment climate.

BP is developing four oilfields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, a move that aligns with larger attempts to broaden the base of foreign partners.

The development plan intends to achieve a significant increase in oil and gas output in the next few years.

According to Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair, the plan aims to reach an oil production level of 450,000 barrels per day, in addition to 500 million standard cubic feet of gas per day.

The four oilfields—Kirkuk, Bai Hassan, Jambur, and Khabbaz—are key oil assets in northern Iraq and represent an important part of the government’s plans to increase production.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company to develop the oil fields, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

Khudair affirmed that BP is a strategic partner in the oil and gas sectors. He noted that working together as a team will support the project’s implementation and help address any obstacles that may arise during the development phases.

World.title: Police search Ritz, glitzy French Al-Fayed properties in trafficking probe
World.content:
Paris – French police have advanced an investigation into a vast alleged international network trafficking women for Mohamed Al-Fayed, prosecutors told AFP Tuesday, searching luxury properties linked to the late billionaire, including the Ritz hotel.

The Paris prosecutor’s office said authorities had searched the famed five-star Paris hotel, the former royal residence Villa Windsor and the Castel Sainte-Therese in Saint-Tropez, one of the most exclusive villas on the French Riviera.

Prosecutors said individuals had been held for questioning and authorities were analysing computers, phones and other digital media in operations that represent a development in a probe launched in 2025 to track down accomplices of Fayed and his late brother, Salah Al-Fayed.

Mohamed Al-Fayed, who died aged 94 in 2023, is at the heart of a vast sexual abuse scandal in the United Kingdom, but died with no charges brought against him despite multiple complaints.

The Ritz was just one of the Egyptian-born tycoon’s high-end ventures where victims have said they faced abuse. Others include London department store Harrods, Fulham Football Club and a fleet of private jets.

Victims have also alleged abuse at the Villa Windsor in western Paris, the one-time residence of the Duke and Duchess of Windsor — the former British King Edward VIII and his American wife Wallis Simpson.

The property was reportedly planned as the residence of Mohamed Al-Fayed’s son Dodi and his girlfriend Princess Diana, before their deaths in a Paris car crash in 1997.

– ‘Courage to speak out’ –

In 2025 Paris prosecutors opened an investigation into claims of aggravated human trafficking, procuring prostitutes and rape in a bid to track down accomplices in an alleged international network supplying victims to Mohamed Al-Fayed and his brother.

French investigators have already heard from at least five complainants — the latest in October, sources close to the case told AFP, with some hesitating to come forward due to trauma or fear.

“Every month, new victims from around the world overcome their fears and find the courage to speak out about what they endured,” lawyers Eva Joly, Caroline Joly and Agathe Barril, who represent several complainants, told AFP in a joint statement.

“We are, however, only halfway through the investigations,” they added.

“But the testimony already points to an organisation in which their immense personal wealth and business empire were allegedly mobilised in the service of their sexual predation: a mechanism devised with cold calculation and meticulous care.”

– ‘Highly organised’ –

Complainants have told investigators of a system aimed at recruiting young women hoping for a career at Harrods, or as assistants, coupled with invasive gynaecological examinations, leading to made-up jobs that put them at the disposal of the Al-Fayed brothers.

Some told AFP they believe they were drugged.

“Trafficking cannot be carried out without a highly organised group of individuals,” said one complainant, a former Ritz employee who was transported between France and Britain, speaking on condition of anonymity.

She praised the French investigation, but said London’s Metropolitan Police were still “beating around the bush”, 30 years after the first complaints.

In a letter to survivors on Tuesday, the Met said the investigation was one of the force’s “largest and most complex”, saying 169 victims have now come forward, and its officers are working closely with French authorities.

The London force has questioned seven people suspected of enabling Mohamed Al-Fayed, but none has been charged.

French and British investigators are now sharing information on the case and the prosecutor’s office said UK authorities were present during the recent operations in France.

The management of the Ritz told AFP it “does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour”, adding it was ready “to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities”.

World.title: Rubio sees ‘no need’ for major combat operations against Iran
World.content:
Paris – US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday said he saw no need to resume major combat operations against Iran because economic sanctions and other restrictions were working so effectively.

“The economic campaign (against Iran) is so devastating that right now there is no need for major combat operations,” Rubio said after a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris. “That’s what I told our allies here today.”

President Donald Trump “has concluded that for the time being there is no need for major combat operations because we are achieving the same objective by economic means,” Rubio said.

But if Iran were to cross “red lines” then the “US military stands ready”, said Rubio, warning of a “terrible price” for Tehran.

European members of the G7 had pressed Rubio at the meeting of foreign ministers of the group in Paris to avoid any new escalation against Iran.

In a surprise move, Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani joined talks on the G7 sidelines with four European top diplomats and the Saudi foreign minister hours after meeting Trump to discuss ending Washington’s war with Iran, Paris said.

Trump had said after meeting Al Thani — a key mediator who is also Qatar’s foreign minister — that there was momentum toward ending the war, which erupted on February 28 with the killing of supreme leader Ali Khamenei.

“The economic pain that is being inflicted on Iran right now and on that regime is extraordinary and it is growing every day,” said Rubio, saying Iranian oil supplies were drying up due to US blockades.

“This radical regime of lunatics is imposing this on their own people,” he said, referring to the Islamic republic’s clerical leadership.

– Downbeat on diplomacy –

But Rubio also appeared downbeat about the prospects of a deal with Tehran, saying Iran currently did not appear realistic about negotiations.

“Iran would love a deal. The problem is, the conditions they continue to place are absurd. They’re not even serious. But that could change,” he said.

But he added: “Eventually, you have to eat, you have pay your own fighters, your own security forces. I think as time goes on that will have an impact… Eventually economic realities penetrate the skull of the most radical lunatic”.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, who chaired the meeting in Paris, warned that the risk of a new escalation between the United States and Iran “has not been completely ruled out”.

“Otherwise, we would not have devoted so much time and energy over the past two days to addressing these issues” with Rubio and the Qatari premier, Barrot said.

British foreign minister Ed Miliband urged an “all-out diplomatic effort” to end the conflict, warning a stalemate of “no war, no peace” was causing economic damage.

“The status quo is bad economically for us and it’s not a stable equilibrium,” said Miliband, urging a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz energy transit hub.

World.title: G7 agrees on need to avoid ‘security void’ in Lebanon after UN force mandate ends
World.content:
Paris – G7 foreign ministers agreed on “the need to avoid a security void” in Lebanon after UN peacekeepers pull out, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Tuesday after a meeting of the group in Paris.

They also backed “the need to move quickly toward a new security architecture” after the mandate of United Nations peacekeeping forces in Israel’s neighbour expires at the end of the year, he said.

But Barrot acknowledged there had been no breakthrough on what should replace the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), which has been in place since 1978 and now counts some 7,500 personnel from nearly 50 countries.

Under US pressure, the UN Security Council voted last year to end UNIFIL’s mandate on December 31, 2026.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told AFP in October that the bloc favoured a UN peacekeeping mandate in south Lebanon.

Lebanese militant group Hezbollah drew the country into the broader Middle East war by attacking Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.

“I am hopeful that we will reach a consensus,” said Barrot. “The objective is widely shared: the withdrawal of Israel (from southern Lebanon), the disarmament of Hezbollah (which is pro-Iranian), and the restoration of a strong state that holds a monopoly on the use of arms — a state capable of ensuring the security and prosperity of all the populations and all the communities in Lebanon.”

Israel now maintains troops in a self-declared “security zone” running around 10 kilometres (six miles) inside Lebanon along the border.

“We underscored the need for a robust, credible, and long-lasting security architecture in Lebanon in support of the Lebanese Armed Forces,” the ministers said in their final communique.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that he had discussed the issue with President Emmanuel Macron and suggested that what replaces UNIFIL “doesn’t have to be a military mission, it could be a civilian mission.”

“We need a verification system trusted by everyone and trusted by both sides that both sides are complying with their obligations under the agreements that are in place,” Rubio said.

A transitional mechanism utilising UNIFIL forces is among the options on the table, a European diplomat said, asking not to be named.

But this could require a UN Security Council resolution and thus run into an American veto, the diplomat warned.

The Europeans are also pushing a proposal for an international military coalition tasked with supporting the Lebanese Armed Forces in their mission to disarm Hezbollah.

However, the formation of such a coalition faces hesitation from Italy, which “remains strongly committed to its presence in Lebanon but appears reluctant to join an ad hoc coalition”, partly due to cost concerns, as such missions are not funded by the UN, diplomats said.

World.title: Iraqi FM participates in Paris Peace Forum
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein has arrived in the French capital to participate in the 9th annual Paris Peace Forum, where he will engage in discussions on key regional and international challenges.

Hussein said in a statement on Tuesday that he will exchange perspectives and explore approaches to de-escalate tensions and advance peace and stability.

The Iraqi foreign minister will present Iraq’s perspective on regional developments, emphasizing the importance of dialogue, diplomacy, and political solutions in addressing crises.

Hussein is expected to meet with international officials and partners to discuss strategies to strengthen cooperation, enhance coordination, and advance shared interests.

According to Hussein, Iraq will remain committed to constructive international efforts to promote regional stability, peace, and sustainable partnerships.

Participating as a featured speaker, Hussein addressed Iraq’s central role in mediating regional conflicts. He confirmed that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi recently conducted an unannounced visit to Tehran.

Al-Zaidi’s secret trip to Iran is part of Baghdad’s active diplomatic bridge to narrow differences, reduce escalating tensions, and work toward ending the ongoing conflict between Iran and the United States.

Hussein stressed that Iraq uses its good connections with the US and strong relationships with Iran to promote peace.

To reduce tension, Hussein had earlier suggested that a regional group of foreign ministers travel to both Washington and Tehran.

During his discussions at the forum, Hussein cautioned world leaders about the dire security and economic consequences of the conflict. He noted that the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz and regional unrest directly harm Iraq’s financial status and threaten worldwide energy, oil, and raw material markets.

World.title: Plane carrying Iran’s football team barred from landing in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq barred on Tuesday a plane carrying Iran’s national football team from landing at Basra International Airport, turning the aircraft back due to strict compliance with US sanctions on Iranian airlines.

The Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority (ICAA) denied landing rights to the flight carrying the Iranian team.

The aircraft successfully altered its course and landed at Abadan Airport in Iran. An official from the Iranian consulate confirmed that the team would continue their journey to Basra by road.

Along with Iraq, Lebanon, and Palestine, the Iranian national team was headed to Basra to participate in a four-nation competition.

Iraq could not risk violating the harsh secondary penalties imposed by Washington, according to an Iraqi civil aviation official.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned earlier that any foreign airports or service providers that assist sanctioned Iranian carriers will be excluded from the US currency system, a step aimed at grounding Iran’s civil fleet worldwide.

After Iraq previously secured a limited humanitarian exemption allowing specific civilian flights from Iran to Najaf, other major Iraqi airports in Basra, Erbil, and Baghdad remain restricted to avoid US financial penalties.

World.title: Excelerate Energy to launch Iraq’s first LNG import terminal in Q2 2027
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is seeing rapid on-site progress, as efforts continue to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq.

Excelerate Energy, the US-based firm implementing the project, anticipates an increase in the pace of work in the upcoming weeks, with construction activities on terminal facilities set to ramp up.

The company aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the military conflict in the region have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026.

The delays forced Excelerate Energy to redirect its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), the Excelerate Acadia, to Jordan for a period of nine months.

To avoid disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed in the region, eliminating the need for such a vessel to transit the strait.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express, according to Attaqa news.

Excelerate Energy indicated that it is attempting to set up the import of LNG from Gulf countries, a remark that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: Iraq, Qatar to lay optical fiber cable linking Singapore to Italy
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ooredoo Group’s international connectivity arm, OFN, has partnered with Iraq’s iQ Networks and the Iraqi Telecommunications and Post Company (ITPC) to build a massive terrestrial and subsea digital corridor connecting Asia, the Gulf, and Europe.

Ooredoo is developing a project that includes a 2,000-kilometer subsea system. This system will feature up to 24 fiber pairs and can support a capacity of up to 720 terabits per second.

The project will link seven Gulf and regional markets, which are Qatar, Iraq, Oman, the UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait.

This dual-arrangement bridges the subsea Gulf network with an overland path heading north through Iraq toward Turkey and Europe, bypassing traditional maritime chokepoints like the Red Sea.

The fiber-optic connection that will bridge Singapore in East Asia to Italy in southern Europe is expected to be completed by 2027.

The Iraqi Ministry of Communications announced that it signed a deal with Qatar to establish the terrestrial and submarine fiber-optic connection.

World.title: 'Worn-out political bogey': Sam Pitroda targets BJP over criticism of Rahul's foreign trips
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Indian Overseas Congress (IOC) chairman Sam Pitroda on Wednesday hit out at the BJP over its criticism of Congress leader

's foreign visits, calling it a "worn-out political bogey".

"Every single time Rahul Gandhi steps outside India, the BJP's well-oiled communication machinery swings into action with manufactured outrage. Rahul Gandhi does not travel abroad to seek foreign intervention or disparage his homeland. He comes to engage with the diaspora, scholars, policymakers, and innovators on critical shifts in the global economy, artificial intelligence, and democratic governance.



To say that discussing the health of Indian democracy abroad amounts to treason is an insult to the intelligence of the Indian electorate", Pitroda said.

His remarks came ahead of the Bharat Summit 2026, which is scheduled to be held at the Hyderabad International Convention Centre (HICC) and is expected to bring together 600 to 700 participants from around 70 countries. Speaking to news agency ANI, Pitroda said the summit would provide a platform for discussions on the state of democracy and the challenges facing democratic institutions worldwide.





Explaining the need for such a gathering, he said, "Bharat Summit is a collaboration of various people. We all came together to have a broader conversation on the state of democracy globally. Progressive Alliance is a group of roughly 100 countriesâ democratic parties. Democracy, in many ways, has been hijacked in many countries."

Pitroda alleged that democratic institutions were being undermined through electoral processes, the capture of institutions, restrictions on civil society and manipulation of the media.

He said the concentration of power and wealth had also weakened the principle of inclusive democracy, leaving minorities, tribals, OBCs and women vulnerable.

He further argued that emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, would require democracies to rethink how they function.

World.title: Indian seafarer injured as projectile hits Liberia-flagged oil tanker in Persian Gulf
World.content:
Oil tanker carrying 6 Indians hit by projectile in Persian Gulf

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A Liberia-flagged oil tanker carrying six Indian seafarers came under attack while transiting the Persian Gulf on Tuesday, leaving four crew members injured, including one Indian national, Union minister for ports, shipping and waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said.The vessel, MT FUJAIRAH ENERGY, was travelling from Al Ruwais to Dubai when it was hit by a projectile, Sonowal said in a post on X."On Nov 10, Liberia-flagged VLCC MT FUJAIRAH ENERGY, carrying 6 Indian seafarers, was hit by a projectile while transiting the Persian Gulf from Al Ruwais to Dubai. Four crew members sustained injuries in the attack, including one Indian national, who suffered minor injuries and has been safely taken ashore for further medical examination," the Union minister said.Sonowal added that the remaining 18 crew members, including the other five Indian seafarers, were safe."The remaining 18 crew members, including the other 5 Indian seafarers, are safe and accounted for. We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security, medical care and wellbeing of our seafarers," Sonowal added.The incident comes amid heightened security concerns over commercial shipping and the safety of Indian seafarers in West Asia, with vessels navigating strategically important maritime routes facing repeated attacks.Earlier, on November 3, ministry of external affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India had lost 23 nationals in the ongoing West Asia conflict.He also confirmed that five Indian nationals had been killed in attacks targeting commercial shipping in the Black Sea region, while two others remained missing.In a separate incident, Indian seafarer Gandhar Nahim Ajij, from Gujarat, was killed when a commercial vessel carrying 14 Indian crew members came under attack off the coast of Oman. The remaining 13 Indian nationals were rescued, and the government was working to facilitate their repatriation.Jaiswal reiterated India's call for dialogue and diplomacy to de-escalate tensions and restore peace in the region.He also stressed that freedom of navigation through international waters and waterways must be restored and guaranteed.

World.title: Parl panel drops NCR air pollution from agenda, Cong’s Maken raises objection
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As the Capital chokes under the haze of polluted air, a Parliamentary panelâs decision to drop the issue without citing any reason from the meeting agenda for Nov 17 has evoked a sharp reaction from Congressâ Rajya MP

who is a member of the standing committee on home affairs.

Highlighting that âDelhi's air-pollution crisis must be treated as a public-health emergencyâ Maken has written to the panelâs chairperson Radha Mohan Das Agrawal seeking restoration of the hearing on the issue on the same date, or an alternate date at the earliest with an explanation for the change.

In the letter dated Nov 7, Maken has registered his âobjectionâ to the omission of the air-pollution hearing from the revised agenda for Nov 17.



âMy concern is specifically the removal of the scheduled Nov 17 hearing at a time when these health risks demand timely scrutiny. Its omission requires an explanation and a definite date for examination,â Maken has further stated.

âGiven the urgency of the health risks, I request that this change be reconsidered and the hearing restored to that date,â Maken states.

Maken recalls that he had requested examination of air pollution in his letter of Nov 2 and that the committee has included the subject in its annual programme list for 2026-27.





He further cites that the original public notice of Nov 5 scheduled the hearing for Nov 17 at 2 pm.

The original agenda circulated among members stated, "To hear the views of Ministry of Home Affairs and concerned agencies on the subject 'Air pollution in Delhi-NCR: Enforcement of Regulatory measures, effective implementation of GRAP measures, protection of vulnerable sections and coordination among law enforcement and government agencies."
