World.title: DOJ starts process to extradite Apollo Quiboloy,  others to US
World.content:
ACCUSED. Kingdom of Jesus Christ Pastor Apollo Quiboloy arrives at the Senate to attend the public inquiry into the reported cases of abuse in KOJC, on October 23, 2024.

Quiboloy and two others have been on the Federal Bureau of Investigation's most wanted list since 2022

MANILA, Philippines – The Philippine Department of Justice (DOJ) finally commenced the extradition process against doomsday preacher and Kingdom of Jesus Christ founder Apollo Quiboloy based on the request of the United States government.

On Tuesday, November 10, the DOJ announced that the US’ request to extradite Quiboloy, Teresita Dandan, and Helen Panilag was filed with Makati City Regional Trial Court Branch 145 on Monday, November 9. Presiding Judge Karen Matti Sy handles the case.

Quiboloy faces cases that include international human trafficking, sex trafficking, conspiracy, and bulk cash smuggling. He has been detained in Pasig City Jail since November 2024.

Locally, he is facing a trafficking case at the Pasig City court and separate cases of sexual abuse of a minor and child abuse in a Quezon City.

He was arrested on September 8, 2024, after months of manhunt and tension in his home turf Davao City.

Quiboloy, Dandan, and Panilag have been in the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s most wanted list since 2022.

The local DOJ said the US-issued warrants remain valid and executable.

“The US Government seeks their extradition to pursue prosecution for the foregoing offenses,” said the justice department.

“An extradition proceeding is sui generis. It is not a criminal proceeding and it does not involve the determination of the guilt or innocence of an accused. His guilt or innocence will be adjudged in the court of the state where he will be extradited,” it added.

What will be the process?

Based on the Philippines’ new Rules on Extradition approved by the Supreme Court, it’s the DOJ secretary who triggers an extradition process. It can also be any designated state counsels of the DOJ’s Office of the Chief State Counsel.

The DOJ may file a verified petition with the extradition court to start the process.

Later, the court may issue a warrant of arrest.

A warrant will be issued if the petition is sufficient in form and substance and compliant with the law and applicable extradition treaty. A warrant will also be issued if there’s probable cause that:

The person named in the petition is the one identified in the warrant, indictment, or judgement issued by the requesting state

The offense is an extraditable offense

The person committed the offense

After a review, the court will grant the petition if a prima facie case exists.

Prima facie, as explained in Wa-acon vs. People, is a situation where evidence “is not rebutted or contradicted, making it good and sufficient on its face to establish a fact constituting a party’s claim or defense.” – Rappler.com

World.title: Abando returns to Gilas as debuting Boatwright banners new FIBA roster
World.content:
High-flyer Rhenz Abando returns to Gilas Pilipinas for the first time in three years as Kai Sotto and debuting naturalized player Bennie Boatwright lead the national team roster in the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian qualifiers’ fifth window

MANILA, Philippines – For the first time since the 2023 FIBA World Cup, high-flyer Rhenz Abando makes his return to Gilas Pilipinas as he rounds out the final-12 roster for the 2027 World Cup Asian qualifiers’ fifth window in Seremban, Malaysia on November 27 and 29.

Hinted as an unnamed surprise addition by Gilas head coach Tim Cone, the Korean Basketball League (KBL) import stands out as the revamped roster’s top attraction alongside new naturalized player and former PBA reinforcement Bennie Boatwright.

Standing at 6-foot-10, the 30-year-old Boatwright creates an intriguing new “twin towers” duo with 7-foot-2 key returnee Kai Sotto, while other young stars AJ Edu, Kevin Quiambao, Quentin Millora-Brown, and Mike Phillips make up the imposing frontcourt rotation.

Dwight Ramos once again takes the backcourt helm alongside former PBA MVP Scottie Thompson, as fellow star guards Juan Gomez de Liaño, CJ Perez, and Chris Newsome complete the rest of the roster.

Following a lengthy Senate naturalization process, Boatwright now takes on the monumental task of filling in the void left by longtime Gilas star Justin Brownlee, who remains away from competitive basketball due to a variety of health issues.

“[Boatwright] is due to come in and meet us in Kuala Lumpur on the 23rd, and that’s tough because he hasn’t been with us in any time at all,” Cone said on Wednesday, November 11.

“We’re gonna have to try to figure out a way to make him effective within a system, and try to tweak the system to get him effective. He’s a talented guy, he’s gonna lend a lot of talent to the team, and size, and shooting, so, he’s a welcome addition.”

The 28-year-old Abando, meanwhile, looks to make the most of his national team return following insistent public demand and a steadying KBL import role with the Anyang Jung Kwan Jang Red Boosters.

In his last Gilas foray, Abando posted promising averages of 5.2 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks in just 13.5 minutes per game under former coach Chot Reyes before missing out on all national team events throughout the Cone era.

Currently 4-4 in the Group E standings, Gilas looks to sweep its Malaysia leg with wins over Syria on November 27 and Iran on the 29th. – Rappler.com

World.title: Oil dependence is bad for the climate and the economy, UN chief tells COP31
World.content:
PROTEST. Activists take part in a demonstration organized by Oil Change International at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, on November 10, 2026.

The discourse on November 10, the second day of COP31 in Turkey, highlights a tension at the heart of the climate debate: fossil fuels underpin the global economy, but also hurt it through costly climate damage and often-volatile energy prices

ANTALYA, Turkey – United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres took aim at oil companies making billions of dollars in profits while families, businesses and governments suffer, as he used the COP31 climate conference to criticize fossil fuel dependency.

Tayyip Erdogan, president of the talks’ host nation Turkey, meanwhile, welcomed an oil discovery in the Turkish mountains, and the country’s climate negotiators pushed governments to sign a pledge to electrify their economies. The pledge does not specify whether the electricity involved would be renewable or from fossil fuels.

Taken together, the discourse on Tuesday, November 10, the second day of the two-week UN conference in Antalya, highlights a tension at the heart of the climate debate: fossil fuels underpin the global economy, but also hurt it through costly climate damage and often-volatile energy prices.

A UN report last month showed the world is poised to warm well beyond the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) threshold scientists say could unleash the worst consequences of climate change, as greenhouse gas emissions continue to grow.

While many people endure the impact of inflation, oil companies have largely benefited from a rise in fossil fuel prices since the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted energy shipments from the Middle East.

“Fossil fuels are not only driving the climate crisis. Dependence on them carries a steep economic and security price — as the crisis in the Middle East has laid bare,” Guterres, who will step down at the end of the year, said.

“Families, businesses and governments are paying the price. Meanwhile, nine oil companies are on track to rake in more than $95 billion in just three months. That is more than one billion dollars a day.”

Guterres did not name the companies. Exxon Mobil, Chevron Corp, BP, and Shell have reported windfall earnings since the Iran war began at the end of February.

Electrification ambition, but will it be green?

Earlier, COP31 host Turkey urged countries to sign up to a goal to increase the share of electricity in global energy use to 35% by 2035 — up from around a fifth today.

Turkey is seeking to incorporate that electrification goal into the formal outcome of the talks, according to a person familiar with the matter.

COP31 President Murat Kurum told a press conference in Antalya that the goal was a way to cut emissions, drive economic growth and ensure long-term energy security.

Climate advocates have criticized the pledge because it does not require that the additional electricity come from low-carbon sources — something Kurum said was not required.

“I put forth a target for electrification. An exit from fossil fuels has already been put forth in previous COPs. You have a path ahead of you today, one is becoming more costly, and one is becoming cheaper. Which one would you prefer?” he said.

The target is meant to help reduce planet-warming emissions by speeding the global shift away from fossil fuel-powered vehicles, furnaces, boilers, cooking stoves, and other greenhouse gas-emitting equipment.

Turkey and Australia rely on coal

The previous COP in Brazil was unable to reach consensus on the need for a global plan to reduce dependency on fossil fuels, but the COP presidency has in recent weeks published a roadmap aimed at keeping that idea at the center of the climate negotiations. The roadmap asks countries to first plan and assess their energy systems by 2028, then work together to reduce fossil fuel supply from 2031.

Turkey, the conference host, and Australia, which is leading the negotiations, both rely on fossil fuels for electricity.

Coal generated about a third of Turkey’s electricity last year and more than 40% of Australia’s, according to government data.

Speaking alongside the Brazilian team at an event in Turkey, former US secretary of state and climate envoy John Kerry said that despite previous COPs having agreed on the need to transition away from fossil fuels, investment poured into new oil and gas fields.

“The hard truth is that fossil fuels story is still moving in the wrong direction,” he said. “We don’t need more promises. We need plans.”

Erdogan on Monday, November 9, had cheered a rise in crude oil production from Turkey.

“Good news keeps coming from the mountains of Gabar,” he said following a cabinet meeting, after announcing that oil production from the Gabar fields in the country’s southeast would exceed 100,000 barrels per day in the second half of 2027.

Climate activist Greta Thunberg, attending her first COP talks in five years, said the UN process was failing to deliver enough action to match the severity of the crisis.

“These COPs have become greenwash circuses, that is the reality,” she told reporters.

“Of course it is absolutely crucial that we still do everything we possibly can because this is an opportunity to mobilise people and to say that the people in power do not have the situation under control.” – Rappler.com

World.title: DOH: 7 in 10 Filipino deaths due to noncommunicable diseases
World.content:
According to the Department of Health, tobacco use contributed to more than 95,000 deaths annually, while excessive alcohol consumption was associated with over 27,000 deaths.

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Health (DOH) on Wednesday said seven out of 10 Filipino deaths were caused by noncommunicable diseases associated with unhealthy lifestyles.

According to the DOH, tobacco use contributed to more than 95,000 deaths annually, while excessive alcohol consumption was associated with over 27,000 deaths.

Meanwhile, more than 4,000 deaths were linked to high sugar consumption.

Article continues after this 

READ: DOH seeks higher taxes on sweetened beverages, junk food

“Seven out of every 10 Filipino deaths are caused by noncommunicable diseases, to which tobacco use, harmful alcohol consumption, and unhealthy diets are major contributors,” Dr. Lester Tan, DOH assistant secretary of health and head of the Local Health Systems Strengthening Cluster, said in a statement.

The DOH urged Congress to pass the sin tax reform and increase taxes on sin products, such as alcohol, tobacco, and sweetened products, to prevent lifestyle-related deaths.

READ: Tolentino: Regulate vape products before imposing more taxes

Senate Bill No. 1074 seeks to impose additional taxes on sin products, including e-cigarettes. It also aims to allocate the revenue collected to fund the implementation of the Universal Health Care law.

“We must raise taxes on harmful products to make them less affordable, reduce consumption, prevent premature deaths, and generate sustainable funding for Universal Health Care,” he said. /mcm

World.title: Rare thumb-sized orchid found in Dinagat mining area
World.content:
RARE FIND. A thumb-sized helmet orchid (Corybas pictus) was photographed growing in a natural forest patch inside Cagdianao Mining Corp. in the Dinagat Islands. Discovered during a 2025 biodiversity assessment, the sighting marks the first documented record of the miniature orchid species in the Philippines. (Photo courtesy of BECS / CMC-MEPEO)

SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur— Environmental researchers have documented a rare, thumb-sized helmet orchid for the first time in the Philippines, recording the specimen inside a forested pocket of an active mining concession in Dinagat Islands province.

The orchid, scientifically identified as Corybas pictus, was found within a natural forest patch inside Cagdianao Mining Corp.’s (CMC) tenement during a biodiversity assessment conducted jointly with Biotope Environmental Consultancy Services (BECS).

Field researcher Archie Along spotted the miniature plant during field surveys, marking a new botanical record for the country.

Article continues after this 

READ: 5 of 7 orchid species found in Cotabato endemic to PH

The discovery adds to a growing list of helmet orchids (Corybas) documented across the archipelago in recent years.

Long considered scarce because of their fleeting flowering seasons and habit of hiding in thick moss carpets, several new species have emerged through targeted field surveys—including Corybas hamiguitanensis in Davao Oriental, Corybas apoensis on Mount Apo, and Corybas circinatus in Palawan.

Unlike its highland counterparts, Corybas pictus was previously known only in neighboring Borneo, Sumatra, and Peninsular Malaysia. The plant has a hooded, dark-maroon dorsal petal resembling a visor and a single heart-shaped leaf etched with white veins.

Because it mimics ground fungi to attract tiny fungus gnats for pollination and spends much of the year dormant underground, it easily evades detection.

Article continues after this 

Members of CMC’s Mine Environmental Protection and Enhancement Office (MEPEO)—a team of licensed foresters, agriculturists, environmental experts, and mining engineers—collaborated in the assessment.

READ: Bohol monitors critically endangered helmet orchid in forest reserve

Article continues after this 

According to BECS, documenting the rare orchid underscores the role of continued field research in cataloging Philippine flora and establishing baseline data to guide habitat protection and conservation, even within commercial mineral production areas./coa

World.title: Witness: Sara Duterte had no GenCorp stake, post from 2022 to 2025
World.content:
Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay, in-house counsel of GenCorp Industries Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corp. Screengrab from Senate of the Philippines / YouTube

MANILA, Philippines — The corporate counsel of GenCorp Industries Inc. on Wednesday testified that Vice President Sara Duterte had no shares or position in the corporation from 2022 to 2025.

GenCorp counsel Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay was called to the witness stand to testify on Duterte’s involvement in GenCorp and Metro City Chow Foods Corp.

Asked by defense counsel Justin Gular whether Duterte had shares or a position in GenCorp from 2022 to 2025, Balucanag-Punay repeatedly testified that the vice president held neither.

Article continues after this 

“She has no stockholdings with GenCorp… She has no position,” she answered.

READ: Analyst stands by VP Duterte’s 20% GenCorp interest

According to Duterte’s statements of assets, liabilities, and net worth for 2024 and 2025, she declared herself a stockholder of GenCorp. She also stated that the date of acquisition of her interest or connection began in 2013.

The defense also referred to the financial forensic report of the prosecution’s expert witness, Atty. Alexander Cabrera, who attributed a 20-percent interest in GenCorp to Duterte.

But Balucanag-Punay reiterated that Duterte was not a stockholder of GenCorp.

“I think it is incorrect… because you cannot attribute 20 percent to the vice president because she has no shareholdings in GenCorp,” Balucanag-Punay said. /mcm

World.title: NCDA warns businesses of legal consequences for rejecting PWD ID
World.content:
FOR PHASEOUT Above is a sample of a valid PWD card, whose holders across the country must register again as part of a systems upgrade and also to weed out fakes. —JAMES SISON

MANILA, Philippines – The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) on Wednesday warned business establishments that they could face legal consequences for refusing to honor existing identification (ID) cards of persons with disabilities (PWDs), as these remain valid throughout the three-year transition period.

In a statement, the NCDA clarified that the mandatory privileges and benefits granted to PWD ID holders would remain uninterrupted despite the shift to a unified PWD ID system, which aims to ensure that only qualified individuals are enrolled in the program.

Refusing to honor legitimate, government-issued PWD IDs constitutes a violation of Republic Act No. 7277, or the Magna Carta for Persons with Disabilities.

Article continues after this 

READ: 3 million PWD ID holders asked to register anew

The NCDA, through Administrative Order No. 001, s. 2026, set in motion the collection of updated information of PWD ID card holders through their local government units (LGUs).

This means that current PWD ID users will have to re-register so their information would be integrated into the new unified PWD system that will run in the next three years.

The move also aims to filter the government’s database of fraudulent IDs and unscrupulous individuals who either fake their ailments to get legitimate PWD IDs or present fake PWD IDs not issued by LGUs.

Upon creating the new digital ID, the individual may immediately use it to claim benefits, such as the 20-percent discount and value-added tax exemption on medicines and basic necessities.

Article continues after this 

The latest data on the NCDA website showed that 3.3 million people are registered as PWDs as of Oct. 21 this year. Of the number only 2.9 million are using PWD IDs, according to NCDA executive director Glenda Relova last week.

The Department of Justice had earlier put the discrepancy between PWDs and PWD IDs at around 6 million. But NCDA officials recently disputed this, saying it was an old estimate presented during a 2024 Senate inquiry. /jpv

World.title: Impeachment court lets Duterte-linked firms’ counsel testify for defense
World.content:
Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay, in-house counsel of GenCorp Industries Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corp. Screengrab from Senate of the Philippines / YouTube

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate Impeachment Court on Wednesday allowed corporate counsel Suzette Balucanag-Punay to testify for the defense despite the prosecution’s challenge to her authority to represent two companies linked to Vice President Sara Duterte.

Balucanag-Punay, the in-house counsel of GenCorp Industries Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corp., was presented by defense counsel Justin Nicol Gular on Day 42 of the impeachment proceedings as the defense’s fourth witness.

After Gular’s offer of testimony, private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan questioned whether Balucanag-Punay had been authorized through board resolutions or secretaries’ certificates from both companies to testify and identify corporate documents before the tribunal.

Article continues after this 

Kapunan pointed out that Balucanag-Punay’s name did not appear in the companies’ general information sheets, financial statements or articles of incorporation.

She asked the defense to present a board resolution specifically authorizing the lawyer to represent both corporations and testify on their behalf.

Presiding Officer Sen. Francis Escudero inquired why Kapunan wanted a board resolution.

READ: Sara Duterte impeachment defense presents witnesses to counter case

According to Kapunan, “The board resolution is important because… we do not want at some point in time that she will call to the attention of the Honorable presiding officer the… or hide behind the attorney-client privilege.”

Article continues after this 

Gular countered that Balucanag-Punay appeared before the tribunal pursuant to a subpoena.

“If the concerns of the good counsel from the prosecution are to hide behind supposedly the veil of attorney-client privilege, it is number one a premature objection; number two, it is not an objection that she is entitled to raise and only the corporate clients can raise that; and number three, Your Honor, the witness will be under oath in respect to her answers, Your Honor,” he added.

Article continues after this 

Escudero said the tribunal would presume that Balucanag-Punay’s appearance was duly authorized, given her position as in-house counsel of the two corporations.

“The court will in the meantime allow the testimony of Atty. Punay on her oath as a lawyer, upon which she owes candor and fidelity not only to the regular courts but to this court as well,” the presiding officer said.

“And although corporations cannot act on their own, we as of yet do not know if, based on the testimony, she will be testifying on behalf of the corporation or only about the corporation,” Escudero added.

READ: VP trial Day 42: GenCorp, Metro Chow counsel to take witness stand

The court also presumed that the witness had waived attorney-client privilege concerning matters involving the corporations’ affairs.

Escudero reminded Balucanag-Punay that she could not selectively invoke attorney-client privilege when answering questions concerning the two corporate clients.

Meanwhile, Senator-Judge Francis Pangilinan sought clarification on the matter, citing a previous instance involving defense counsel and spokesperson Michael Poa. The prosecution had declared Poa a hostile witness, and he declined to answer questions from senator-judges by invoking attorney-client privilege.

Pangilinan said establishing that the companies had waived attorney-client privilege would speed up the proceedings.

Escudero reiterated that the tribunal was presuming the corporations had waived the privilege and that the witness could not invoke it selectively in matters concerning the companies.

Balucanag-Punay confirmed that she understood the court’s instructions before proceeding with her direct examination.

READ: Live updates: Sara Duterte impeachment trial, Nov. 11, 2026

The defense presented Balucanag-Punay to testify on the corporate status and operations of GenCorp and Metro City Chow Foods, as well as to dispute allegations concerning Duterte’s stake in the companies.

Based on Gular’s offer of testimony, the defense further intends to establish that Duterte exercises no control over or supervisory role in GenCorp’s management and operations.

As for Metro City Chow Foods, the defense acknowledged that Duterte is listed as a stockholder, director and member of its Compensation Committee but intends to show that she does not perform the functions and responsibilities attached to these positions and exercises no control over the corporation’s operations.

Duterte is accused of betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution for allegedly amassing unexplained wealth, failing to accurately disclose her assets, liabilities and net worth in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth, and failing to divest her business interests during her tenure as vice president. /mcm

World.title: Girl, 8, killed as speeding police car hits motorcycle in Koronadal
World.content:
The damaged police patrol vehicle involved in the fatal collision with a motorcycle at the intersection of General Santos Drive and Sinsuat Street in Koronadal City on Nov. 10, 2026. Photo courtesy of PRO-12

KORONADAL CITY – A speeding police patrol car that crossed while the traffic light was red hit a motorcycle in downtown Koronadal, killing an eight-year-old girl and wounding her grandmother.

The collision occurred at around 6:40 a.m. on Tuesday at a traffic light intersection along General Santos Drive and Sinsuat Street in Barangay Zone 4, according to a police report, which identified the victims as “Mina,” 8, and her grandmother, Meriam Salan Antiquera, 51, both residents of Purok Silangan, Barangay Morales.Cpl. Elton John Javien Rombawa, 30, assigned to the 1st Sultan Kudarat Provincial Mobile Force Company, drove the speeding patrol car.

READ: Speeding van with lost brakes blamed for deaths of 6 in ZamboangaThe speeding police vehicle was allegedly leading a convoy when the incident happened.

Article continues after this 

In an interview, Antiquera said their lane had the green light and other vehicles had given way in respect to traffic rules.

She recalled that the police car was still approaching at high speed as they were crossing the intersection and hit them.Antiquera said her granddaughter was thrown several meters away from the motorcycle and suffered a serious head injury.

The child was initially brought to a private hospital but had to be transferred to another facility because of the lack of adequate medical facilities and doctors, she said.The girl later died from her injuries, while her grandmother is recuperating.

South Cotabato Gov. Reynaldo Tamayo Jr. expressed his condolences to the girl’s family and assured them of the provincial government’s assistance.

Tamayo said he was saddened and angered by the incident and vowed to hold accountable those responsible under the law.Brig. Gen. Alan Manibog, Police Regional Office 12 (PRO-12) director, said police took Rombawa into custody following the incident.

Article continues after this 

The official ordered the policeman to undergo drug and alcohol tests as part of the investigation.

READ: Woman killed as overtaking jeep causes crashManibog also directed the Koronadal police to pursue appropriate charges against the driver and his commissioned officer, depending on the findings and the evidence gathered.In a statement, PRO-12 expressed its condolences to the girl’s family and wished her grandmother a speedy recovery.

Article continues after this 

It assured the public that the investigation would be impartial and transparent, stressing that no one was above the law.In a separate directive on Wednesday, PRO-12 ordered all police commanders to strictly enforce existing rules on the safe driving and proper use of government vehicles.The directive reiterated a June 25 memorandum stating that vehicular incidents caused by negligence, recklessness, lack of supervision or failure to observe traffic rules and safety procedures would be subject to appropriate administrative action./coa

World.title: Sandiganbayan rejects Revilla bid to dismiss P92-M flood control case
World.content:
Former Sen. Ramon “Bong” Revilla Jr. INQUIRER FILES

MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Third Division has dismissed the bid of former Sen. Bong Revilla and his co-accused to dismiss the malversation case involving an alleged ghost flood control project in Bulacan worth more than P92 million.

Third Division Clerk of Court Atty. Dennis Pulma shared the information on Wednesday. He said Revilla filed a motion for leave to file a demurrer to evidence on October 19.

READ: Bong Revilla asks Sandiganbayan to junk P92M malversation case vs him

Article continues after this 

“The court issued a resolution denying the motions for leave to file demurrer to evidence by all of the accused in the Revilla case,” Pulma told reporters.

The other co-accused in the malversation case are former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Bulacan district engineers Brice Hernandez, Jaypee Mendoza, Arjay Domasig, and Emelita Juat, as well as DPWH personnel Juanito Mendoza and Christina Pineda.

Pulma added that the court had “merely noted” the attachments filed by Revilla and had taken no action on them.

A demurrer to evidence is a motion filed by an accused seeking the dismissal of a case on the ground that the prosecution failed to present sufficient evidence to establish guilt.

Pulma said the initial presentation of the defense’s evidence is scheduled for November 24-25, 2026.

World.title: 3-year-old boy killed, mom hurt in Batangas road crash
World.content:
A three-year-old boy was killed, and his mother was hurt in a vehicular accident in Rosario, Batangas, on Tuesday morning, Nov. 10, 2026. INQUIRER FILES

LUCENA CITY – A three-year-old boy was killed, and his mother was hurt in a vehicular accident in Rosario, Batangas, on Tuesday morning.

The driver of an owner-type custom-built jeep lost control of his vehicle at 9:55 a.m. and slammed into the rear end of a parked tricycle, which was sent hurling at the mother and child who were in its path at Barangay Poblacion D, the Calabarzon police said Wednesday.
