World.title: Ukraine-Russia talks resume in Abu Dhabi after nine-month pause, with US mediation
World.content:
Russia-Ukraine talks resume

Trilateral talks between the United States, Ukraine and Russia aimed at ending the war in Ukraine resumed in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, on 10 November. The meetings will continue on 11 November.

The main issues on the agenda include security guarantees for the post-war period, a ceasefire and the future of Ukraine’s eastern territories.

This is the first meeting in this trilateral format since February 2026. The United States is mediating the talks.

Who is taking part in the talks?

Ukraine’s delegation is led by Rustem Umerov, head of the Foreign Intelligence Service. Russia’s delegation is led by Vladimir Medinsky, an aide to President Vladimir Putin. US President Donald Trump is represented by his special envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

At the initial stage, the Ukrainian delegation held meetings with representatives from the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, NATO and the European Commission. The talks then continued in a trilateral format involving Ukraine, the US and Russia.

According to Rustem Umerov, Ukraine’s main priorities include ending the fighting, securing reliable post-war security guarantees, rebuilding the country’s economy and resolving humanitarian issues.

At the start of the meeting, US representative Jared Kushner said recent contacts had helped narrow the differences between the sides. “He [Trump] asked us to make an extra effort to find a solution that, hopefully, will end the war and put both sides in a much stronger position, giving them the opportunity to realise the full potential of their countries,” Kushner said.

Meanwhile, Russian delegation head Vladimir Medinsky expressed hope that the talks would bring progress towards peace, in the interests of the people of both countries.

Donetsk and post-war security guarantees

One of the most difficult issues in the negotiations concerns control over territories in eastern Ukraine, particularly in Donetsk region.

Russia demands that Ukraine surrender the parts of Donetsk region it still controls. Kyiv, however, refuses to give up land that Ukrainian forces have spent years defending.

At a briefing on 9 November, an unnamed US official said both sides had shown some flexibility on territorial issues during closed-door discussions.

However, the official stressed that they could not reach an agreement on this issue until they had established what the post-war security arrangements would look like.

“They will not be able to resolve the issue of Donetsk or the territorial question until they understand what the post-war security architecture will look like. It is important to understand that neither issue can be finally agreed without the other,” the US official said.

According to the official, security guarantees for Ukraine could include a mechanism similar to Articles 4 and 5 of the NATO treaty, providing for consultations and defensive assistance in the event of a security threat.

A senior Ukrainian official told Reuters that Kyiv was not discussing territorial concessions. The official said the issue could only be addressed by the countries’ leaders and only in the context of providing Ukraine with appropriate security guarantees.

Europe seeks a role in the talks

Ahead of the trilateral meeting in Abu Dhabi, representatives of Ukraine, the US, the EU, NATO, the UK, France, Germany and Italy also gathered in the city.

On 9 November, following a conversation with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said:

“The European Union will be represented, together with our partners.”

She also backed efforts to restore freedom of navigation in the Black Sea and called for an end to attacks on food and energy infrastructure.

European leaders insist that Europe itself must have a say in decisions concerning the security of the continent.

In their view, lasting peace in Ukraine will be impossible without reliable security guarantees.

Russia, however, said that the ongoing talks in Abu Dhabi should involve only Russia, Ukraine and the United States, with European representatives excluded from the meetings.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the Americans had their own channels of communication with the Europeans, as did the Ukrainians.

Why have the talks resumed now?

The previous trilateral meetings between the US, Russia and Ukraine on the war took place in January and February 2026. The latest round was held in Geneva on 17–18 February, but the sides failed to reach an agreement.

One reason for the pause was the war between the US, Israel and Iran, which shifted Washington’s attention away from Ukraine to other developments.

On Thursday, 5 November, Donald Trump met Kirill Dmitriev, a representative of the Russian president, at the White House.

Following the meeting, Trump said a “big deal” to end the war in Ukraine could be reached. He suggested the agreement would go beyond Ukraine and involve other European countries.

“This will be a big deal, and it won’t be limited to Ukraine alone. You could say that all of Europe will be involved,” Trump said.

Ukraine remains sceptical that Trump’s proposed deal could deliver a just peace. Kyiv insists that the war must not end at the expense of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

The talks in Abu Dhabi will continue on 11 November. It remains unclear whether the sides will reach a concrete agreement. Their main disagreements still concern territorial issues and the format of security guarantees for Ukraine.

Russia-Ukraine talks resume

World.title: Why did Abkhazia’s president travel to Russia to be baptised? Several theories are circulating, all political
World.content:
President of Abkhazia Badra Gunba and his wife and two sons have been baptised. The ceremony took place at the Sretensky Monastery in Moscow, prompting mixed reactions on social media.

Some saw it as a sign of the Kremlin tightening its control over Abkhazia. Others linked it to the church schism within the republic, while a third group pointed to the lack of fully fledged Orthodox institutions in Abkhazia.

The ceremony was initially due to take place at another Moscow monastery, the Donskoy Monastery. However, the organisers moved it to the Sretensky Monastery because the Donskoy site lacked suitable baptismal facilities.

Metropolitan Feognost, who also heads the Russian Orthodox Church’s (ROC) Synodal Department for Monasteries and Monasticism, baptised the Gunba family. He began his career as a priest in Abkhazia many years ago and later provided extensive support to Abkhaz students at the Moscow Theological Seminary.

Badra Gunba was baptised under the name Bogdan. Sergei Kiriyenko, first deputy head of the Russian presidential administration and the Kremlin’s official overseeing Abkhazia, attended the ceremony. Gunba’s decision to be baptised as an adult reflects the relatively “democratic” approach to religion in Abkhazia. Some Abkhaz people are Orthodox Christians, others are Muslims, while some remain followers of the traditional Abkhaz belief in the god Anцэа. Even Orthodox parents often choose not to baptise their children as infants, allowing them to grow up and decide for themselves which faith to follow.

Abkhaz society generally welcomed the president’s baptism, but most people felt he should have undergone the ceremony in one of Abkhazia’s own churches rather than in Moscow.

Some social media users saw this as one of the consequences of a long-running conflict between the two unrecognised churches: the Abkhazian Orthodox Church, led by Father Vissarion, and the Holy Metropolis of Abkhazia, headed by Archimandrite Dorotheos.

In effect, Abkhazia currently has no officially recognised church. The republic’s religious institutions lack international recognition, just as Abkhazia itself does. The Russian Orthodox Church (ROC) does not even recognise the Abkhazian Church as autocephalous.

Archimandrite Dorotheos believes this is precisely why Badra Gunba travelled to Moscow to be baptised.

“This sends a signal to the entire Orthodox world: until the issue of the Abkhazian Church is resolved and a fully fledged institution of the Orthodox Church of Abkhazia is restored, even the republic’s top officials cannot receive the Sacrament of Baptism from an Abkhaz bishop, however much they might wish to. This is simply because the entire Orthodox community’s unwillingness to address the issue for 33 years has left our country, our people and its leadership without episcopal pastoral care,” Dorotheos said.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

World.title: ‘An example of shadow justice’: another letter from jailed former Georgian prime minister Garibashvili
World.content:
New letter from Georgia’s former prime minister in prison

Former Georgian prime minister Irakli Garibashvili, who is currently in prison, has described the decision to hold his trial behind closed doors as an example of “shadow justice” driven by fear.

In another letter sent from prison – probably his tenth – the politician, who served two terms as prime minister, again speaks of political persecution, selective justice and discrimination against him.

“‘This is a violation. Cases involving other individuals, whether in the same context or over similar charges, have generally been heard in open court. My trial, however, is taking place behind closed doors. This shows that the procedure is being used not to uphold the rule of law, but as an instrument of selective justice. It is a clear example of “shadow justice” and an attempt to prevent public scrutiny,’ Garibashvili writes.

The former prime minister says he intended to use the court hearings to speak about the pressure he had faced and the political persecution he had experienced.

“‘The authorities have made this decision out of fear, seeking to keep the proceedings shrouded in “darkness”. I want to make this clear: I have nothing to hide. That is why I insist that the trial be open and brought into the “light”.’

In another statement, Garibashvili recalls telling the judge at the previous hearing that he had faced psychological pressure and blackmail. He describes it as ‘psychological terror, torture, moral suffering and interference in political activity’.

The former prime minister claims that the defence was not allowed to submit to the court a letter containing threats and blackmail that he had received. His lawyers were also denied access to some of the case materials.

Garibashvili writes that the prosecutor’s office failed to launch an investigation, despite receiving information from him about possible signs of a crime. He says the opposite happened: authorities brought new charges against him in line with the ultimatum mentioned in his letter.

Garibashvili also alleges violations of Articles 3, 6 and 18 of the European Convention on Human Rights. These articles concern, respectively, the prohibition of torture and inhuman or degrading treatment, the right to a fair trial, and the limits on the use of restrictions on rights. The former prime minister claims that, taken together, these rights have been violated in his case.

Why is the trial being held behind closed doors?

On 2 November, the Tbilisi City Court began hearing the bribery case against Irakli Garibashvili on its merits. It was the first hearing that the former prime minister attended in person.

At the start of the hearing, he stressed the importance of an open and transparent trial and opposed holding the proceedings behind closed doors.

The prosecution asked the court to hold the hearing in private. It argued that the case involved classified procurement by the Ministry of Defence, required the questioning of other senior officials and contained personal data.

The defence objected, pointing out that courts had previously heard similar cases in public. Judge Tamar Mchedlishvili ultimately ruled that the hearing should take place behind closed doors.

Garibashvili’s letters from prison

Irakli Garibashvili, once a favourite of Georgian Dream’s honorary chairman and oligarch Bidzina Ivanishvili, was arrested in the courtroom on 12 January 2026.

For several months after his arrest, the former prime minister and his family remained silent and made no comments to the media.

On 17 August, the former prime minister sent his first letter from prison. It marked his first major public statement, in which he accused Bidzina Ivanishvili and the government of blackmail. “They left me no other choice; I have no option but to fight,” Garibashvili wrote.

According to the letter, he had been offered a deal: if he pleaded guilty to a new corruption charge, authorities would release him on condition that he never return to politics.

More letters followed.

In his subsequent letters, the former prime minister gradually shifted from a defensive stance to making political statements. He accused several senior officials, including Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, of orchestrating a political vendetta against him.

He also referred to more serious offences, including cases in which people had been driven to suicide. In addition, he said he had no intention of returning to politics.

In one of his most recent letters, he even reflected on his time in office.

Criminal cases against the former prime minister

Irakli Garibashvili currently faces charges in two criminal cases.

In the first, prosecutors charged him with laundering a particularly large amount of illicit income. On 12 January 2026, he pleaded guilty and reached a plea bargain with the prosecutor’s office. The court sentenced him to five years in prison and fined him one million lari.

In the second case, prosecutors accuse the former prime minister of accepting a particularly large bribe. According to the prosecution, Garibashvili received 750,000 lari in connection with classified procurement by the Ministry of Defence.

The case is linked to the criminal proceedings against former Defence Minister Juansher Burchuladze. Garibashvili denies the charges and describes them as politically motivated.

Harsh prison conditions

Irakli Garibashvili and his family have repeatedly spoken about the harsh conditions of his imprisonment. On 7 November, his brother-in-law, Lekso Tamazashvili, said that the former prime minister had seen his children only twice in the past 11 months.

He called on the Special Penitentiary Service to show compassion and allow the children to see their father.

Meanwhile, Garibashvili’s lawyer, Lili Gelashvili, said that authorities had cancelled a planned meeting between her client and his children. She linked the decision to the publication of letters Garibashvili had written in prison.

The Special Penitentiary Service rejected the lawyer’s claims. According to the agency, Garibashvili had already used all the visits allowed under the law, including two extended visits and standard short-term meetings.

The service explained that authorities treat any additional visits as a form of reward, and the head of the correctional facility has discretion over whether to grant them.

The agency also said that no additional visit had ever been scheduled, so there could have been no cancellation. The issue of restrictions on visits with his children first became public in late August. The circumstances were similar then: authorities cancelled a planned meeting between Garibashvili and his family, although the Penitentiary Service denied the report at the time.

New letter from Georgia’s former prime minister in prison

World.title: ‘Democrats do not see TRIPP as project exclusive to Trump administration’: opinion from Yerevan
World.content:
US midterm elections and implementation of TRIPP

The US midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party won control of both chambers of Congress, have also become a major topic of discussion in Armenia.

Government officials and experts are discussing the Democrats’ victory in the context of developments in the South Caucasus. In particular, they are focusing on the implementation of the Armenian-American TRIPP project (the “Trump Route”).

TRIPP (Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity) is a road that will connect Azerbaijan with its Nakhchivan exclave through Armenian territory. The project also aims to reopen regional transport links. As a result, Armenia will gain access to third countries via Azerbaijani territory. For several years, Yerevan and Baku failed to reach an agreement on the issue. Azerbaijan demanded a road that it called the “Zangezur Corridor”. Armenia’s authorities said they were ready to reopen all transport routes. However, Yerevan rejected the term “corridor”, which implies that the country would lose control – and therefore sovereign rights – over this territory. The two sides reached an agreement in Washington on 8 August. Under the deal, the road will remain under Armenian sovereignty, while the US will join the process as a business partner. The initiative took the name “Trump Route” after the mediator.

Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan stressed that national interests must come first in such matters. Individual political figures and teams may adjust the course of policy, he said.

“I am confident that what we are now doing with the US benefits the United States itself. I do not think the Democrats will have no interest in getting TRIPP built as soon as possible,” he emphasised.

Political analyst Tigran Grigoryan explained that US presidents often lose ground in midterm elections. According to him, their approval ratings usually decline during the first year or two in office, as public dissatisfaction with their policies grows.

Grigoryan described the Republicans’ midterm results as “a historic-scale fiasco”. Nevertheless, he does not expect any significant changes to the implementation of TRIPP.

“There is bipartisan consensus in the US on TRIPP. Democrats do not see TRIPP as a project exclusive to the Trump administration. They recognise its importance for the South Caucasus and for maintaining peace,” the political analyst said.

At the same time, he noted that Yerevan should do more work with its American partners, both at official and expert level. He said Armenia needed to make one message clear to them: “Under no circumstances must the implementation of the Trump Route be put at risk.”

“There will be no problems” – Armenia’s Security Council secretary

Speaking at the Third World Armenian Summit, Security Council Secretary Armen Grigoryan recalled that the Trump administration had developed the TRIPP project.

“However, I am confident that TRIPP is not simply Trump’s personal business project. It is also a business project for the state.”

Grigoryan said Armenia and the US had agreed on TRIPP at state level. He believes the project will encounter no problems during implementation.

Journalists asked the Security Council secretary whether he was concerned that, after the elections, Trump might turn his attention to domestic issues and lose interest in the South Caucasus.

“TRIPP is not an initiative that depends on any one administration or a single factor. It is an important agreement that aims, among other things, to eliminate a casus belli – a pretext for starting a war,” Armen Grigoryan replied.

“The US will also have opportunities” – US chargé d’affaires in Armenia

At the same summit, David Allen, the US chargé d’affaires in Armenia, also discussed the TRIPP project.

Allen noted that TRIPP aligns with the Armenian government’s Crossroads of Peace initiative, which aims to turn the country into a regional trade and transit hub.

“For the US, it creates commercial opportunities for American companies and advances our strategic interest in seeing the South Caucasus become a stable, prosperous and interconnected region.”

The diplomat said the US believes that trade links between neighbouring countries reduce the likelihood of war.

“When roads and railways cross borders, they carry not only goods but also trust.”

Comment

Political analyst Tigran Grigoryan says:

“Many people link the midterm election results to the US decision to go to war with Iran. That move had a significant impact on oil and fuel prices and, consequently, on consumers. However, in a broader sense, the events of the past two years led to this historic outcome.

What should we expect in the context of Armenia? I believe oversight of the Trump administration’s policies will become much stricter.

The US system of government is essentially designed so that no branch of power can impose its policies on another.

In theory, even if a Democrat-controlled Congress tries to restrict the president’s decisions, he retains the power of veto and the authority to issue executive orders. During his second term, for example, Obama often governed through executive orders, bypassing Congress on many issues. However, on many other issues, the administration cannot make progress without congressional involvement.

The Democrats’ main advantage is their oversight role. They will now control key committees in the House of Representatives. This means that Democrats will scrutinise all matters relating to TRIPP, including its funding.

They will also pay much closer attention to possible corruption. Reuters recently published an interesting report examining the business interests of Konstantin Sokolov, head of the TRIPP+ Foundation, in Armenia and the potential for conflicts of interest.

This could, for example, become an important area of scrutiny for the Democratic majority.

The TRIPP+ Foundation operates as a separate investment fund. Its main purpose is to finance the Trump Route project. The 52-year-old financier and investor Konstantin Sokolov also heads Dynamic Frontier Holdings. The company recently acquired the Teghut copper and molybdenum mine in Armenia. Since 2024, Sokolov has also owned a 20% stake in Viva Armenia, a mobile network operator. Some experts also suspect him of having links to Russia. Sokolov was born in Russia and moved to the US at the age of 21. He is known for investments in telecommunications, energy and financial services.

The Trump administration’s characteristic approach to foreign policy, often based on nepotism and favouritism, has attracted the Democrats’ attention. This includes the involvement of Jared Kushner, Steve Witkoff and other figures close to Trump in various matters. We should therefore expect Democrats to take a much closer interest in this issue.

Of course, we want TRIPP to be seen as more than just a project of the Trump administration. We need to strengthen that understanding. And we should take active steps to achieve this.”

Background

The Trump Route offers Armenia an opportunity to reopen regional transport links in practice. For Azerbaijan, it provides the shortest route connecting the country with Nakhchivan.

The 43-kilometre section running through Armenian territory will include a railway. A motorway, energy infrastructure and digital communications networks will also run along the same route.

All infrastructure located on Armenian territory will remain under Armenia’s sovereignty and jurisdiction.

The ratified framework agreement provides for the creation of the TRIPP Development Company, which will oversee the project’s development and implementation.

Initially, the US will own 74% of the company’s shares and Armenia 26%. After 49 years, if the parties extend their cooperation for a further 50 years, Armenia’s stake will rise to 49%.

On 7 November 2026, Armenia, the US and Azerbaijan issued a joint statement outlining steps to advance the TRIPP project as quickly as possible:

“The parties agreed to launch the first two trilateral technical planning groups, focusing on areas such as transportation and electricity transmission. Establishing these technical groups marks an important step towards resolving complex technical issues and moving on to the next stages of implementation, including ensuring connections with other regional infrastructure.”

According to the statement, the format brings together politicians and technical experts from the three countries to work jointly and help ensure stability, economic viability and commercial prosperity in the region.

The statement came from US Assistant Secretary of State for European and Eurasian Affairs Brendan Hanrahan, Armenian Deputy Foreign Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Trade Vahan Kostanyan, and Azerbaijani Deputy Foreign Minister Elnur Mammadov. However, they provided no further details.

US midterm elections and implementation of TRIPP

World.title: Have people in Georgia become more cautious about what they say on social media? Street survey in Tbilisi (video)
World.content:
Street survey on social media in Georgia

We asked people walking the streets of Tbilisi whether they or those close to them had recently become more cautious than before about expressing their opinions on social media.

Background

On 1 June 2024, a unit tasked with combating “hate speech” was established in Georgia. It monitors people’s statements in the public sphere. According to the Georgian Dream party, the unit aims to reduce hate speech and online campaigns involving insults.

Since the unit began its work, authorities have launched numerous administrative proceedings based on social media posts, affecting hundreds of people. Most received fines ranging from 1,500 to 6,000 lari, and some were fined more than once.

The law also provides for administrative detention, although courts generally try to avoid imposing it.

To date, authorities have used this measure only a handful of times – twice against the same person, journalist Vakho Sanaia. He is currently in detention. A court first sentenced him to 14 days in detention and later handed him a 30-day sentence.

Lawyers have described the initiative as an attempt to restrict freedom of expression and legalise censorship. Meanwhile, social media users have nicknamed the unit the “scrolling and screenshot department”, reflecting the nature of its work.

What did people in the survey say?

Respondents were almost evenly divided over whether these restrictions had affected them. Half said the fear was tangible, whether or not people felt ready to admit it openly.

The other half insisted that this repressive measure had made no difference to them or their social circles.

Here are some notable responses:

* “Lately, I’ve been weighing my words carefully. It’s not exactly conformism, but at some point – I see it among my acquaintances, and I notice it in myself too – a thought creeps in: ‘Maybe I’ll wait a little; perhaps all this will somehow blow over.’ There is fear involved! Perhaps people have simply become frightened. Do you see what I mean? And yet there is a certain line: once you cross it, there’s no going back.” This was the view of writer Aleko Shugladze, whom we met on the streets of Tbilisi while conducting the survey.

* “Personally, I don’t restrict myself at all. I don’t even try to edit the opinions I want to post in any way. Because if we start worrying today that saying something could get us into trouble, tomorrow even the thought of expressing an opinion could become punishable.”

* “In a way, it does affect people. Knowing that restrictions, fines and the risk of arrest exist has an impact. I’ve always been afraid. Of course, you also start having doubts – you wonder what might happen next and what the consequences could be.”

We also met people who knew nothing about the new unit. As often happens, many avoided the camera and declined to take part in the survey.

Others told us they had never really used social media much.

Street survey on social media in Georgia

World.title: Sergei Shoigu: ‘Georgia prevented coup in 2024 and began defending its national interests’
World.content:
Russia increasingly praises Georgian Dream

Russia’s Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu praised the course pursued by the Georgian government and welcomed closer economic ties between Moscow and Tbilisi.

Shoigu made the remarks in Moscow on 9 November at the 14th annual meeting of security council secretaries from Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) member states.

“In 2024, the Georgian authorities successfully thwarted an attempted coup initiated by the pro-Western opposition and set out to defend the country’s national interests,” Shoigu said.

At the same meeting, Shoigu spoke about the development of economic cooperation between Russia and Georgia.

“We welcome the active development of trade and economic cooperation between Georgia and Russia. I would also like to stress that regional problems should be resolved through political and diplomatic means, without interference from outside countries,” the Russian Security Council secretary said.

Shoigu also highlighted the importance of resuming the work of the regional 3+3 consultative platform. The format currently includes Russia, Iran, Turkey, Armenia and Azerbaijan.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan first proposed the 3+3 format in 2020 during a meeting with Ilham Aliyev in Azerbaijan, following the end of the Karabakh war. The initiative envisaged a regional cooperation platform involving Turkey, Russia, Iran, Azerbaijan, Armenia and Georgia, aimed at securing lasting peace and stability in the South Caucasus. Despite repeated calls from Russia, the Georgian government has said it will not take part in meetings under this format. The first meeting took place in 2021 and the second in 2023. Georgia attended neither.

Shoigu also addressed the situation in the South Caucasus.

He said the situation in the region was improving and that “the normalisation of Armenian-Azerbaijani relations and the de facto establishment of peace in the region are producing results”.

Georgian Dream responds to Shoigu’s remarks

Giorgi Volski, the parliament’s first deputy speaker, told journalists that Shoigu’s remarks served merely as a “lifeline for those media outlets – and the politicians who support them – that are waging a fierce campaign against the state”.

He added that Georgia had, in effect, faced an attempt to overthrow the government by force, and that Shoigu’s assessment of the events was irrelevant.

“I don’t know what you mean by ‘praise’, but what actually happened was an attempted uprising, a coup and an attempt to overthrow the government by force – although some tried to portray it as a ‘peaceful change of power’. How Shoigu chooses to describe it is completely irrelevant,” Volski said.

As for the 3+3 format, Volski noted that Georgia was not the only country reluctant to join. Other countries originally envisaged as participants also showed little enthusiasm for the initiative.

Background

Shoigu’s remarks are not the first instance of senior Russian officials speaking favourably about the policies of Georgian Dream.

Over the past year, Moscow has repeatedly sent signals of support for the course pursued by the Georgian government.

Last week, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said, that Moscow stood ready to support initiatives aimed at deepening cooperation between Russia and Georgia. She also said she would like to see a Russian embassy open in Tbilisi.

In August, Russian Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev praised the Georgian government’s “pragmatic course”. Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin also said that Georgia’s successful development depended on cooperation with Russia rather than confrontation.

Earlier, in April, Galuzin said, that Russia stood ready to normalise relations with Georgia, but the extent of this process depended on Tbilisi’s own willingness.

In March, Zakharova also said, that Moscow was ready to deepen relations with Georgia, adding that “the Georgian side is also interested in constructive relations with Russia”. In February, Galuzin stressed that “cooperation with Russia is one of the key factors behind Georgia’s ‘unprecedented economic’ recovery”.

On 2 September 2008, following the war that August, Georgia severed diplomatic relations with Russia. The decision came after Russia recognised the independence of Abkhazia and the Tskhinvali region and occupied Georgian territories. Economic ties have gradually recovered since then, but political dialogue remains limited.

Similar statements also came from Moscow last year.

In December 2025, Mikhail Kalugin, director of the Russian Foreign Ministry’s Fourth Department of the CIS Countries, said that Tbilisi was demonstrating “sound pragmatism” and pursuing a multi-vector foreign policy.

He welcomed Georgia’s decision not to join Western sanctions against Russia, saying that this approach had helped develop economic ties between the two countries.

Russia increasingly praises Georgian Dream

World.title: Tashkent and Ashgabat offer vision for Central Asia’s climate future - ahead of COP31
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 11. Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan intend to use the COP31 World Leaders’ Summit in Antalya to advance initiatives aimed at addressing Central Asia’s climate challenges. Both countries are linking their national environmental priorities to broader regional cooperation, but are pursuing different approaches: Tashkent is focusing on measurable commitments and practical projects, while Ashgabat is emphasizing the establishment of international institutions and the development of technological cooperation.

The participation of the two countries in the summit on November 11 gives this agenda additional political weight. For Central Asia, a region facing water shortages, land degradation, desertification and the consequences of climate change, COP31 offers a platform not only to discuss national targets but also to coordinate long-term mechanisms for regional cooperation.

Uzbekistan moves from climate commitments to investment projects

Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has consistently advanced his country's climate agenda on international platforms, viewing it as both an environmental security issue and a driver of economic development.

Addressing the COP29 World Leaders’ Summit in Baku in November 2024, he stressed that climate change had become a global challenge with a direct impact on Central Asia.

"Climate change has become the main global challenge and is directly contributing to growing geopolitical tensions. We are acutely feeling its consequences in Central Asia," Mirziyoyev said.

At the time, the Uzbek leader also outlined a number of initiatives calling for closer international coordination. These included establishing an International Centre for Assessing Climate Loss and Damage, developing a UN declaration on environmental security and the health of river ecosystems, with particular attention to the Aral Sea issue, and setting up a regional genetic resources bank. Tashkent also proposed establishing a UN Innovation Hub for Agro-Industrial Development in Landlocked Countries and an Alliance of Climate Capitals of the World.

These proposals complement Uzbekistan's national commitments. The country has set a target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions per unit of GDP by 50% by 2035 compared with 2010 levels. In addition, renewable energy is expected to account for 54% of electricity generation by 2030. The development of solar and wind power, green hydrogen and electric transport is seen as part of a broader economic transformation.

At COP31, this approach is already translating into practical action. On November 10, the Climate-resilient Landscapes in Central Asia (CLiCA) programme, approved by the Green Climate Fund, was launched. Uzbekistan is set to receive investments worth 103.7 million euros for projects in 15 districts across four regions. The programme covers the restoration of 18,000 hectares of forests and 123,000 hectares of pastureland, the introduction of drip irrigation and support for farmers.

During a meeting with the Green Climate Fund's Executive Director, Mirziyoyev also discussed expanding national institutions' access to climate finance. Uzbekistan's joint project portfolio with the fund already exceeds $200 million.

Thus, the president's participation in COP31 enables Tashkent to link its previously announced international initiatives with concrete financial instruments. In the longer term, this could strengthen the country's capacity to adapt its agriculture and natural landscapes to climate change, while attracting additional funding to address the challenges facing the Aral Sea region.

Turkmenistan proposes regional centres and international mechanisms

Turkmenistan is approaching COP31 with a different set of priorities, placing particular emphasis on regional institutions under the UN umbrella, climate technologies and international dialogue platforms. Promoting these initiatives has become a consistent element of the country's environmental diplomacy.

National Leader of the Turkmen People and Chairman of the Halk Maslahaty Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov has consistently advocated broader international cooperation in clean energy and climate technologies. At the Vienna International Energy and Climate Forum in April 2026, he reaffirmed Turkmenistan's commitment to the Paris Agreement and proposed stepping up joint projects in solar and wind energy.

Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov also placed particular emphasis on hydrogen energy. Turkmenistan is considering its development based on natural gas and has proposed drawing up a ten-year Global Programme for the Transition to Hydrogen Energy under the auspices of the UN.

"Now that we are embarking on the practical development of hydrogen energy in Turkmenistan based on natural gas, we are ready to work in this area on the broadest possible scale and with all interested international partners," he said in Vienna.

A key element of this strategy is the proposal to establish a UN Regional Centre for Climate Change Technologies in Central Asia in Ashgabat. The initiative envisages promoting scientific research, facilitating technology exchange and supporting regional countries in adapting to climate change.

President Serdar Berdimuhamedov, in turn, has been advancing the regional dimension of this agenda. At the Regional Ecological Summit in Astana in April 2026, he drew attention to declining water resources, land degradation and accelerating desertification, stressing that these processes affect virtually every aspect of people's lives.

At the 13th summit of the Organization of Turkic States in Ankara in October, Serdar Berdimuhamedov again called for the establishment of UN regional centres in Ashgabat focusing on climate technologies and combating desertification. Another important initiative was presented at the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku in October, as a proposed instrument for international environmental cooperation.

"To make a practical contribution to the development of international environmental cooperation, Turkmenistan is putting forward an initiative to establish the Ashgabat Climate Dialogue - a multilateral platform for exchanging experience and coordinating approaches to climate change adaptation, combating desertification and drought, the sustainable use of water resources and promoting green solutions," Serdar Berdimuhamedov said.

At the same time, Turkmenistan can offer not only institutional initiatives but also experience in reducing methane emissions. Following its accession to the Global Methane Pledge in 2023 and the establishment of a national commission dedicated to this area, the country reported an 11% reduction in methane emissions by the end of 2024, exceeding its planned target.

The arrival of Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov at COP31, alongside Serdar Berdimuhamedov's efforts to advance the regional climate agenda, highlights the continuity of this policy at different levels of the country's leadership.

In the longer term, implementing Turkmenistan's proposals could establish permanent regional infrastructure for exchanging climate technologies, developing joint projects and attracting international financing. This is particularly relevant for arid areas of Central Asia, where water security, desertification and agricultural resilience are closely interconnected.

Two complementary approaches

Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan are advancing different but complementary approaches to climate cooperation. Tashkent is seeking to translate national commitments and international proposals into projects backed by financing, while Ashgabat is pushing for permanent regional mechanisms capable of supporting such projects and facilitating technology exchange.

Over the longer term, combining these approaches could contribute to a more systematic response to challenges shared across Central Asia. The two countries' climate initiatives address not only emissions reduction and clean energy development, but also water resource preservation, land restoration, protection of the Aral Sea basin's ecosystems and strengthening communities' resilience to climate risks.

The significance of Uzbekistan's and Turkmenistan's participation in the COP31 World Leaders' Summit therefore goes beyond presenting their respective national positions. It creates an opportunity to advance a regional agenda in which political commitments, international institutions and practical investment projects are designed to complement one another.

World.title: Italy’s Gamma Meccanica, Uzbek partners sign €104M memorandum (Exclusive)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 11. Italian engineering company Gamma Meccanica, Uzbekistan’s ECO BASALT and the administration of Namangan Region have signed a trilateral memorandum of understanding outlining a €104 million industrial development program in Uzbekistan’s Chust district, focusing on mineral wool production, insulation materials and plastics recycling, Gamma Meccanica told Trend.

The agreement was signed following a visit by a Namangan Region delegation led by Governor Shavkatjon Abdurazakov to Gamma Meccanica’s manufacturing facilities in Bibbiano, Italy, on October 30, the Italian company said.

During the visit, the delegation met with Gamma Meccanica President Andrea Burini to discuss industrial development, technological modernization, and opportunities for long-term cooperation between Italian and Uzbek businesses.

The program envisages modernization and expansion of existing mineral wool production facilities, including the installation of additional equipment to manufacture mineral wool substrates for hydroponic agriculture.

Another key component involves establishing a new production facility for insulation materials and sandwich panels intended for industrial construction and building insulation.

Additionally, the development program includes a dedicated facility for manufacturing environmentally friendly stone wool-based substrates for greenhouse operations and hydroponic cultivation.

Further phases could involve the production of extruded polystyrene (XPS) insulation boards and the introduction of technologies for recycling plastic waste, including agricultural plastic films.

The overall program is scheduled to be implemented in stages through 2030.

Investment and technological cooperation

The memorandum outlines an estimated investment program of €104 million. The amount covers construction of production facilities and supporting infrastructure, raw material procurement, technological equipment, installation, and other expenses associated with launching the planned facilities.

Gamma Meccanica will contribute its engineering and industrial expertise, drawing on 50 years of experience in designing, manufacturing and integrating equipment for mineral wool production and processing.

Depending on individual project requirements and commercial agreements, the cooperation may include equipment supplies, engineering services, technical assistance, installation supervision, commissioning support and personnel training.

Moreover, the parties identified plastics recycling, resource efficiency and environmentally sustainable industrial technologies as potential areas for further cooperation.

The memorandum establishes a general framework for collaboration, while technical specifications, financing arrangements, individual contract values and implementation schedules will be determined through separate agreements and relevant approval procedures.

Further details on production capacities and project timelines are expected to be announced as individual project plans are finalized.

The initiative marks another step in expanding industrial and technological cooperation between Uzbekistan and Italy, with Namangan Region seeking to attract foreign expertise and develop higher-value manufacturing capabilities.

World.title: Fluor’s Q3 adjusted EBITDA falls 11.8% to $142 million, guidance kept
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 9. Fluor’s adjusted EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization) fell 11.8% year-on-year to $142 million in the third quarter of 2026, according to Trend’s calculations based on company data. The company affirmed its full-year 2026 guidance for adjusted EBITDA of $500-525 million.

The adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 3.8%, compared with 4.8% a year earlier. The year-earlier margin had included an 80-basis-point benefit from the Santos revenue reversal.

For the first nine months of 2026, adjusted EBITDA declined 14.6% to $351 million from $411 million. The nine-month margin was 3.0%, against 3.6% a year earlier. The company has already earned between 66.9% and 70.2% of its full-year guidance range.

To reach the full-year guidance range, the fourth quarter would need to deliver between $149 million and $174 million of adjusted EBITDA (or around $161.5 million to reach the guidance midpoint). That would represent an increase of 4.9% to 22.5% from the third-quarter figure of $142 million (and +13.7% for the midpoint). The first half of the year produced about $209 million of adjusted EBITDA.

On a GAAP basis, EBITDA was $213 million in the third quarter, compared with a loss of $469 million a year earlier. For the nine months, GAAP EBITDA reached $456 million against a loss of $356 million in the same period of 2025.

Fluor Corporation is a global engineering, procurement, construction and project management company founded in 1912 and headquartered in Irving, Texas. With nearly 23,000 employees worldwide, the company provides professional and technical solutions across a wide range of industries through its Urban Solutions, Energy Solutions and Mission Solutions business segments.

World.title: Ukraine and Russia discuss possible large-scale POW exchange - Zelenskyy
World.content:
Photo: Official website of the President of Ukraine

BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 11. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that the possibility of a large-scale prisoner-of-war exchange was discussed during trilateral talks involving Russia, the United States, and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi.

Zelenskyy made the remarks while speaking to journalists in Denmark.

According to him, the parties are considering an exchange in a "1,000-for-1,000" or even a "1,500-for-1,500" format.

He noted that U.S. representatives would hold talks with the Russian side regarding the proposal.

Zelenskyy also said that the Russian delegation raised the territorial issue during the meeting. In response, the Ukrainian president stressed that any discussion of this matter should take place at the level of heads of state.

The next round of negotiations is expected to focus on de-escalation, energy security, and the situation in the Black Sea.

World.title: Turkmenistan reports 13.6% growth in transport and communications services
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 11. Turkmenistan's transport and communications sector increased the volume of completed work and services by 13.6% in January-October 2026, with the strongest growth recorded in air transport and communications.

Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Batyr Annayev reported on the sector's performance at a government meeting chaired by President Serdar Berdimuhamedov.

According to Trend's calculations based on official figures, the overall growth rate for completed work and services declined by 5.5 percentage points compared to January-October 2024.

Freight transportation plans across all modes of transport were fulfilled by 108.5%, while passenger transportation plans reached 101.9%. Compared to the same period in 2025, the freight plan fulfillment rate improved by 7.9 percentage points, whereas the passenger transportation indicator decreased by 3.1 percentage points.

Among individual agencies, the State Service Türkmenhowaýollary recorded the highest growth in services, at 18.3%, followed by the Ministry of Communications at 15.1% and the Ministry of Automobile Transport at 14.9%. The Ministry of Railway Transport reported 7.4% growth, while the State Service for Maritime and River Transport recorded 1.4%.

Trend's calculations show that railway transport improved its growth rate by 1.4 percentage points year-on-year and 4.6 percentage points compared to 2024. Automobile transport also accelerated, posting increases of 1.8 and 4.9 percentage points, respectively.

Air transport recorded an 8-percentage-point improvement year-on-year. However, its growth rate remained 36.2 percentage points below the level recorded in January-October 2024. The maritime and river transport indicator declined by 7.2 percentage points year-on-year and 12.6 percentage points compared to 2024. Communications services also slowed by 4.9 percentage points year-on-year, although the rate remained 0.5 percentage points above the 2024 level.

Following the report, President Serdar Berdimuhamedov stressed the importance of further modernizing the transport and communications sector's technical infrastructure. He instructed the Deputy Chairman to take measures to increase passenger and freight transportation, make more effective use of digital systems and expand the range of services provided.

Meanwhile, Turkmenistan's geographical position gives it access to several major transport routes linking Central Asia with other regions. Located on the eastern coast of the Caspian Sea, the country connects the landlocked states of Central Asia with the South Caucasus and markets further west, while its southern borders with Iran and Afghanistan provide potential routes towards the Middle East and South Asia. The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) identifies Turkmenistan as a critical node of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor, noting the country's role in developing links between Central Asia and Europe.

This position places Turkmenistan at the intersection of two major transport axes. The east-west direction connects China and Central Asia with the Caspian Sea, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Türkiye, forming part of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, also known as the Middle Corridor. The north-south direction links Kazakhstan with Iran through Turkmen territory, providing access to Persian Gulf markets. The Turkmenbashi International Seaport is central to these routes, serving as a maritime gateway for Central Asian cargo moving across the Caspian. The World Bank included Turkmenistan among the nine countries covered by its September 2026 assessment of the Trans-Caspian corridor, highlighting the potential of coordinated infrastructure investment to expand trade and improve connectivity between Asia and Europe.

At the same time, Turkmenistan is developing its domestic infrastructure to support this transit role. The railway connecting Ashgabat with the Turkmenbashi seaport is an important link between the country's eastern and western transport networks and is being prepared for comprehensive modernization. The line is also connected with international routes such as Lapis Lazuli, TRACECA, North-South and East-West. Alongside railway upgrades, the country is expanding its highway network, including the Ashgabat-Turkmenabat high-speed road, while continuing to develop maritime infrastructure. These investments are intended to make the country's geographical advantages more practical for freight operators by improving connections between ports, railways and road networks.

World.title: Kyrgyzstan's industrial output rises across all four main sectors in 2025
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 9. All four main industrial activity groups in Kyrgyzstan recorded higher production volumes in 2025 compared to the previous year.

These figures were calculated by Trend based on statistics published by the National Statistical Committee of the Kyrgyz Republic.

Water supply, waste treatment, and recycling posted the highest growth rate among the groups, expanding by 23.1% year-on-year.

Mining output increased by 14.2%, while production in electricity, gas, and steam supply expanded by 11.2%. Manufacturing, which accounts for 79.4% of total industrial output, rose by 9.8%, slightly below the 10.6% growth rate of the industrial sector as a whole.

However, the upward trend was not observed across every manufacturing activity. Production of electrical equipment declined by 33.9% compared to 2024, machinery and equipment production decreased by 40.7%, and output of computers, electronic, and optical equipment fell by 66.2%, marking the steepest drop among reported activities.

In practical terms, the 2025 output of computers and electronic equipment was only about one third of the previous year’s level.

Electrical equipment production stood at roughly two thirds of the 2024 level, and machinery and equipment production at around 59%. The figures show that growth in 2025 was broad-based across main industrial groups, although declines in engineering and electronics contrast with the overall positive dynamics.

World.title: Seven people hospitalized after car hits pedestrians in Glasgow
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 11. Seven people have been taken to hospital after a car struck pedestrians in the western part of Glasgow, Scotland.

This was reported by the city's police.

According to a law enforcement statement, seven injured people were taken to hospital for medical treatment and examination. The driver of the vehicle was also assessed by emergency medical personnel at the scene.

No information is yet available regarding the condition of those injured.

The incident is being treated as a road traffic accident.

World.title: Mamedyarov finishes 20th in blitz stage of Total Chess Pilot 2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 11. Azerbaijani grandmaster Shakhriyar Mamedyarov has concluded his campaign in the blitz stage of the Total Chess Pilot 2026 tournament, currently underway in Budapest, Hungary.

Mamedyarov finished 20th among 24 participants, scoring 3.5 points over nine rounds. He recorded three wins, one draw, and five defeats.

In the eighth round, the Azerbaijani chess player drew with Vietnam's Le Quang Liem while playing with the white pieces. In the final round, he defeated Dutch grandmaster Jorden van Foreest with the black pieces.

Norway's Magnus Carlsen won the blitz tournament with seven points. France's Maxime Vachier-Lagrave finished second with 6.5 points, while Armenia's Levon Aronian took third place with six points.

The group stage of the tournament begins today, November 11. In the event of a tie on points, the results of the blitz stage will be taken into account.

The tournament will run until November 20.

World.title: Judge issues $75K warning after labour hire firm fails to pay foreign workers
World.content:
A federal judge says a $75,600 fine for a labour hire company should put any other organisations that might be failing to pay their workers properly on notice.

Four Seasons Workforce and its director Pik Yok Chey were fined in the Federal Court after the firm was found to have failed to comply with two notices issued by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

The compliance notices required the company to back-pay entitlements to two migrant workers who it had supplied to pick blueberries on Coffs Harbour region farms.

In his judgment, Judge Robert Cameron said the workers were vulnerable given they were employed as pieceworkers on temporary visas and had limited English skills.

"A penalty should be of a kind that would deter similar contraventions by like-minded persons or organisations," he wrote.

"A failure to comply with a statutory notice is serious."

The workers had worked on blueberry farms. (ABC Rural: Brandon Long)

The Fair Work Ombudsman became aware of Four Seasons Workforce underpaying workers after it received two complaints from Chinese and Japanese backpackers.

The pair worked for the company at different intervals in 2023 and 2024.

The company was fined $63,000, while Ms Chey was fined $12,600 as Four Seasons Workforce's sole director.

The Fair Work Ombudsman said the workers were paid on a piecework basis according to the total weight of the blueberries they picked.

The ombudsman's media director Matthew Raggatt said the labour hire firm failed to pay them the guaranteed minimum rate, which was applied across the horticulture award.

"So for each day you work as a pieceworker, you have to be paid no less than the minimum hourly rate for casual fruit pickers under the relevant award," he said.

Kun Du worked on a blueberry farm in the Coffs Harbour region. (Supplied)

Chinese National Kun Du, who was one of the two workers involved in the case, said in a statement earlier this year that others should not be afraid to come forward.

"I just want to tell them to be brave, to fight for yourself and fight for more people," she said at the time.

" If you need help, you can access people's help. Don't be afraid. Be brave. "

More investigations underway

Mr Raggatt said the case against Ms Chey and Four Seasons Workforce was not the only case it had taken to court this year, as it continued investigations into the horticulture sector across the Coffs Coast and Nambucca Valley.

"Those investigations are ongoing, but we have filed another litigation [against an individual] in 2026 in the Coffs Harbour region, and that was in July," he said.

He said that case involved the alleged underpayment of two Japanese fruit pickers working on a farm in Halfway Creek, north of Coffs Harbour.

Matthew Raggatt says pieceworkers need to be paid the minimum hourly rate according to the award. (Supplied: Matthew Raggatt)

It has been alleged the two workers were underpaid about $7,000 over a seven-week period. The matter is still before the courts.

Elsewhere, the ombudsman secured more than $180,000 in penalties in Queensland in August this year in a case involving the horticulture industry.

Mr Raggatt said compliance notices were issued before court action was taken to give employers a chance to rectify the issue.

He said improving compliance in this sector and taking action to protect migrant workers were priorities for the regulator.

"Where employers do not comply, including with compliance notices, we will take appropriate action to protect employees," he said.

World.title: Breaking: John Setka expelled by CFMEU, denies 'misappropriating' $3.3m in union funds
World.content:
Former Victorian CFMEU boss John Setka says an allegation from the union's administration that he misappropriated more than $3 million in member funds is "absolute bullshit" and he plans to appeal his expulsion.

In a statement his afternoon, the CFMEU's administration said it had expelled Mr Setka from the organisation after he had faced 27 disciplinary charges under union rules.

"An investigation by the CFMEU administration alleged Setka had failed in his duty as secretary of the union and diverted $3.3 million in revenue from union merchandise and site vending machines to his companies," union administrators said in a statement.

In the statement, CFMEU administrator Michael Crosby said the union would pursue Mr Setka in a bid to recover "the millions that his company has received".

The CFMEU administration says John Setka's expulsion will take effect immediately and last five years. (AAP: Joel Carrett)

"John Setka held a position of responsibility but abused that privilege to take millions of dollars from the members of the CFMEU," Mr Crosby alleged.

"John Setka's conduct is shameful. He has failed in the most basic duties of a union official — to put members' interests above all."

The union administration said Mr Setka did not respond to them about the allegations.

John Setka says allegations are 'absolute lies'

The press release did not provide specifics of the alleged misappropriation and the ABC does not suggest the claims are true.

When contacted by the ABC, Mr Setka said the allegation was "absolute bullshit".

"I will be going to court, and I will be appealing the decision because its absolute lies and it's defamatory," he said.

"I have never taken one dollar of union members' money — that is an absolute lie."

Mr Setka led the Victorian division of the CFMEU for several years. (AAP: Stefan Postles)

The CFMEU administration said Mr Setka's expulsion would take effect immediately and last for a "legal maximum term of five years".

The construction arm of the CFMEU has been in administration since 2024, amid allegations of corruption and bullying in the union.

In September, Mr Setka faced court over an Instagram post he allegedly made attacking union administration figures.

World.title: Overseas stranger finds Australian family filmed in 1960s mystery video
World.content:
A British TV director has harnessed the power of talkback radio to find an Australian family who appeared in forgotten footage filmed in the 1960s.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised this story contains the name and images of a person who has died, used with family permission.

The video shows a classic scene from suburban Melbourne in 1965: a redbrick house, kids playing in the driveway under the watchful eye of two adults and their older children, flanked by grandma on the garden path.

The owner of the footage, Karen Walsh, was immediately struck by the video.

But she didn't have a clue who the family was.

It was shot by her father, Arthur Howes, who visited Australia in 1965 when he was considering emigrating with his young family.

Arthur Howes (second from left) with his family in England. (Supplied: Karen Walsh)

Mr Howes never took the plunge of permanently relocating, but he returned home from his adventure with moving pictures of Melbourne, Sydney and Perth to show his kids.

Now a TV director in the UK, Ms Walsh recently tackled the task of sorting through her father's old film reels.

The clip of a group of strangers was less than a minute long, but it was too precious for the cutting room floor.

"It is an absolutely charming little piece of video," she said.

"I just feel like I'm the curator of the footage. I don't feel I own it.

" I think the footage really belongs to the family who were being filmed. "

Bristol local Karen Walsh started the international search. (Supplied: Karen Walsh)

Needle in a haystack

The only lead Ms Walsh had to work with was the fact the 8mm film was shot in Melbourne.

Ms Walsh knew the reach of a talkback station, having worked in radio previously.

So she tried her luck and emailed 774 ABC Melbourne.

"It would be great to find out who these people are," she said.

The 774 Breakfast show broadcast Ms Walsh's call-out, and directed listeners to watch the footage online.

Amateur sleuths on socials noted the common brick design of the house, and distinctive green-striped garage door.

Volkswagen Club of Victoria historian Chris Scane identified the green van in the driveway as a standard split-window 1962 Kombi manufactured in Clayton, Victoria.

"We'll be chasing all our members to dig in their files and see if they can find this car," he said.

Some speculated two boys pictured leaping off the letterbox in the video were wearing Xavier College uniforms, but the school's archivist checked the records and ruled it out.

The van's number plates were a promising clue, but privacy laws prevented VicRoads from shedding any light on its owners.

'It was just mind-boggling'

By a stroke of luck, a medical student in Sydney helped solve the mystery.

Zac de Boeck called the talkback line to share that the video showed three generations of his family. (Supplied)

Zac de Boeck, a Palawa man, was scrolling social media when his mother sent him the ABC Melbourne reel to see if he too could recognise the faces.

Mr de Boeck immediately identified five people in the video.

So he called the talkback line.

The ABC has since confirmed the video from 1965 captures three generations of Mr de Boeck's family: his nan, great-uncle, great-grandparents and great-great-grandmother.

In the 1960s they lived in the Melbourne suburb of Mitcham.

The younger children playing in the film are believed to be extended family.

"As I opened the video, I initially spotted my great-grandmother, Dorothy Vanner," Mr de Boeck said.

Mrs Vanner, a Palawa woman, died 10 years ago, and would have turned 101 this year.

In the clip, she and her husband Ron Vanner are in their 40s, flanked by their two children.

"When I was born, great-grandma was 70, so in my brain, I only know her as an old lady," Mr de Boeck said.

"Seeing her only 10 years older than I am now, it was just mind-boggling."

Zac de Boeck, as a child, with Dorothy Vanner. (Supplied: Zac de Boeck)

A glimpse of the past

Mr de Boeck's nan, Kathryn Holland, is the older girl on the driveway in the clip, standing near her parents.

She doesn't remember the film being taken, or the visitor behind the camera, Arthur Howes.

But the clip offered her a rare chance to see her late mother, father and grandmother.

"I've got lots of photos, but I haven't seen them on film. It was quite a surprise," she said.

"I look so young!"

Kathryn Holland (right), pictured with Dorothy Vanner (left), Zac's mother Donna Bradbury and Zac as a baby, says she has plenty of family photographs but she has never seen moving pictures from her childhood. (Supplied: Zac de Boeck)

Mrs Holland was astonished by the lengths a stranger took to track her down.

"I just think she's extra special, going to all this trouble to find out who it belongs to," Mrs Holland said of Karen Walsh.

"It's fabulous."

Ms Walsh confessed she never expected her plan to work.

"I had no faith," she said.

"You know, I was so close to putting the film in the bin when I was going through the footage.

"Something made me stop and go, 'You know what, let's just see if we can find who this is.'"

World.title: Council backflips to ban climate group's protests on community land
World.content:
A NSW council has banned a climate action group from protesting on community land "now and into the future", sparking fears among activists about their right to peacefully protest.

Newcastle's Lord Mayor Gavin Morris used his casting vote on Tuesday to pass a motion opposing the use of "community-owned land for the purpose of Rising Tide's events/protests".

Those events include The People's Blockade of Newcastle Harbour, which was planned for February next year.

Previously, the City of Newcastle council had allowed Rising Tide to stage its event at Camp Shortland, adjacent to the harbour.

Police have argued that previous anti-coal protests in and around Newcastle Port have put police and protesters at risk. (AAP: Rising Tide)

Cr Morris told ABC Newcastle Breakfast that safety concerns raised over previous Rising Tide events were the catalyst for his decision.

"The constant request for them [Rising Tide activists] to remain within the boundaries has been broken, and it's been a constant breaking of promises," he said.

"Sadly, they keep pushing the boundaries beyond the realms of safety and something just needed to be done."

The council motion also noted the ban would apply to groups associated with Rising Tide.

Gavin Morris says safety concerns have influenced the decision. (ABC News: Keely Johnson)

Cr Morris, a former television weather presenter, said it was to ensure other groups did not "take over" the climate-action protests.

"That clause was put in there to ensure that all groups and associations that are linking up with Rising Tide can't come in under a separate name," he said.

Newcastle Greens councillor Siobhan Isherwood voted against the motion.

"I believe democracy only thrives when we have the right to free speech, the right to peaceful protest," she said.

"As a councillor who has some control over council land, I believe I should be defending that right."

Protesters respond

Rising Tide activist Zach Schofield has questioned the reasoning behind the ban.

Zach Schofield says the Newcastle council's decision has gone "too far". (ABC News: Xanthe Gregory)

"I want to reiterate we've had three people's blockades with hundreds and hundreds of people on the water en masse [and] we've had almost no serious safety concerns," he said.

"I think this has gone way too far.

" I'm desperately disappointed in Gavin Morris, but he's clearly picked a side. "

Rising Tide is also planning an anti-coal paddle out on Newcastle Harbour this Saturday, but that does not involve the use of community land and will not be affected by the council ban.

Rising Tide has argued that the "Paddle for the Planet" event will not be a blockade like previous events. (AAP: Rising Tide)

Right to gather threatened

President of the NSW Council for Civil Liberties Timothy Roberts said the decision threatened people's rights to peacefully gather.

"Frankly, council does not have the power to ban so broadly the huge sections of the community … from exercising their constitutional right to assemble," he said.

" Banning apparently any associated group without really defining what that is, I think, pretty unique. "

Timothy Roberts says Newcastle council's decision is concerning. (ABC News: Nick Dole)

Supreme Court action

Meanwhile, the Supreme Court is today hearing a NSW Police application for an order prohibiting this weekend's Rising Tide paddle out.

The court heard up to 785 people could attend the event, with at least 500 registered so far.

NSW Assistant Police Commissioner Dave Waddell told the court he had grave fears about what could happen.

"Particularly about the inability of people to make their way back to shore," he said.

"Last year some people ended up hundreds of metres down Horseshoe Beach.

"It is a risk, and you cannot possibly provide water safety to them from those positions."

The matter has been heard in the NSW Supreme Court. (ABC News: Jak Rowland)

Five hours have been set aside for the event, but Assistant Commissioner Waddell said he was worried about counter protests when that time frame ended.

"I have seen people talking about taking things into their own hands and having their own protest," he said.

The court was told more police resources had been called in, with officers from the public order and riot squad to patrol on land.

Rising Tide's Anne Hodgson told the court a prohibition order could backfire.

"It could have the opposite effect," she said.

"People are very passionate about this issue, and to have a court say we cannot protest in Australia might make people think we should have a right to protest on the public harbour."

World.title: How grooming claims against David Walliams came to light
World.content:
David Walliams, a British comedian, judge on Britain's Got Talent and children's author, has lost a legal bid to suppress accusations he groomed and preyed on teenage girls.

Walliams has denied the claims, which were published by ITV News and the Guardian overnight after a three-year investigation.

A court fight had prevented the news outlets from publishing their investigation for months, but a judge rejected Walliams's injunction request last week and the protection of his identity expired late Monday, UK time.

Here's what has come to light since.

Warning: This article includes allegations of sexual assault and references to suicide some readers may find distressing.

Who is David Walliams?

Walliams, 55, rose to fame in the early 2000s through Little Britain, a provocative comedy sketch show he created with Matt Lucas that broadcast on the BBC.

The pair won three BAFTAs and two International Emmys for the show, but in the two decades since it ended, it has been criticised for using blackface and mocking characters from marginalised groups.

David Walliams co-created sketch comedy series Little Britain with Matt Lucas. (Supplied: BBC)

Walliams is also a best-selling children's book author and has sold more than 60 million copies worldwide, with titles The Boy in the Dress and Gangsta Granny among his most popular.

Walliams joined Britain's Got Talent as a judge in 2012, a role he held until 2022 when remarks he made on the show were leaked. He later apologised for "disrespectful comments" about contestants.

He was married to Dutch model Lara Stone from 2010 to 2015 and they have a son.

He was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 2017 for his services and charity to the arts.

David Walliams was awarded an OBE at Buckingham Palace in 2017. (Reuters: Philip Toscano)

What are the accusations?

The accusations published by ITV News and the Guardian date back to 2003, when Walliams was in his 30s.

The Guardian said multiple women had alleged Walliams "abused his power and position as a celebrity to prey on them for sexual purposes when they were teenagers or young women".

One woman alleged she was sexually assaulted by Walliams at his London home when she was 15, while others accused him of grooming them when they were teenagers.

The allegations include:

One woman alleged Walliams groomed her from when she was 15 and they had sex when she was 17 and he was 34. She said it was consensual but it felt "pushy" and he treated her "like a prostitute". His lawyers said he believed she was 18.

Another woman alleged she met Walliams when she was 15 after he contacted her via social media. Aged 36, he allegedly invited her to his house and pulled up her top and sucked her breast.

Several women say Walliams first contacted them on social media, including six who were models aged between 19 and 22 at the time. One woman claims Walliams tried to kiss her while showing her around his home.

Walliams allegedly had an inappropriate sexual relationship with a junior female employee at HarperCollins UK and pursued another.

The Guardian and ITV News said their investigation involved more than 30 sources with first-hand accounts.

What has Walliams said?

The Guardian said Walliams had written a letter to the investigating journalists, denying that he abused his position of power.

"Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with," he wrote.

"I realise I did not always take people's feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.

"And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.

He added: "I am not a sexual predator."

"I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me," he said.

How did the accusations come to light?

Guardian and ITV reporters have investigated the accusations over the past three years.

Walliams had sought to block publication of the allegations primarily on the grounds he would attempt suicide if they became public.
